    Chapter 1

    Light.

    Not the kind of light the sun brings when it rises in the east, nor the kind that it takes away as it falls in the west. It’s not the dim light of the moon, the kind where its visible enough to know that it’s there but the one that doesn’t want to lighten the night sky and dampen the shine of the stars.

    It’s not the light of fireflies either.

    ‘Those are actually part of the Lampyridae family. And the glow, the glow that you see, that comes from a chemical reaction called bioluminescence.’

    No. It was too bright and white and harsh to be that of the forest stars either. All Natasha knew was that she wanted someone to turn the goddamn lights off. “You know I was quite enjoying the afterlife until you installed these new light fixtures. Glowy bastard.” Natasha said, only realising the croakiness of her voice and the sandpaper of her throat after the words had left her mouth. A few chuckles nearby pulled her out of her thoughts. That was a new feature. Huh. Maybe the lights could stay if she was no longer alone.

    “Of course, that’s the first thing you say after coming back from the dead.” A low voice mumbled exasperatedly to her right. The voice was full of emotion, which would usually be unnerving to Natasha, but she was more focused on the words that had just been spoken. Back from the dead? Okay. Sure. Because that’s plausible.

    You used to get emails from a racoon Nat.

    That’s not in the same realm as resurrection.

    And now you’re also talking to yourself and in the third person. Huh, God has really done a number on you today, Nat. Yeah, he’s definitely not a thing. And if he is, well, he is a horrible host.

    Her eyes slowly adjusting to what Natasha had concluded was the horrible artificial lighting of some hospital somewhere brought her out of her head once more. The grey of the ceiling now stood out amongst the squares trying to blind her, the white walls no longer playing the same game as the lights. A slow thumping in her head also brought attention to the aches in the rest of her body, and any normal person would have stayed in the same position in case moving brought on more pain but hey, pain only makes you stronger. Natasha somewhere finds the strength to push herself up, feeling hands behind her and words being spoken before she actually sees the rooms other occupants. When she is comfortably laid back on the now upright bed, she brings her hands to her eyes and rubs them. The room now comes clearly into focuses when she brings her hands away from her eyes. It looks incredibly similar to the medical room at the Avengers Compound and yet, it is not the same. And Natasha would know the difference. She spent a lot of time in there over the years. Feeling stumped yet again, she spins her head slowly to where the voices appeared from before to find wide and familiar eyes watching her. Clint and Steve look uncomfortably rigid in how they’re sat up in the leather armchairs that adorn the side of the bed she’s sat on, whilst Fury leans in the doorway, arms crossed with his usual mirth glimmering in his eye.

    “You know, sitting like that can’t be good for your guys’ old man backs.” The redhead said, croakiness slowly leaving her voice the more she spoke. A roll of the eyes from Clint and a breathy chuckle from Steve was all it took for a smile to take over Natasha’s face as she took them in. Her best friends looked tired. Clint’s hair was dishevel- Yeah not the best argument Natasha, it always looks like that. The bags under his eyes were dark, and she could’ve sworn he now has an extra scar over the bridge of his nose. So much for being retired. His ear now adorned what Natasha assumed was a hearing aid, which made her notice his body position slightly favoured having that ear turned towards her. Flicking her eyes to Steve. Well, he looks the same. Super solider serum and all that. Turning her head away from the several men in the room, she lays her head back on the pillow and closes her eyes before taking a shaky breath in.

    “Fill me in.” Natasha says forcefully. “And get me my phone.”

    “So, new Avengers compound huh? Pepper kept some of Tony’s flair I see.” Natasha pointed to the weird abstract statue in the corner just off from the kitchen. “Even though the bugger is dead, still always getting his way.” She continued as Steve placed a PB&J in front on her, alongside the half full glass of water she was harbouring.

    “You know Tony. His will was full of strange requests. And Pepper… has always been good at her job.” The dirty blonde said as he took the other seat opposite her, beside Clint who was chuckling softly at the conversation.

    “I can’t believe he is actually gone.” Natasha said, staring out of the window behind the two men. The early morning sun beaming down on the well-kept lawn. Probably another request of Tony’s. Pulling herself out of her grief, Natasha reached for her phone that sat on the table, scrolling a text chain as if the action would incite a reply. After a couple minutes of comfortable silence, and no new message, the redhead pulled her gaze off her phone and back to Clint and Steve. Steve’s eyes were full of confusion and hesitation. Natasha knew he wanted to ask about what was her sad desperation for a text message. She sighed before turning to rest her gaze on Clint. He was fiddling with his hands as if nervous, which was something she had only seen the archer do when he told Nat that he was thinking about proposing to Laura.

    “Clint.” The man’s eyes flew up to Natasha’s face as she said his name. “She’s alive.” He said almost immediately as he saw the unasked question in the redhead’s eyes. A breath Natasha didn’t know she had been holding in tumbled out of her mouth. She held Clint’s gaze begging him to continue, his eyes flicked to Steve whose head was bouncing between the two of them. Natasha waved Clint’s non-verbal question away quicker than it could be vocalised.

    “Are you sure? How do yo-“ “She tried to kill me.”

    Natasha snorted. “And yet you’re very much breathing. She can’t have been trying very hard.”

    “I was blue and green for months after that. Believe me. She tried. Her knife was very much on my throat when I decided to do your guys’ whistle. Figured I’d be dead if I didn’t try or dead if she hated that someone who wasn’t you did it.” Clint said, his eyes sobering up as the memories obviously came flooding back.

    “How long ago?”

    “Uh. About 10 months ago. Give or take?”

    Natasha sighed at Clint’s answer, running her hands through her hair.

    “Uhh, who are we talking about?” Steve’s waving hand coming in between her and Clint breaking the silence that had taken over. A smirk glazed over Nat’s lips as she turned her gaze to Steve. This was going to be fun.

    “моя маленькая сестра.”

    “Nat. Don’t know if being dead frazzled your mind but I still don’t speak Russian.” Natasha laughed at the look on his face. “Mind is fully intact Rogers. We are talking about Yelena.”

    Steve gave her another confused look. “Who?” Meanwhile, Clint just sighed, standing up from the table, taking the dirty dishes to the sink which sat a few metres away. Natasha chuckled softly before taking a breath.

    “My little sister.”

    Chapter 2

And before you argue with me and say you did whatever the nightmare says you did, you didn’t. It’s not your fault Yelena. The- They… they abused you, used you, manipulated you… that… you ugh. I don’t see you often, I know, but I like to feel like I know you pretty well by now. You are not who your mind is showing you Lena. I don’t believe it, and neither should you. Don’t you think on it. Don’t you think on it for one second.” Kate rambled out, squeezing Yelena tighter every time the blonde winced or opened her mouth to fight back.

    When the two women finally let go of each other, no words are spoken between the two. Something that even took Kate by surprise, seeing as she cannot normally keep her mouth shut. Yelena had only turned around and grabbed two sets of cutlery out of the draw. Yes. Kate had finally caved and bought more cutlery. The blonde wordlessly handed a set to the brunette before picking up the two boxes and dropping them on the kitchen table, kicking out the chair next to the one she had sat down in. A silent invitation for Kate to join her. A silent invitation which Kate understood as Yelena saying ‘Thank You’.

    Chapter 3

    Kate didn’t even flinch when Yelena grabbed her keys out of her back pocket to unlock her front door. In all honesty, Kate didn’t even realise she had locked the door and taken the keys with her, and it wasn’t until her apartment swung into view did a wave of embarrassment wash over her. Kate wasn’t often embarrassed. She wasn’t often caught off guard either, but at the sight of her apartment, Kate felt as if Yelena had dumped a bucket of icy water over her head. The brunette wished Lucky wasn’t in Iowa to drag the attention to him instead as the door swung fully open. As Yelena nudged her into the apartment, locking the door behind them, Kate ran her eyes around the room. There was shattered glass on the kitchen floor from where she dropped a cup, the aftermath of being on the phone with her mum’s lawyers. The take-out boxes from the beginning of the week before Kate’s life had changed were still there, the brunette being too busy run off her feet at Bishop Security to bother to throw them out when she came home exhausted and collapsed on the couch. Her archery equipment was in a mess on the floor, the punching bag normally hung up under her stairs was splattered with her own blood and her dining table definitely had one less chair with four legs than it did a week ago. Kate didn’t even need to go upstairs to know her bedroom floor had become her wardrobe or to see the crack in her bathroom mirror. The open wounds on her knuckles reminded her clear enough.

    A light touch on her lower back brought her out of her musings as Yelena nudged her towards the couch. Kate had no opposition to the pillows swallowing her whole and so followed Yelena’s indication and threw herself backwards into the cushions. The brunette’s hair splayed over the back of the couch; legs thrown up on the coffee table. Kate heard her mother tutting at her, for her dirty boots were surely getting dirt all over the wood. With her mind off elsewhere, the brunette didn’t notice Yelena’s movements as she closed her eyes. The blonde watched the brunette slump back into her own head, eye’s fluttering slightly as her head relaxed and fell deeper into the couch cushions. Yelena started by grabbing a trash bag from under Kate’s sink, picking up the broken chunks glass on the floor along with the multitude of empty pizza boxes dotted around the room. Her eyes flitting to the brunette every couple of minutes, green eyes unconsciously falling on the rise of Kate’s chest. Whether or not that was to check she was still alive and breathing or for another reason was Yelena’s business alone. The blonde then tackled the mess under Kate’s stairs, propping the bloodied punching bag against the wall, before slotting the archery equipment back in the assorted crates to the wall opposing the kitchen. The blood on the bag prompted Yelena’s memory of Kate’s knuckles, taking two steps at a time, Yelena wandered up to the brunette’s bedroom and subsequently the bathroom where the younger Hawkeye kept her first aid kit. Yelena carefully stepped in-between items of clothing, not wanting to soil them with her probably muddy shoes, although knowing Kate, half of them where supposedly a ‘dirty laundry pile’ and were yet to be washed. As light flooded the bathroom, Yelena’s mind was sprung back to the last time she was in the archer’s proximity. Her nightmare had scared Kate shitless and confused the young woman to no end, and yet she had stayed. Not only did she stay, but she also bought Yelena breakfast from a diner Kate had seen the blonde eyeing up. And that scared Yelena shitless, no one was meant to be able to read her that easily, and yet Kate had achieved it like it was as easy as pulling a bowstring was for her. The blonde ran her fingers over the crack in the mirror, wondering whether this is how Kate initially injured her knuckles or whether she had beaten the bag to its demise before that. Yelena wished the brunette had done neither. At least with the crack in the mirror Yelena couldn’t see the state of herself. She was sure her face was splayed with emotion, something that was not common for the assassin.

    “Fuck.” Yelena muttered to her broken reflection before letting out a shaky sigh. Her fingers turning white as she gripped the edge of the sink harder than she needed to lean down and pick up the first aid box. Taking one last look at the smashed mirror Yelena plunged the bathroom back into darkness before heading back down to Kate.

    The brunette hadn’t moved an inch since she had sat down. Her breathing was deep and heavy, but Yelena could tell she wasn’t asleep. Just emotionally and physically exhausted. Tapping Kate’s thigh lightly before sitting down next to her, the brunette’s head rolled slowly to her right to face her.

    As Yelena reached for Kate’s closest hand, gently bringing it to rest of her own thigh, Kate’s eyes slowly opened.

    “Leave them.”

    At Yelena’s lack of response and her continued motion of prepping the items she had pulled out of the first aid kit, Kate spoke again whilst moving her hand off Yelena’s thigh and back to her own.

    “Leave them Lena.” The words came out tiredly and with a lack of fight. Yelena only rolled her eyes at the brunette’s stubbornness, once again gently pulling Kate’s hand towards her, this time meeting the blue eyes staring at her, not needing words to convince Kate she was cleaning them whether she wanted her to or not. Kate didn’t take her eyes off Yelena the whole time as the blonde cleaned and wrapped her bloodied hands, her calloused hands gentler than Kate thinks anyone else in the world would’ve expected. The blonde finished wrapping both hands and was cleaning up the wrappings of the bandages when the words tumbled out of the brunette’s mouth.

    “My mom’s dead.”

    Yelena was quiet for a moment, and without turning to face the brunette, granted her a response, happily willing to focus on shutting the first aid kit instead. “I know.”

    “She was stabbed.”

    “I know.”

    “Her lawyers think it was some of Kingpins goons. T-the good ones, n-not the… idiot ones.” Kate’s eyes fighting off sleep as she spoke dejectedly, waving her arm as she finished her sentence.

    “Smart lawyers.”

    “I think anyone could have figured it out Yelena. Heck, Lucky could’ve figured it out.” At this the blonde finally turned her head to face the brunette. Kate saw her normally sharp and cold green eyes soften slightly as they landed on her, the brunette’s mind didn’t have the energy to wonder why the assassin was letting her emotions run so clearly across her normally blank face before Yelena was adjusting her body. Her back now leaning on the arm of the couch, moving to tuck her toes under Kate’s thigh. A small smile flickered across Kate’s face at the contact before turning sullen again. “I-I I-I’m-“ “Kate. You don’t have to talk about it.”

    The brunette shook her head with a force Yelena wasn’t expecting. As if she had shaken all the tiredness out of her, Kate pulled herself more upright, although her head still leant backwards facing the assassin. “I jus- I just… ugh.” Kate said before falling silent again. Her mouth opening and closing a few times in the minutes after whilst her eyes roamed around her apartment.

    “You didn’t have to tidy my mess up for me.” She spoke quietly a few moments later. “I know. Felt like upholding a tradition. Cleaning up after you, saving you from having more bruised ribs.” Yelena said with a small teasing smile, earning a light scoff out of Kate. The brunette’s mouth turning slightly upwards, making the smile on Yelena’s face linger for longer than it would normally.

    “Mom’s team have managed to keep it quiet for now, they’re announcing it…” Kate paused as stopped and patted her body to search for her phone, before stopping again and shoving her hand in-between the couch cushions, pulling it out in one swift motion as if the act was something common for her. “In the morning.” She finished her unfinished sentence with a sigh, the hand holding her phone flopping to her side. Yelena opened her mouth to say, well, she wasn’t sure, but Kate’s words sounded first.

    “I haven’t even cried.” The brunette all but practically spat. “What kind of daughter doesn’t cry when her mother dies. I don’t even fee- I was 18 when my grandma died. I cried for hours, and hours, and I saw her a couple times a year at best, but God was I sad. I didn’t eat for days, I just slept and cried. And now my mother is brutally murdered, and I don’t even feel upset. I-I…I’m so relieved.” Kate rambled out. Yelena was sure Kate didn’t even breathe in when she paused between words. The blonde’s eyebrows furrowed slightly as she recognised what Kate had actually said, but before she could question further Kate stood up from the couch, wobbling slightly in reaction to the speed at which she had got to her feet. The brunette rounded the coffee table before she started pacing back and forwards in front of the Yelena. The blonde turned her body off the couch, so her feet were firmly back on the floor. legs apart as she rested her forearms on her knees, holding her own hands in the gap, as she watched the young woman pace so hard she may as well be leaving footprints as if she was walking on snow.

    “Relieved sounds horrible doesn’t it. Relieved.” Kate scoffed, almost laughing at herself. “And I’m so angry at her, at Kingpin, at the tracksuits, the prison guards, her legal team, the whole world. And at Dad. If he was here, I think I would kill him myself. But I’m not even angry she’s dead!” Kate shouted as she flopped back down besides Yelena, her bandaged hands gripping her head. “She’s dead. She’s with Dad and I’m stuck here. I’m stuck here with her dead body and all the mess that oozes out of it. Her blood money, her enemies, her goddamn company and even her shitty expectations. She said she did all that she did for me and yet she left me to deal with all her shit, without a care in the world of how that would affect me.” The brunette huffed out, the strength in her body seeming to dissipate, so much so, Yelena ended up with Kate’s thighs leaning against hers, and a shoulder covered in brunette locks. The blonde shuffled slightly at the new position, trying to get some support for her back in the crumpled cushions. Kate jumped back from the assassin at her movement, her eyes wide and mouth stuttering with a ready apology. Yelena rolled her eyes, wrapping her right arm around Kate’s back and pulling her back into her side. The brunette hesitated for a moment before allowing herself to sink all her weight into the blonde, her face turned slightly into Yelena’s neck but not enough to block her sight of the bursting pocket seams on Yelena’s vest.

    Yelena was never normally one to touch, almost actively finding a way to avoid it but somehow Kate had weaselled her way past that boundary and Yelena couldn’t find fight enough in her to stop it. The blonde could feel Kate’s warm breath hitting her neck as she exhaled, the brunette’s weight seeping further into Yelena as her breath’s became deeper again. The blonde knew she was tensed up under Kate. Touch was something foreign to her and well, there was a hell of a lot of Kate on top of her right now. Not that Kate was an unwanted presence in her space or on her body, no, she was kind of the opposite of that, and yet Yelena’s body physically reacts as if she has just been shot. Thankfully, before the seeping pain of a bullet can spread throughout the assassin’s body, Kate’s stomach rumbles. Yelena chuckles softly, some of the tension releasing from her body.

    “When did you last eat маленький ястреб?”

    “Not hungry.” Kate mumbled into Yelena’s neck, gripping to the blonde tighter as if that would stop Yelena getting up to go and get food.

    “Your stomach clearly disagrees.” The blonde poked a finger into Kate’s side making her squirm, before she stilled, and the noise erupted again. Kate only tightened her grip in response. “It’s cute you think that I cannot stand up from this couch whilst you grip me like a koala.”

    “You think I’m cute?” Kate’s face emerges from Yelena’s neck with a small smirk. Yelena rolls her eyes at the brunette before wrapping her fingers around Kate’s wrist and pulling her waist free of the archer’s grasp. Kate doesn’t fight the blonde, just throwing her body backwards so she’s splayed flat on her back. Yelena ignores the brunette’s dramatics before heading into Kate’s kitchen with the lowest of expectations, which were strongly exceeded by the contents of Kate’s fridge. Said contents being a sad looking orange and a jar of cranberry sauce. Shutting the fridge door, Yelena peers back to where Kate hadn’t moved from the couch, on arm thrown over her eyes, the other hanging off the side.

    “I will get food. I be back soon.”

    Kate moved to sit up as the Russian woman pulled on her coat which had somehow appeared in her apartment. This realisation made Kate’s eyes find a large leather duffel bag also sat by her front door before the blue eyes made their way back up to the green ones staring at her, waiting for an answer.

    “You’re staying?” Kate’s comment brought out yet another eye roll from Yelena. “We’re friends, no? You struggle. I help.” The blonde shrugged as if her prolonged presence in Kate’s life was something not unbeknownst to the two women. Yelena saw Kate’s features soften and the brunette’s lip quiver slightly before a small smile appeared. The only response the blonde got was a small nod before Kate fell backwards once more.

    “I shall return Kate Bishop.”

    “I’m keeping your stuff indefinitely if you don’t. No takebacks.” A fragile and wavering voice sounded from the couch. Yelena chuckled softly before shutting and locking Kate’s front door behind her.

    Yelena wandered back from the very sad excuse of a shop she had visited to make sure Kate Bishop did not waste away. Yelena pondered on the thought that she had hoped a few days would be enough time to comfort Kate, but the sight of the brunette on the ledge of that rooftop flashed through her mind. And it wasn’t long after she crossed back into Central Park did the image of Kate’s broken body lying on the concrete break into her mind also. The blonde rebuffed these images, muttering to herself the obscenity of her imagination. After all, as long as she was nearby, Kate couldn’t be harmed. Yelena couldn’t pinpoint why this rich kid from New York had invaded her mind so, but the more time she spent with Kate, the harder it was to push away from what Yelena knew deep within. Holding the grocery bag in one hand, Yelena fiddled with her phone in the other. It wasn’t hard to obtain Clint Barton’s phone number, after all Kate hadn’t made it hard for anyone looking in her contacts to find exactly, The World’s Second Greatest Archer had glared out at Yelena almost immediately. Kate hadn’t mentioned Clint’s name once since Yelena had found her earlier today, and the blonde had been an assassin long enough to know that was suspicious; the one person Kate idolises more than anyone in the world and went head-to-head with a Black Widow for, you would assume he would have been mentioned in the event of Eleanor Bishop’s death. Yelena was surprised Clint hadn’t heard about it before her mom’s lawyers or Yelena herself. Plus, the blonde has a clear enough idea of Barton’s character by now to know that he would’ve been on the first plane out to be with Kate if he knew. The main question was why hadn’t Kate told him?

    Every question and possibility jumbled Yelena’s insides like her cells were being popped like corn or tumbled around like clothes in a washing machine. The blonde’s stomach churned with emotion as she passed the park’s grandstand, pulling up Barton’s number on her phone, sensibly labelled as Bint Clarton, and she hesitated. A Black Widow doesn’t hesitate. Yelena groaned before hitting her phone on her head a few times. It seems as if a Hawkeye’s effect of wreaking internal havoc were not limited to Kate. Clint Barton did not scare Yelena. It should be as easy as clicking the call button and speaking to the man she tried to kill almost a year ago as if she hadn’t?

    A car horn broke Yelena out of the prison in her head and alerting her to the fact that she needed to turn left now unless she wanted to walk an extra five blocks to get back to Kate’s. She passed the little hole in the wall places that Kate had pointed out on their walk back from Kate’s ‘The Battle of the Alleyway’ as the brunette so lovingly called it: the hidden bar down the tiniest side street, Trent’s hot dog stand that always stood on the corner of 106th Street and the drain that Kate had dropped a bagel down not once, but twice. Yelena hadn’t met many rich people, okay that’s a lie, but she hasn’t met many rich people like Kate. Most would turn their noses up at the humble places the brunette frequented, opting to travel to locales boasting wealth and prestige instead. And yet Kate seemed to fit right in wherever she went. Yelena may be good at pretending to be someone she isn’t when she needs to be, but Kate was such a complex character that she had all of Yelena’s possible pretences curled up inside her already.

    She was a walking contradiction.

    A rhyme wrapped in a riddle.

    Yelena passes the restaurant she knows Kate pretty much keeps in business, partially because the brunette was hopeless in the kitchen but also because she loves the old man who owns the place. Yelena has a strong suspicion that Kate prefers his company to his food, but she knows the brunette would never admit to that. After all, if the archer was to semi-insult his cooking, Kate might no longer get her discounted meals and Yelena was sure that would be like the end of the world to the brunette, and the end of the blonde’s hearing when a passionate rant about the subject was bound to come out of her mouth. Sometimes her friend spoke so fast that Yelena had a hard time translating what she was saying, and yet when Kate had told her over drinks that she got even more chatty when she had consumed alcohol, Yelena couldn’t have stopped the smile that had spread over her face, even with her Red Room Training. Kate was a contagious ball of energy, and yet Yelena couldn’t help but feel calm in her presence.

    Simply put, Kate was her friend. Not a widow, someone with no obligation to be her friend, not someone entangled in the web of her past and someone who saw her as Yelena Belova and not a little girl running from what haunts her. Kate wanted to be her friend and as much as that scared Yelena shitless, Kate made her feel human in ways no one else ever had.

    As Kate’s apartment building came into view, Yelena had made up her mind. It was because Kate was her friend that she was going to contact Barton. He was Kate’s primary parental figure now, and even though Yelena had missed out on two of those in her life for over 20 years, she knew how impactful that figure could be, both good and bad. The blonde leant against the brick wall of the building opposite Kate’s, the side Yelena had scaled her way up to ‘break in’. She could just about see Kate’s feet from her spot, still in the same position on the couch as she had been when Yelena left. This brought a small chuckle out of the assassin, releasing some of the tension she felt building in her jaw as she clicked on the call button.

    Chapter 4

    Chapter Notes hope everyone who celebrates had a lovely christmas! thank you for all the love on this story, have been writing a bit over the holiday period due to having a couple of days off work so have the next two chapters after this almost fully written.

    sorry this chapter is a little bit shorter than the ones previously, needed a good place to end it and it just so happened to cut the word count a bit short. trying to move the story along so miniscule jumps are needed so i am not writing every hour of kate and yelena's days especially now more characters are becoming involved. if anyone has any small suggestions of what they would like to see like specific moments or dialogue just comment them and if i can include them i will try my best to do them justice! to anyone who has bothered to read this note, there is alot of angst coming in the next chapter and not just from kate and also dun dun dun we get a sneak peek at a softening yelena :)

    “Clint. You suck.”

    Clint laughed as Natasha groaned at him again for about the fiftieth time in the past five minutes. She was sat on the couch opposite from him, Steve next to her, his arm slung around the back of the chair. A large woollen navy blanket draped across their legs; Nat’s fallen sideways to rest on the side of Steve’s thigh.

    “I’ve told you my side of the story. You should wait and hear Yelena’s from her. Plus, I can’t say I know a lot about what happened except from when she was in front of my eyes. Kate didn’t say all that much apart from that Yelena said she was your sister.” Clint explained, rubbing his forehead as Natasha rolled her eyes again. The redhead’s excessive eye movement was causing Clint’s already hurting head more pain. The three of them had hardly slept since Nat had awoken the previous morning, the clock on the wall bearing a time of 5:05am. It was Steve’s turn to groan this time as Nastasha punched him in the arm. “Steve. Get him to tell me. Otherwise, you have my permission to lob your shield at his head.” Nat smirked at Clint, raising an eyebrow in a threatening manner. Clint only chuckled again before raising his hands in surrender. After a long minute of silence, and an unbroken gaze, the redhead peeled her eyes away from Clint, throwing her head back so it rested on Steve’s arm, her eyes finding the ceiling instead. “Fine.” She sighed, a yawn escaping her mouth a moment later.

    “Anyone up for some sleep? I know I certainly am.” Steve said as he watched Nat yawn and then shake her head in response to his question.

    “I’ve been asleep for what… 24 months? I’m good. But you old men feel free.” The redhead said as she pulled her head back up and brushing a strand off of her face. Clint had opened his mouth to respond before his phone rang. Pulling it out of his pocket, a crease appeared between his eyebrows.

    “Who is it?” Steve asked. Natasha’s head tilting slightly right, non-verbally mirroring his question. Clint shrugged, flipping the phone screen towards the two sat across from him, the words ‘Unknown Number’ travelling across the screen. The archer stood up and slightly wandered across the room. He could hear Steve and Nat mumbling between themselves and so answered the call before pulling the phone to his ear.

    “This is Barton.” He said as he leant back against the kitchen counter, Steve and Natasha directly in his eyesight. Their gazes travelling to him every so often. “Is that seriously how you answer your phone?” A familiar Russian accent sounded through the phone.

    “W-wha… Oh my god.” He whisper shouted, turning his back on Steve and Natasha, “Yelena?”

    “Yes, it’s me Barton. Do not sound so shocked. It is not hard for an international assassin get your number after all. You should know this.” The sound of a city sounded in the background of the call.

    “That is not… Are you calling about Natasha?” Clint asked hesitantly. “What? Why would I be calling about my dead сестра?” The blonde spat down the phone. Clint held his breath for a moment, before exhaling shakily.

    “Did you not get any texts recently…?” The archer dragged his sentence out slowly, not knowing how to traverse this conversation. At least not with the pretty volatile personality that he had experienced with Yelena the last time.

    “No Barton. I did not. Now listen to me, Eleanor Bishop is dead. Kate is oka-“ “What?”

    “What is it with men and interrupting? Вот почему мне нравятся женщины,” He heard the Russian grumble down the line, the foreign language spoken to fast and in too low a tone for Clint to pick up on what the blonde had said over the city noise.

    “I heard from Kate on… Thursday evening. It’s now Monday morning. You’re telling me she dropped dead over the weekend and Kate hasn’t called me?”

    “Yes.”

    “What happened? Is Kate okay? Where is she? Where are you?” Clint spoke so fast he reminded himself of Kate for a split second.

    “If you had let me finish Barton, you would have all this information by now.” Yelena drawled down the phone. Clint thinks she was enjoying having all the information far too much.

    “Tell me Yelena or so help me…” The archer surprised himself at how low his voice went. “Working theory is that Kingpin had some of his good men imprisoned. The smart ones, not the pathetic ones chasing you around on Christmas. They attack Eleanor Bishop for what she did, and what she owed.”

    “Stabbing?”

    “Hole in one Barton. Actually, it was four holes. Two in the abdomen, one in the femur and one in the back. Ouch.”

    Clint frowned at Yelena’s nonchalant tone.

    “And Kate?”

    “Tried to jump off a roof.”

    “She did what?” Clint heard his raise so loud he practically made himself jump. He heard questioning calls of his name from behind him. Turning around so he could face them, he held a finger up, signalling them to wait, “She is fine. I pulled her off the ledge. I clean her apartment and fix her wounds. Now I am buying her food.” Yelena said so calmly and indifferently, Clint fought the urge to throw his phone and his best friend’s little sister across the room. “She found out on Friday from her mom’s lawyers. I found out Saturday morning. Another widow ID’d the body for me, it’s definitely her and she’s definitely dead Barton. Nick Fury obviously forgot to share his faking death pills.” The blonde continued as Clint walked back over to Steve and Nat, throwing himself on the couch.

    “I can be there in forty-five minutes.” Clint said sternly, a verbal warning to Yelena that he wasn’t in the mood for her subtle digs right now.

    “The hawk has flown his nest.” Yelena stated, a door slamming opening and closing in the background. “Where are you, Barton?” Her voice was quieter now.

    “Yes, because I am going to tell the person who tried to kill me my location.” Clint deadpanned, ignoring the widening of Nat’s eyes and the hand Steve moved to grip Nat’s thigh.

    “I thought Tony Stark was the big ego Avenger. Did he transfer it to you in his death?” Yelena paused a moment. Clint’s mouth opened and closed without a retort. “I have more important things than to hunt you down Barton. If I still wanted you dead, it would not have taken me almost a year to do so. Did you ever cook at Kate’s apartment whilst you were here? Her oven is so weird. So weird.” A chuckle came through the phone at the end of Yelena’s rant. An eyebrow raised slightly on Clint’s face.

    “You’re cooking for her? At 5am?” Clint’s tone rising in surprise.

    “Do not sound so shocked Barton. I am not a monster. God knows when she last ate, I’m not going to let her die of starvation. That would not be a cool way to die.” “Hold on, can we backtrack a little? How did you find out about Eleanor?” “She was an ex-employer I never fulfilled the job for Barton. It is always best to keep an eye on all your possible enemies at one time.” Yelena said as it that was supposed to be obvious. “Eleanor is a threat? To you?” Clint questioned shocked. He was even more shocked when a laugh sounded down the phone.

    “No Barton. No.” The blonde said between laughs. “But to Kate? Maybe by association.” The assassin said, sounding as if she had shrugged as she said this.

    “And Kate’s safety suddenly matters to you why?” Clint asked, head now thrown back, resting on the back of the couch. One hand coming up and rubbing his forehead between his thumb and index finger. Yelena was quiet for a moment before a snort erupted from Clint’s phone speaker.

    “She hasn’t told you. Huh. And here I was thinking Kate couldn’t keep her mouth shut for anything.”

    “What is it Yelena?” Clint’s eyes widened as the assassin’s name slipped out of his mouth. His gaze snapped up to look at the redhead in front of him. Her eyes were full of emotion and the only thing holding her off from bolting to grab the phone from Clint’s hand was Steve holding her back. Clint pulled the phone away from his ear and put it on speaker. “We’re friends.” Yelena’s tone was cool and yet soft. Natasha’s eyes softened even more and began to well with tears as she heard the familiar Russian drawl of her sister. “Friends?” Clint sounded sceptical as he watched Steve pull Nat into his side, his hand rubbing comforting patterns on her side.

    “We shared mac and cheese and play fought across the top of that Rock Building thing. That was fun. Oh and Kate asked me if I wanted to grab a drink with her before I kicked her through that doorway.” Yelena softly chuckled through the phone. “So, we got drinks on New Years. Then I saved her arse before we had a movie night. What else? Oh, we had breakfast together one morning. And now I am here again, taking care of маленький ястреб.” “I think Katie Kate and I need to have a little chat about befriending people who try to kill her a week previously.” Clint chuckled as he shook is head in disbelief. So many emotions were crawling through his head at this moment, he didn’t know which one to focus on. He was shocked about Eleanor, and about the fact Kate hadn’t told him. Shocked about Yelena and Kate’s apparent friendship, which once more Kate hadn’t mentioned, and about Yelena’s sudden phone call in general. He was also worried about Kate. Concerned about the nonchalantly mentioned jumping off the roof thing? And most of all, Clint felt overwhelmed with joy at that look on his best friend’s face at hearing her sister’s voice alive and well. “I did not try to kill her.” Yelena’s voice sounded insulted.

    “You threw her off a roof.”

    “What is it with hawk’s? I put her on a wire to remove an obstacle. And then I made her mac and cheese. All was forgiven.” The scraping of metal cutlery against a bowl sounded out before a shuffling clothing noise was muffling the microphone. “I’m about to wake her up to eat if you want to talk to her Barton.”

    Clint only hummed in the alternative, the three avengers listening intently as they heard Yelena softly calling Kate’s name multiple times, before a grumbling American accent rang through the room.

    “Lena?” Nat’s eyebrows raised at the nickname for her sister. Yelena did not like nicknames. “Sit up маленький ястреб. You need to eat. Come on, eat please. My daddy says its good for you.”

    “What is it?” A silence passed before Kate’s voice was heard again. “It’s so annoying how you’re good at everything.” At that they heard Yelena laugh softly before both ends of the line went quiet again. A short gasp was heard by the group of three a few minutes later before the brunette’s voice echoed out of Clint’s phone.

    “Clint.”

    “Katie Kate.”

    Chapter 5

    Chapter Notes happy new year! (its 4am on the 4th as i'm writing this but still counts :)) starting this year off with some good yet bad news.

    work hours are decreasing so have 3 days off coming up next week which means more time to write! but also less income :/ i hope you all enjoy angst because there is alot of it coming up in the next few chapters. upto chapter 7 is fully written in draft, it needs proof reading and maybe some add ins but we're getting there. i'm officially over the 20,000 word mark in total so longer chapters are coming (around 3500-4000 words per chapter ish)

    enjoy discovering a complex kate and an even more complex yelena! both of which will have many more future appearances.

    “Why didn’t you call me Katie? I could’ve been there as soon as you knew.” Clint mumbled down the line. Kate guessed he was moving around from the interference over the line. The brunette didn’t respond to his question for a while, preferring to eat the bowl of chicken, rice, and veggies that Yelena had pushed into her hands instead. The blonde was sat quietly beside her, halfway through eating a granola bar, obviously not wanting such a meal at 5am. “Kate? You still there?” Clint’s voice sounded again, breaking the long silence between the three of them. When Kate didn’t respond again, Yelena leant forward to where her phone lay and picked it up before she turned to the brunette. Kate’s hands were trembling and her eyes glassy. The blonde squeezed her thigh with one hand whilst taking the phone off speaker and bringing it to her ear.

    “Barton. I’ll call you back.”

    “Yelena. What’s happening?”

    “I’ll call you back.” The blonde said, finality in her tone. She threw her phone across the couch, it slightly bouncing off the cushions, as she lowered herself to crouch on the floor in front of Kate. Gently taking the half-eaten bowl of food from the brunette’s hands and replacing the space with her own, she squeezed tightly, bringing the blue eyes that had been fixated on the wall to meet with her green ones.

    “Breathe маленький ястреб.” At this Kate took a sharp and shaky breath, before exhaling the same way. Her breath’s coming in were more like short and hyperventilating gasps for air, but Yelena thought it was better than Kate having no oxygen at all. After almost another minute of Kate’s chest heaving up and down, Yelena realised the situation was quickly getting out of hand. The brunette’s widening eyes only signifying she was panicking more at her own panic.

    “I know, I know маленький ястреб , but you have to breathe for me, okay?” Kate only shook her head at this, adamant that her lungs could not do that right now.

    “Okay, okay, come here,” Yelena said as she moved behind Kate’s shaking body and wrapped her legs around Kate’s form. Kate weakly struggled against the hold that she’d been put in, before giving up at the strength Yelena was displaying at restraining her. Kate’s chest was still heaving for air and was beyond any reasoning at this point as she sobbed and struggled. Yelena just pulled her closer and rested her chin on her shoulder.

    “Kate, you’ve got to breathe with me. Inhale… hold it… and deep breath out…” Yelena whispered, and whilst not even thinking placed a kiss behind her ear, happy as she saw that Kate was at least trying to control her panicking lungs.

    They sat there for what felt like hours, but it was in fact only around 10 few minutes, before Kate’s panic had faded into a soft, and silent stream of tears with the occasional sniffle here and there. She had collapsed back into Yelena’s arms as soon as her lungs let her gasp for air, who sat drawing patterns on her stomach with the arm she had crossed over it, the other, stroking baby hairs off the brunette’s clammy forehead. Kate’s eyes were fluttery at the motion, her breath’s getting deeper and heavier, in complete contrast to just a few moments ago. Her body was getting heavier against Yelena as her muscles relaxed, and her exhaustion of the past two days seeped over her. Yelena kept her gentle movements going as Kate sunk deeper and deeper into the affection she was receiving. The blonde knew the brunette was on the brink of falling asleep in her arms, but she didn’t have the heart or the want to move her. Looking down at the young archer, Yelena exhaled her own shaky breath as she relaxed into the couch cushions.

    Kate had brought up a sense of playfulness in Yelena that she quite enjoyed. The brunette was almost incomprehensible to the blonde, she was good-natured, light-hearted, stubborn, a little bit annoying, childish, uncomplicated, and even though Yelena could pick out all of these traits and more she knew about the Avenger wannabe, Kate was still a continuous surprise to the blonde. And enough of a mystery that she kept Yelena coming back again and again.

    First at New Years, the drinks invitation lingering in at the front of her mind as she spent the holidays in Russia, even with the now familiar pang of longing that set up camp in her chest at her sister’s absence. Yelena had returned to New York a day before the end of the year, wanting to fulfil her dreams she had of the city, visiting the landmarks that were on her list, plus the ones recommended to her over a pan of mac and cheese. They were almost as she expected them to be: packed with tourists, mixed with smells of street food and the normal New York staple of garbage and yet they were as magical as everyone said they were. They were dancing lights, familial laughter and true happiness all rolled into one. The blonde had then returned to Kate’s apartment, this time on a friendly matter. Yelena didn’t speak much after she had managed to lure Kate out to a bar, the brunette more than happy to carry the conversation, asking light questions about the places Yelena had been, retelling her run in with Kingpin and how Lucky enjoyed Iowa so much so that she had left him under Clint’s watch for the foreseeable. And even though Yelena didn’t participate much in the conversation, she had never felt more seen and never not so alone.

    The second time was a little further into the new year. Spring was slowly peering round the nearest corner as she had descended into the city for her third time ever. She was here for work this time, not pleasurable drinks with the man’s who she was supposed to kill protégé. Yelena had come across the brunette fighting four brutes down an alleyway, her bow on the floor, and close combat being Kate’s only viable fighting option. The blonde had sighed before stepping in to help and then all control had spiralled away from her. The next thing the assassin knew, she was slumped on Kate Bishop’s couch next to her watching The Sex and the City movie. Who knew that the series had a film?! They had had pizza box sprawled open between them, as well as several bowls of sides as well. What? They had worked up an appetite, okay? Kate was happy to lie on the couch with the assassin, nothing in her body language was guarded against the blonde, confusing Yelena as to how the woman she had thrown of a roof not 3 months ago was so relaxed and comfortable in her presence. And the third time, Yelena was in New York with the only reason being for Kate. Entering the brunette’s apartment and making her jump made the blonde smile, and nothing in that moment could’ve driven Yelena away from believing her choice of making the long flight was nothing less than worth it. The nightmare kind of put a fork in the blonde’s plans of a normal girl’s night with her new friend, but how Kate had handled it only confirmed that Yelena would be back once more.

    And now she was back again, this time with Kate being the one in turmoil. An orphan at 22, with a not step-dad step-dad, an Avenger friend and his family, and assassin as her support system. The blonde watched the brunette’s eyelids flutter gently as she manoeuvred Kate in a way so she could pick her up and carry her to bed. She hardly knew this woman, who had now seen her in one of her lowest, weakest moments, and a part of Yelena despised herself for that. And yet as Kate grabbed Yelena’s shirt with one hand and the archer’s face nuzzled into her neck, Yelena realised that maybe the brunette seeing her at her lowest made Kate trust her to take care of her now in the wake of her mother’s death. Letting her be there when she wouldn’t even let Clint. The blonde placed Kate down in her bed, pulling the covers over the brunette had her body relaxed into the mattress.

    “Clint?” Steve questioned as the archer threw his phone down into the couch cushions. Nat was still in his arms, her mind running at a thousand miles an hour after hearing her little sister’s voice for the first time in years. Talk about déjà vu huh?

    The other man just shook his head before picking up his phone and his jacket that had been splayed over the back of one of the dining chairs. “I’ve gotta go.” He mumbled before rushing down the stairs and out of view. Clint rushed into the driving seat of one of the car’s sat in the compound’s garage, pushing it into gear, slamming the accelerator down as far as it would go. He didn’t know what he was going to find when he reached Kate’s apartment, but heck was walking into the unknown and an assassin that tried to kill him better than not knowing at all.

    Upon his arrival at Kate’s apartment, he slammed his fist into the door multiple times over before it swung open with very familiar face of a pissed off looking blonde. She hadn’t changed much since he had last seen her, although apart from the scowl covering her face, she looked much more relaxed. Her hair was down and slightly waved, her bangs swooping over her face, which was free of makeup. Her black suit was gone and replaced with grey jeans and a green top, and a vest which brought a slight smile to Clint’s face. When he finally met her eyes, they were as guarded as they had been before their emotional confrontation on the ice rink that would be put back up a few blocks away in a month or two. “Must you break the door in? She’s finally asleep.” The blonde snarled in a quiet voice, as she turned her back to him and headed back into the apartment. Clint didn’t respond, only shutting the door behind him, whilst watching Yelena move around the apartment almost as if she lived there herself. The blonde was making trips back and forth to the laundry room from the bottom of the stairs where bags of clothes sat. Clint raised an eyebrow as they locked eyes when she finally returned from the last trip, joining Clint in Kate’s kitchen. “How’d you know I wasn’t going to slit your throat as soon as I opened the door?” The blonde questioned as she unzipped her vest, throwing it over the dining table and quickly pulling a purple hoodie that definitely didn’t belong to her over her head. Clint chuckled lightly as he walked past her and sat on one of the three chairs that still had four legs. “Your sister would’ve killed you if you had.”

    If Yelena was taken aback by his blunt response, she didn’t show it.

    “Ha. Jokes on you, I would not let a living person kill me, let alone a ghost.” The blonde deadpanned, her face still giving nothing away. Clint thought Nat was good at concealing her emotions, but maybe her sister was slightly better, just slightly.

    “Well, jokes on you. She’s alive.”

    “Anyone ever told you you’re not funny Barton?”

    “I know it sounds crazy.”

    “It sounds like a shit joke.” Yelena flatly said, but something in the man’s eyes was telling her that he was not lying.

    Clint didn’t offer a response this time, only reaching into his pocket and pulling out his phone. He pulled up Natasha’s contact before hitting the call button and passing it to Yelena so she could see it in real time. Only when the call connected, and the redhead’s voice ring out of the speaker did Yelena’s façade break.

    “Clint?”

    “Наташа? Это правда твоя сестра?”

    “Младшая сестра. Да, it’s me Yelena. It’s me.”

    “H-ho-how?”

    “That is the question on everyone’s mind.”

    “Где ты?”

    “I’m at the Avengers Compound. Steve Rogers is here with me.”

    “Ah Captain America. Do not tell Papa. He might come and hunt him down to relieve his glory days as the Crimson Dynamo. Тупой идиот.” Natasha softly laughed down the phone at this remark, making the tears glistening in Yelena’s eyes visible to Clint as one escaped to roll down her cheek. Clint’s eyebrows raised in questioning as to the line of conversation, but Yelena waved him off nonchalantly.

    “How did Clint find you so easily Младшая сестра? Losing your touch?”

    “I am at Kate’s.” replied the blonde, giving no elaboration as she put the phone down on the dining table and walked around pulling out the chair opposite Clint, the very same one she had happened to sit in the first time she was at Kate’s apartment. This realization didn’t escape the assassin, a smirk crossing her face, which didn’t escape Clint. His head tilted like a dog which Yelena rolled her eyes at. For not being related, the two Hawkeye’s do share a lot of mannerisms.

    “Sorry to interrupt but can we circle back to the Crimson Dynamo thing?” Clint said slowly, fingers pinching the bridge of his nose for a few seconds before looking up and locking eyes with Yelena. Her façade fully gone now as a chuckle erupted from her lips, making her nose and eyes crinkle. Natasha’s laugh also sounded from the other end of the line, making a smile appear on Clint’s face at the sound of the two women who have been so much, finally experiencing simple joy’s together, even if it was at his expense.

    The two assassins were now speaking fluidly in solid Russian, too fast for Clint to follow along with. He picked himself up from his seat slowly, his joints popping as he got to his feet, years of being battered by aliens finally showing its toll on his body. Leaving the eagerly chatting blonde at the table, he headed up the stairs rather gingerly, to go check on his fellow archer. Slowly opening the bedroom door, he finds the brunette tucked in tightly underneath the purple duvet. The cover came up to her chin, one hand tucked under her cheek whilst the cover had a loose grip on the pillow beneath her head. Even asleep Kate looked tired. She had dark circles under her eyes, her complexion was dull and if Clint didn’t know what she was going through, even looking at her he would have known something was wrong. He sat carefully on the edge of her bed, reaching and brushing strands of hair off of her forehead, before sighing softly.

    Why hadn’t she told him?

    Clint was pulled from his musings by Yelena’s head appearing round the doorway. His phone held out towards him in her hand, façade pulled all the way back up again. He reached his own arm out, gently plucking the device out of her hand and pushed it into his jacket pocket, barely taking his eyes off of Kate for a moment. He heard Yelena sigh before she turned out of the bedroom and her footsteps took off down the stairs. Having been broken from his train of thought, Clint’s eyes moved towards the clock. The time now a glaring 8am, making his tired eyes flutter at the thought of the amount of sleep he hasn’t had over the past few days. Hey, maybe he has some kind of superhero power after all because a normal human being should not be functioning right now.

    Slowly raising himself from the bed, Clint raised his arms above his head with a stretch and a yawn before dropping them down to his sides. Taking one last look at the sleeping brunette he gently headed towards the door, pulling it too behind him and belatedly following Yelena down the stairs. The blonde was pottering around Kate’s kitchen, making two cups of what smelt like coffee. She didn’t turn around when Clint’s feet hit the floor, but the man had no doubt that she knew he was there. Sensing no interaction was going to come from the assassin, the archer wandered over to the sofa where he fell into the cushions, a grunt falling from his mouth as the impact shocked the air from his lungs. His eyes had just about closed when he heard a cup being placed on the coffee table in front of him and quiet footsteps trailing away and up the stairs. With eyes half closed, Clint reached for the mug, bringing the steaming liquid to his lips, and downing a few mouthfuls before putting it back down again. His body too exhausted to even hold the mug up for any longer.
