    Yelena left the zombie looking man on the couch and headed up to Kate’s bedroom. Natasha had invited her to come to the compound to see her as the redhead did not want to risk being seen in public. Announcing her resurrection was not something on her immediate to do list apparently. Opening Kate’s door and quietly closing it behind her, the blonde slowly started moving around Kate’s room, packing the brunette a duffle bag of clothes and necessities’ that she will need over the next couple of days.

    Natasha technically hadn’t invited Kate also, but the blonde was in no way shape or form leaving the new Hawkeye alone in her current state of mind. The images of brunette hair mixed with splattered blood on New York sidewalks all too clear in her head. Yelena’s bag was already packed, still sat by the front door where it had been left when she first arrived at Kate’s apartment. Looking back, everything had kind of gone tits up from that moment on. Her sister was back from the dead. A thought she had never seemed plausible enough to cross her head let alone believe to be true. A possibility she hadn’t given any thought to and so now was conflicted in how to act towards her sister. Angry that she had abandoned her once in the red room, then again years later for the group of people she had left Yelena for in the first place, or to be overjoyed that her family was whole once again and that she has the person who meant the most to her in the whole wide world back again.

    It had been somewhat surreal to hear her older sibling’s dulcet tone over the phone, she could hear the smile on Natasha’s face and the thought of it being her who caused it filled Yelena with something she hadn’t felt since learning about bioluminescence all those years ago.

    “I could have stayed home.” Kate said quietly, her head resting on the car’s window. Her hair was wavy from the braid Yelena had plaited in it at some point last night, flowing freely and not trapped up in a ponytail for once.

    The blonde turned her head slightly towards the woman next to her before focusing her eyes back on the road. She scoffed lightly at Kate’s comment, not even dignifying it with a response. If Kate thought that Yelena was leaving her alone in her crappy little apartment alone a few days after her mother had died, she had officially lost it. Let alone the news had been broken publicly this morning, and Kate’s residence was not exactly hard to track down. Leaving the brunette there would’ve been like throwing her to the wolves. Clint had offered to stay with Kate whilst Yelena travelled to the Compound alone, however Kate’s face didn’t seem too keen on that idea, so the Russian had politely turned the man’s offer down. That is how it had led them to this situation of following Clint’s shoddy driving through the city to the one place Yelena swore she would never go, not after her sister died. This was the place her sister had left her behind for.

    It symbolised everything Natasha had had whilst Yelena was under Dreykov’s control for many years.

    “I would’ve been fine. I’m not a child.” Kate mumbled, pulling Yelena’s gaze to her as she pulled the car into park behind Clint’s.

    They had stopped outside the gates of the compound, Clint hopping out of his car to speak into the flashy tech pad on one of the white pillars. The blonde watched as the older archer’s mouth moved, a smile tugging at his lips, obviously something her sister or Captain America had said something that amused him.

    A sigh from beside her pulled Yelena’s focus back to the brunette beside her. Her dark circles had not been eliminated from the 12 hours of sleep she had gotten, nor had the empty look on her face left either. The reason Yelena had barely spoken a word to Kate that morning was because she did not know what to say. Her sister was back from the dead and yet Kate’s mom was dead. The irony was not lost on Yelena, and neither was the fact that celebrating Natasha being back seemed a bit like throwing a punch directly at Kate’s face. “I told you I was staying.” The blonde said finally breaking her silence, pulling Kate’s gaze from where she was watching the gates to the compound open, to her instead. “At my apartment? Not attached to my hip.” Kate drawled sarcastically. “What is it you Americans say about finding prints?” Yelena shrugged as she pushed the car into drive, the gates slowly shutting as the car trundled through.

    “Fine print?” Kate’s tone raised, signalling her obvious amusement to Yelena. “You should read them.” The blonde said flatly, pretending as if she didn’t know that it was already the right saying and thanking the heaven’s above for Kate’s simple humour in making fun of Yelena’s English.

    After a few minutes of following Clint down the perfectly tarmacked driveway he had led them to, a state-of-the-art facility came into view. What serves as the central hub for Earth's mightiest heroes looked like a normal Western world building to Yelena. Sure, it looked fancy with its edgy architecture, and its monochrome colour palate. Anyone with enough money on this side of the world could build something identical. It was nestled in a discreet location, which Yelena had to give the group props for, and she was sure the compound is a technological marvel, blending cutting-edge Stark models with the danger its inhabitants threatened to warn off anyone who should want to attack Earth.

    As the blonde stepped out of the car, she could more fully appreciate the fact the place was surrounded by lush greenery. Trees of many shapes and sizes were dotted around the lawn, whilst the entire sprawling property was enclosed by thick woodland. Slamming the car door and waiting for Kate to do the same before locking the vehicle, Yelena looked up at the building. A tall and dirty blonde man stood in the window; his arms crossed as he looked down at them. She glared back as he didn’t break his gaze.

    It wasn’t that Yelena didn’t know who the man was, everyone in the world could spot Captain America when they saw him. His face was plastered all over the world at one point in time. Yelena was not the one to break first, Steve finally looked away and walked away from the window and out of the assassin’s view. The blonde turned to see Kate leaning against the car, her head zipping around at speeds that a neck probably shouldn’t travel at, taking everything in. Clint was stood on the front step watching the two of them from afar, a small smile on his face at the wonder plastered over Kate’s.

    God, Yelena had forgotten Kate’s love of the Avengers until this moment, and now she wondered to herself if the brunette might’ve been better at home.

    “You two coming or not?” Clint yelled, breaking both women out of their heads as the front door swung open, revealing the man from the window.

    Yelena watched as Kate’s mouth fell open slightly before she snapped it shut again. The blonde snorted at this, Kate’s head swinging round to glare at her.

    “What?” The brunette questioned hastily.

    “Nothing сладкая птица. Nothing at all.” Yelena chuckled softly, the tone that came out of her mouth even shocking herself slightly. Kate didn’t say anything for a few moments and then her facial features softened, her blue eyes boring into green.

    “You okay?” The archer questioned, her head tilt mimicking that of Lucky’s. “I feel like that question is better directed at someone else, considering the circumstances.” Yelena said, not breaking the eye contact as Kate pushed herself off the car, now standing tall next to the assassin.

    “It’s not every day your sister comes back from the dead.” Kate shrugged. “Your mom doesn’t die every day either.” Yelena shot back, making Kate’s gaze drop to the ground for a moment before it moved back up to meet Yelena’s.

    “Guess we’re even then.”

    “Ha. You wish маленький ястреб.” Yelena barked out with a laugh before moving towards Clint who now had the front door propped open with one foot, the rest of his body turned to face the two women. The blonde could hear Kate following her, grumbling about something but Yelena’s mind was too preoccupied with the fact that Natasha was just moments away.

    Steve stepped back from the door, leaving Clint propping it open and turned the corner back up the stairs and into the kitchen where Nat was pacing back and forth. Her hair was longer than Steve remembered it being, the red seemed to linger for longer now, the blonde tips on the end reminiscent of the Battle of Wakanda. It flowed freely behind her as her boots thumped onto the floor with each step. Her head came swirling around to face him when she realised his presence.

    “Where are they?” The question came tumbling out of Nat’s mouth as soon as their eyes locked.

    “Give them a minute Nat. They just got out of the car. Think they bought Clint’s new kid with them. Is your sister blonde or brown-haired?” Nat snorted at this. “She’s not brunette Steve.” The redhead emphasised, sparking an eye roll from Steve. “How does she look?”

    “The brunette or the blonde?” The super solider teased, pulling out a chair at the table before sitting down. When no answer came from Nat, just a glare he had seen to many times to be scared of anymore, he continued, “She’s short, blonde and even if you aren’t biologically related, she definitely taken something from you.”

    “What?”

    “She stared me down through the window.” Steve shrugged whilst a small smirk passed over Nat’s face. Footsteps sounded coming up the stairs making Steve and Nat’s heads fly towards the stairwell. Clint emerged first, his feet dragging with every step, dark circles under his eyes accompanied by an emotion Nat didn’t have the mental capacity to place at the moment. He braved a small smile when they made eye contact before he threw himself onto the sofa in the corner of the kitchen, eyes closing immediately. Steve snorted as he watched the archer’s movements, but Nat’s eyes stayed firmly on the staircase.

    Quiet voices could be heard softly speaking to one another, getting louder as they approached. Nat didn’t think her heart could take much more waiting, the organ threatening to jump out of her chest. Luckily, her sister didn’t make her wait much longer as the blonde hair she had been so longing to see since she had awoken those few days ago emerged from the staircase.

    The first thought that came to her head was that Yelena’s hair was down. Nat realised she hadn’t seen her sister’s hair down since they were little and back in Ohio. It fell down past her shoulders, resting just above her chest, swopping bangs and layers framing her face. She looked older… mature.

    Her neck was adorned with silver jewellery: a chain and another necklace with a small knot in it, her fingers matching, adorned with an assortment of rings on pretty much every finger. The blonde’s outfit was casual, a change from the tactical suits Nat was accustomed to seeing her in. She wore high waisted blue jeans with a tartan yellow coat, adorned with broaches. Underneath Nat could see a glimpse of a small crop top, white with black detailing around the neckline and other seams. One thing that hadn’t changed was the staple black boots Yelena wore on her feet, their chunky sole and silver buckle bringing a sense of familiarity to Nat’s mind.

    Nat’s attention then moved to the woman just the left and slightly behind Yelena. Her hair was long and wavy, the dark brown tresses reaching her mid torso. She wore a coat similar to Yelena’s, slightly longer and in a more mundane and less garish colour, the grey and black tartan a lot less for Nat’s eyes to take in.

    She wore similar blue jeans, the ends rolled to sit just above the Doc Marten’s on her feet, the black a contrast to the white of her casual tee she wore on top. The woman wore just one piece of jewellery, simple silver necklace where the chain made up the bowstring, with the arch of the bow being a solid silver arch. Nat seemed that it was quite fitting, the woman did after all have a bow and quiver slung over one shoulder.

    Nat broke herself out of her staring, making eye contact with Yelena for the first time. Her sisters face didn’t budge, she had pulled up a stony façade, her eyes blank and her facial muscles frozen.

    “Are we going to talk like grown-ups?” Nat’s voice came out shakily. This got a little twitch from Yelena’s mouth. Her little sister rolled her eyes, the tension dissipating from the blonde’s shoulders and her eyes softening.

    “Is that what we are?” The Russian accent Nat was so fond out came spilling out of Yelena’s mouth and Nat couldn’t move fast enough. Her feet took her towards Yelena before she could think better of it. Yelena didn’t move a muscle, making Nat do all the hard work of moving to her.

    Natasha didn’t even hesitate when wrapping her arms around her sister, one hand cradling the back of her head whilst the other wrapped around her, wanting to hold her tight and never let go. Yelena was tense in her arms for a minute before she obviously realised Nat wasn’t going to let go, the blonde hesitantly wrapped her arms around the redhead’s waist, squeezing once before lightly pushing away. Natasha let go reluctantly but not fully, her hands now resting on the sides of Yelena’s shoulders.

    “Давно не виделись... сестренка. You look good.” Nat said, her teasing not lost on Yelena. The blonde gently shoved her hands off her shoulders before moving to pick up the two duffle bags she had dropped to hug Natasha. She dropped them once more on the dining table, before turning back around to face her sister again.

    “You look like shit.” Yelena deadpanned, her eyes running over Natasha, lingering on the dark circles on her face. Nat watched her turn to study the two men in the room. The redhead took this chance to head towards the kitchen island to take a sip of her glass of water, anything to help her distract her from her exhaustion. Clint was still passed out on the sofa and Steve was sat at the table watching the exchange with much curiosity in his eyes. The dirty blonde was the only one of the three Avengers who didn’t look dead on his feet seeing as he had fallen asleep after Clint had disappeared last night. Yelena didn’t say anything to the blonde at the table, instead turning instead and walking back towards the stairwell where the brunette still stood. Nat watched her sister approach the brunette, who looked up from where she had been staring at the floor. Yelena must’ve whispered something to the other woman as the brunette nodded before shrugging her shoulders. The blonde then placed a hand on the brunette’s forearm before gently tugging her with her, heading back towards the kitchen.

    “Сестра, this is Kate Bishop.” Yelena said, meeting the redhead’s eyes as they came to a stop on the edge of the kitchen.

    It did not escape Natasha that Yelena had not let go of the brunette’s wrist. A small smirk implanted itself on her face before her attention moved to the brunette. “I hope Yelena hasn’t caused you too much trouble.” Nat said, her comment making Kate’s eyes brighten just a little bit. Natasha knew very little about this woman, but something tells her she was missing her usual spark.

    “I’ve been trouble since I was born. What’s a little more?” Kate’s demeanour lightened as she said this. Nat watched her little sister elbow the woman next to her, a small smile on her face. “W-what I mean is I want no trouble. Absolutely none at all. No tracksuits, or fiery cocktails thrown in my window or assassins throwing me off roofs…” Kate rambled out making Yelena snort rather loudly.

    “Oh маленький ястреб, you are fooling no one.” The blonde said whilst shaking her head. Nat and Steve both shared questioning looks, these not escaping Yelena. She didn’t acknowledge her sister, or her friend’s want for more information, instead turning the conversation back to a topic she wanted to talk about.

    “How long have you been back?” Yelena asked Natasha as she lifted herself up to sit on the kitchen counter, her sister watching her with an eye roll. Kate followed the blonde slowly, leaning back on the counter next to the blonde, instead of making the effort to sit on top of it. “There are things called chairs you know?”

    “Answer the question.”

    “Not long.” Natasha spoke, her eyes wandering to Steve for an actual answer. She’d been awake for a couple of days but now that she thought about it, she didn’t have a clue how long her body had been back on Earth. Steve leant back in his chair, eyeing the blonde slowly, contemplating how to answer the question without a knife ending up in his neck. “Carol got in contact a few weeks back. Fury had contacted her about power surges happening throughout the universe and at several key jump points within it. Carol, Monica Rambeau and some kid named Kamala went to investigate and found out a Kree woman named Dar-Benn was trying to siphon energy from our sun to reignite Pama.” Yelena rolled her eyes before she made a show of fake yawning. Kate slapped her arm gently, not taking her eyes of Steve, obviously wanting him to continue the story. The blonde halted her complaining and Steve took this as his note to continue.

    “One of the surges occurred on Vormir, where Nat died, and where the Red Skull resides. Naturally Carol went storming in there, only to find Red Skull dead and Nat’s body back up on top of the mountain… with a pulse.”

    “Who killed the red guy?” Yelena’s tone was low yet inquisitive.

    “We don’t know.”

    “How did Natasha come back from the dead?”

    “We don’t know that either.” Steve repeated once more.

    Yelena scoffed, her demeanour shifting ever so slightly as she stares at Steve. Natasha doesn’t have to dwell on what her sisters thinking as she soon switches her attention to the brunette next to her.

    “See Kate Bishop, the Avengers don’t have the answers to everything.” The blonde spat before sliding off the counter and picking up the bags from the table. “Where’s our rooms сестра?” She said beginning to walk out of the kitchen before Nat had even begun to answer her.

    Chapter 7

    Chapter Notes a week later and we are back!

    hours at work have gone down so shifts have been spread out giving me the equivalent of 4 days off, woophee! this means this past week i've really knuckled down to write as much as i can before work inevitably drives up again :)

    loved seeing the feedback from the last chapter where we got the Nat and Yelena reunion. I wanted to make it interesting and have Yelena not forgive Nat immediately because ultimately her death caused Yelena a hell of a lot of shit and that's not easy to get over - plus Yel strikes me as the type to hold a grudge.

    word count: 3628 overall word count written: 40,347 (lots to come as you can see!)

    Yelena woke early the next morning, pulling herself out of bed and almost drowning herself in the shower before the sun had even risen. The blonde had been hiding out from her sister since yesterday afternoon, having not even left her room for food. The assassin was conflicted. This was her sister who she shared a bedroom with when they were little, the one who pulled a gun on soldiers four times her size at the age of 11 because they threated Yelena and the sister whose death had stopped Yelena’s world turning for over a year. Now the redhead’s back, spending her evenings talking to Barton about his kids, catching up with Steve and learning about the musical named after him. Yelena spent way too long eavesdropping on her sister insisting she has to see it, ignoring Clint’s well issued warnings of it being a shitshow, no pun intended. The conversation lasted way into the evening, spanning to more sombre topics of Nat wanting to go and visit Tony Star’s wife to pay her condolences and learning about some witch’s mishap in a town called Westview. Kate hadn’t left her side since they had arrived at the compound. She had invited herself into Yelena’s room after unpacking in her own, the brunette had figured out their rooms had adjoining doors and so had propped it open. Yelena had no plans of closing it again. Kate had sat on the blonde’s bed whilst she opened the air vent, letting the voices from the living room float into their room for free listening. They had sat in complete silence for a while, listening to Steve and Nat and then Clint when he rejoined the world of the living. The brunette had fallen asleep eventually, her head resting on Yelena’s thigh where she had settled herself in her half-asleep state. The assassin’s fingers had begun running themselves through Kate’s hair at some point during the evening, the blonde remembers the brunette sighing deeply in contentment even whilst asleep at the movement, so hadn’t had the heart to pull her hand away when she realised what she was doing. After all, what harm could a little physical comfort do?

    The blonde pulled herself out of her musings as a rather strong wind blew across the front of the balcony. Yelena had escaped out here after her shower, not wanting to wake Kate with her rather loud thinking. Her mind now a bit clearer from the cold breeze, she noticed a figure approaching the front door, dressed in all black.

    Nick Fury.

    Yelena grumbled under her breath at yet another Avenger being in her immediate surroundings. Maybe Kate had had the right idea about staying put at her apartment. The blonde knew from many a rumour that when Fury came looking, normally no good news followed. Taking one last look at the end of the sun rise, she turned back around, sliding open the balcony door before shutting it quietly behind her.

    Kate was still fast asleep, wrapped up in the cocoon of blankets Yelena had created around the brunette after she had gotten out of bed herself. The archer’s hair was fanned out all over the place, a little bit of drool escaping her mouth. Yelena couldn’t help the small smile on her face or the roll of her eyes at the sight. And then the sweet moment was broken by Kate’s stomach rumbling. The blonde stifled a chuckle before sighing.

    She couldn’t let the struggling brunette suffer even more by her own selfishness of not wanting to speak to her sister. Kate had barely eaten in the past week, without needing Yelena indirectly influencing her to not leave the room for food since yesterday afternoon. With a shake of her head, Yelena pocketed her phone before quietly slipping out of the bedroom door.

    The blonde met no one when she entered the kitchen, the morning light making the room somewhat cosy, the only noise being the hum of the appliances. Yelena got to work, scrummaging around the fridge and the cupboards.

    For the array of talent, the Avengers are known to have, food shopping was obviously not one of them.

    The assassin found half a tub of yoghurt, some blueberries, and just enough dry ingredients to make some pancakes. Yelena was halfway through cooking the bowl of pancake batter when footsteps sounded from down the hall. Pausing her movements, she turned her head towards the direction of the sound, only raising her eyebrows slightly when Nick Fury appeared round the corner. His eyes met her own and after a minute, without verbally acknowledging his presence, Yelena turned back to what she was doing. The only difference being the tension that had appeared throughout her body.

    “This might be only the second ever meal to be made in this kitchen.” Fury’s voice sounded after about ten minutes of silence.

    Yelena’s hand paused over the yoghurt lid; she hummed noncommittally before dolloping a good amount on top of the two pancake stacks in front of her. The assassin could hear more chatter approaching the kitchen now, the voices of the three musketeers – Kate had nicknamed Nat, Steve and Clint that last night – now easily detectable, even over the thick silence that hung in the kitchen.

    As they entered the room, their chatter stopped. Yelena didn’t have to turn around to know their heads were swinging between the two who occupied the room before their arrival. The blonde threw a couple of handfuls of blueberries over the stacks, picking up the two plates before turning around. The three newcomers were all wearing mildly amused expressions, until they made eye contact with Yelena. The assassin ignored the three men in the room in favour of scowling at her sister before stalking out of the room.

    “Your sister’s a better cook than you Romanoff.” She heard distantly as she reached her destination.

    “I can kick your ass at any time Fury.”

    Yelena lightly kicked open the bedroom door, her hands currently occupied with the freshly made breakfast. Her eyes drifted immediately to Kate whilst she put the plates down on top of the dresser, her breathing was shallower and her eyelids fluttering more consistently. The blonde knew these were tell tale signs that the brunette would wake up soon. She lowered herself onto the end of the bed, tucking one leg under her whilst the other kept one foot on the floor.

    Yelena grabbed her plate of food, shovelling it into the mouth, eyes flicking between the pile of sugar and the sleeping woman. The assassin was just scraping her plate clean when Kate stretched out, and then slowly opened her eyes. They looked around the room for a moment before they settled on Yelena. A small smile glazed over the archer’s face before it vanished, and she buried her head back into her pillow.

    “Tis’ too early.” The brunette’s grumble could just be heard by Yelena, her voice gravelly and low from just waking up. The blonde raised her eyebrows, but didn’t say anything back, just leant towards the dresser and swapping her empty plate for Kate’s. She stuck her leg out, gently hitting Kate’s calf with her foot, pulling Kate’s head back out so she could see her. When Kate’s eyes landed on Yelena again, the smile stayed this time.

    “For me?” The archer’s voice was quiet, almost as if she couldn’t believe the sight in front of her. Kate slowly pulled herself up, her back leaning against the headboard. When she was settled, Yelena passed the plate over. The brunette studied the plate for a moment, picking up the cutlery and flashing one last smile to Yelena before she devoured the stack of pancakes in what the blonde deemed a record time.

    If it wasn’t somewhat impressive, it would’ve been disgusting.

    Once the plate had been thoroughly scraped clean, Kate placed it on the bedside table to her left before slumping against the headboard. Yelena hadn’t taken her eyes off her yet, something that hadn’t escaped Kate.

    “Come ‘ere” The brunette mumbled boldly, her grogginess making her throw all caution to the wind once again. The blank expression on Yelena’s face didn’t change. “Lena.” Kate spoke louder this time, patting the space next to her a couple of times before leaning her head backwards and shutting her eyes.

    The irony of this situation didn’t go unnoticed by the assassin, very little does. Her Hawkeye’s emotional intelligence once again noticed Yelena was feeling some sort of way before she had even unpacked the emotion herself. The blonde sat rooted to her spot for a while, fiddling with the rings adorning her fingers, something she had recently realised had become quite a habit. Another new constant need that had come to her attention was her yearning for physical touch. Having been deprived of it for so long, Yelena reasoned with herself that it would not be unusual for her mind and body to now want it after years of being denied. After all, it’s a human need and as easy for most people as it is to breathe. Another way of looking at it was that the blonde was finally in a mental space where she has reluctantly come to terms with the fact that it is okay to want things she didn’t need before. Human instincts of survival change all the time. Back in the Red Room, she had to keep her head down and follow the rules, but now her circumstances have changed. If her body is telling her she needs something to survive, Yelena’s gut instinct is to follow it. It was the way she was trained after all, trusting her senses, studying her surroundings. And in this moment, her senses were filled with the smell of Kate’s perfume mixing with the lingering sweetness of the long-devoured breakfast, and her surroundings were somewhat safe. The wider area of the compound was still up for debate, but in this enclosed room where the only people were herself and the dozing brunette, she had become unwillingly fond of, Yelena figured she would give into her desires, at least for right now. Yelena must’ve been stuck in her own head for quite some time as when she next looked up from her hands Kate’s eyes were open and studying her every move. The blonde not one to back down from a challenge just stared back. Tilting her head to the side, she studies Kate’s face, an odd expression taking over her striking dark features, which, Yelena wasn’t going to say were ever hard on the eyes. She chuckled internally when she realised this could go on for a while, Kate was as stubborn as she was.

    Taking her free chance of staring at the brunette, Yelena delve deep again. Her eyes roaming Kate’s face as if she might be able to understand the person in front of her if she stared long enough.

    Kate, ever the instigator, let her look.

    To the outside world, Kate seemed perhaps overly confident. Yelena would place a significant amount of money on that fact. Martial arts, archery and all things mini superhero had taken up the 23-year-olds life since she was 11. Activities like that took a lot of nerve, and well, one thing Yelena had most definitely learnt about Kate is that the brunette has it in bucketful's.

    Even before her father died Kate seemed to have been an outgoing kid. Yelena had found record after record and photos upon photos of Kate being front and centre in school plays, being honoured in high school competitions for her archery; the brunette was anything but shy. Her first meeting with Yelena was hardly far from quiet: having the intention of shooting her, being gutsy enough to eat dinner with an assassin who could’ve killed the brunette quicker than she could think about archery and even calling Yelena out on her own actions. That last one took some nerve no matter who you are.

    But the image Kate puts out does fail her on occasion. Yelena remembers when she mentioned the woman’s mother over their pot of mac and cheese. Her right eyebrow furrowed, her lower lip slightly falling to one side, her shoulders tensing almost immediately. After all, this was the woman knowingly and willingly killing to keep her pockets lined with money, even if Kate didn’t know that then. Playing with New York mobsters with double her experience to continue living the lifestyle she was used to, and that Kate was used to as well. This was the woman who tried to raise Kate to a spitting image of herself only to blame her child when it didn’t turn out that way.

    Kate couldn’t be more the opposite of her mother and that is the part of her she does not know how to be confident about, because she never had someone teach her that it was okay to be or how to be. Yelena thinks most people would probably look over this part of Kate, thinking she was having an off day, or her mind was just somewhere else, but the blonde has to do little more than a glance to figure the brunette out.

    After all, this is the Kate who is the kindest person that she has ever experienced and yet the archer looks like she wants to run for the hills anytime Yelena hesitates in her presence. An onlooker would think Kate has just suggested they go and kill a dog in cold blood, not for Yelena to simply sit next to her.

    The brunette is unsure in her kindness because her mother was cold.

    But to Yelena, Kate couldn’t be warmer.

    “Okay,” Yelena says with a nod, before lowering her head and breaking the eye contact. Kate doesn’t say anything in response, but Yelena can still feel her eyes on her. The blonde slowly pushes herself up the bed and shuffles into a spot next to Kate, who exhales heavily as the assassin comes to a still beside her. The brunette’s face is soft yet incredibly nervous. Yelena holds in a chuckle as she relaxes into the pillows behind her, hoping the ease will encourage Kate’s.

    Her plan did not work in the slightest, Kate still rigid beside her.

    “I don’t bite Kate Bishop.”

    Kate’s only response was an amused huff, some of the tension leaving the brunette’s body. When her face slowly turned to face Yelena with an eyebrow raised, the blonde rolled her eyes.

    “Okay fine, I take that back.”

    Kate’s eyes only widened.

    “What? You fight someone? They choke you? Biting is a good escape.”

    The cogs seemed to whir in the brunette’s head for a moment before the thinking relented and a neutral expression took over her face.

    “Have you ever thought of boomerang arrows? Clint didn’t think they were a good idea.” She came out with suddenly, bringing a smile to Yelena’s face. “But you’d never run out of arrows because…well…they come back.” Kate paused as if she realised what she was going to say was quite obvious.

    “It might not be smart to have an explosive arrow coming back at you.” Yelena said, her smile turning into a smirk.

    “Well yeah. You-you’d have to dodge.” Kate shrugged, her shoulder hitting into Yelena’s. Both girls chuckled lightly before the conversation lulled.

    “Nick Fury is in the kitchen. Propose your idea to him.”

    Yelena could practically hear Kate’s excitement.

    “The Nick Fury is in the building. The guy who could make me an Avenger. And you’ve conveniently forgotten to mention this until now?!” The brunette exclaimed, turning slightly to face Yelena, throwing her hands up in the air.

    “He is not cool.” Was all Yelena had to say.

    Kate’s excitement dwindled immediately, but Yelena couldn’t bring herself to feel bad. This was the man who had started Natasha’s career as an Avenger and therefore he carried at least some of the blame for her death.

    The air between them had thickened again and suddenly Yelena was too close. Kate was too close, and she needed out.

    The blonde stood up suddenly, Kate’s eyes tracking her every movement with a concerned look on her face. Neither woman said a word as the blonde grabbed her jacket off of the hook on the wall and left without so much of a backward glance.

    There were definitely more than four voices in the kitchen when Kate finally left the room hours after Yelena had made her exit. The brunette knew that she was not going to be downstairs or anywhere on the property, but she had grown sick of the same four walls. Upon deciding walking into a room of at least four Avengers alone was too daunting Kate headed down the next flight of stairs, after all no where had been labelled as off limits. The double doors at the end of the small corridor opened automatically as she approached them, revealing a large hanger. A singular Quinjet sat at the opposite end to where Kate stood, its size greater than Kate could’ve fathomed it being in her head. Her eyes scanned the room looking for something else to pique her interest, but what did it was actually outside the window. An array of targets sat arranged down the slight slope away from the building, their red and white circles increasing Kate’s heartrate on sight.

    After running back upstairs, grabbing her bow and quiver, and legging it out of the far door of the hanger, the brunette stopped at the line of shooting. She paused for a moment, half bent over, hands on her knees trying to catch her breath. This is what she needed. When her lungs had stopped heaving for oxygen and she had stopped battling her internal thoughts about how shit her cardio was, the archer studied the layout. She could visibly spot 9 targets from her spot and yet in her bones she knew there were 2 more hiding somewhere. This was undoubtedly Clint’s set up and he always shot in sets of 11.

    Spinning her head round and probably doing a semi-decent impression of an owl, more red and white caught her eye. A target sat on the lawn in the middle of the driveway probably about 50 and a bit yards away from her. The 11th target to its right, hanging on the side of the building, its wooden frame swaying in the wind. These final two targets brought a grin to Kate’s face. Clint was always one to make it interesting.

    For the first time since her mother died, Kate drew her bow, drawing an arrow back and letting it fly. She didn’t need to look at it buried deep in the centre of the first target, but she did anyway. The second arrow hit just barely before the third. The fourth target shuddering under the force of the next arrow not a second later. Kate reached back into her quiver again, turning her bow sideways and taking aim at numbers five and six, number seven following suit. The next two arrows also hit their respective targets with a resounding crack, splinters of wood falling into the pile already accumulated underneath them.

    Even though the brunette was in no rush, she reached back into her quiver at speed. The audience from the window not even catching her eye for a second.

    “She’s going to be better than you Barton.” Nat’s voice sounded from beside him. “Good. Maybe it’ll stop her from getting beat up too bad.” Clint grumbled back, not taking his eyes off the brunette on the lawn below.

    Her eyes were focused on the far target on the drive. Clint could tell from the way she had hooked her arrow and the stance of her feet. She knows her way around a bow and arrow, he couldn’t fault her on that.

    “She needs to be more left surely. Winds blowing a gale out there today.” Nat whispered, her confusion clear in her quietness.

    Clint didn’t respond, nor did his face change. Kate was going to hit that target even if she was facing backwards.

    One by one, Kate nocked, aimed, and released three arrows in quick succession. Clint couldn’t fight the smile as they rhythmically all fell in the bullseye. The brunette then sharply turned, nocking two arrows at once and firing them into the target on the side of the building. He heard a small hum of appreciation from Fury, and noticed a surprised raise of the eyebrows from Steve before turning to Nat.

    “Being dead has made you rusty.” Hawkeye said, nudging his elbow several times into the redhead’s ribs making her lightly shove him away.

    “Honey honestly, she’s been back for all of ten minutes. Give her a grace period before you start your bullying.” A hand snaked his way around Clint’s elbow, a small smile on her face as her eyes flickered from her husband to Nat and then outside to Kate. “She looks okay.” Laura said in a small voice, only to be heard by Clint and Nat. Steve and Fury having wandered off into deeper parts of the compound. Clint’s hand moved up to lay on top of hers on his bicep.

    “She tried to jump off a roof Laur.” The archer grumbled, his pain at the thought splayed all over his face. Clint was never one to hide his emotions when off the battlefield. “That’s what Yelena says. Have you spoken to Kate about it?”

    When Clint didn’t answer, Natasha butted in.

    “This is the first time we’ve seen Kate since this time yesterday.”

    Laura’s face turned into a frown, matching that of the one permanently etched on her husband’s face.

    Chapter 8

    Chapter Notes hello again!

    this chapter is the longest so far but it does include the main introduction to the general plot besides the element of kate and yelena of course. hope you enjoy the idea i've come up with and am currently trying to flush out as I continue writing.

    I've just finished chapter 14 and I am going to go on record and say its my favourite chapter I've ever written.

    P.S go to the end notes for a lil preview of chapter 9 :))))))

    See the end of the chapter for more notes When Yelena returned the compound, the sun had set, and the moon rising. She knew she had probably freaked Kate out, the look on the archer’s face had been one of confusion and of despair. The brunette had been nothing, but kind and Yelena threw it all back in her face. The blonde wandered over the walkway above the kitchen rather than walking through it to get to her room. The usual four culprits sat around the table; bottles of beer dotted around between them.

    The shitty alcohol wasn’t what caught her eye, it was the fifth figure. A middle-aged woman, with layered brown hair. She was sat way to close to Barton to not be his wife, so Yelena figured this was the great Laura Barton that Kate adored. Instead of going to find Kate in her room like she had planned, Yelena used her secret position to scout out the new person in the compound.

    It’s not like she was a total stranger. She was married to Barton, so obviously had some background in the intelligence community, that was a given. The assassin could probably find out in less than 5 minutes if she cared to look but she was 99% positive the answer had something to do with SHIELD and that was enough for her to go on.

    Kate had met the woman only once in person and had always had good things to say so Yelena figured she must be pretty decent given the high praise. She knew her sister was also fond of her, although the redhead’s opinion didn’t carry much weight for Yelena right now so that didn’t gain Laura Barton any extra points.

    Sitting down on the walkway, half her body hidden in the shadows, Yelena’s phone vibrated. Have you lost a certain little bird?

    The blonde’s eyebrows furrowed. She moved her fingers to reply as another text came through.

    I know you just left but you might want to make your return prompt. Come to this location. Little bird is in a spot of bother. Oh, and that Avenger sister of yours might be useful. Yelena didn’t bother with a reply. She was out of the compound door, only her guns for company.

    As she pulled up outside the modest apartment building, she spotted her almost immediately. Swinging her bike into the parking spot, killing the engine, and ripping off her helmet as the familiar figure walked over.

    “I thought I asked for Avengers.” The woman with caramel skin and long, dark hair drawls. Her tone light and definitely teasing.

    “Sonya.” Yelena said bluntly, her tone obviously not dissuading the woman. “I was expecting the blonde with the thunder, not a grumpy blonde with an attitude problem.” “Be nice Sonya. I’ve had a long day.”

    “Oh, and don’t I know all about it.” The woman rolled her eyes before beckoning Yelena to follow her down an alleyway. The blonde followed willingly, trusting her fellow Widow’s judgement on this, after all she was on the scene first.

    “I’d popped out to replenish my vodka cupboard seeing as someone keeps drinking it all,” A glare directed back towards the blonde before she continued, “Then I spotted a familiar looking bird having a conversation with some people I expect you wouldn’t be happy with her talking too.”

    Yelena was about to reply when Sonya held her hand up and stopped. The dark-haired women beckoned her forward slightly before nodding her head to the right. The blonde shuffled half a step-in front of Sonya, peeking her head quickly round the corner of the building before ducking back. Around eight hefty looking men stood by a small doorway, large guns strapped to each of their waists.

    Above their heads was a covering, the Russian expected it was probably just a tarpaulin, hiding their presence from any windows that may cast them a glimpse. The area was dark, shadowed by the tall New York buildings around it, the only light being the far glow of a streetlight from around the corner and over end of the alleyway.

    However, a widow’s eyes were trained to be keen.

    “Soviet slugs. No rifling.” Yelena muttered as she turned her head back towards Sonya. She nodded in response, indicating to the blonde that she’d noticed as well. “They’re a long way from home.” Sonya mumbles back, a third gun now strapped to her thigh. When she looks back up at Yelena, the blonde is overcast in thought. “Anyone home?” She says quietly, knocking her fist on Yelena’s forehead. The blonde just rolls her eyes, turning back around for another glance before turning back.

    “Too close to home. Look at their forearms. The two on the left.”

    Sonya’s head peeked around for another look. No reaction occurred on her face leaving Yelena to explain.

    “It’s the mark of the KGB. Soviet Security and Armed Forces. Alexei has the same mark.” “So, their blood matches their guns.” Sonya drawls.

    “Not quite. There are numbers beside the marks. They are labelled. Accounted for.” The blonde’s brow furrowed. Turning back around the corner again, she risked her neck for a longer look. It was obvious what they were guarding. The door. It was the question of why the door needed eight men to guard it which was troubling Yelena.

    “Always getting the short straw.” One of the men grumbled, cracking his knuckles against the palm of his other hand.

    “Shouldn’t be too long today. She was practically all bone, no meat to tear through first.” Another drawled, their accents definitively Russian.

    Yelena tensed at his words. Sonya’s hand on her arm as if she was expecting the assassin to do something rash. The blonde shook her off as the man closest to them turned his back to face the rest of the men behind him. What he didn’t know was this revealed the back of his neck.

    “Fuck me.”

    “Yelena, you are telling me you’ve spent days for months on end around the gorgeous woman that is Kate Bishop, and instead you want to climb that man like a tree?!” Sonya hisses, making Yelena swing her head round.

    Sonya grins when she meets her eyes, and yet she grins even wider when Yelena’s lip slightly twitches showing her amusement. Only a fellow widow would’ve been able to spot it and Yelena slaps herself for not preparing herself for Sonya’s company a second time in one day. “They are super soldiers.”

    “But they’re Russian.” Sonya states blankly.

    “Pizza would still be pizza if it was topless.” Yelena bites back sarcastically, only spurring Sonya on.

    “No. It would be a crime. Pizza should always have toppings.” She emphasised, earning herself a slap on the arm from the blonde.

    “Remember 2005?”

    “Hurricane Katrina happened, the French were fighting and oh, Destiny’s Child broke up.” Sonya says, clutching her heart as if she was in pain.

    “The mission in Tallinn. We were snowed in for hours, couldn’t stop the cold coming in from the draft under the door. Taliya lost a toe?” Yelena slowly explains, and when Sonya nods in recognition, she continues, “When the second team arrived to help us out, they had a man with them. The one who pulled open the bunker door. He bore that mark.” The blonde gestures to the small circle on the back of the man’s neck.

    “Your dad has always said he was the Soviet’s only ever super soldier.” “Daddy says a lot of things. He is an idiot.”

    Silence stills between them for a few moments, both their eyes just tracking the movements of the men around the corner. They were big guys, smaller than Alexei in body fat but they definitely made up for it in muscle. Their legs were thick and strong, meaning the place to aim for was the neck, or under the arms. The armour given to them weak in the groin and also the armpit.

    “When half the world disappeared, there were rumours of a new superpower in Russia. An underground adjective to take over the world whilst it was what they viewed as at its weakest. There were rumblings for a while, a few bombings in northern cities, threats placed on government heads, but nothing was ever carried out. In the widow network, they went by the name, Lufuthai. Ayanda circled it back to a vast and forgotten tongue from the beginnings of the Soviet Union. It roughly translates to ‘War Folk’.” Sonya said quietly, her gaze vacant. “And nothing since?”

    “Until now.” Sonya’s eyes bore into Yelena’s. “Think we can take them?” The taller woman questioned, unlatching the safety of her gun.

    Yelena just hummed noncommittally.

    “A god from space would’ve been helpful.” Sonya grumbled, before taking her stance beside Yelena.

    “Next time I have access to a rocket, I’ll go find him for you.” Yelena stamped on the other woman’s foot, earning her a kick of the calf as she stepped out from their hiding spot and summoning the attention of all eight men upon her. They all grasped their guns and knocked them towards the blonde until Sonya jumped out firing like there was no tomorrow.

    “What is it with groups of angry men and duct tape? Surely, they could find better things to play with than duct tape. Like Jack and his swords. At least those are cool.” “Probably not a good idea to be wishing the guys who grabbed you and smuggled you down an alley to be playing with swords Kate.”

    “Would make it more interesting. I’ve got to say I can normally entertain myself quite well but you’re really disappointing me today, Mr Voice-In-My-Head-Guy.”

    Kate’s inner monologue was broken by two large boots arriving in front of her. The brunette didn’t have to look up to know whose feet stood inside them.

    “We meet again Miss Bishop.”

    “I’d say it’s a pleasure, only you couldn’t have picked somewhere nicer?” Kate said looking around, her sight being freed of the blindfold she’d been wearing. It wasn’t much different to the Tracksuit’s headquarters. It was a derelict looking room, no windows, had a load of mean looking guys in it. Only differences the brunette could spot on the off was the lack of a ball pit and the tracksuit outfits she’d become all too familiar with. Oh, and that she was sat on a normal wooden chair instead of a rocking horse.

    “I’d watch what you say Miss Bishop. Wouldn’t want to end up like dear old Mom now, would we?” The large bald man stared down at her. Kate clenched her teeth together hard, digging her nails into the palms of her hands simultaneously.

    “Ah, I seem to have struck a nerve.” He continued, taking a few steps to his left, large thumps sounding whenever his boots hit the floor. “Yes, such a pity. Eleanor was finally finding her feet in this whole business too. Shame she didn’t find them fast enough.” His gaze landing back on Kate as it finished.

    “Mom may not have taught me much about anything she did, but even I know it’s rude to have a guest and not introduce them to your friends.” Kate spewed out quickly, trying to keep the large man talking. His eyebrows raised in surprise at her cockiness. “Your mother should have also taught you it is not common practice to make demands when in someone else’s house.” He spat.

    “You live here? Business can’t be going that well, this place is a dump.” Kate spoke calmly this time, her tone changing to match her judgement. “Even if my mother was bad at business, at least she had rather decent taste in furnishings.”

    A growl sounded from the man in front of her at this, and Kate thought she was about to face the consequences of her bigmouth when muffled gunshots could be heard. His attention swung to two men, nodding his order before turning back to the brunette. “Your Hawkeye is no match for these men. A normal man against 15 of Russia’s finest super soldiers. Let’s see how far he gets.”

    “No Hawkeye wields a gun, Wilson.” Kate said smugly, her lips turning upwards at the look on Kingpin’s face.

    “If the old bird isn’t the one protecting you, then who is?”

    “Protecting me?”

    “You do not know. Those around you have kept you in the dark. Ha,” Kingpin threw his head back laughing, “Such fools. I put out a hit on you. First person to bring me Kate Bishop alive and relatively unmaimed gets an, in my opinion, all too generous, sum of money. No one accepted the job, so I reached out to some old contacts. Someone has placed a blanket of protection over your snobby little head, and no one daren’t go near you. So, Miss Bishop, I’ll ask you once more. Who is protec-“ The sounding of a gunshot made his sentence fall short.

    Nat smiled to herself as she looked around the room. It was like the old times only with some slight differences. Clint and Laura were sat in the corner of the couch, the archers arm thrown around the back of Laura. They were exchanging conversation with Fury who had lowered himself into the armchair on their right, complaining about his joints cracking as he did. This had garnered a few laughs from the room. Nat herself was on the opposite side of the couch, her legs spread out on the recliner.

    Steve sat a few paces from herself, which wasn’t shocking to the redhead, he had barely left her side since she’d been back. Her gaze was pulled back to Clint as he threw his head back laughing at something Nick said, Laura shaking her head with an amused smirk. The archers action made Nat remember Yelena’s similar reaction yesterday.

    Her content smile faded at this.

    Yelena had always been a tricky character. Her witty demeanour and lack of vulnerability making her seem cold and distant had always been hard for those around her. Natasha only had Yelena’s childhood friends to base this off, after all, Nat had barely seen her sister interact with anyone who wasn’t their makeshift family and she thought she was never going to get the chance too.

    But even now they’re both here, under the same roof, Nat felt what she thought was her second chance drifting away.

    Yelena had barely said two words to her since she’d arrived, and what she had asked were questions Nat did not have the answers too. The redhead knows of the blonde’s inquisitive nature, it had been there since she was born and only developed more by what she was taught in the Red Room. After not being told anything for the majority of her life, Nat could understand the blonde’s desire for information, to know the facts behind her presence once more. But the redhead would also like for her sister to just be her sister. When Natasha had heard Yelena’s voice on that phone call, images of what could happen had travelled through her head at a speed faster than a Quinjet: Christmas at the Barton’s.

    Visiting an animal shelter to get Yelena the dog she always wanted.

    Returning to Ohio for a roundtrip.

    Having a food fight in the kitchen.

    They were all real and tangible to Nat until Yelena pushed herself out of that hug and Nat had seen the look in the blonde’s eyes. There was emotion in them that Nat couldn’t quite put a finger on. She knew Yelena was angry, angry at her, her sacrifice, probably at herself. But there was something else swimming in green which she couldn’t place, but it was familiar to her all the same. With new motivation to figure out what else was going on in her sister’s head, she pushed herself off the couch to go and find her. Maybe tonight they would talk like grown-ups and if not, Nat was in the mood to go a couple of rounds in the ring. She knocked on the door of the room Yelena was staying in a couple of times. After getting no response, she puts her ear to the door to hear any movements or anything really. “Yelena?” Nat says rather loudly. Once again, she gets no reply. This time she goes for the door handle, expecting it to be locked. When it’s not, Nat definitely doesn’t stumble through the doorway and almost go head over heels. She scoffs at herself as she regains her balance. Maybe you are a little bit rusty Nat.

    Shaking her thoughts from her head, her eyes settle in to focus on the room. Anyone glancing around would see a normal lived in room, but she was a widow, and this was her sister’s space. Nat has always had a keen eye for being a little be nosey. Clint had always deemed it to be a problem.

    The first thing that caught the redhead’s eye was the adjoining door being propped open. Peeping her head into the next room, she also found it empty with no Kate in sight. However, that was not the only glaring thing to hit her. The brunette’s clothes were unpacked, rather messily, some items on the floor, but the bed had not been slept in. Not only that, but the bed also had the girls empty bag sat on top of it, along with a couple miscellaneous arrow ends and her bow. The matching quiver leaning against the bed near Nat’s feet. Popping back into Yelena’s room, her eyes roamed the space once more. Both sides of the bed had been slept in, pillows having obviously been moved a few times, their current position in being propped against the headboard. An empty plate sat on one bedside table, its matching set on top the dresser across the room. Natasha could tell this room was Yelena’s by the neatness alone. Her wardrobe door was actually shut and upon opening it, clothes were folded and in sections by item.

    Old habits die hard.

    Natasha promptly shut the wardrobe door before leaving the room, making sure to close the door behind her. The blonde would be even angrier if she knew someone had been in her space, and the redhead could only imagine Yelena’s hand reaching for her knife. She rolled her eyes at her sister’s problem with impulsiveness as she re-entered the living room. Several heads turned to face her as she sat down.

    “How’d it go?” Clint spoke up warily, his fingers running across Laura’s shoulder. “It didn’t. She’s not here.” Nat shrugged nonchalantly.

    “Even you couldn’t get out the compound undetected, Romanoff.” Steve teased, elbowing her lightly.

    “She was the greatest child assassin the world has ever seen. She’d be losing her touch if she couldn’t.” Nat snorted, not before seeing the widening eyes of some of the room’s occupants. Obviously that fact hadn’t been mentioned.

    “Hey Friday. When did Yelena leave the building?” Steve spoke suddenly, his head titling up to the ceiling as if the AI was above his head.

    “Good evening, Mr Rogers. Miss Belova has made several movements today.” Friday spoke automatedly, her voice ringing over the speakers.

    “Tell us them all please Friday.” Fury spoke this time, his tone curious. “Miss Belova first left the compound at 9:57am this morning before returning earlier this evening at 6:37pm. She left once more at 6:42pm.” Friday spoke calmly. All eyes in the room turned to look at eachother.

    “Did you ask Kate where she went?” Clint’s voice spoke up once more, his body position the only one relaxed.

    Nat opened and shut her mouth a few times before answering, “She’s not here either. Friday?”

    “Miss Bishop left the grounds on foot at 3:14pm. She has not since returned.” Clint got to his feet, pacing a few times before coming to a stop, arms crossed facing out towards the window. Laura spared him a few glances before walking into the kitchen, pulling her phone up to her ear, obviously trying to get a hold of Kate. The woman had no such luck. “Straight to voicemail. Didn’t even ring.” She spoke calmly, her eyes fixed on her husband’s back. Nat watched as Clint’s shoulders tensed even more.

    “Clint. The kid’s from New York. She kno-“ “That’s the problem here!” Clint exploded, turning around to face the room, “She’s out there, probably alone, days after the guy who practically owns New York murdered her mother. It’s not her getting lost I’m worried about Steve.” He turned back towards the window, leaving his words to stew in the silence of the room.

    The room remained deafly still for quite a while after Clint’s outburst. For once, they were all speechless.

    Natasha watched as Laura silently comforted her husband, running a hand up and down his back, his muscles tensing and untensing as she did so. The redhead turned her gaze away from the couple after a couple of minutes, feeling like her staring was probably not helping Clint feel somewhat more at ease. Instead, she turned her head around to Steve and Nick whose heads were titled together, both looking at something pulled up on Fury’s phone. When the man looked up and met her gaze, she knew the silence wasn’t going to last much longer.

    “Barton you must be barking mad son.” He said flatly.

    Laura turned her head round slightly, a confused look on her face. Clint didn’t budge. “I go off planet for just under a year and all my people lose their minds.” Nick continued, slowly standing up to walk the room.

    Natasha watched Steve’s eyes follow the man, his eyebrows furrowed as if he was trying to put all the pieces together in his head. The redhead had seen this look on his face so many times before that if the room wasn’t as tense as it was, she may have let out a little chuckle. Clint turned around slowly, his eyes tracking Fury, trying to figure out what the man was going on about. Laura looked just as confused as herself, the two glances between the women not going unnoticed by Steve.

    “Clint’s protégé. She’s Eleanor Bishop’s daughter.” Cap came out with, making Clint frown even more than he had been.

    “You know of Eleanor?” The archer asked shocked.

    “Kingpin has been on SHIELD’s books for decades. He practically runs New York. We’ve had people on the inside of his operations for years, trying to minimise his influence in Avenger business as much as possible, but he is a powerful man.” Fury states plainly, his tone serious.

    “And what of Eleanor?” Clint hurried the man.

    “Eleanor came onto our radar over two decades ago, when she married Derek Bishop. He was an up-and-coming entrepreneur at the time and SHIELD was interested in the technology he was designing under his father’s firm, Bishop Security. The deal fell through when Hank Pym discovered he was also in talks with the Russian Military. If the deal was to go through with the Russians and it was released to the public that SHIELD and the Soviet Union got their technology from the same manufacturer… there would’ve been an uprising.” Fury paused.

    “It is unknown to SHIELD how Derek Bishop first became involved with Wilson Fisk, however, we do know that they did not come into contact until the Russian’s cut their ties with western security developers, stating they had made their own protection and were no longer in need of ours. Of course, this worried American intelligence, and we promptly investigated.”

    “And?” Laura questioned.

    “Pull on one string, two others appear.”

    “Meaning?” Clint quickly butted in, obviously wanting to hurry the story along. “SHIELD discovered the Red Room and the dealings of General Dreykov.” Fury spoke solemnly, his head turning to face Natasha with a slow nod. “That was where you came in Clint, and subsequently, starting Natasha’s defection to SHIELD.”

    “Failed defection more like it.” The redhead muttered.

    “That as it may have been, it eventually led us to uncovering more about the Winter Solider programme. Most of the intelligence agency didn’t believe it existed, even when Natasha got shot out in Odessa. If they couldn’t see it with their own eyes, they didn’t want to think a power like that could exist freely until- ”

    “Bucky.”

    Fury hummed in agreement.

    “Are you suggesting that Kate’s parents were involved with Hydra?” Clint said. “Kingpin and Derek Bishop drew up an agreement. Bishop Security would develop the technology needed for Fisk to keep his illegal affairs buried and in return, Kingpin would fund his father’s slowly failing security company. When Derek’s father died, the agreement changed. With Derek in the CEO role and a position on the board, he had gained more power. The company had become the most successful security company in the country after Fisk’s investment, and so Kingpin had a lot of leverage to manoeuvre when it came to Bishop bending his morals and grasping for more influence within New York. Fisk and Bishop had always kept themselves clean of active criminal activity, leaving that for those in a lower stature than themselves. This new position within New York society made them cocky. A deal with a European Mafia went awry and eventually ended in Bishop’s death.” “Kate...” Clint whispered under his breath.

    “The Battle of New York gave the mafia the cover they needed. After all, Derek was a high- profile citizen, his murder would have big story if he wasn’t one of the faceless thousands.” “How did he die?” Clint asked hesitantly.

    “Gunshot to the head. Not exactly the work of a Chitauri blaster.”

    This was apparently the end of Clint’s tether as he threw his fist into the nearest wall, putting a hole straight through the plasterboard. Laura left her husband to his rage, plopping herself down next to Nat. She sat motionless, her shock evident on her face.

    “And Eleanor?” Clint questioned through gritted teeth. One hand propped up on the wall, his head facing down towards the floor.

    “She found the body, knew something had gone horribly wrong. Eleanor moved to CEO in Derek’s wake, taking her away from the frying-pan and into the fire. She dealt with Fisk’s demands, killed on his behalf, and found herself becoming more and more compliant the more money she made. And the-“ “Then she set up a shell company in her fiancé’s name to funnel money to Kingpins goons, murdered her fiancé’s uncle after he got too close to discovering the truth and then her daughter got too involved so hired an assassin to kill the one helping her.” Clint cut off Fury and rambled out in one breath.

    “Bullseye.” Fury said whilst taking a seat once more.

    “And then you just left Fisk to his own devices?” Clint asked, noticing the gap in the tale between SHIELD’s last involvement and his own.

    “His case got handed over to the CIA. We were creating and killing an A.I powered mass murdering robot if my memory serves me correctly.”

    The room fell silent once more. Clint had dropped to the floor, his head leaning back against the wall, eyes directed away from the blood dripping down his knuckles, not that he was in anyway bothered by the all-too-common sight of blood. Laura’s eyes were on him, watching the heavy rise and fall of his chest. Fury and Steve were in a tense silent conversation, their eyes saying multitudes to one another that Nat wasn’t even to try and to being to decipher. But Natasha did have one question which had yet to be asked.

    “And this comes back to Kate how?” She spoke quietly, bringing all four sets of eyes to her. “Huh?” Clint’s head rose off the wall, her question sparking his interest. “Nick called you barking mad in reference to Kate. I’m just wondering why.” This made all eyes turn back to Fury who didn’t say a word. Natasha didn’t even need the man to speak after making eye contact. The look on his face said it all. Clint had obviously picked up on the same thing, standing to his feet at a speed Nat didn’t know was in the archer.

    “You think she’s involved with Kingpin?”

    “She’s in the perfect position to be. With both parents gone, the kids got a hell of a lot of inheritance. She’s grown up knowing the ins and outs of the high society and she’s got the skill set to be deadly weapon for hi-“ Fury states emotionless.

    “She’s a kid Fury.”

    “So was I Clint.” Natasha butts in, her tone solemn.

    “That is different in so many ways and you know it.” Clint argues back, his eyes full of anger. “We’ve got to look at every possibility here. A Bishop just happens to put on your Ronin suit and befriend a Black Widow assassin, and that doesn’t seem suspicious to you?” “Kid was a trainwreck when I first met her. A little overzealous and definitely cocky, but she was frightened even if she was too proud to admit it. There is no way she has any idea about any of this. The fact that you’re even accusing her of i-“ Clint stopped and shook his head, seemingly not wanting to waste his breath on Fury anymore. He glared at the man who had been his boss and friend for so many years before heading to the door. When he reached the door, his feet stopped and as if it was an afterthought he added, “And to think Kate admires the lot of you.” Clint spat, turning on his heel and out of the room.

    Chapter End Notes chapter 9 sneak preview:

    “Are you in position?” Yelena’s voice came through her ear like a whisper. “I’m a sitting dog down here.”

    Sonya couldn’t help her snort. “Duck, but yes be a good doggy and wait for me to undo the screws on this blasted thing.” Her teasing did not garner a response from the blonde, but Sonya had seen Yelena’s eye roll enough times to add it into the conversation herself.

    As Sonya continued to unscrew the vent cover, she took a peek down into what they’d be walking into. Yelena wasn’t going to like it.

    “Are you going to keep your head?” Sonya questioned bluntly.

    “I am not planning to letting it roll off my neck.” Yelena snapped back, only earning herself an exasperated sigh from Sonya.
