    Chapter 9

    Chapter Notes See the end of the chapter for notes After Sonya’s shots rang out, all hell broke loose. The two sets of combatants locked eyes, their expressions filled with equal determination and of silent threat. The air crackled with anticipation as they observed one another’s movements. One of the soldiers made the first move, jumping off the wall, he flipped over Sonya and Yelena’s heads, closing them in the alley and within a circle of super soldiers. The two assassins shared a quick glance and a nod before making their move.

    With a sudden burst of speed, they lunged towards the soldiers closest to themselves, fists flying and their feet pivoting. Each blow was a symphony of brutality, the impact of each landed hit reverberating through the air. Sonya delivered a powerful right hook, aiming for the jaw, while Yelena deftly dodged a hit to the head, the blonde countering with a swift kick to the midsection.

    Their movements were both graceful and savage, a deadly ballet of punches and kicks. No sweat glistened on their brows as they weaved in and out of the larger assailant’s reach, their size being a detriment to their speed. That didn’t stop them from exchanging blows with a surgical precision though.

    A thunderous roundhouse kick whirled through the air, its aim true. Yelena just about anticipated the other combatants attack, narrowly evading the devastating blow. Her eyes catching a glimpse of Sonya putting a bullet through another’s skull. In an instant, Yelena turned back around and retaliated with a spinning backfist, catching her opponent off guard, staggering him momentarily. It was enough for Yelena to be able to jump the tall man’s stature, wrapping her legs around his neck and swinging him to the floor with a crack. Two down.

    Six to go.

    Blood dripped from a cut above one fighter's eye, where Sonya had given him a fist to his occipital bone. He growled as he launched himself forward, launching a flurry of strikes down on the dark-haired woman, each blow infused with raw power, but it was not enough to beat the small assassin. She weaved through each of his thrusts, her slight figure too quick making it easy to evade him. She eventually made her way behind him, her disappearance from his view making him flustered. He spun his head round, but Sonya just anticipated his movements, before she knocked a devasting kick in the back of his neck, forcing his face into the ground with a crunch.

    Upon turning around, Sonya found Yelena had taken down another, a knife making a fountain out of his femoral artery. The blonde was fighting the ringleader now, a man at least twice her size. Sonya circles her own assailant, watching Yelena disarm her opponent out of her peripheral. It seems both widows had the same idea. Sonya kicks out, knocking the rifle from the man’s hands before running after Yelena towards the alley wall. They both jump and kick off the brick for momentum, slamming a knee or an elbow into their opponents’ heads. They flurry across to the other side of the space, the thinness of the alley not being forgiving in this battle, the two soldiers heads cracking open against the wall.

    Sonya swears she hears a snort from Yelena as both bodies crumple to the floor. Walking the few paces to join the blonde, she notices a few whisps have escaped from her braid, but that seems to be the only ailment between the pair of them. The blonde spares her a glimpse and then a smirk, “Still want that god from space now?”

    A single gunshot sounded from inside the door.

    “Maybe don’t take him off speed dial yet.” Sonya muttered as their legs took them towards the door as fast as they would move.

    “You know, this whole being strapped to a chair thing is kind of uncomfortable. This might be TMI but my but-“ “Vat is a TMI?” One of the other men in the room spoke up, his accent thick. He sounded like Yelena. Kingpin is working with Russians?

    “Oh, it means too much information, like I gave you too many details or stuff that you didn’t actually need to know or wasn’t very helpful, but I said it anyways.” Kate rambled out explaining, her usual rapid hand movements the only thing missing.

    When the man didn’t question her further, she continued, “I see you’re not one for follow up questions. Maybe I should explain the general laws of conversation, normally one person says something, they get a response, and this continues and swaps between the people involve-“ Before Kate could stop her mouth from moving, Kingpin was in front of her again and wrapped his hand around her throat. Her blue eyes widened in shock, her heart rate taking off as the fear begun to set in.

    “You run your mouth too much little girl. At least Eleanor had some poise.” He spat, his grip tightening before he spoke once more, “I don’t care who thinks your life is so important to scare off all my hitmen. You will pay for your parents’ misdemeanours no matter who threatens my life as a consequence. That is no worry for me.” He growled, the only sound in the room after he stopped being the choking noises coming from Kate’s pleading throat. He dropped his hand, leaving Kate to gasp for breath as he stepped back, a violent cough emerging from her.

    After a few moments, Kingpin turned his back to her, walking over to one of the men in the room, whispering in his ear. The man nodded, waving his hand to two others who followed him willingly. As the door slammed behind them, Kate made the impulsive decision to open her mouth again.

    What? She can’t help it, okay?

    “Tell… me… about… Dad…” She breathed out hoarsely, struggling to get the words out. “You really are a stupid girl.” Kingpin drawled out, turning on his heel. His face was dark now, matching his beady eyes that grossly roamed over her figure. An involuntary shiver ran down Kate’s spine. Normally, Kate would’ve had a witty response to his smugness but now that silent threat had been made, she was more worried about her livelihood than her comeback game.

    “Your father was a swine.” Kingpin drawled, his tone slimy and full of malice. He pulled a gun out of his pocket.

    “Dad… was… good…” Kate huskily started before a reverberating pain shot through her gut. A gunshot sounded simultaneously.

    She winced before her body slumped forward as much as the ties would let her. The brunette assumed that was the body’s automatic response to being stabbed in the gut. A bullet hole could only be found in the ceiling.

    As Fisk’s footsteps walked away from her, the sound echoing throughout the building, Kate dared not speak again. For fear of that bullet in her gut next time.

    She also daren’t hope on those muffled gunshots.

    For all she knew, someone had just robbed the bodega on the corner.

    Yelena kicked the door open, Sonya entering behind her seconds later grasping her elbow. The blonde stopped, letting Sonya whirl her around to face her. If it had been anyone else turning her back on the enemy, Yelena would’ve swung herself back round instantly. Sonya, however, was the quickest shot she knew, with a gun anyway. Yelena trusts her with her life. “I know you care for her-” The dark-haired woman started.

    Yelena scoffed.

    “I am merely concerned for what happens to Barton’s wife after he dies of his guilt.” “Yelena.” Sonya said again, not letting go of the blonde’s arm’s when she twisted slightly. “A rash decision is not the move here. We don’t know what we are walking into.” “A room full of the men we just kicked arse against outside. To answer your previous question, yes, I think we can take them.” This time the blonde did yank herself out of Sonya’s grip, although her feet did not move from her spot.

    “Yel-“ “I am not calling моя сестра.” Yelena spat. She could handle this on her own. She didn’t need any Avengers waltzing into her battlefield and blowing up Kate Bishop. She’d been through hell and back all on her own for years, bringing Kate out of that building unharmed was going to be the easiest thing she’d ever done in comparison.

    Yelena was not about to the let the one good thing in her life slip from her grasp that easily. Sonya rolled her eyes but kept her mouth shut at the signs of Yelena’s obvious internal struggle. She changed the magazines in all three of her guns before Yelena’s eyes met hers again.

    “If this goes tits up… I’m never letting you live it down.” Sonya said with a smirk, walking backwards and stepping around Yelena with her arms held out to her sides as if she was bragging about what she’d just said. Yelena let out a soft chuckle before breaking into a jog, Sonya followed her lead.

    A set of double doors appeared before them, the widows having agreed on being rash, albeit Sonya somewhat reluctantly, pushed the doors wide open. Before them stood a large room, filled with cardboard boxes. The dust was impressive to say the least, seeing as the building was most definitely seeing some sort of use.

    The two widows shared a glance as footsteps sounded from behind the opposing door on the other side of the room.

    Sonya moved to the left, taking up a position by the wall beside the door so she would be covered from sight when it opened. Yelena didn’t copy her fellow widow, instead standing slap bang in the middle of the room. Sonya rolled her eyes at the blonde, disappointed in, but alas still thriving in Yelena’s want of chaos.

    At least her time spent in the blonde’s presence was never boring.

    The doors swung open, revealing three men. They look identical to the ones that had been outside and Yelena couldn’t hold back her laugh.

    “Ha. Nice to see you again.” The blonde snickered at the confused looks on their faces. Sonya took their moment of hesitation to sneak up behind all three, slashing the backs of their knees. They toppled down like dominoes, just leaving the two widows to knock them out and bind them together.

    The doors that had been swung open revealed a corridor. It was in the same nick as the rest of the place, drywall pocking out through deteriorating wallpaper, what Yelena believed was probably a nice carpet had been trashed with muddy boot prints. The blonde knocked her head towards Sonya who was stood glaring down at the unconscious soldiers before heading down the small passage, her speed picking up when hearing Sonya’s footsteps behind her. Another set of double doors welcomed them at the end and Yelena just knew Kate was on the other side.

    She was about to reach for the doorhandle when Sonya stopped her. Hearing murmuring from the other side of the door, she didn’t verbally state her idea, but nodded up to the vent. Yelena nodded her okay before kneeling down to act as a step for Sonya. Once they had gotten the vent open, Yelena pushed Sonya upwards so she could climb into the old vent space. Stealthily and quietly, Sonya tracked her way through the tunnel, weaving around the ceiling until she was over another vent cover where the voices were loudest. Looking down at the vent she noticed the screws were still in place unlike in the other one. The dark-haired woman quietly reached to her calf; the position rather uncomfortable to grab her smallest knife to undo the screws.

    “Are you in position?” Yelena’s voice came through her ear like a whisper. “I’m a sitting dog down here.”

    Sonya couldn’t help her snort. “Duck, but yes be a good doggy and wait for me to undo the screws on this blasted thing.” Her teasing did not garner a response from the blonde, but Sonya had seen Yelena’s eye roll enough times to add it into the conversation herself. As Sonya continued to unscrew the vent cover, she took a peek down into what they’d be walking into. Yelena wasn’t going to like it.

    “Are you going to keep your head?” Sonya questioned bluntly.

    “I am not planning to let it roll off my neck.” Yelena snapped back, only earning herself an exasperated sigh from Sonya.

    Kate Bishop was tied to a chair in the middle of the room, she was hunched over and to the naked eye looked relatively unharmed, but Sonya’s eyes were ones to rival that even of the Hawk’s. Even from her high and impeded vision she could make out an object protruding from Kate’s stomach.

    There were also five super soldiers in the room, a group of three on the left and two more on the right. Yelena would be five on one as soon as she opened the door. Trying to plan through the best way to go about this whilst she undid the last screw, Sonya did not mean the shocked breath to escape her lungs when a new body wandered into her frame of vision. “Sonya?” Yelena’s voice perked up again, but not in a happy way.

    “That Kingpin guy is here. He’s got five friends with him. Two on your right, three on the left.” Sonya muttered quietly, now was not the moment for her voice to echo in the vents. “Do you have eyes on Kate?” Yelena’s voice seemed even quieter at this question. “She’s alive.” Sonya said.

    A moment of stillness occurred before the double doors below sounded, indicating them being swung open. Sonya shook her head to no one but herself as the heads she’d been looking down on turned to face Yelena.

    “Oh, fuck it.” Sonya said, slamming her knee down as hard as she could from her limited angle, the vent cover landing right on top of one of the soldier’s heads. Upon landing on the opposite side of the group from Yelena she said, “Woops. Sorry! I never was any good at physics.”

    Sonya ran her eyes over their opponents quickly. Their eyes roamed the room, flicking back to Kingpin every so often. They were looking for a way out for him, planning to sacrifice themselves for their leader. The dark-haired woman tried to make eye contact with her partner to see if she’d noticed it too, but the green eyes were too focused to something just to the right and beyond Sonya. The dark-haired woman would’ve turned and looked to see if the little hawk was still breathing but she couldn’t do that if Yelena was distracted. She took a subtle step to the right, blocking Yelena’s view. Her eyes flicked quickly to Sonya’s who nodded at the blonde hoping she’d get the message.

    The blonde, already grasping one gun in her left hand, pulled another out of her back pocket to sit in her right. This got the men’s attention.

    “Ah. Kate Bishop’s secret protector to save the day.” Fisk drawled, his hands rubbing together like he’d hit the jackpot. “It was foolish of you to come here tonight, now you shall both be dead, and I shall live on with the Bishop empire in my grasp.” “I’m sorry. Who are you?” Yelena spoke, her voice calm yet threatening. Kingpin only chuckled. “My dear girl, do not kid, you know who I am.”

    “Oh my! Are you in Sex and the City? Stanford Blatch?” Yelena fake fangirled, her smile growing wider.

    Sonya would’ve laughed if the smile wasn’t somewhat creepy.

    Whilst Yelena kept the boys entertained with her ramblings about her favourite show, Sonya turned her head slightly to check on the brunette behind her. Her breathing was slow and heavy, definitely a sign of bradycardia. The area of blood staining her jumper was growing bigger by the second. Her throat was littered with blood blisters and was most definitely going to bruise. They were going to have to hurry this up. She swung her head back around to Yelena to inform her of this, her rapid movement was never not going to attract the attention of the blonde.

    “…and that is the end of season one.” Yelena finished as Sonya dialled back into the conversation, “Идиоты.” The blonde raised both guns, shooting the two on her right point blank in the head and Sonya had never seen a man as big as Kingpin move so fast. She watched the blonde’s eyes track his movement as he moved out of the room, and Sonya had no doubts she would’ve taken him on if she wasn’t dealing with two super soldiers. Sonya’s opponent had had enough, swiping under her legs pushing her onto her back. The dark-haired woman huffed out a laugh.

    “What is it with masculinity and not being able to be content on the bottom? Я бы сделал это приятным в любом случае.” The man’s eyes widened at her comment, leaving Sonya a window to spring a surprise knife in the side of his neck.

    She hit his coronary artery point blank, blood spurting out of it like a fountain, narrowly missing her face. She pushed his heavy weight off of her as quickly as possible before standing and shaking herself off. “That was so gross.”’

    Sonya’s eyes travelled back to the only movement in the room. Yelena had taken down one opponent, his body still shaking on the floor from the blonde’s widow bites she had not turned off, now sharing blows with the other. Sonya hurled herself into the fight, sliding down and taking the ground out from under his feet.

    “I’ve got this. Get Bishop.” She huffed out as she and the solider got to their feet once more. Yelena, not about to argue with Kate’s safety, nodded deftly before running back to the middle of the room.

    Kate knew there was fighting going on all around her, but her vision was too blurry and her mind to lethargic to acknowledge it properly. The sounds of gunshots were muffled in her ears, and the blow to the head and knife in the stomach were also probably not helping. Neither was the roughness of her throat and the struggle it was to breathe. A figure knelt down in front of her, and hands cupped her cheeks. Kate tried to open her eyes, but they fluttered closed again, her body too tired to carry on. One hand moved to the side of her neck, making the brunette wince and Kate could hear words being spoken but nothing was clear enough to her to make it out. The gentle contact let go of her, and soon her arms were free of their binds leaving her body limp. She toppled forward, expecting to hit the ground with a thump, Kate internally braced herself for impact, not trusting her arms to be able to catch herself in her current state. But when the ground did not meet her and the soft hands returned once more, she finally let her mind rest.

    Yelena watched Kate slump in her arms, all tension left in her muscles evaporating. The blonde braced her knees before properly lifting Kate into a bridal hold, Sonya quickly running over and adjusting the girls head, so she was tucked into Yelena’s neck. The dark- haired woman did not miss that the arm Yelena had wrapped under the girls back ended with her hand on her wrist, fingers in just the right position to feel her pulse. Sharing a grim glance at one another, they headed back the way they came in, Sonya leading, two guns drawn just in case they met any unfavourable company.

    When the cold New York breeze hit her face, Yelena let herself breathe again. She took a quick glance down at the brunette in her arms to see if the cold had shocked her body into response, but luck did not seem to be on Yelena’s side today. She instead placed her eyes back onto Sonya, not even questioning where she was leading them too. The dark-haired woman stopped as they reached the end of the alleyway, signalling for Yelena to give her a minute or two and then she stepped out of sight.

    The blonde took this minute for herself, leaning back into the brick wall of the alleyway, jostling Kate’s body as gently as she could to get a firmer grip. The brunette was losing too much blood, her fingertips were turning purple, and Yelena could only picture the blue her lips probably were. She willed Sonya to hurry up, placing a gentle kiss on Kate’s forehead as a car swung into the entrance of the alleyway. Her friend jumped out of the driver’s seat opening the back door for Yelena. The blonde shuffled Kate in first, laying her down across the seats before she climbed in herself, scrunching herself up small enough she could sit on the floor beside the brunette.

    Sonya slammed the door behind the blonde, taking a minute to open and close the trunk before she returned to the driving seat, swinging the car around with one hand as she passed something to Yelena. It was a blanket. The blonde spared Sonya a glance but now her eyes were firmly on the road and foot too focused on pushing the accelerator into the floor. Yelena placed the blanket on Kate’s legs whilst stripping off her own jacket, scrunching it up and placing it around the knife protruding from the brunette’s gut. When the pressure and pain did not wake Kate, Yelena pulled the blanket up to Kate’s chin, keeping her hand underneath and the pressure strong.

    “Sonya. Your apartment is not this far.” Yelena growled.

    The blonde knew she and Sonya could fix this up in no time. The dark-haired woman’s apartment stocked with blood bags and medical equipment. Every widow being pretty much an honorary doctor from the number of times they’ve patched themselves up over the years. “The Avenger’s Compound is.”

    Yelena opened her mouth to reply but Sonya cut her off.

    “Kate Bishop is not us. She does not need a shitty patch up job because she does not feel lesser at asking for help. You want her to live. Your sister has a state-of-the-art facility, and the most expensive medical equipment money can buy. Ты можешь злиться на Наташу, это нормально, но не вымещай это на Кате.” The dark-haired woman said with finality. Yelena was going to say Kate was not that much different from themselves in terms of asking for help but decided against it. She did not say another word until the car stopped moving.     Chapter 10

    Chapter Notes we back bitches!

    quite a fast-paced chapter this I realised as I did my final proof read but oh well. thank you for all the love, its very much appreciated!

    haven't written a word yet this week so am going to try and buckle down to write some now, have just worked the past five days in a row so its been a little cray cray!! enjoy!!

    In a room full of superheroes, Laura Barton was seemingly the only one who could keep her cool.

    Her husband was still stewing in front of the window. He had re-entered the room about an hour after storming out, his jaw tensing every couple of minutes, the tension his body was gaining never slowing.

    Natasha was sat on the couch, her head resting in her hands as her eyes bore holes into the back of Clint’s head, it was a strange sight to see Clint this openly worked up, something she had only seen in the blip. His hand clenched his bicep tighter every couple seconds and Nat could only think he was imagining clutching the Ronin sword and swinging it to whoever’s hands were possibly on Kate.

    Fury, ever the peacekeeper was muttering to himself in the kitchen, brewing a pot of tea. He was the epitome of calm, humming a tune every now and again before reaching for his phone, only to nod and put it down again. Everyone in the room knew Fury had contacts all over the globe, he was not checking his phone for a social reason. And after dropping his opinions on a woman he hadn’t even met, it was probably best he keep himself to himself, and away from Clint.

    Steve hadn’t said a word. A silent and strong presence, he sat alongside Nat, his eyes keen on staring a hole in his own flesh. He had been hunched over wringing his hands together for however long they had all been sat there, not looking up for even a moment. Steve was a planner and Laura would bet all the money she owned that he was mentally prepping for every scenario.

    Laura, the non-superhero in the room, had taken to looking in Kate’s room to find any evidence of where she had gone. The group had figured Yelena going missing for hours at a time wasn’t something to concern themselves about. Nat had willingly agreed and had even muttered a comment about how her sister may as well not be at the compound anyway. Steve had been the only one to react, putting a placating hand on Nat’s shoulder for just a moment before pulling away.

    Upon opening Kate’s door, Laura let out a fond chuckle. There were clothes strung all around the room, as far as a sock hanging off the ceiling fan. A purple hoodie strung over the radiator and then a whole bundle of clothing pouring out of the semi-open wardrobe door. Laura had no doubt that if the door was moved even a smidgen, everything inside would come crashing out. The brunette’s bow and quiver sat centre stage, their presence here alarming Laura to the glaring fact Kate was out somewhere in the city unarmed. Laura knew the kids close combat was good, having seen her brawl Clint in the front yard over Christmas, but her shooting would be the thing to save her life.

    Laura turned slightly, noticing the adjoining door was propped open. She entered the next room along the corridor warily, noting the fact that the space belonged to a Black Widow assassin. Yelena’s room couldn’t have been more of a juxtaposition to Kate’s. The only thing out of place was the unmade bed. Everything else seemed to have a place, even if only temporary. Laura glanced around the room, floor to ceiling to see if Nat had missed anything. Sure, Nat was good, but Laura did this once too and not being out in the field only made you more aware when you were. The first thing that caught her eye was nothing much of importance but something Nat hadn’t mentioned. The air vent had been opened, the vent covering leaning against the wall outside on the balcony. Laura figured she’d keep this information to herself, thinking a group of spies and Steve would not appreciate their conversations being listened to by someone propped to be the greatest child assassin of all time. The second thing Laura Barton noticed was the ending of a black square protruding from underneath the bedside table. Reaching down, she pulled it from its hiding spot. Kate’s phone.

    -

    Natasha heard Laura’s rapid footsteps before she saw the woman. She flung her head round as the head of brown hair she’d become so fond of came racing into the kitchen and made an abrupt stop. Her hand was raised in the air with-

    “Kate’s phone… we’ve been… calling a duvet…cover.” The woman breathed heavily. Her arm dropping fully to her side as she finished her sentence.

    This caught Clint’s attention, he swung around from the window, grasping his phone from his back pocket before bringing it to his ear.

    “Where th-“ He growled before stopping, someone obviously interrupting on the other end of the line. His head flung back around to the window before spinning back to the room again. “Open the gate.” Clint’s face was sombre.

    “What?” Steve broke his silence.

    “Open the fucking gate, Steve.”

    “Right turn, 10 yards.” Yelena muttered as she propped herself up on her tip toes, reaching across the width of the car, trying to find Kate’s pulse in her neck, it now being too weak in her wrist to get a clear count.

    Sonya whipped the car round the bend, the familiar road sparking Yelena’s memory. She grabbed her phone and pressed on her Bint Clarton contact without hesitation this time. “Open th-“ Yelena started as soon as he answered.

    “Where th-“ Clint spoke before stopping at Yelena’s next words.

    “It’s Kate. Open the gate.”

    Sonya pressed her foot all the way down on the accelerator as Yelena hung up the phone, the opening gate coming into view as the car rattled up the one-way road. The dark-haired widow didn’t slow the car down as the entered the compound, tires screeching as it hit each bend in the driveway.

    “Med bay is third floor, second door on the right. Elevator is on the left as we walk in.” Yelena said as the car stopped abruptly.

    Sonya didn’t acknowledge her statement but jumped out of the car, opening the passenger door next to Kate’s head. She would pick Kate up under her shoulders and carry her out whilst Yelena followed by moving through the car, bringing Kate’s legs with her, trying not to aggravate her injury too much. The widows were halfway through this manoeuvre when the compounds inhabitants came running out. Sonya and Yelena didn’t spare them so much of a second glance as they focused on getting Kate’s bottom half out of the car safely. When all three girls were out of the vehicle, Yelena glanced up briefly. Her sister and Captain America had stopped short at the door, whilst Clint was hovering over Sonya’s shoulder, his eyes focused on Kate’s face and neck before flitting to her stomach. The blonde was about to begin yelling at the lot of them when Laura Barton came running out of the front door with a wheeled stretcher alongside her. Yelena could’ve kissed her as she met Sonya and Yelena halfway to the door. No words were exchanged as the two Bartons and the two widows made their way into the elevator and up to the med bay doors.

    Natasha and Steve had followed them on the stairs, all of them coming to a stop outside the ward. Yelena moved to shove open the double doors when Nat grabbed her arm. “Let go of me.” The blonde growled at the redhead.

    “You cannot operate Yelena. You’re too close. Пусть Соня и Лора займутся этой сестрой.” Natasha said placatingly, trying to spread her calm to the blonde.

    Yelena only scowled more at her sister. “And who are you to ask that of me?” She questioned.

    This comment made Nat drop her arm and step back, raising her hands in surrender whether she needed to or not. Yelena nodded to Sonya who shoved open the double doors, leaving Laura and her fellow widow to wheel Kate in.

    Once they were in the medical room, Sonya took charge immediately.

    Without hesitation, she ordered Yelena around the room, making her find the needed equipment. Laura assessed the situation quickly and her field agent medical instincts kicked in as she grabbed a bottle and needle from a nearby cabinet. Sonya only glanced at the woman as she begun injecting around the stab sight. It wouldn’t do much for Kate’s pain, but Sonya agreed that it was better than the young woman having no relief at all. They didn’t have the luxury of time to intubate and anesthetise the archer.

    Sonya cut away Kate’s clothing, throwing it and Yelena’s jacket on the plastic sheets the blonde had laid on the floor. The sight of a chunky knife and the blood oozing from Kate’s abdomen sent a chill down Yelena’s spine, but she maintained a calm exterior. She knew that treating a stab wound required swift action and a steady hand. If it had been on herself Yelena wouldn’t have cared, but this was Kate.

    "Mrs Barton, find me clean towels and some hot water. We need to clean the wound and stop the bleeding," Sonya ordered, her years of medical experience taking charge. Yelena couldn’t stop her eye roll at her friend’s politeness even in the current situation. As Laura rushed to comply, Sonya put on a pair of disposable gloves and carefully prodded around Kate’s shirt. The wound was deep, and blood continued to seep out. The widow’s mind raced as she assessed the situation, considering the potential damage to internal organs. Sonya glanced up at Yelena as Laura returned with the towels and hot water in hand. The heart monitor was beeping slowly as the women exchanged glances.

    “We don’t have time to hesitate Sonya.” The blonde muttered under her breath. “We don’t have time to x-ray either. Pulling this knife out is incredibly risky becau-“ “It could be acting as a plug to tamponade the bleeding, however, if we leave it and wait to let her pressure balance out, we lea-“ Laura butted in, earning herself an eyebrow raise from both widows.

    “Leave the risk of her bleeding out anyway.” Sonya finished. The dark-haired woman took a few deep breaths before making eye contact with the two woman across the table from her. “Laura, hang two bags of bloo-“ “She’s O positive.” Yelena butted in.

    “And run an I.V of morphine and add some tranexamic to hopefully help her blood clot. Yelena, grab a shit ton of gauze and the coagulator and be ready to blast that shit everywhere.” Sonya rambled out, the three women running around the room must’ve looked like headless chickens.

    They all met back at the table minutes later. Drugs now running through Kate’s system, an oxygen tube up her nose and Sonya’s hands steady above the knife. Yelena and Laura were prepped with hands of gauze, ready to pack the wound and soak up any blood, to clear their field of vision so Yelena could get the coagulator in as soon as possible. This plan was probably for the best as the moment the knife left Kate’s body, blood splurged out of her abdomen. Yelena and Laura acted quickly, packing the deep hole with gauze, replacing it every time no white material was left. After multiple rounds of gauze, the rate of the brunette’s blood flow decreased, leaving Yelena a window to cauterize the source of the blood flow. The blonde was steady as she took the small tool to her friend’s abdomen, the gravity of her role not lost on her.

    Moments later Yelena let out a long breath as she stepped away from the table, leaving Sonya to put some internal stitches in, as well as closing up the wound on Kate’s stomach. The blonde leaned over the counter on the other side of the room, before standing straight and pulling her bloodied top off her body. She headed over to the sink, scrubbing her arms violently, wanting to get Kate’s blood off her body. Too many times her skin has been blood stained, leaving memories she did not want to linger in plain sight for days on end. Kate was not going to be a stamp in that pattern.

    Yelena didn’t know how long she stood there scrubbing herself before a presence arrived at her side. Laura Barton had cleaned herself up and put on a change of clothes, so the blonde figured she’d been at the sink awhile. The brown-haired woman handed her a familiar looking hoodie, a deep purple. Yelena nodded gratefully before pulling the soft material over her head. Laura then nodded to the door and Yelena followed without even thinking about it. They walked in a comfortable silence before arriving at another door. The blonde didn’t have time to question where this led to before Laura opened the door, her eyes nudging Yelena in. It was a small recovery room, with a hospital like looking bed and in it laid a certain Kate Bishop. Sonya hovered by her bedside, still in the same clothes as before, fiddling with the IV stand next to the bed. Upon noticing Yelena’s presence, she smiled. “She’s stable for now. Stitches are holding and her vitals have levelled out.” Sonya said as she passed Yelena, heading towards the door where Laura stood holding it open. The widow squeezed Yelena’s shoulder on the way past.

    “First aid kit in the cupboard, just in case you want to clean her face up a little.” Laura spoke up softly, the motherly expression being somewhat of a warm blanket to Yelena. The blonde looked from Kate to both the women in the doorway.

    “Thank you.” She said quietly before the exited the room with small smiles on their faces.

    The two women headed down to where the other compound dwellers were dotted around the living room. Clint had his head in his hands, his right foot jumping up and down, making the rest of his body jolt at each movement. His head shot up when the two women entered the room.

    “How is she?”

    “She’s stable. Hasn’t woken yet but that will come with time.” Laura said and headed straight for him, sitting on the arm of the chair, pulling him into her side.

    “Yelena’s with her.” Sonya added but stayed on the edge of the group, not taking a seat. Steve was wandering around the kitchen, fiddling with bread and fillings to make sandwiches for everyone. Himself and Nat had realised no one had really eaten in the past couple of days and Steve wanted something to do rather than sitting around and waiting. Patience had never really been Steve’s thing.

    Fury was sat at the dining table by himself, his eyes roaming across those gathered in the room. Natasha watched as he sized Sonya up, his gaze steady and unwavering. The redhead got up from her spot and approached the dark-haired woman. They had never really been close, not like her and Yelena. They were several years apart, so never crossed paths in the Red Room. However, all widows were like sisters, so Sonya was a most welcome presence. The redhead opened her arms as she got a few steps away bringing a chuckle out of Sonya. They embraced gently before pulling away, Nat’s hands coming to rest on Sonya’s upper arms.

    “Приятно тебя видеть. Я рад, что ты выбрался.”

    “Всем этим я обязан Елене.” Sonya said back, the faith in her voice unwavering. Natasha smiled at her sister’s friend before beckoning her to follow her and have a seat. As they sat down, Clint looked up. His eyes were red raw, but his gaze couldn’t have been softer. He reached out an arm towards Sonya who reached out willingly. Clint squeezed the widow’s hand, his message conveyed clear as day. Sonya just nodded her head before turning back to Natasha.

    The two women’s conversation did not last uninterrupted for long as Fury made his presence known. He stalked his way over from the dining table before lowering himself into a chair in the shadows of the room where the lamp hadn’t been turned on. Natasha smirked at the expression forming on Sonya’s face, it was one of cheek and something she had seen on Yelena all too often.

    “Who the hell are you?” Fury questioned.

    “You give me your name horse master and I shall give you mine.” Sonya pulled out a very impressive Scottish accent and brilliant impression of Gimli from Lord of the Rings. Natasha shared a grin with Laura and Clint who were stifling laughs of their own at the look on Fury’s face.

    “Nick Fury.” He replied blankly, obviously not amused.

    “Are you often angry?” Sonya bounced back with, this time making Nat snort rather loudly. As her eyes met the redhead’s, they glistened with her own amusement. Natasha smiled wider at this. Sonya had lived through the same experience as Yelena and was so full of life. The redhead knew that was rather a tunnel vision perspective to have but seeing Sonya like this gave Natasha hope as to her relationship with her sister. Natasha hadn’t been chemically subjugated so she couldn’t pass judgement on what that was like. Yelena was closed-off and distant whereas Sonya was a bundle of excitement and a breath of fresh air in the compound. The redhead knew their experiences would have their differences but seeing how carefree Sonya could act after all she had gone through; she could only hope that Yelena would one day let herself live like that too.

    Yelena didn’t know when she fell asleep but what she did know was who ever had just entered the room had disturbed her comfortable position in the small hospital like chair next to Kate’s bed. She knew Sonya had been in multiple times to check Kate’s vitals but with her widow training, she didn’t wake Yelena once and for that she was grateful. You would think at the absurd amount of money the Avengers Compound cost they would’ve invested in some comfier chairs but apparently not.

    Cracking open one eye she found her only company besides Kate was a worse for wear looking archer. The blonde picked her head up from where it was rested on the chair’s arm, her movement bringing Clint’s head to her. His eyes were red and puffy. Yelena had never been good with comforting those who are upset so decided to stick to what she knew instead. Awkward small talk with the man she’d tried to kill, who also happens to be her recently resurrected sister’s best friend.

    “Sonya said she still hasn’t woken up?” Clint asked quietly, his voice raw. Yelena hummed, her gaze travelling to Kate. She had a few scrapes and bruises on her face, a particularly nasty one on the back of her neck from where it had spread from the bump on her head. Her neck was mottled in purple and greens. Her face had regained its colour since Yelena had been asleep and that was only ever a good thing. The blonde slowly peeled back the thin blanket, seeing that Kate’s bandages hadn’t been bled through. Another good sign. Her stomach was a plethora of colours. A deep purple closest to the wound, spreading through gradients of green to yellow further up her ribs and down her abdomen. The brunette was lucky not to have any broken ribs.

    “What is it, Barton?” The blonde asked before slowly taking her eyes of Kate and turning to the archer sat across the bed from her, his eyes boring into her.

    “Thank you.” He said, his eyes gleaming in his gratefulness.

    “For what?”

    “Being there for her when I wasn’t. You didn’t owe that to anyone.”

    “I did not do it for you.” Yelena said back flatly, not knowing how to accept his thanks. After all, not many people have ever thanked her for doing what was practically her life’s work, apart from those who’d paid her to do it. And even then, it was more of an obligatory thank you, not a heartfelt one like that of Clint Barton’s.

    “I know. You did it for you.” He shrugged.

    “What’s that supposed to mean?” Yelena’s eyebrows furrowed.

    “Doing a good deed. Wiping out the red in your ledger. Trying to make amends.” Clint listed as if it was a common experience for him, which Yelena guessed it was based on the amount of time he’d spent with Natasha.

    “You cannot wipe out that much red.” Yelena scoffed. “And I know that is what моя сестра says, but she is kidding herself.” She continued as Clint opened his mouth to rebuff her statement.

    “Not even sacrificing yourself to save half the population?” Barton questioned hesitantly. Any emotion that had been on Yelena’s face disappeared as she steeled herself completely. “All that time she spent posing, all the good she was trying to do, to make up for all the pain and suffering she caused? She never once thought about me. She never thought about the pain she caused me.”

    “She thought you got out Yele-“ “And then the сука jumped off a cliff.” Yelena continued her rant, cutting off Clint. “She saved the world, Yelena. She did it for you.” He was pleading her to see reason now. “You are walking a thin line, Barton.” The blonde growled.

    “She only ever wanted you safe.”

    Yelena rolled her eyes at him repeating his speech from the ice rink. “If she was ever going to do it for me, she would have let you run off that cliff. She was my world. And that was the one world she couldn’t seem to save. That pain and suffering she wanted to erase, she transferred instead… to me.” Yelena paused, needing to catch her breath. Clint didn’t say anything, his eyes studying the rare emotion plastered over the blonde’s face. “Pain and suffering is every day for me Clint Barton. Моя сестра and I are still trained killers, whether she wants to try fool herself or not. Except I’m not the one that’s on the cover of a magazine. I’m not the killer that little girls call their hero. I’m not the killer that’s past has been forgiven and buried at the bottom of a cliff.” The assassin spat; her tone low. She stared at Barton for a few more moments before turning her gaze to anywhere else in the room.

    A few minutes passed before the creaking of a chair sounded and footprints headed towards the door. The archer pulled it open, making Yelena only look up when it didn’t shut immediately. When she caught his eye, he spoke once more before shutting the door behind him.

    “Your sister loves you, Yelena.”

    The blonde wishes people would stop saying that to her.

    Chapter 11

    Chapter Notes NOTE: The italics in the long Yelena and Sonya dialogue is all in Russian - I just didn't want you all to have to translate that much of it.

    See the end of the chapter for more notes “Look who has decided to finally grace her oldest friend with her presence.” Sonya teased as she opened the door, waving Yelena in.

    The blonde only rolled her eyes as she took in the woman before her. It had been a couple months since she’d seen the dark-haired woman in person. A new tattoo on her arm catching the blonde’s eye immediately. Sonya’s dark brown eyes glistening when she had seen Yelena looking.

    “Go ahead blondie, you can complement me once in a while.” She grinned. “Some of us have a reputation to uphold.” The blonde said blankly as she threw herself onto Sonya’s couch, putting her feet up on the coffee table. Yelena threw a smirk at Sonya as an annoyed grimace glanced over her face, her eyes stuck on the blonde’s boots on the table. Her fellow widow didn’t say anything however, just taking a seat next to her. They exchanged pleasantries for a while, which mostly consisted of talking about Sonya’s late-night escapades, so maybe not all pleasantries in hindsight. Yelena knew Sonya had noticed her mood when she had arrived, her widow training not being enough to throw Sonya off that scent, she just hoped the dark-haired woman would keep talking about the man she had picked up in a bar the other night and Yelena never hoped for Sonya to keep talking in these instances.

    “So enough about me. How is Kate Bishop?” Sonya turned her body, resting her temple on her fist as her arm lay across the back of the sofa. The widow went as far to batter her eyelashes at the blonde. “Is she still smoking hot?” She emphasised.

    Yelena scoffed.

    “She’s in bed.”

    “Your bed?” Sonya teased, not knowing how much truth there was hiding within her question.

    Yelena didn’t answer, just rolled her eyes before standing up and walking into the kitchen. The blonde headed straight for the cupboard under the sink, pulling out one of the many bottles of vodka Sonya had stashed. Yelena studied the bottle as Sonya sauntered into the room after her. The dark-haired woman leant into the counter on her hip, her arms crossed. When Yelena met her eyes, her amusement was clear.

    “Oh. She was so in your bed!” Sonya exclaimed, her eyebrows raising along with her tone. Yelena genuinely thought her friend was about to start jumping up and down. “You little minx!” Sonya continued as Yelena swung the bottle back, the alcohol warming her as it ran down her throat. The blonde still didn’t justify her friend with a response as she walked back to the couch, but Yelena knew her silence gave Sonya all the ammo she needed. “And here I was under the impression that ‘it’s not like that’.” Her friend continued as she retook her own seat, doing an awful impression of Yelena as she did.

    This finally got a smirk out of Yelena and a shake of her head.

    “That was so bad.” The blonde stated making Sonya gasp in insult. She clutched her chest before whacking Yelena gently in the head.

    “You are awful at girl talk. Details. Go.” Sonya said whilst tucking her legs up under herself, both hands cupped around her mug of some tea concoction that Yelena knew was disgusting just by the smell.

    “Kate quite enjoyed our girl’s night actually.” Yelena smirked, knowing her friend was coming to the wrong conclusion but the blonde couldn’t help herself.

    Two could play at this game after all.

    Sonya let out a girly scream that Yelena didn’t even know she was capable of and as entertained as she was, Yelena decided to put her friend out of her misery, or cause it, seeing as Sonya’s smile soon faded.

    “We hid in my room, listened to some top-secret Avengers conversations and she fell asleep stealing my body heat.” Yelena shrugged.

    “And?”

    “Then I woke her up with pancakes and now I’m here.” Yelena waved her hand around to gesture at Sonya’s apartment.

    “How romantic.”

    “Сука.” The blonde grumbled, taking another swig of the bottle still firmly in her hand. Sonya seemingly had had enough of her teasing for one day, or just didn’t feel like getting her head pummelled in when Yelena finally snapped.

    “How is she really?”

    “As good as she can be.” The blonde said simply.

    Sonya just hummed.

    “And you?”

    “I am fine.”

    “You are drinking vodka at 11am.”

    “I am Russian.” She deadpanned.

    “Touché.” Sonya raises her mug, clinking it against the bottle in Yelena’s hand. Several minutes of silence elapsed between them. Yelena knew Sonya was staring at her, trying to get a read on why the blonde was in her apartment and not back at the Compound. Yelena focused on the swirling liquid in the bottle she was spinning in her hand, the drink glistening in the sunlight streaming through Sonya’s windows.

    And Yelena let herself breathe.

    Until… Sonya opened her big mouth.

    “Did you cuddle?”

    Yelena couldn’t help the groan that escaped her mouth, and if there was a smile on her face as well, that was only for her and Sonya to know.

    Kate grimaced as she opened her eyes, the bright light streaming in from the window blinding her almost immediately. Whoever was in the room with her must’ve noticed as she soon heard the noise of the shutters being closed and she sighed in relief when she next opened her eyes.

    The room was dark and yet Kate knew where she was immediately. She turned her head lightly to the opposite side of the room to the windows, wincing slightly as she hit a sore spot on the back of her head.

    Right. I got my head hit into a brick wall.

    Her wince soon disappeared as her eyes landed on a familiar sight. Laura Barton was sat in the chair next to her bed, watching her with teary eyes. Kate couldn’t stand that sight for long so as soon as her brain and her arm became friends again, she reached out her left arm to grasp Laura’s hands that rested on her bed. The older woman squeezed her hand lightly, as if she was the most fragile thing in the world, then stood, not releasing her hand, and placed a kiss on her forehead. Kate squeezed her eyes tightly at the motherly gesture, her own eyes becoming watery now. Laura must’ve noticed this when she pulled back a few moments later as she sat on the side of Kate’s bed, leaning forward so Kate didn’t have to and gently moving Kate’s head into the crook of her neck to embrace the young woman as well as she could, given the situation.

    “I’ve got you.” Laura mumbled softly whilst she stroked Kate’s hair.

    The brunette relaxed into the woman for a few minutes before she slowly pulled back, lowering her head back gently against the pillow. Kate closed her eyes once more as Laura mumbled something about being right back.

    Steve rested his arms on the barrier that stood between him and a drop onto the gym floor. The compounds gym had always been a centre of energy within the building, its pinpoint location and marvel design made it so. The gym was on the ground floor of the compound, all though its extraordinarily high ceilings made it protrude onto the first floor. That is where Steve was now.

    The second floor of the gym was open to look down on the first, giving anyone who walked by, or any dedicated spectator a bird’s eye view of what others were doing down below. The lifting machines were on the right, cardio equipment towards the back wall opposite to Steve. A standard issue boxing ring and a larger arena of floor mats directly below where the super solider was. The walls were decorated with targets, the painted walls behind them chipped and prodded by missed shots, adding a used and yet homely feel to the room. There were a lot of memories for a lot of people down there.

    Steve’s eyes were tracking the only movement coming from the gym floor below him when company joined him in his quiet spectating. Clint only nodded in acknowledgement when he also leant his body on the barrier, his eyes joining Steve’s in tracking the fight below. Yelena and Sonya were brawling on the mats spread out on the floor. The blonde had stormed downstairs, barking something at her fellow widow in Russian and this is where the two had ended up.

    Sonya, her raven-black hair pulled back into a tight ponytail, a change from her usual braid, glistened with sweat as she danced around her opponent. Her muscles, sculpted through relentless training, rippled with each powerful movement.

    Steve had an idea of how powerful a black widow assassin was, but watching two of them battle one another, that was something else.

    Yelena circled her. Both fighters knew each other well, having trained together for years. They shared a nod, acknowledging the camaraderie that comes from pushing each other to their limits.

    The two women locked eyes, and the gym faded away from Steve completely. It was just them and the primal rhythm of their movements. Sonya lunged forward with a quick combination, but Yelena deftly slipped the punches, her footwork evoking the grace of a dancer.

    The sound of leather meeting leather echoed through the gym as Sonya retaliated with a powerful left hook. Yelena, undeterred, countered with a series of jabs, aiming to break through Sonya’s quickly put-up defence. The intensity of their exchanges showcased the years of training and the raw yet efficient methods they had been taught. The relentless dance of skill, strategy, and power continued for well over 10 minutes. The assassins pushing themselves to the limits, testing their endurance and refining their techniques.

    Yelena flurried a high kick to Sonya’s shoulder, the fellow widow anticipating the movement and ducking. This only allowed Yelena to mount her shoulders, twisting and flinging Sonya over so she landed on her back with a thump. Steve watched as the blonde smirked as she found herself in a position of victory. She helped Sonya up, their respect for each other evident in the shared glint of exhaustion and satisfaction.

    Steve was sure they could’ve done that all day.

    “I’m glad that wasn’t me this time.” Clint muttered beside him as they watched the two widows chat down below.

    Steve turned and smirked at the archer a little.

    “She threw you like that?”

    “Nat did too. It’s becoming a pattern.” The archer sighed sounding annoyed, but Steve could see the amusement in his eyes.

    “She’s good. Dare I sa-“ “Don’t say what I think you’re about to say.”

    Steve opened his mouth to respond but Clint spoke again.

    “I’m not saying I don’t agree, but Nat could be anywhere, and we’d never hear the end of it.” He mumbled quietly, paranoid of a certain earwigging redhead.

    Steve chuckled quietly thinking about Natasha’s overly competitive spirit. He wondered if Yelena shared the same trait, looking down at the two women in the gym and seeing the smirk on the blonde’s face, he could only theorise in the affirmative. “Pretty impressive, aren’t they?” Clint spoke louder this time, knocking Steve from his thoughts.

    “Something like that.” The super solider agreed.

    Yelena and Sonya were still down below, still trading punches, but this time they seemed to be verbal. Their gossipy tones ringing around, in Russian nevertheless, but Steve saw the small smile on Clint’s face when Yelena burst out laughing at something Sonya had said. It was nice to see Natasha’s sister in a different light than what they had been shown by the blonde. After all, one tense conversation when she had arrived had not left them with much of an idea of who their friend’s sibling truly was and the redhead hadn’t said much more than the blonde had. Steve knew he knew some of their story and had more insight than most into Nat’s life, but he knew Clint had a much clearer idea of who Yelena was. “She smiles then?” Steve asked simply, nodding in the direction of Yelena when Clint cast him a confused look.

    “That’s only the second time I’ve seen it.” He shrugged.

    “She reminds me so much of Natasha and I don’t even know her.” Steve continued his musing out loud.

    Clint let out a small chuckle.

    “Don’t let her hear you say that.” He was shaking his head slightly when Steve turned to him. “Why?”

    “Hates being compared to her sister.”

    Was all Clint managed to say before Laura came hurtling down the stairs. “Kate’s awake.”

    Footsteps sounded from the kitchen, bringing the rooms occupants out of their trance at Laura’s words. The older woman had left, hurtling back up the stairs but Clint and Steve had just paused. They would finally get their tale from the other night as Sonya and Yelena had refused to say anything without Kate being there too.

    “I’ll tell Yelena.” Natasha spoke from the doorway before disappearing from view.

    “You do not have to stay Sonya. I am fine.” Yelena grimaced as she wiped the blood from her lip where one of Sonya’s punches had made her lip catch her tooth.

    Sonya just rolled her eyes.

    “I am not staying for you.” She wiggled her eyebrows at the blonde before discreetly casting her eyes up towards where Barton and Steve Rogers were watching them. Yelena fake barfed before Sonya lightly punched her arm.

    “I am only kidding. I would not take Natasha’s man.”

    “What?” Yelena exclaimed.

    “However, there is a certain brunette in the building who does take my fancy.” Sonya ignored Yelena’s hurried question in favour of her teasing.

    The blonde scowled, before casting a perfectly neutral face over her features. “Kate Bishop is free to sleep with whoever she likes.”

    “Good for her. Now what about Laura Barton. How easy is her husband to take down?” Sonya questioned so casually that Yelena couldn’t hold back her laughter. “Look at him.” Yelena deadpanned.

    Sonya snuck a glance at the archer above but found his body was turned to the side so she wouldn’t have seen him looking anyways.

    “Oh Laura Barton. Where are you?” Sonya sung as she turned back to Yelena and headed towards the gym doors skipping.

    The blonde laughed again, watching her friend skip away, when suddenly the gym doors opened, revealing her sister. Yelena scoffed to herself, of course Natasha had to come and ruin her perfectly content afternoon. She planned to ignore her, bending down to pick up her towel and heading after Sonya when her westernised accent filled the room. “Kate’s awake.”

    Yelena shoved past her sister and Sonya who both stood in the doorway and took the three flights of stairs two steps at a time. By the time she got to the corridor of the recovery room, Clint and Steve were stood by the rooms window, looking on as Laura Barton fussed over the brunette. Fury was leaning against the wall on the opposite wall, his head slowly turning to the blonde as her footsteps approached. Sonya and Natasha soon sounded behind her, their casual chatter filling the corridor and turning the other two men’s heads in their direction also.

    Yelena stopped in the middle of the corridor, facing the three men as Sonya and Natasha came up behind her. The redhead joined Fury on leaning against the wall, sharing a few words with the man whilst Sonya waltzed right into Kate’s room. She watched her friend introduce herself as a friend of Yelena’s and the blonde held back a snort at the look on Kate’s face.

    “Huh. I didn’t realise she had any.” Yelena read Kate’s lips as she responded, making Yelena roll her eyes.

    It was at this moment Sonya opened the door and stuck her head out.

    “Are you not going to come and defend your honour?” The dark-haired woman smirked. Yelena watched Kate’s head twizzle round trying to see her as if she had x-ray vision. The window of the room was one way. You could see from the outside in but not vice-versa, which the blonde thought was a little creepy but who was she to judge. She’d done worse. When the blonde met Sonya’s eyes again, she did not miss the mirth swimming in them. “Chcę, żebyś tam był, kiedy zapytam Kate Bishop, czy się przytulany.” Sonya teased in Polish. The one language the two of them spoke that the rest in the room did not. The blonde just huffed before barging her shoulder into her friends as she walked into the room. Laura Barton sending her a kind smile as she departed, freeing the seat on the left side of Kate’s bed for her, a tray of clean bandages open on the chair of the opposing side. When she finally made eye contact with Kate, the brunette didn’t say anything, but Yelena saw the sigh that left her body along with the tension in her shoulders.

    Yelena realised her presence brought Kate comfort and she didn’t know what to do with that information.

    Shaking her head lightly, she propped herself on the side of Kate’s bed, her hip by Kate’s. As soon as she sat herself down, she rolled her eyes at Kate before tilting her head back a smidgen.

    “You can go Sonya.” The blonde drawled, waiting a moment before she turned her head round to look at her fellow widow.

    Sonya pouted her lips, before turning her gaze to Kate and making puppy dog eyes. Yelena could tell Kate was about to open her mouth so held up a finger to the brunette without turning to look at her.

    “Sonya.”

    “You’re so booorring Tsarina.” The dark-haired woman huffed before exiting the room, shutting the door behind her.

    “She seems nice.” Kate said.

    “She’s annoying.” Yelena muttered as she turned back to Kate.

    The brunette just sent her a weak smile before laying her head back once more and closing her eyes. Yelena shuffled herself back on the bed a little, her hip now touching Kate’s. The blonde didn’t miss the twitch of Kate’s lip threatening to break into a smile. “How are you feeling маленький ястреб?” She said softly, her voice betraying the emotions she’d been trying to contain.

    Kate’s eyes, though tired opened and held their usual spark of resilience. "Like I've been hit by a truck," she admitted, her voice raspy from disuse. "But I'm alive. Guess it comes with the territory." She mumbled the last part as if she was afraid Yelena would berate her for it. “Truck is not bad. If you had said train, I would’ve been concerned.” Yelena said, her voice still softer than she’d like.

    Kate’s brows furrowed.

    “I don’t know if I should question what you mean by that or if I should be insulted that insinuates you weren’t concerned about me having a knife in my stomach in the first place.” Yelena couldn’t fight the smile that the brunette’s familiar demeanour made burst out across her face.

    “You were not going to die Kate Bishop. You are too stubborn for that.” “I’d say you’re wrong… about the stubborn part… but we both know you’re right. However, the dying part I want to come back to. Laura said it was close.” Kate’s eyes had grown serious now and Yelena stopped her teasing.

    “You lost a lot of blood. You’re going to have to throw out your jacket.” The blonde said shrugging, her eyes roaming Kate’s face, lingering on the small cuts littered across it. Even though the blonde kept her tone light and made a humorous comment about the brunette’s jacket, Kate saw right through her.

    “I’m sorry I scared you.” The younger woman said, her voice quieter now. Yelena barked out a small laugh as if Kate was being absurd, but it didn’t last long. Kate began to move and shuffled herself to sit up more.

    Yelena’s hands were on her immediately, bringing the bed up into a position where she could sit up but whilst leaning back slightly so her stitches were not crumpled over. When the brunette was situated, she released a sigh, the energy she had just extorted being exhausting due to her stab wound. Yelena moved to bring her arms away from where they were resting on top of Kate’s forearms, but the brunette beat her to it and squeezed the underneath of her own tightly, not letting go.

    “Yelena.”

    The blonde moved her gaze back to Kate’s eyes, her blue delving into Yelena’s green. “I am not scared of anything Kate Bishop.” She forced out another chuckle. “I’m sorry I scared you.” Kate whispered, the break in her voice willing down Yelena’s defences as if they were a banana being mashed with a fork.

    Yelena tilted her head up to the ceiling, her lungs taking a deep breath before exhaling it out once more. The blonde willing the emotion welling up in her eyes to disappear. When it didn’t go, Yelena reminded herself of what she had been telling her mind since she made the decision not to kill Clint.

    It’s okay to care, Yelena. It’s okay to want things.

    And with that swimming through her mind, the blonde brought her head back down and moved forwards to rest her forehead against Kate’s shoulder. She felt Kate’s reaction of being slightly taken aback but the brunette soon brought an arm up to run her fingers through the end of the blonde’s hair, in its most knotty form, still in its two ponytails, one on top of the other, after brawling with Sonya.

    The usually chatty Kate Bishop must’ve needed the embrace as much as she did. Yelena’s mind seemed to calm as she turned her head and pressed her cheek against the brunette’s collarbone, the low thud of her heartbeat pulsing down to her ear drum. The thought of this moment being seen by the others in the compound didn’t even cross her mind as the subtle pressure of Kate’s other hand arrived on the side of her torso, drawing small patterns up and down her side.

    Yelena was quickly learning that the sensation of physical touch was a type of magic that could not be rivalled by whatever witches and sorcerers her sister was friends with. It spoke volumes for Yelena where her words faltered and even for Kate, who was an expert at saying a lot of words rather quickly, it acted as another language for a different type of expression. The blonde’s newfound vulnerability would have once been met with great judgement and a violent hand to rid of it but since she had thrown a certain brunette off a roof, it had been met with understanding and not one lingering sense of judgement.

    Yelena cast her mind back to all the times she’d been close to Kate. The simple act of skin-to- skin contact had become an anchor for the pair of them when life sent challenges and uncertainties there way, which seemed to be all the time at the current moment. And yet the sneaky thought came into Yelena’s mind that she would take all the shit in the world if she could just have more quiet moments with Kate, or even loud ones too.

    After all, listening to Kate’s rambles was pretty quickly becoming one of the blonde’s favourite pastimes.

    The blonde’s train of thought was interrupted when Kate’s fingers started tapping on her upper back, having moved out of her hair. Yelena brought her head back slightly, meeting Kate’s eyes. She didn’t even need to prompt Kate to ask her question. “Can you tell me what happened? Cause it’s all a bit fuzzy for me after, you know, I got a butcher’s knife in my gut.” Kate rambled out; her hand having fallen to sit on Yelena’s hip. The brunette’s voice sounded rough and raspy, with the archer wincing every now and then when she would speak.

    “Are you hungry?”

    “That wasn’t my question.”

    “Well, it was mine. Kate Bishop. I am giving you an excuse to get out of this room and to ride in the great chariot known as The Wheelchair.”

    It was Kate’s turn to roll her eyes as the blonde stood up and placed her hands on her hips. The brunette did take the hand offered to her and as slowly as the two women had ever moved did Kate eventually end up sat in a place that wasn’t the bed.

    “This food better be good.” Kate mumbled as Yelena draped a blanket around the brunette, so it covered her whole torso.

    The blonde rested her hands on the handles of the chair as she bend down to whisper in Kate’s ear.

    “You know I am a great cook мой маленький ястреб. Besides I’m just using your stomach as an excuse to only have to tell the tale once.”

    Yelena stood herself back up straight as the door swung open by a smirking Sonya’s hand. “Am I always just going to be a means to an end with you?” Kate asked exasperatedly, her joking evident to Yelena.

    The blonde chuckled and shook her head as she watched Sonya’s face light up even more. She opened her mouth to respond but her friend beat her too it.

    “Every story has to have a great climax.”

    Yelena could not help but snort and shake her head.

    “I feel like I’m missing something.” Kate mumbled from in front of the blonde, making Sonya die of laughter even more.

    “Хороший оргазм - это то, чем вы оба являетесь отсутствующий.” The dark-haired woman mumbled, her voice quiet enough the Russian speakers in the corridor could not hear her.

    Yelena slapped her arm anyway.
