    hope y’all enjoy and lemme know your thoughts :)

    See the end of the chapter for more notes “None of it makes sense. What do the Russians want with me?” Kate asked, her eyes focused on Sonya, who was sat on the couch across from the brunette.

    She had just finished recalling what she remembered from her encounter with Kingpin and was desperate for someone else’s thoughts on the matter besides her own. She hadn’t even heard Yelena’s opinion as the blonde had insisted that she tell the group what she experienced first, before her and Sonya told their side.

    “Kingpin hates you. Russian’s work with Kingpin. Russian’s hate you.” Natasha bluntly shrugged.

    “No. No. For once, she is right. It does not make sense.” Yelena opposed from Kate’s right. “Okay rude.” The brunette mumbled under her breath.

    Yelena fought to hold her smirk back at Kate’s reaction, hitting her foot into the brunettes instead. This turned Kate’s head to her in a questioning glance, but the blonde just kept facing forward. When Kate huffed and turned her attention away from her, she smirked again. Clint and Laura were sat on the couch with Sonya, the man of the three on the right, with Laura in the middle. Steve sat next to Kate, sandwiching her between a Black Widow and Captain America which only Kate could’ve found more exhilarating than intimidating, especially when Natasha was in the armchair on the other side of Steve. Fury, her mirror on the other side of the group.

    “How global is the Bishop Security Database?” Yelena suddenly snapped her head to face Kate who just shrugged.

    “Global.”

    “Like Russia global?”

    “Its global Yelena. Last time I checked, Russia is on the globe.” Kate shrugged again, not really sure what the blonde was getting at.

    Yelena reached for Kate’s phone which sat in her lap, careful not to hit the brunette’s wound. The brunette’s back was propped up with an abundance of cushions just so she could sit comfortably on the couch without risking the health of her stitches. The blonde logged onto the database through Kate’s login, recounting the numbers beside the marks the super soldiers bore the previous night.

    The room waited as Yelena typed ferociously on the device, the only sound being her fingertips hitting the screen, and when the phone was placed on the coffee table with a thump, they waited with baited breaths.

    “Your database is shit.” She deadpanned to Kate.

    Kate just shrugged once again, tipping her head back to lay on the mountain of pillows behind her.

    “Ни в одной базе данных не будет аккаунтов российских суперсолдат, о существовании которых даже мы не знали до вчерашнего вечера, Елена.” Sonya said lowly. Her comment perked up the ears of Nat, Clint and Laura who’s heads all swivelled between the two widows.

    “What?” Natasha’s question was loud, directed at her sister.

    Yelena just sighed and sent a glare Sonya’s way, before hitting Kate’s thigh gently with one hand to make sure she was still awake. The brunette lifted her head up and met Yelena’s eyes before the blonde refaced the room and started talking.

    “They were not just Russian thugs. They hit hard and took ages to kill.” The blonde emphasised before continuing, “They carried Soviet Slugs an-“ “No rifling.” Natasha mumbled loud enough for the whole room to hear.

    “And bore the mark of the KGB. There were numbers beside the marks. New man, different number. They were labelled…accounted for.”

    “Untraced Russian super soldiers?” Steve questioned, earning a nod from Sonya. “Whilst all of you who were here during the snap either went on a murderous rampage or were still in high school, darker corners of the world took advantage of the situation. With half the population missing, those in desire for power took their chance.” Sonya stood up as she spoke, moving behind the couch she was sat on and started slowly pacing. “World governments were in a frenzy. Presidents had vanished, councillors, border control, people of interest, all gone in split second. The parts that were still working tried to band together to take a hold of the good left in the world. Turn a bad situation into a tactical advantage. Rumours were flying that if Thanos had only wiped-out half of Earth, we’d have an easier time protecting those who were left behind. More resources, more land and plenty of money left lying around without a legal holders.”

    “None of this is news.” Fury spoke when Sonya paused.

    “Let her speak.” Clint muttered shortly.

    “But when it was public knowledge that it was not just Earth affected, some of the less secure lost their heads. Old alliances shattered - criminal gangs, tribes. Decades of progress were thrown away as quick as Thanos’ snap because people were scared. Even Earth’s protectors were not an exception to the rest of the world, with only a handful of you surviving and those of you that did, well, scattered.

    The Russian’s wanted to take advantage of this. Strike the rest of the world when it’s at its weakest and they’ll have no choice to comply. The ideas of Hydra never truly died in the North. After all, Hydra was founded on the belief that humanity could not be trusted with its own freedom. Thanos however, found a solution to their one problem. Humanity once resisted when freedom was restricted, but they could not fight against people turning to dust. There was no tangible solution.

    In Russia, Hydra was never a parasite. It was a culture. Even today, its beliefs are prominently valued in the most Northern territories. Government programmes like The Red Room and The Winter Solider prove that. For 70 years, undercover operations have been secretly reaping war without revealing a source. Some of us in this room are living proof.” Sonya took a moment for her words to sink in, eyes meeting with those sat around the room. “After you took down Project Insight and freed Зимний солдат in 2014,” She continued, making eye contact with Nat and then Steve, “Russia retreated back to their old methods. They had become too exposed. They began crawling back into the shadows, striking in secret. The Red Room still existed and so did many more methods like it. When Thanos snapped his fingers, Earth encountered a power surge. There were rumblings amongst the intelligence community that Russian scientists wanted to harvest it and pour it into something else. Make the bad into good. They thought it would obtain them global support. This was their way in to taking control of Earth. Thanos may have taken half the universe’s freedom for what he believed was a good cause, but he, how do you say it in English, облажался?” “Fucked himself over?” Nat suggested, earning a grin and a pointer finger from Sonya. “Да. He gave temptation. He made people greedy.”

    “Can we cut a long story short?” Fury questioned.

    “For decades, Russia only ever had one known super solider. Красный Страж.” Sonya said with a smirk, earning groans from Natasha and Yelena. The rest of the room’s occupants shared confused glances at the sister’s reactions.

    “Then Зимний солдат became more widely known and less of a ghost. Although, it was never publicly confirmed he was of Soviet Property. We in this room, however, know this to be true. When half the world disappeared, there were rumours of a new superpower in Russia. There were whispers for a while, a few bombings in northern cities, threats placed on government heads, but nothing was ever carried out. The widow network did some snooping and turns out they go by the name, Lufuthai, which roughly translates to ‘War Folk’. It is believed they were created with the power harnessed from The Snap.” Sonya clapped her hands together, bowed slightly before throwing herself back into her seat besides Laura. The room was deathly silent.

    “You expect us to believe that Russian scientists somehow harnessed the cosmic energy of the infinity stones without anyone noticing, and transferred this into humans, creating something similar to that of a super solider serum.” Fury all but spat. Sonya shrugged.

    “And why should we believe you?”

    “Cause we’re the only lead you’ve got.” Yelena flatly spoke, her face blank. “This is crazy.” Laura said quietly, her head in her hands.

    “I will not risk open war with Russia. Not for the sake of one kid.” Fury argued, his voice however somewhat steady.

    “Open war is upon us whether you’d risk it or not.” Steve spoke calmly, looking up from his lap, “They made the first move years ago, we’ve just been blind to it. We’ve been playing their game like pawns on a chessboard.”

    “How’d you mean?” Clint asked.

    “Disbanding the Avengers. The Blip. Disbanding the Avengers again. They made themselves stronger to become the world’s leader and when that didn’t pan out, they bet on a second head.”

    “You’re trying to tell me they had a Plan B and it just happened to play out exactly how they wanted it too?” Nat spoke up.

    “Think about it Nat. They hope on us cutting the head off the snake. Thanos is gone. Bad news for them since everyone came back… but is it? Cut the head off one snake and…” “Two more shall take its place.” The redhead was thrown back into Arnim Zola’s brain. “They got rid of Thanos and then us, just by happen chance and what did they gain? Undercover soldiers around the globe; a lot of people relocated during and after the snap. It’s not unusual for apartment buildings around the world to have ten plus nationalities living in them at one time nowadays. That gives them the element of surprise and freedom of operations. Most of us moved away from New York, that gives Fisk a wider berth and less concern of his dealings being interrupted by one of us. More dealings go down, more people involved, more money made.” Steve listed off on his fingers.

    “Still doesn’t fully explain what they want with Kate. If they have money, it’s not that. If the Russians have the technology to harness energy from a big purple goblin snapping his fingers, then I’m sure они могут развить то, что сделал Дерек Бишоп. Take those two options out and it leaves what exactly?” Clint proposed to the room, saying the part about Kate’s dad being involved in a language the brunette didn’t understand. “Her devilishly good looks?” Sonya broke the silent moment, earning a few snickers from around the room.

    “She’s my new favourite.” Kate wacked the back of her left hand into the side of Yelena’s arm.

    The blonde just rolled her eyes at the brunette, the furrow between Yelena’s brows not disappearing even in the moment of levity.

    The room fell into a hushed silence, no one having anything more to add to the number of revelations that hung in the air. Faces buried in hands, eyes wide in silent conversation, a collective gasp withheld from escaping from stunned lips.

    A myriad of emotions swirled beneath the surface of Kate’s skull - confusion, disbelief, and a tinge of vulnerability. It was as if the very foundations of her reality had been uprooted like a diseased tree, leaving herself and everyone present grappling with the implications of what Sonya had just disclosed.

    Her blue eyes darted around the room, hopeful in seeking confirmation or perhaps reassurance from others who wore the same expression of incredulity. Conversations that had once filled the space now lay suspended, replaced by an unspoken understanding that a tumultuous Christmas had turned into a cold war.

    The silence, though heavy, spoke volumes.

    It was a pregnant pause, a moment of collective introspection where Kate’s mind raced with an overwhelming number of thoughts about what was to come. But another thought came to her mind with a greater importance.

    “Kingpin did mention one other thing, which in all fairness I don’t think you can get mad at me for forgetting about up until this point because, well, given the circumstances I was a bit out of it and high on low blood pressure. Ha. That’s funny. High on low. No? Okay wel-“ “Kate.”

    “Right. Get to the point. Got it.” Kate saluted Steve, who was just shaking his head with a small smile.

    When Kate did in fact, not get to the point, just freezing after dropping her hand from her salute, Yelena gently hit her thigh, bringing her back to the world of the living. “It doesn’t make any sense unless it was you.” Kate turned her head, so she was directly facing Yelena, thinking out loud.

    The blonde could see the cogs whirring in Kate’s head as the brunette tried to figure out whatever secret she was sat on before she shared it. Yelena just titled her head in confusion and watched her favourite pair of blue eyes gloss over for a moment or two before Kate blinked.

    “He mentioned he placed a bounty on my head.”

    “What?” Clint exclaimed.

    “Reached out to all his contacts but no one would take the job because apparently someone has placed a ‘blanket of protection’ over me or something.” Kate shrugged after having brought up her fingers up from her lap, to indicate that she was in fact quoting Fisk. From connecting this to Kate’s previous comment, all the heads in the room then turned to Yelena. The blonde just held up her hands in mock surrender.

    “It was not me.”

    “It is not a far-fetched assumption. You have the means.” Natasha shrugged with a raised eyebrow.

    “I am scary.” Yelena smirked and nodded to herself, making Kate laugh softly beside her. “If it wasn’t you, then who was it?” Laura asked.

    “Someone who values Kate’s life more than their own neck.” The blonde shrugged, her nonchalant movement hiding the concern plastered in her eyes.

    “Slim pickings there.” Kate mumbled under her breath.

    Yelena was pretty sure she was the only one who heard the brunette, as no one else in the room reacted besides her. She sent a glare the archer’s way, only to be met with a face of feigned innocence as if she didn’t know what Yelena was glaring at her for.

    As evening fell, Kate carefully and yet rather painfully, trudged her way up to the rooftop stairs, wanting to spend a moment with her own thoughts. The brunette had always found that whilst perched atop a quiet rooftop, the world below seems to hush, maybe that’s just the innate Hawkeye wannabe in her though. She breathes out a heavy sigh as she sits on the ledge, her legs and a concrete wall being the only thing standing in the way of her and the floor. Looking up, the night sky stretches out and with it an endless expanse of cosmic wonders for Kate to think of.

    Carol Danvers was up there somewhere.

    Thor too.

    Maybe even Rocket.

    Kate didn’t know what to think of him.

    The cool surface of the concrete beneath her invites a moment of clarity, its cold a respite from the humidity of the crazy down below. The cityscape could be seen on the horizon, with its twinkling lights and distant echoes, making Kate realise her longing for the city centre and how, even though she was technically in her home state, it didn’t feel like home at all. The rooftop becomes her personal observatory over the next few days and nights. Kate settles herself up there after breakfast, only to return downstairs when she’s run out of snacks or needs the bathroom. She’d return down to sleep of course, although that wasn’t coming as easy for her as it used to. Kate tried to fall asleep in her own bed most nights before calling it quits and heading out to sleep on the sofa instead, or crawling into Yelena’s before the blonde made her way to bed in the early hours. The assassin hadn’t complained about her presence in her bed yet, however she was always gone by the time Kate woke up, the only evidence of her being there at all was the way she folded the duvet back once she had gotten up for the day.

    Kate practically did not see another soul for those few days, skulking around the Compound, avoiding the noisiest rooms, accidentally learning the rough schedules of everyone staying in the building. Yelena came and sat on the roof with her a couple times, no words were shared. It was as if Yelena could read her mind of wanting the quiet, just to dwell in her own thoughts and grief, but Kate would be lying if she said the blonde’s presence wasn’t a nice reminder that she wasn’t all alone.

    The sound of the city's hustle fades away after a hours, Kate’s ears trained to block the hubbub out after all these years, and then a profound stillness settles in. The air over the Hudson carries a gentle breeze, and the only sounds are the occasional rustle of leaves or the distant hum of machinery from somewhere in the Compound.

    The rooftop perch offers a sense of liberation for Kate, much more than her crumbling one on top of her apartment did. It's a reminder that, despite the intricacies of everyday life, there an entire universe waiting to be explored. Kate knows that if she had said that out loud to anyone in the Compound, they’d tell her the universe is filled with far more people who would want to kill her than be friendly but the brunette’s not all that phased by hostility anymore. She grew up in the high society of New York for goodness sake. The worries that seem so imposing from the ground are miniscule in comparison to what is floating above their heads.

    Kate doesn’t even know how that whole concept works.

    Are other galaxies and planets floating above us?

    Or are we below them?

    Or do you have to go through a door to get to other galaxies?

    The distant hum of the city below seemed muted, drowned out by the weight of her thoughts. In her hands, she clutched her phone as if it was a crumpled newspaper, the ink blurred in places from tear-stained fingers.

    The headline screamed at her from the light on the screen, ‘Tragedy Strikes Again. Bishop Security CEO, Eleanor Bishop, found dead in cell at Rucker’s Prison.’

    Taking a deep breath, Kate began scrolling through the article. Her eyes traced the words that detailed the events leading to her mother's untimely demise.

    New York City, October 27th.

    In a shocking turn of events, renowned businesswoman and CEO of Bishop Securities, Eleanor Bishop, was discovered dead in her prison cell late last week. The circumstances surrounding her unforeseen passing have been kept under lock and key by her team and no further details are to be revealed at this time.

    Eleanor Bishop, aged 54, had been serving time in the maximum-security prison following her arrest last year, after being convicted of the murder of Armand Duquesne III, a fellow wealthy socialite. The trial had been a high-profile affair, with the media closely following the case after Mrs Bishop had a public run-in with Wilson Fisk ‘Kingpin’ on Christmas Eve night.

    Reports suggest that Eleanor's sudden demise has raised questions about the circumstances of her imprisonment and the potential involvement of external forces. While initial sources point to entirely natural causes, the timing of her death amidst the Kingpin controversy has sparked conspiracy theories and suspicions among the public.

    Miss Kate Bishop, aged 23, the heiress to the Bishop fortune and a double-major at Columbia University, is now faced with the daunting task of inheriting not only her family's legacy but also the fallout from her mother's legal troubles. The Bishop estate, known for its extensive philanthropic efforts, has been a cornerstone of charitable work in New York City. Miss Bishop, known within New York’s high society for her sharp wit and exceptional archery skills, is now thrust into the dual role of defending her mother's legacy and upholding the Bishop name.

    Kate also becomes the only surviving Bishop. Derek Bishop, Kate’s father, and husband to Eleanor, passed in 2011 in the Battle of New York. The tragic loss of Derek left Eleanor as the sole caretaker of their daughter Kate and the steward of the Bishop legacy. And now the pattern repeats once more, leaving the couple’s only child to take up the position. In the aftermath of her late husband’s passing, Eleanor, who had already been an integral part of the Bishop Foundation, took on the mantle of CEO. She steered the family's philanthropic efforts to new heights, becoming a formidable force in the world of charitable giving. Eleanor's resilience and determination earned her respect within the corporate community, and she worked tirelessly to rebuild the family's fortunes while honouring Derek's memory.

    Miss Bishop has not been seen since her mother’s passing. The surviving Bishop not having been present at Bishop Security, where she works as an intern, since last Monday. Times Magazine has reached out to the Bishop’s representatives for comment.

    She read about the investigation, the unanswered questions, and the speculations surrounding Eleanor Bishop's death. The journalist had dug into every detail, attempting to unveil a truth that had remained elusive. Kate clenched her jaw, anger and frustration welling up within her. The public scrutiny was one thing, but the unresolved mystery of her mother's death gnawed at her soul.

    It wasn't just the public scrutiny that irked her; it was the realization that her parents, once beacons of inspiration for her, were now entangled in a web of controversy and scandal. The legacy she had cherished, the memory of her mother and of her father, seemed tainted and marred by secrets.

    The brunette felt an overwhelming sense of anger not just at the circumstances that led to Eleanor's demise but at the choices both her parents had made. The ideals of heroism that had defined her upbringing now seemed like a façade, and Kate struggled to reconcile the images of her parents as perpetrators.

    As the wind whispered through the silent night, Kate's gaze remained fixed on the city below. The glow of the moon reflected the conflict within her – the anger at the choices her parents had made, the frustration at the tarnishing of their legacy, and the determination to unravel the truth, no matter how painful it might be. The rooftop offered solace, but the storm of emotions within Kate was far from settled.

    On her third day of solitude, she was not so alone.

    She heard his footsteps before she saw him. His usual tread sounding out rather loudly on the gravel floor of the roof. When she knew he was pretty close, the brunette turned her head around to watch him approach.

    Her mentor was carrying a thick blanket under one armpit, whilst his hands were occupied with two thermos flasks. He smiled awkwardly as she caught his eye, and silently handed her one of the flasks as he got within arm’s length.

    “Can I join you?”

    “S’pose so.”

    Clint huffed at her response, placing his flask down on the ledge, before sliding his legs over to sit on it like Kate. Once he was settled, he opened the blanket and threw it round the brunette’s shoulders as well as his own, before picking up his flask again. The pair of archers were quiet for a few moments.

    “I don’t thin- I- I wasn’t actually going to jump off that roof.” Kate mumbled quietly, deciding to bite the bullet and go straight to the hard stuff.

    Clint didn’t say a word, nor did he look at her. His eyes firmly fixed on where the horizon met the city.

    “I was drowning.” Kate’s voice broke.

    Clint broke out of his stare, immediately bringing an arm around the brunette, tugging her into his side.

    “Everyone was moving on, had something going for them and I-I was barely above the surface.”

    “You’re gonna have to elaborate kiddo.”

    “I almost got folded like a deckchair by Kingpin, then imprisoned my own mother, dropped out of college, took over the family business which I hate and then Mom got murdered which is just great because now I’m the sole owner of her dodgy company and have to plan her funeral and carry out her will and do all of this whilst trying not to get my neck snapped by some angry Russians and a big man in a suit.” Kate said, throwing her arms up in the air, wincing at the pain that erupted from her abdomen. “Oh, and I got stabbed.” Tears now flowed freely from her eyes, breaking the seal that had been firmly in place since Eleanor’s passing. Clint took his arm not around the brunette and gathered Kate’s hands together on her lap, holding them in his. Kate’s chest was rapidly breathing, her heart rate rampant.

    “Katie. Hey. Kid, look at me.”

    Kate’s head turned to face her mentor slowly, the pain in her face making Clint’s heart break. “Why didn’t you call? I’d been on the first plane out.” He said whilst stroking tears from off her cheeks with his thumb.

    “You have three kids who’ve already missed you for long enough. I know what it’s like to grow up without a dad Clint…” Kate half-heartedly shrugged, her voice wavering. “The kids would’ve shoved me out the door if they knew you needed me, and I hadn’t gone. They adore you, Kate.”

    “That’s because they’re too kind, just like their mom. I’m not your responsibility Clint. You guys don’t owe me anything.”

    “If you had called and say… Laura’s sister had asked me where I was off to? Do you know what I’d have said?”

    Kate just shrugged.

    “I’d have said, my kid needs me. Simple as that.”

    “Clint…” Kate said shakily, her tears back in full force.

    “I mean Laura would’ve had to clear up any confusion about timelines and parentage and whatever, you get the point.” Clint said nonchalantly, waving his hand around as if it was to be no bother.

    Kate went to open her mouth, but the older man cut her off with a look. “Don’t even try to argue it kid. You’re family. Laura’s probably ready to sign adoption papers.” He threw his hands up in exasperation, but Kate saw the fondness in the action. “So, no more hanging off the ledges of roofs, okay?”

    “What about for missions? And stakeouts? Oh, and for spying.” Kate listed. “Who are you spyi- actually you know what? I don’t want to know.” Clint said shaking his head. “Now can we please go downstairs so you can say a proper hello to my wife before she storms up here and throws you off the roof herself.” He continued, standing up collecting their empty cups and rolling up the blanket before offering Kate a hand. Kate hesitated for a moment, taking one last look at the view before clutching Clint’s hand and swinging her legs over the ledge and back to the solid ground of the roof. They walked in silence for a moment, making their way down the first flight of stairs, Kate wincing at each step, when Clint spoke again.

    “And maybe hesitate a bit of caution next time before making friends with someone who wanted to kill you a week before.” He rolled his eyes as they reached the top of the next flight of stairs.

    Kate huffed before a smirk took over her face.

    “Technically she never wanted to kill me. Looking back, we had a lot more fun than we should’ve done given the situation.”

    “I think I need to get a spanner in that brain of yours and see if you’ve got a screw loose.” Clint flicked her in the side of her head.

    Chapter 13

    Chapter Notes surprise!

    a second chapter this week woohoo! those of you who follow me on tumblr would've known this was coming but for the rest of y'all, here it is!

    my tumblr: https://www.tumblr.com/thebestpeopleinlifearefreefic Natasha watched from the couch as Kate and Clint walked into the kitchen. Kate’s eyes were red and puffy, and Clint seemed reluctant to move far from the girl. They wandered up to the kitchen island slowly, Yelena’s head spinning around from the stove, catching Laura’s attention who also turned on the spot. Nat didn’t think she’d ever seen Laura smile so wide as when she laid eyes on Kate, her expression slightly faltering when she noticed that Kate had been crying.

    “Come here sweetheart.” She opened her arms when she rounded the island. Kate didn’t waste a second, launching herself into Laura’s arms, which squeezed the brunette tightly. The two women stayed like that for a good while, the redhead watching as Laura spoke into the brunette’s hair.

    Wanting to give them the privacy they deserved, Nat turned her attention back to the other side of the island where Yelena stood. The blonde was stood side on towards the stove, absentmindedly stirring the contents of the pan whilst she watched the embrace. The redhead could see her sisters concern for the younger Hawkeye in the furrow of her brow and in the way she was discreetly biting the inside of her cheek.

    Natasha knew her sister better than the blonde thought she did.

    Clint had pulled out a stool from the island, his back now to Natasha. He must’ve said something to Yelena in which she replied with a short reply. It must’ve been in Russian because Nat couldn’t make out what the blonde had said. She’d always found Russian much harder to lip read than English.

    When Laura finally let Kate go, she pulled out a stool next to her husband. Nat was expecting Kate to join the pair of them but instead the brunette went and joined her sister by the stove. “No Kate Bishop. Shoo.” She made out Yelena’s voice over the low chatter of Steve and Fury beside her.

    “I was only going to offer my help.”

    “Kate. You sent an onion flying across your apartment trying to cut it. You would be more of a hindrance than a help.” The blonde reached a hand up to Kate’s cheek, gently patting it twice.

    The brunette only pouted in response.

    “Besides all this galivanting on rooftops has probably not helped this heal. Go sit.” The blonde pointed to Kate’s stomach before turning her pointed finger in Natasha’s direction. Kate grumbled something under her breath before her shoulders sagged slightly. “Now маленький ястреб.” Yelena said sternly this time, turning her full attention back to her cooking to signify the end of the conversation.

    Natasha could see Clint and Laura’s shoulders jostling up and down ever so slightly, indicating their amusement to the redhead. She turned her attention away from the couple when Kate came closer in her line of sight. Nat flashed her a small smile as she walked into the living area and slumped painfully into the armchair on Nat’s left. “What’s моя сестра cooking then Bishop?” Nat asked the brunette who had thrown her head backwards and shut her eyes.

    Kate’s head jumped back up again at the redhead’s voice. Natasha could see it in her face that she hadn’t expected a conversation to take place between them.

    “Something spicy probably.” The brunette said quietly, turning her head back towards the kitchen for a moment.

    “How mad is she at me? On a scale? 1-10?” Nat whispered, her eyes flicking between the brunette and the back of her sister’s head.

    “Uhhhh I don’t know.”

    Nat studied her with a look that said she knew otherwise.

    “I-I seriously don’t. I promise y-you. But if I did which I don’t but if I di-did I wouldn’t tell you because that’s not any of my business really and its Yelena’s choice if she wants to talk to you and I-I’d try really hard to keep my mouth shut but you probably also have super-secret powers which would make me spill my guts and I’m known to run my mouth quite a lot s-so, oh wait, I probably shouldn’t have told you that, dammit.” Kate nervously rambled. “С какой стати Елена с тобой подружилась?”

    “I really need to learn Russian.” Nat’s response was the last straw for the brunette, her head flying back again and her eyes shutting.

    “You are something else, Bishop.”

    “I’m going to take that as a compliment. I think?” Kate responded from where she was, not bothering to bring her head back up.

    Nat just snorted in response before turning away from the brunette and tuning back into Steve and Fury’s conversation.

    Yelena sighed as she looked down at the simmering pot on top of the stove. Clint Barton’s eyes were baring down the back of her neck.

    Could she not get a moments peace in this place?

    The blonde turned around, first noticing the apologetic smile on Laura Barton’s face. The blonde didn’t acknowledge it outwardly but maybe Laura’s awareness of her husband’s doing amused her.

    “What Barton?” She huffed as she met his eyes.

    “Thank you.”

    “I do not know why you keep thanking me, but I would like it to stop.” The blonde said flatly as she rested a palm on the island, leaning her body weight onto that arm. “For saving Kate’s life.”

    “I did not save her life. She was not going to jump.” Yelena shrugged before heading to turn back around.

    A small presence on her hand stopped her. Yelena’s whole body tensed. “How’d you know?”

    “I have been trained to read body language and facial expressions since I was 6. She was not going to jump and… she told you as much…” Yelena added on as she studied Clint’s eyes. “I swear you and your sister are magic in some way.” He mumbled annoyed as he pulled his hand back.

    Yelena smirked.

    “Thank you for being around for her these past months honey. She might have jumped if you hadn’t been.” Laura said softly.

    “You do not have to thank me for being Kate Bishop’s friend.” The blonde turned back to the stove.

    “I am not. I am thanking you for giving her something to live for.”

    “I do not understand why you are using this saying.” Yelena turned her head slightly to see Laura’s expression.

    “You will someday.” Laura’s eyes sparkled as she stood up. “I’ve got the rest of this sweetheart.” She said as she shooed Yelena out of the kitchen.

    Yelena went gladly to get herself out of that rather confusing conversation, plus, she knew Clint wanted to tell his wife about his and Kate’s conversation and Yelena did not want to impose on the details when it wasn’t coming from Kate herself. The blonde wandered to where the brunette was sat, the archer slouched in the armchair with her head in a position that can’t have been comfortable. Nat turned her head slightly to see the blonde approach and shuffled down the couch to make room for her on the end closest to Kate. Yelena flashed a polite smile at her sister before shaking her head slightly and moving to stand behind the brunette who had her eyes closed.

    The blonde stood over Kate’s for a moment just studying her before letting out a huff. How is she so unaware she does not notice me here?

    “This is why you get kidnapped Kate Bishop.” She mumbled quietly to the brunette. Yelena’s eyebrows raised when Kate did not jump at the sound of her voice, only reacting to the blonde’s presence at all by the smile that came over her face.

    “I knew you were there. You aren’t a threat.”

    At this the blonde stood a little closer to the back of the armchair, her hands finding the ends of Kate’s hair. She moved her hands up a smidge, reaching just underneath the crown of the brunette’s head, combing through the strands that sat there. The unspoken intimacy in the simple act of playing with Kate’s hair struck Yelena as the archer tilted her head slightly, welcoming the affection from hands that had carried out so much violence. Sonya chose this exact moment to waltz into the room from wherever she had been. “Who’s not a threat?” She questioned as she slumped into the couch beside Natasha. “Lena.” Kate said unbothered, lazily pointing her arm up towards the blonde before dropping back down.

    “I do not know whether you should be insulted or not?” Sonya twisted her head towards the blonde.

    Yelena didn’t say anything, her eyes focused on Sonya’s neck, her hands still running through Kate’s hair out of sight from those in front of their eyes.

    “Как поживает граф Дракула?” The blonde smirked.

    Sonya only rolled her eyes before pulling down her top to uncover her collarbones as well. Yelena only rolled her eyes at her friend’s lack of shame.

    “He is good. Твоя мама звонила мне раньше.”

    “Please tell me it wasn’t in the middle o-“ “Еще две вдовы. Южный Судан. Она сказала мне, что ты не отвечаешь на ее звонки.” “I cannot go. Take Anya with you.”

    “She cannot go. Кейт прекрасно справится без тебя неделю.”

    “Take Antonia.” The blonde said bluntly, her tone final.

    Sonya only rolled her eyes at the assassin before turning her head to Nat who had been listening to the conversation intrigued.

    “How many have you freed?”

    “Not enough.” Yelena answered her sister.

    “How many are left?”

    “Too many.”

    Natasha glared at the blonde for her answer, and Yelena knew that she was biting her tongue from having an outburst at all the things she wanted to say. However, the redhead didn’t say a word more, instead wandering off into the kitchen to join Laura and Clint. “You’re telling me I’ve been gone three days, and you still haven’t sorted that?” Sonya exclaimed under her breath.

    “Melina also does still not know.” Yelena muttered quietly making Sonya burst out laughing. “Oh Tsarina! We are in trouble.”

    Laura shushes her husband as Nat approaches, flinging herself into the stool beside Clint. The couple just look at her for a moment before turning back to a different topic of conversation. It was a common habit for the two to fall into talking about the kids whenever they needed to hide what they were really talking about. They chat for a while about how the kids are and what they are getting up to with Laura’s sister, their aunt, whilst they’re away. Nat turns around several times during their whole conversation before a slight snort erupts from her chest. Laura and Clint turn to look at her confused, meeting her eyes when she turns back to face them once more. When the redhead doesn’t elaborate on what caused her amusement, Laura and Clint both turned to look through the large open doorway, revealing Kate, Yelena, and Sonya chatting.

    “What was so funny?” Clint muttered.

    “Just look.”

    Clint waits for a moment before turning around again, not noticing how Laura had already turned back to Nat with a small smile threatening to beam across her face. He watched as Sonya asked Kate a question, the brunette tilting her head to the side so she could see the dark-skinned woman without fully lifting her head. Kate’s mouth then started moving at a mile a minute, Sonya interrupting her every now and again to clarify on what the archer was saying. Knowing Kate and how her brain gets thrown around inside her skull on the daily, he could only dare to imagine what their conversation consisted of.

    It was nice to see some aspects of Kate had stayed the same.

    He then cast his eyes to the third woman of the group. Yelena Belova was still somewhat of an enigma to Clint, pretty much getting all of his information from Nat. He’d never say it to the redhead, but he had a feeling that everything she knew about the blonde was rather outdated, after all Yelena had changed a lot since she and him first met. Clint had no doubt she’d changed an awful lot since the sisters had reunited those few years ago. The blonde wasn’t participating in the conversation at all, at least not verbally. She stood behind Kate, a small smile appearing on her face at certain parts of the other’s chatter, a rare sight to see from a black widow. Clint had felt rather protective when Yelena had called him and dropped the bomb that the two were friends, feeling rather put off from the coldness he had experienced over Christmas and from the glimpse he’d gotten at the blonde’s rather intense yet withdrawn personality. She was very much like how Nat had been when she first defected from SHIELD: untrusting, solitary and above all else, wary.

    But looking at the same assassin, who had tried to kill him, now, he could not help but wonder how different the two sisters really were.

    Yelena’s hand motions caught the archer’s eye, the miniscule action not noticeable at a quick glance but after all, the three of them sat at the island had been taught to immediately see fine details. Clint knew that Nat would never be that openly intimate. A quick hug from Nat in public was an honour, let alone the uncomplicated yet layered motion of simple touches. And when Yelena finally asked Kate a question and the brunette tipped her head back to look at the blonde upside down, Clint could not explain the peculiarity of that image to himself let alone to explain it to someone else. Kate’s mouth started rambling again, Yelena’s lip quivering in her attempt to keep her expression blank. The blonde tilted her head when Kate paused, only to roll her eyes when it the chatter started again seconds later. Having known Natasha and her experience as a Black Widow for many years, he knew the pain and complications that came with starting life like she had. His time as the Ronin had solidified that understanding as his blood-filled path was too caused by being unable to control his own mind. Except his was caused by grief and rage, whilst Nat’s was as a result of brutal conditioning. They weren’t on any page fully comparable, but Nat always said Clint understood more than most.

    Natasha had always been rather cold to those she didn’t know or trust. He saw it every day with the Avengers, at the beginning anyway. She’d be the upmost professional, knew her role and did what was needed. Whilst others were sharing their life stories, telling jokes and reminiscing, Nat would keep her cards close to her chest. This became less evident over the years as she found her family within the group of heroes, but Clint knew if anyone new ever came knocking, Nat would be guarded with them for quite a while.

    This is why the sight in front of Clint’s eyes was kind of inconceivable to him. Natasha’s sister who the redhead had always pitched as the deadliest assassin in the world looked utterly content whilst chatting with his protegee.

    The blonde playing with the brunette’s hair like it was the most natural thing in the world to her.

    At that moment, Kate’s laughter echoed around the room and Yelena, with an affectionate look on her face, reached slightly higher than she had been to tuck a strand of hair back behind Kate’s ear which had come loose when the woman erupted into giggles. It was a simple gesture, yet it spoke volumes about the tenderness that existed between them and how Kate had somehow dug her way into Yelena’s heart without being thrown off another roof. Clint likes to think he knows Kate well enough to know that the two’s friendship probably hadn’t been smooth sailing. After all, Kate is rather well known for putting her foot in her mouth.

    There’s a joke in there somewhere about how that is not even able to shut Kate up. She thrives in chaos and mystery and is driven by the values drilled into her by her mother, not sticking to them but trying to do the opposite. Her ambition is unparalleled, and Clint could only guess it was fuelled out of spite. And he guesses the blonde was similar in that way. Yelena wanted to break out of the mould the Red Room trapped her in, but also not wanting to spend her life being compared to Natasha. She was strategic and clever, and unmatched in relentlessness if Clint’s bruises at Christmas were anything to go by. It had just never occurred to Clint that they would find the comfort they needed in one another. He’d gotten the impression that Yelena would steer clear of them for the rest of her life after Christmas but obviously not.

    He couldn’t argue it didn’t make sense, because it was probably the one thing that made the most sense in the past five years of his life.

    It seems as if a Black Widow is always destined to find a Hawkeye.

    “Can’t sleep маленькая сестра?” An all too familiar voice sounded from a few paces behind Yelena.

    The blonde kept her cool, not whipping her head around to face the noise which shockingly took her by surprise. At least she knew Nat had not lost her touch of sneaking around after being a poser all these years.

    Yelena just hummed in the affirmative. Nat didn’t need to know she was just wasting time, waiting for Kate to make herself comfortable in the blonde’s bed before she headed to get some sleep herself. She knew that the brunette hadn’t been sleeping well since she had made the silent decision to sleep in her own room and had even slept on the couch some nights, liking the feeling of people always being awake around her due to the compounds buzz of activity even in the early hours. Yelena also knew that Kate wouldn’t sleep on the couch if there were people sat in the living room and would crawl into Yelena’s bed instead, hence Yelena’s current position.

    Natasha took her response as an invitation to sit down. A cloaked olive branch coming from the blonde, but an olive branch, nonetheless. The two sat there for a while, the awkward silence echoing around the room. One of them had to start the conversation but neither knew what to say, so Nat decided to stick with what was easy for her.

    Teasing Yelena.

    “Mini Clint seems quite taken with you.” The redhead burst out with, leaning back in her seat, crossing her arms.

    Yelena scoffed before finally taking her eyes off the floor and turning to face her sister. “Don’t call her that.”

    “Why ever not?” Nat held back her smirk.

    “I do not like Barton.”

    “Ah, but you do like Kate.”

    “She is my friend.” Yelena nodded her head before a downcast look took over her features. Natasha furrowed her brow and slammed her lips shut before her next comment escaped from the tip of her tongue. Yelena looked back to her in the redhead’s silence, sighing when she realised her face had given away her distracted mind.

    “You want to talk about whatever is going on up there?” Nat pushed gently, pointing to the blonde’s head, when Yelena didn’t acknowledge being caught out.

    Her sisters only response was a shake of her head.

    “You should probably know something.” Nat started, not knowing why her smart mouth had decided to bring this up now when Yelena was seemingly already struggling. “Can we not do this now?” The blonde groaned, hiding her head in her hands. “I don’t have the energy to shout at you and when we do this. I would like to shout.” “Thanks for the heads-up? But it’s not about us.” The redhead started sarcastically before turning serious.

    This caught Yelena’s attention, bringing her head out of her hands before levelling her sister with a look to prompt her to continue.

    “Fury thinks Kate is involved with Kingpin.”

    “What?” The blonde shot up in her seat, no longer slouched.

    “Long story short, Kate’s mother was on SHIELD’s radar for decades because of her husband’s previous conversations he had had with the Russian military about a possible technology deal. A deal SHIELD also wanted to broker with Bishop Security. Kate’s dad then became involved with Kingpin after the deal fell through, with the Russians stating they were no longer in need of western protection systems. SHIELD investigated these claims, and thus discovered the Red Room.”

    “Your defection to SHIELD.” Yelena said, figuring out the timeline Nat was creating. The redhead nodded in confirmation before continuing.

    “Kingpin and Derek Bishop brokered a deal when Brian Bishop died, leaving Kate’s dad as CEO and with a lot more power than he had previously held. Kingpin took advantage, both of them wanting to expand their power holdings within the city, but they got cocky.” “Kate’s dad didn’t die in the Battle of New York, did he?”

    Natasha confirmed Yelena’s statement with a small shake of her head.

    “Deal with the European Mafia went south. Earned himself a bullet to the back of his head. The Chitauri were an excellent cover up.”

    Yelena got up and started pacing in front of her sister.

    “How did I not find this when I looked into the Bishop’s in the first place?” “You looked into them? Why?” Nat questioned curiously. Her interest in her sister’s new friend spiking.

    “Clint didn’t tell you?”

    “Tell me what?”

    “Eleanor Bishop is the one who wanted me to kill him.”

    The redhead’s eyes protruded so far from her skull as they widened, Yelena was almost worried they’d come rolling across the floorboards towards her.

    “Clint very conveniently left that piece of information out. The case was handed over to the CIA back in 2015. Their system makes it harder to stumble across information if you’re not actively seeking it.” Nat shrugged when she overcame her initial shock. “Mmmm. Eleanor knew then. About the true cause of death?”

    Nat nodded.

    “Nick Fury wants to believe Kate is involved with Kingpin because both of her parents were. Is h-“ “He doesn’t want to believe it. He does believe it. Both parents dead, all their worth know belongs to her. Plus, she knows New York’s rich like the back of her hand and she’s not a bad asset to have in a fight.” Natasha interrupted.

    “Это ерунда.” Yelena growled. “And he still believes it? After Fisk put a knife through her stomach?”

    Natasha just shrugged, not knowing the answer to her sister’s question. The blonde stopped pacing, as she reached the side of the room with the doorway. She turned to look at her sister.

    “You did not have to tell me. Why did you?” Yelena was hesitant in her statement. “Ты моя семья, сестренка.”

    “They are your family too. Fury is your boss.”

    “They are…” The redhead said, no room for argument in her voice.

    She paused for a moment. Yelena bowed her head, making way to head out of the door but before she could, Nat opened her mouth once more.

    “But Kate is yours.”

    Yelena whipped her head to look at the redhead once more with a look that Nat could decipher.

    “You helped me realise I could help save this family once,” The redhead gestured to the compound around them as she said this, “Kate needs you сестра. I am merely returning the favour.” Nat shrugged as the blonde kept her eyes fixed firmly on her from her position across the room.

    Natasha watched as Yelena’s hand gripped tighter where it lay on the doorframe, her knuckles getting paler by the second.

    In that moment, Yelena felt a pang of longing she hadn’t felt for her sister since the day she arrived at the compound. The walls she had built around herself, the barriers of isolation that had defined her tortured existence, began to crumble in an instant. Natasha's words, delivered with a soldiered yet motherly strength, reassured Yelena that the bonds of family extended beyond blood and shared history. The realisation crept through Yelena until it filled her up. The feeling made a shiver run down her spine. Kate, with her quirks and imperfections, had become a staple in Yelena’s life. A main character in the narrative and an unexpected connection that went beyond what she thought the confines of her dangerous profession would ever allow her.

    The blonde shook herself out of her head and nodded once at her sister in thanks. Natasha only managed to send her a small smile back before Yelena had disappeared from sight.

    Chapter 14

    please leave comments <3 See the end of the chapter for more notes Yelena turned the corner to head down the corridor to her room when she ran into Laura and Sonya in the hallway. Both women turned to face her as she approached. Laura Barton was stood in her pyjamas, leaning against the doorframe that led into her and Clint’s bedroom. Looking past Laura and into the room, she could see the couple’s suitcases packed and sat at the end of the bed. Sonya was stood in front of the woman, her sleek black bag sat at her feet. “You okay honey?” Laura asked as Yelena got about a foot away from the two, the end of her sentence finishing when she stopped beside them.

    Yelena nodded, unsure of how shaken her voice would be if she dared open her mouth. It was uncommon of the blonde to feel unsure in herself and her abilities and that shook the blonde even more. She could feel Sonya’s eyes tracing the outline of her features, definitely knowing something was up with her fellow widow. Yelena hoped her voice would stay steady, for she just wanted the attention off of her.

    “В Санкт-Петербург?” She questioned the woman with the darker complexion, nodding to her bag on the floor.

    “Да. Клинт разрешил мне взять Квинджет.” Sonya answered with a large smile directed towards Laura.

    “Повезло тебе.” Yelena answered somewhat sincerely, her distain for the Barton man becoming ever harder to maintain.

    “I will fly first to pick up Antonia and then we will head to Sudan. You are more than welcome to come.” Sonya said, her eyes flashing the offerings of an escape from the compound should she need it.

    “You just want me there because Antonia is not the most talkative.”

    Sonya groaned at Yelena’s statement, only emphasising the truth that the blonde had spoken. “If I fall asleep on the job, and never come back, you know why.” Sonya mumbled lowly. Laura chuckled at the two widows softly, making both their eyes turn to her. “Why are all widows so dramatic?” She said, fondness dripping from the voice. “Childhood trauma.”

    “Attention seeking.”

    The two widows said at the same time making Laura laugh quietly once more. “You are leaving.” Yelena then spoke directly to Laura. To her credit, the woman did not react at all to Yelena’s observation, obviously very used to Nat also seeing what most other people would usually miss.

    Laura hummed before answering.

    “Yes. My sister has been gracious enough to stay with the kids, but I cannot expect her to stay forever. I have managed to persuade Clint to come back with me, but he is reluctant to leave without Kate.”

    “She should go. It is safer for her away from the city.” Yelena agreed reluctantly not wanting Kate to leave her sight after what had happened the last time she’d left the brunette, but what she said out loud was true. “It will not be easy to convince her of this.” The blonde added as an afterthought.

    “Stubborn as anything that one.” Laura rolled her eyes, “The invite stands for you too Yelena.”

    “Thank you but n-“ “Кейт пойдет, если ты пойдешь.” Sonya cut the blonde off.

    “I am inclined to agree.” Laura shrugged, her eyes sparkling.

    Yelena only sighed before flitting her attention between the two women. They both seemed so confident in her ability to keep Kate safe when all she had done her whole life had caused pain, and now they wanted her to convince the brunette to go to Barton’s home when she’d been on rough footing with him for a little while. Yelena knew she was good at a lot of things, manipulation being one of them, but she couldn’t do that to Kate. “I’ll pass on the offer to her, but I cannot promise the answer you want. I will not force it.” Yelena gave Barton’s better half a small smile, before taking a half step closer to Sonya, squeezing the woman’s bicep before continuing her way down the corridor.

    The room was bathed in the muted glow of moonlight as Yelena entered the room, unspoken concern etched on her face as her eyes landed on the figure curled up in her bed. Kate Bishop tossed and turned restlessly, the rhythmic ticking of the clock on the wall seemed to mock the futility of the archer's attempts to find reprieve, sweat clinging to the woman’s forehead. Yelena had observed the subtle signs of Kate's inner turmoil for nights now. The rhythmic rustling of sheets through the propped open door, the occasional sighs that escaped her lips, a muted whimper joining them every now and again. Yelena could only imagine the distant gaze from her blue eyes that lingered on the ceiling. The room, with its expensive mattress and technological architecture, should have been a haven for rest, but the blonde had become a silent witness to the silent struggle playing out on Kate's face. Even being in the place of her childhood dreams could not bring peace to the brunette’s mind it seemed. The lines of exhaustion etched on Kate's face bore the toll of her recent injury and the influx of information she had received regarding the man who wanted her dead. Yelena, attuned to the nuances of her friend, felt a pang of empathy. This was the life Kate wanted to lead and she was just beginning to learn how unforgiving it was, and sleep often proved elusive, slipping through their fingers like sand. For someone who liked to sleep, the brunette had chosen the wrong business.

    Yelena debated whether to break her silence, to reach out and offer a comforting word, waking the brunette up totally or simply slip in beside her, hoping her presence alone would calm enough for Kate to drift off peacefully. The whimper that Kate let out when she rolled over once more caused her to intervene. With a silent resolve, Yelena moved from her spot and approached the bed, sliding in under the covers beside Kate.

    The brunette’s back was towards her, her hair loose and undoubtedly going to be in a whole heap of tangles when she awoke. Yelena was in a half mind to shuffle over and wrap her arms around Kate from behind to stop the brunette fretting around in her sleep. She was twitching and shaking her head as if to reject something, muttering something indecipherable under her breath. When Kate jolted, her body flinging herself over to face the blonde, Yelena made her move.

    The blonde shuffled closer to the brunette, sliding her left arm under the archer’s waist whilst using the right to slowly roll Kate over some more so half of her chest rested on the front of Yelena’s. The brunette stirred slightly at the forced movement, moving her body slightly to get comfortable in the new position. Kate ended up waking up completely as she kicked out a leg, stubbing her toe on the bed frame.

    Her head jolted up from where it had eventually landed on Yelena’s collarbone. It probably would’ve gone flying into the blonde’s chin if she didn’t have as quick reaction times as she did. The archer looked down at her foot wide eyed before exhaling rather loudly. It was when she turned back around to lie her head back down did, she notice where she was. The brunette tried to move off Yelena, simultaneously opening her mouth to probably splutter out an apology. She got a chance to do neither as the assassin beneath her kept her hand tightly gripped around Kate’s back, indicating she didn’t mind the brunette staying where she was. When Kate stubbornly didn’t lay down again, just stared at her like a fox in headlights, the blonde wanted to say something but found the lump in her throat to be suffocating. She could only nod and squeezed the part of Kate’s waist where her hand rested. The brunette only blinked. If the moment wasn’t so vulnerably intimate Yelena might’ve laughed at the look on Kate’s face, but instead she rolled her eyes so fondly she want to puke at herself and pulled Kate closer. Kate’s body followed the force, her head landing near the crook of Yelena’s neck once more. After a few moments, Yelena felt Kate relax, her body sinking into her side, and the arm that had been hesitantly laid on the assassin’s stomach was stretched over it instead to pull herself into Yelena’s side even more. Kate then nuzzled her face slightly higher, her nose burying itself into the base of the blonde’s neck.

    "Sleep now маленький ястреб.” Yelena's voice, though gentle and whispered, cut through the oppressive quiet of the room. Kate’s mouth upturned, the blonde feeling it move against her skin. The brunette hummed sleepily in return.

    Yelena let the archer’s heartbeat against her own help ground her.

    Something about Kate Bishop fascinated her so much she was actively seeking her affection. Sure, Kate seemed to need it and it seemed to help but Yelena couldn’t convince herself that her motive didn’t have some purely selfish elements within it.

    At first, Kate was just so wildly out of pocket that her presence had taken her by surprise. After living a childhood of strict routine and complex rules, the archer was the most intriguing person she had ever come across. After Yelena had left New York for the holidays she thought about the Bishop woman once or twice. You can’t blame her for that. She was stuck on her parent’s farm, and after the run up to Christmas the blonde had had. Being there was like watching paint dry. There wouldn’t have been a dull moment if Kate had been there with her. Looking back now, Yelena was sure Kate would’ve fallen over in the pig pen, and the look on the brunette’s face would’ve been enough to make her year. But now, the archer had become addicting, and Yelena couldn’t get enough. Everything she did with the woman, she enjoyed, and Yelena hates most things. Kate had this light around her which made everything seem brighter. For god’s sake, Kingpin was threatening the woman’s life and here they were cuddled up in Yelena’s bed. Maybe after all the dark the blonde had experienced in her life, a mortal man did not seem that large a threat, but normally she would be out chasing leads for days, sleeping in dingy motel rooms and hiding in the shadows. Not hiding out at the Avengers compound, laughing, and chatting with Kate’s friends and Sonya, and definitely not falling asleep with a woman in her arms. The assassin had always defined herself as a loner. Maybe it came with the territory or maybe Yelena was just one of those people who enjoyed her own company more than she cared for other people. However, now she had found a person who made her not want to be alone and maybe that is why she knew Kate, in whatever way she had not yet figured out, was different. For the first time ever, Yelena preferred someone else’s company over her own. Kate mumbled something under her breath, her deep breathing indicating she was definitely asleep. Yelena’s thoughts had been broken by the noise close to her ear so rather than going back to twisting her mind up in knots, she refocused on Kate’s heart against hers and the warmth exuding from the woman on top of her.

    All she needed was right here, encompassing her in warmth and a feeling of contentment she’d never known before.

    Yelena fell asleep.

    Sun rays crept through the curtains, casting a gentle glow around the room but also a bright beam right into Yelena’s eyeline. The woman groaned as she stirred, emerging gradually from her sleepy state. Her eyes fluttered open, after having moved her face out of the light filtering through the window. A heavy presence in her side made her look down, Kate still lay in her embrace, the same way she had fallen asleep. Yelena watched the archer's quiet expression, the anxiety of the night presently supplanted by a peaceful calm.

    What took her by surprise was that the brunette was already awake.

    The sheets, although unkempt from a night of shifting and turning from the brunette, once more wrapped around Kate like a cocoon. The brunette rested quietly on Yelena’s chest, her fingers running up and down the blonde’s side with a featherlight touch. She obviously had not realised the blonde beneath her had awoken and the simplicity of the gentle act made the blonde’s heart lurch. Never had anyone been as soft with her as Kate Bishop and she did not know how to respond.

    Hesitantly and with an uncommon delicateness, she reached the arm not wrapped around Kate up, and brushed a strand of hair away from Kate’s face. The room, already noiseless but for the cadenced breathing of its tenants, filled with a soft sigh as the brunette relaxed even deeper into the blonde’s side.

    “What time is it?” Yelena broke the silence softly, her voice just above a whisper. “Near enough 11.” Kate mumbled, her eyes still shut and body dozy.

    “We’re sleeping the whole day away.” Yelena whined, pushing her head back into the pillow with a groan. “You’re a bad influence Kate.” She whined again as Kate’s chest bounced up and down on her own as she laughed at the blonde’s complaints.

    When the brunette’s laughter stopped and gentle quiet took over the room again, the blonde let out a deep sigh. Gently rolling onto her side, bringing Kate with her, the two women now face to face. Kate flopped her head into the pillow, her forehead resting on Yelena’s collarbone, as the blonde propped herself up on one elbow. Yelena absentmindedly had thrown her arm over Kate’s waist, her hand sliding up and down the brunette’s spine, tracing over each bump.

    The fact that Yelena trusted Kate this much to be so openly affectionate made Kate swoon. A badass assassin slash super spy who could take down an entire empire with her little toe, was seemingly more than happy to waste away in bed with her, despite her fake protests. Yelena’s gentle touches down her back soon trailed lower, tracing over toned muscles through her shirt. Kate hummed in pleasure as the blonde’s hand moved back up her body to run her fingers lightly over the brunette’s defined collarbone.

    When Kate finally opened her eyes and lifted her head slightly to see the blonde slightly towering over her, she could not help the soft expression that washed over her face. Her blonde locks were piled on top of her head, unlike Kate’s that were going to be a mission to brush this morning. She didn’t meet her eyes as Kate watched her, more than happy to stay in her daydream as she engaged in soft affections. Kate was flooded with a spread of warmth and in her flushness, she shifted closer to Yelena, going as far to wrap her own arm around the assassin’s waist, and pushed her leg in between the blonde’s own to get a close as she could.

    Yelena did not move away from Kate as she bundled into her front, the warmth gladly welcomed as the temperature dropped outside. Winter was on its way and the blonde could not think of any other way she’d want to get warm rather than where she was right now. Of course, if anyone asked her this, she’d give any other answer, but she didn’t need to lie to herself.

    Yelena thought back to the conversation with her sister last night. She needed to tell Kate the truth about her parents, but she knew the brunette well enough by now that she would undoubtedly go off and do something stupid. Maybe she would get her out of the city first, give her the incentive of information if she agreed to go to Clint’s farm. It was a good plan in theory, but this was Kate, and she was unpredictable.

    The blonde took a deep breath, looking down at the top of Kate’s head before resting her chin on top of it with a mixture of hesitation and resolve.

    “There’s something I need to tell you маленький ястреб. Something I’ve learned, but…” Kate hummed before taking her head out Yelena’s chest, the two’s eyes meeting for the first time that morning.

    “Why is there always a but?” Kate slouched into the mattress even more, her arm loosening around Yelena as she tipped back slightly more to get a better view of the assassin’s face. “But… I need you to promise you won’t do anything reckless. Especially with this.” Yelena reached down a lay a hand over the bandage of Kate’s stomach. She was healing well, especially with the Avenger’s fancy medicines but her closed wound was still fragile and not to be pushed too far. After all, they can’t see how the internal healing process is going. Kate furrowed her brow, the new seriousness in Yelena’s tone resonating with her. "What is it? Is it about Kingpin? About the super soldiers? Did you find something? Wait. How have you had the time to find something? You’ve been here every day.” The brunette rambled. Yelena hesitated for a moment before delivering the news that had been weighing on her all night. "I've received information about… your parents. It’s linked to someone who might be involved with some dangerous people with a lot of connections that we do not need to get involved with. I need you to stay calm and not jump into anything until we’ve had more time to flush out the intel."

    Kate's eyes narrowed, a flicker of concern crossing her face. "My parents? Dad too? Who is it? Do they want something to do with me? Who’s your source?"

    Yelena paused, choosing her words carefully. "Kate. Going after them now, especially with your recent injury, would be extremely stupid. We need to approach this cautiously." Kate's fists clenched where they were laid on Yelena’s top, the frustration evident in her voice. "Yelena, I can't just sit here and do nothing. If they're a threat, I need to stop them." Yelena placed a reassuring hand on Kate's cheek, her gaze unwavering. "Маленький ястреб. Your safety is my priority. This information has been passed through many people; we don’t know how much truth it holds. We'll find a way to handle this together, but rushing in blindly, to a location we don’t even know, won't help anyone."

    The room fell into a heavy silence as the weight of the news settled between them. Yelena's concern for Kate's well-being was palpable, and the archer, though eager to act, could recognise the wisdom in Yelena's words, however, Kate had never been patient when it came to being made to wait for information. It’s why Clint had let her run into Maya’s building over Christmas. She got too distracted by the simplest of things to be any good on a stakeout. However, Yelena's guidance served as a steadying force, a reminder that sometimes patience was the greatest ally, especially if the stakes were as high as the blonde was making them out to be.

    Kate wasn’t a fool though and she knew Yelena knew this. The brunette knew what the assassin was alluding to was to do with her parents and Kingpin. This also meant it had everything to do with Kate getting stabbed and Yelena’s focus on pointing out the seriousness of her injury. The blonde was obviously expecting a fight when the time came, and Kate knew Yelena would also try to keep her as far away from it as possible. “Does anyone else know?” Kate sighed, too sleepy and comfortable in the precarious show of affection that was taking place.

    “Yes.” Yelena still had her hand on Kate’s cheek. She dropped her head off her elbow, placing it on the pillow, a small distance from Kate’s. The woman did not move her hand, more than content to keep stroking her thumb across Kate’s cheek.

    “That’s not what I asked.” Kate whined and threw her head back slightly in her faux annoyance.

    Yelena did drop her hand then, bringing them both under her cheek to rest between the pillow and her head. Kate tried to keep her expression from looking dejected at the loss of contact, but obviously failed when she felt Yelena’s leg’s squeeze the brunette’s one that still lay between the blondes.

    “I answered exactly what you asked.” The blonde shrugged with a smirk. “I hate you.”

    “Okay Kate.”

    “It’s true.”

    “You seem rather happy to be in my bed for someone who hates me.”

    Kate could not help the blush that spread over the cheeks, nor could Yelena help the smirk that appeared on her face.

    Yelena with her sharp wit and cocky demeanour, found an abundance of pleasure in watching Kate’s expressions. The woman had a myriad of them. Kate, typically flappable and more than a tiny bit chaotic, could also be serene, overjoyed, defeated and Yelena’s personal favourite, sleepy. However, another one rather high on Yelena’s list was flustered. The brunette, Yelena was learning, could not help but blush under the onslaught of the blonde’s teasing remarks, although Kate had a few good lines of her own.

    Whether or not the blonde made a sly comment, committed to a lively wink or a slipped a not so well-hidden innuendo into casual conversation, she took every opportunity she could to tease Kate. After all, the assassin had many years of simple banter between friends to make up for. The archer often only responded with a rankled glare with a pretence of offense, but on occasion did she bite back.

    Kate, with a playful glint in her eye, responded to Yelena with a mischievous smirk, "Well, Yelena, you know what they say - keep your friends close and overenthusiastic assassins closer. It's all part of my master plan for world domination… obviously." Yelena raised an eyebrow, a hint of amusement in her stoic facade. "World domination? Ha. With a shit plan like that, you might want to reconsider your career choice." Kate shot back, "Oh, I'm just getting started baby. You’ll be the first person I model to when I design the perfect superhero costume to rule the world in. I might even let you be my sidekick."

    Yelena chuckled, appreciating the banter, and trying to ignore the pet name. "Sidekick? If that’s the title you’re giving me, just remember: I’m the sidekick with the better hair, the more intriguing backstory and could gut anyone like a fish with my pinkie finger.” Kate, ever quick-witted, retorted, "Well, you'll have to earn the title of Co-World Ruler first. Assassins as efficient as yourself don't just get a free pass, you know." Yelena fully laughed out loud then, her forehead bumping into Kate’s as the brunette also succumbed to her own giggles. When the two women finally calmed down, their foreheads no longer touching but not separated by a large distance either, Yelena spoke again. “I think you should go with Clint and Laura.” The blonde said softly, words measured but with an undertone of urgency.

    “Where are they going?” Kate questioned, her eyebrow raising almost instantly. “To their home.”

    Kate let out a small “Oh.”

    “Do Clint and Laura want me there?”

    “It was their idea actually.”

    “So… they know about what you won’t tell me about.”

    “They do.”

    Kate's expression shifted, a mix of surprise and contemplation but also one of slight betrayal. “You will find out soon enough Kate. I wish you won’t but… you should know…just not here.” Yelena gestured, throwing her once relaxed arm up in the air, to indicate to what she was referring to.

    “You’ll tell me if we go to the Barton’s?”

    “You will find out when you’re there, yes.” Yelena worded her statement carefully, not wanting to commit to agreeing to going to Barton’s if Kate was happy to go without her. The mention of Clint Barton's farm, a place with the promise of peace and respite, stirred emotions that lay dormant beneath the surface. Yelena, perceptive as ever, could sense the internal struggle within Kate.

    “Kate. The city is not safe for you. I know you think this is running and giving Fisk what he wants but we need time, as much as we can get, and we are not going to get the respite here to do that. You’ve been struggling Kate. We all have. The weight of our choices, our families choices, and the ghosts from our pasts, they’re all creeping back up again and taking their toll.” Yelena breathed out slowly, her hand cautiously moving back to the dip of Kate’s waist and drawing small patterns there. “Barton’s farm will give you a chance to sleep soundly, and fully heal.”

    Kate sighed, the weariness in her blue eyes mirrored the concerns she saw swimming in Yelena’s. “I get it, I do. But it’s not just us affected; we can’t just leave. There’s always more people being drawn into his clutches, there’s always more people to save.” “You’re never going to be able to save everyone Kate. And promise me you won’t try to. That’s how people get themselves killed.” Yelena’s voice wobbled at the silent indication of her sister’s act.

    “You keep saying you. Aren’t you coming too?” Kate ignored the blonde’s plea of a promise. There was a pause as Yelena recollected herself and simultaneously tried to find an answer to Kate’s question. Her gaze lingered on her hand that busied itself on Kate’s top, letting a flicker of vulnerability cross her features for a minute as she met Kate’s eyes once more. “I have some loose ends I need to tie up. Need to talk to some people.” Yelena admitted, what she had said not being a total lie but not the honest truth either.

    Kate's expression shifted, a mix of concern and understanding.

    “I need to pick up Fanny.” Yelena quickly spoke up again to placate the brunette. “And I need to tell Melina and Alexei that Natasha is alive.” She groaned as she said this last part. Kate sighed, realizing the complexity of Yelena's circumstances. “Fine. You do that but then you fly straight to Clint’s farm with Fanny so her and Lucky can become best friends.” "Fine." Yelena conceded, mocking Kate with a hint of a smile.

    Chapter End Notes follow me on tumblr for sneak previews https://www.tumblr.com/thebestpeopleinlifearefreefic p.s should i make a twt account for this?

    Chapter 15

    Chapter Notes chapter a day early for you all!!

    I am off to visit a friend at university on Tuesday so you wouldn't have had a chapter for a week bang on if I had posted it tomorrow and that seemed crazy to me for some reason. I am also going to post chapter 16 on Monday evening before I leave and then chapter 17 is most likely to come out next weekend.

    As for where I currently am in the story, I am currently writing chapter 28. Follow my tumblr if you'd like regular writing updates and just weird thoughts that pop into my mind.

    This is my Kate central chapter so here we get a little insight into more of her thought processes at the moment but also more of a focused view on her relationship with Clint and also Laura.

    Enjoy!

    Kate sat on the front step of the large building behind her, her eyes fixed on the scuffs that littered the leather of her rather battered Doc Martens. A pair of puncture marks sat on either side of her left boot, a set of holes from Lucky’s overexcitement when she had arrived home one day. She hadn’t had the heart to be mad at him. After all, the brunette knew she would be bored out of her mind if she had to stay home alone all day without having any actual entertainment.

    To her left, a Quinjet’s engine hummed with energy as Sonya and Yelena trekked up and down its ramp, diligently loading it with their personal bags, as well as some supplies that Nat and Steve had insisted, they take back to Melina’s farm for the widows staying there. Kate watched as Sonya expertly maneuvered multiple heavy duffel bags into the many storage compartments, their contents including anything from canned foods to ammunition. The brunette couldn’t help but admire how each of her movements was so efficient, her tactical gear radiating a sense of discipline which Kate could never imagine someone else thinking about herself.

    Beside Sonya, Yelena moved with a more relaxed, yet equally purposeful manner. Kate supposed that was due to the blonde not going on the mission and therefore was not so worried about the tactical equipment as much as Sonya. Her slight yet muscular frame hoisted crates up the ramp with ease. The brunette held back a chuckle at the look on Sonya’s face when Yelena dropped a crate at her feet, maintaining a playful smirk as she did so. Even from her position across the lawn, Kate could see how the widows luggage, weapons and various supplies were strategic in their arrangement. She could the feel the experience of the two women rolling off them in waves as their hum of conversation echoed across the tarmac, occasionally punctuated by a burst of laughter. Sonya stood still for a few seconds, wiping loose hairs off her forehead with the back of her hand, casting a sidelong glance at Yelena who was leaning against the side of the Quinjet’s opening. The blonde was stood mocking the darker woman wiping her brow, as if boasting she herself had not broken a sweat. The young archer couldn’t help but succumb to a small smile at the two widows antics.

    Kate’s musings were soon broken as the loading ramp closed with a metallic thud, the supplies sealed within and out of Kate’s sight. The two widows now walked back towards the compound, slow conversation occurring between them.
