    The brunette’s gaze turned away from them, moving to the other group of people collated on the same track of tarmac. Clint’s truck had been filled to the brim with gas, and its cargo bed filled with the Barton’s suitcases as well as Kate’s duffel. An extra surprise at also been thrown at Kate this morning when she found out Natasha was going to the farm as well, so the redhead’s luggage was also present.

    Laura and Clint were tying down a tarp over the top of the bags, making sure they’d be kept dry if it was to rain at any point during their journey to Iowa. Steve was checking the trucks tires even though he had been assured by Clint they were completely fine multiple times over. And the aforementioned redhead was sat in the passenger seat, facing out of the door, her feet on the truck’s step. She was exchanging conversation with Laura whilst periodically glancing down at the phone in her hands.

    A set of legs blocked her vision, dragging Kate out of her staring once more. Looking up, she was met with the owners of the legs and a smirking Sonya. The widow extended a hand which Kate took willingly, letting the strong woman heave her up to her feet. Sonya looked her up and down for a few moments making Kate feel rather uncomfortable, the dark-haired woman snorted at the look on Kate’s face before reaching out and squeezing her upper right arm.

    “Do not be an idiot.”

    “What?”

    “I’m trying to tell you not to do anything stupid whilst blondie over there is not attached to your side. Clear?” Sonya raised an eyebrow at the confused looking archer. Kate rolled her eyes and crossed her arms as Sonya dropped her hand from her bicep. “I can take care of myself you know. I’m 23.”

    “Yes. Seems like it.” Sonya deadpanned, earning a huff from Kate.

    The tension between Sonya and Kate hung in the air for a moment, like an invisible thread waiting to be pulled. Sonya eyed Kate once more, this time with a mixture of concern but also a stern authority. The brunette bristled at the tried interference, her body’s exuberance already refusing to concede to the weight of a strangers expectations.

    Sonya let out a sigh, breaking the silence. "You're a skilled archer Kate, probably one of the best from what I hear. That however will not be enough to take on an army of Russian super soldiers and Kingpin by yourself. I know you want to make them pay, but alone? That is not the best way to do that.”

    "Sonya. I've been training for this practically my whole life. I wish everyone would stop treating me like a stupid kid.” Kate's eyes narrowed, a hint of her stubborn defiance shining clearly through.

    Sonya's expression softened, the sternness giving way to a touch of understanding. "I don't doubt your skills, Bishop. It's your wannabe superhero attitude. You're not invincible, and no matter how good you are, you cannot control every variable out there. Having help does not make you weak."

    “I get it, okay? You're probably saying all this because Yelena put you up to it. But I can handle my problems on my own." Kate shuffled her feet awkwardly.

    "It's not about handling them, Kate. It's about surviving them. And sometimes, survival means knowing when to ask for help and when to listen to those who've been around people who want you dead a few more times than you." Sonya sighed again, a hint of a smile playing on her lips.

    "Fine, I'll try not to do anything stupid. Happy now?" Kate reluctantly conceded. "Good. And Yelena did not ask me to do anything. I would just hate to see your hot bod dead on a table.” Sonya winked, hip bumping her as she walked over to the group standing around the truck.

    The widow’s departure left Kate standing on the front porch with a mix of exasperation and jadedness in her expression.

    The brunette glanced around a couple of minutes later, the group from the truck having now separated. Sonya had obviously said her goodbyes, as she was currently hopping up into the Quinjet’s cabin, stopping to salute to Kate as she noticed her looking. Clint and Laura had settled themselves in the truck, having hugged Steve goodbye who was now embracing Nat. Fury was nowhere to be seen, but Kate had come to expect that of the man. She was sure that he had more important things to do than trivial goodbyes. The brunette swung her head around to spot the last person who she knew was around the compound somewhere, when a low voice sounded behind her.

    “Looking for someone милый маленький ястреб?”

    Kate turned her body just enough to lay eyes on the blonde as she slowly stepped forward to stand next to the brunette. The Russian’s piercing gaze and overall presence had an air of familiarity in this world of superheroes, which had grown on Kate as something surprisingly comforting.

    “I had a feeling you’d try to slip out unnoticed.” Kate shrugged, averting her gaze to Nat and Steve across the lawn who were still avidly chatting.

    “I might have done once upon a time. But now, I would not leave without saying goodbye Kate Bishop.”

    The brunette could feel Yelena’s body turn to face her own, her green eyes boring holes in the side of her skull.

    “Did you tell Sonya to te-“ Kate started.

    “No. What did she say to you?” Yelena sounded impatient.

    “Just gave me a whole ‘don’t be stupid’ lecture. I have a feeling I’m going to get one again, so I just thought I’d let you know that the topic has been covered.” Kate sighed, her shoulders slumping.

    “She meant you no pain Kate.”

    “No harm.”

    “Huh?” The blonde’s head tilted in her confusion.

    “Don’t worry. I know she meant well; I just hate feeling like I’m being treated like a kid. Mom did it my whole life even though I’d been practically looking after myself since Dad died. I’m fine on my own and I’ve also been doing this superhero stuff for a while now.” Yelena moved from beside Kate to stand in front of the brunette, placing her hands on the top of the archer’s hips.

    “I do not believe you are a child Kate.”

    Kate scoffed.

    “No Kate. Listen to me.” Yelena tightened her grip on the brunette, the taller woman still not meeting the green eyes below her. “This situation is no longer one man and his idiots going after you. This is life or death. The Russian super soldiers? This is my specialty and Sonya’s and Natasha’s and even Captain America’s to an extent. This is not about your age Kate or the fact you’ve been doing this for a much shorter time than the rest of us. This is about previous personal experience with these people and us having a clearer picture of how they work than you do.”

    At Yelena’s sigh, Kate finally met the blonde’s eyes whose gaze softened almost instantly. “You are the one with a target on your back Kate. You cannot afford to be stupid.” Kate’s mouth opened to make a quick retort about being to afford a lot of things, but Yelena pre-empted her joke and held up her hand in warning.

    “I cannot afford for you to be an глупый идиот.” The blonde said quietly whilst tugging lightly on Kate’s hips, trying to enforce her point.

    Kate did not say anything in return. The brunette slowly raised her arms over the blonde’s shoulders pulling her into her chest. Yelena hesitantly followed the movement, feeling Nat and Steve’s eyes on them from across the driveway. The archer above her buried her head down into Yelena’s shoulder, and the assassin immediately wrapped her arms tightly around Kate’s waist. Kate, catching the subtle shift in Yelena's demeanour, let a soft smile take over her face. The blonde feeling the movement against her clothed skin. Yelena's usually guarded expression softened as she squeezed Kate gently.

    “Don’t miss me too much.” The brunette whispered.

    “You’re so funny мой маленький ястреб.” Yelena whispered back as the two women eventually parted.

    The blonde gave Kate’s hips one last squeeze before nodding in acknowledgement and with a final glance, turned her back and made her way towards the Quinjet. Kate could only stand there, watching Yelena scale the aircraft and making it look effortless. As the Quinjet’s engines roared even louder, Kate began to walk over to the truck, watching the plane lift off at a lightning quick speed. She passed Steve on her way up the drive, the man giving her shoulder a quick pat before continuing his way back to the main building. Nat was leant against the side of the truck as she trudged over. The brunette could make out Clint’s head in the front seat, Laura in the back on the opposite side. “Front or back?”

    Kate just shrugged at the redhead before watching her slip in the passenger seat. The archer pulled open the back door, taking her seat behind her mentor. The trucks engine roared to life as Clint shifted gears and pushed down on the accelerator.

    Soon, a familiar hum of the road filled the cabin and the city that Kate had called home all her life blurred past the windows. As they reached the border of New York City, the brunette felt Laura’s eyes on her as she rested her head on the window. She didn’t meet the woman’s gaze as she had nothing to say. The atmosphere inside the truck carried a sense of familiarity but also an undertone of unresolved tension.

    Clint glanced at Kate though the rearview mirror, and the brunette could sense his expression conveyed worry, but she also knew he was relieved that she was here and not in the city alone. Laura met his gaze in the mirror instead, sending her husband a comforting smile even though she herself was just as concerned as he was. The Barton family truck, usually a symbol of comfort and full of life, now felt like a SHIELD ship carrying them away from the aftermath of a storm.

    As they drove closer toward the Barton farm, Kate couldn’t shake the feeling crawling up inside of her. The landscape passing by now was a blur of unfamiliar fields and trees and the deathly quiet of the truck, bar the quiet hum of the crackling radio, only heightened her unease and discomfort. The sky was turning darker from the length of their travel and Kate couldn’t help her fingers restlessness, tracing absentminded patterns on her knees. The weight of recent events felt even more confining whilst in the cramped space of the truck. She couldn’t help but wonder if her presence, her choices, and parents choices, had become a burden to those around her.

    Kate couldn't help but feel like somewhat of an outsider. Even though Clint had spoken all those nice things about thinking of her as another one of his children, she still felt like an intruder in a truck where those around her carried burdens she could only imagine. The idea that she might be a source of concern rather than one of support gnawed at her, creating a knot of self-doubt.

    The sky was fully black when the Barton farm came into view, its familiar silhouette outlined by the outside lights. The long driveway gave Kate even more unwanted time in her head. The desire to be surrounded by the warmth of the family that resides here clashed with the fear of being a burden and no matter how hard she tried to remind herself of Clint and Laura’s kindness, she couldn’t help but think her presence was going to disrupt the peace the couple had tried so hard to maintain for their three kids.

    When the truck finally slowed to a stop, the engine still idling, Kate couldn’t open the door quick enough. She jumped out of the truck, ignoring the three heads that turned to look at her. Once outside and she had accidentally slammed the truck door, the loud sound breaking the stillness that engulfed them, the brunette took some large paces away from the vehicle before taking a deep breath. Kate felt the cool November air fill her lungs and hit her face. The scent of the countryside and the distant fumes of wood smoke would usually have comforted her but tonight it only soothed her worries of instant danger. It could not fix her inner turmoil. The archer rubbed her temples in circular motion as she heard the other’s exit the truck and begin unloading the cargo bed.

    Kate didn’t know how long she stood there in her own head until Laura’s distant voice was carried towards her by the gentle breeze.

    “Kate sweetheart?”

    Realising she couldn’t delay it any longer, the brunette turned back towards the house, the soft glow of the farmhouse lights and the warmth emanating from the familiar decor she could see through the windows beckoned to her. The archer walked slowly up to Laura who wrapped an arm around her waist and gently coaxed her through the front door.

    As Kate cautiously stepped inside the familiar Barton farmhouse, she couldn't shake the lingering thoughts battling around her brain. The warmth and laughter that typically greeted her seemed muffled, but she reasoned that was just because the kids weren’t due back from Laura’s sisters until tomorrow morning. She flitted around the kitchen, just hovering awkwardly as her three elders bustled around her. Nat was headed up to her old room, the wide grin that had not moved from her face since they’d arrived still beaming as she said her goodnights and wandered up the stairs.

    The living room flickered with the glow of several lamps that had been quickly flicked on, casting a warm and inviting ambiance. Laura was pottering around, shutting the curtains, and moving items from bags and back to their rightful place. The brunette hadn’t even realised Clint had wandered down to the basement, the staircase and its doorway being wider than Kate remembered, until he bounded up the stairs.

    "Kate, we've got something to show you," Laura announced, her eyes sparkling with excitement after sharing a glance with her husband.

    The couple headed to the bottom of the stairs, beckoning Kate to follow them upstairs. Perplexed, Kate followed them up until they got to a familiar hallway. The creak of the stairs beneath their footsteps resonated in the air as they ascended to the upper level of the farmhouse. The upstairs of the house was tight in space but as homely as could be. Nat’s room was the first door on the left, followed by Lila’s, the two rooms sharing a jack and jill style bathroom. The hall bathroom door was on the wall directly opposite the stairs. On the right, Cooper’s door faced Lila’s and Nat’s opposed Nate’s. The master bedroom was just passed the youngest Barton’s room, its door in the corner nook above the stairs. Clint and Laura stopped outside what Kate knows to be their eldest sons bedroom but when Clint swung the door open, he revealed a transformed space that left Kate momentarily speechless. The once stereotypical teenage boy bedroom had undergone a complete renovation. It now bore the unmistakable signs of thoughtful care and attention, most definitely all the décor being decided by Laura.

    "Welcome to your new bedroom, Katie Kate." Clint gestured towards the room, a soft grin on his face.

    Before her stood a cozy bedroom, adorned with warm hues and personal touches. The walls were painted in calming tones, and a comfortable bed, neatly made, served as the focal point. The room exuded a welcoming atmosphere, making it clear that the Bartons had put considerable effort into ensuring Kate felt at home. The roof slanted down on one side, this part slating over the double bed tucked into the corner. The ruched white bedding and fluffy beige throw could not have been more inviting to a sleepy Kate.

    An off-white and rustic bedside table sat on the side of the bed not up against the wall, a small lamp and potted plant sat on top of it. The rooms window sat just over the top of the right side of the table and spread further across the wall. Its double panelled window probably a large source of light during the day. In the corner sat a new flat, yet thick dog bed, with ‘Lucky’ embroidered in italics in its left front corner. A small vanity opposed the wall her bed sat against, a rustic mirror with exposed wood on the wall above it. It seemed Clint had fixed wired bulbed lights around its edges, giving Kate the lighting, she needed to do her makeup or skincare at any time of the day, it was probably more likely to be used to patch up small cuts, but the archer didn’t need to know that.

    The space on top the vanity was empty, along with empty organisers sat on top of it, ready and waiting for the brunette to make it undoubtedly messy. On the same wall as the door sat a matching dresser to the bedside table and the vanity, a collage of empty picture frames hung above it. The vase on top of the dresser caught her eye, it being filled with the set of LEGO flowers Kate had built when she was here at Christmas but hadn’t had the heart to carry back to New York in case of breaking them. The cladded ceiling was white whilst the matching cladding on the walls was a dusky grey with a hint of purple as to not be too overbearing. A fluffy beige rug was laid on the floor, the light hardwood floor still visible around its edges. "You did all this for me?" Kate's eyes widened in surprise, and she turned to Clint and Laura with a mix of gratitude and disbelief.

    "We wanted you to have a space that feels like yours rather than in the guest room… Nat’s room.” Clint spoke. Kate heard the unspoken explanation about Nat being back in his pause. Kate nodded, turning back to the room, scanning it with her eyes once more before turning back around to the couple rather hurriedly.

    "But what about Cooper?”

    "Don't worry about Coop. Come, we'll show you." Clint chuckled, placing a reassuring hand on her shoulder as the brunette was about to start fretting.

    They guided Kate back down the stairs and then down the next flight to what used to be the kids playroom. The once-childish decorations had been replaced with a more mature and sophisticated design. A couch sat under the stairs; a TV mounted within a rack of bookshelves across from it. All of Nate’s toys sat in organised boxes under the entertainment wall. A new wall had been built on the right of the stairs, with a two doors matching the ones that ran throughout the rest of the house. It was evident that a lot of thought had gone into transforming it into a space that suited the whole family.

    "We thought Cooper might appreciate a more grown-up room, and he was more than happy to move down to the basement away from his siblings.” Laura explained as they walked into the space, opening the two doors so Kate could peek inside.

    “He didn’t need the whole space, so we split it up a little bit, leaving the kids with their space down here for their games and for when their friends come round. He’s got his room there and now we’ve got an extra bathroom too.” Clint carried on their reasoning, before they walked back up the stairs and stopped in the kitchen.

    “When did you do this?” Kate questioned, still trying to wrap her head around the day without having this surprise thrown on top of it.

    “Over the summer. Kids helped with the demo whilst they were off from school.” Clint shrugged before he picked up Kate’s bag and nudged her up the stairs.

    Laura followed behind them, giving Kate a quick hug goodnight before she headed down the landing to the master bedroom. Clint put Kate’s bag down at the end of her bed, in between it and the dresser. Kate, zombie like, plopped down on her new bed. Clint watched her for a few moments before squeezing down on the end next to her.

    “You okay kiddo?”

    Kate didn’t reply for a couple of minutes, the brunette in a trance like state as her mind and body tried to catch up with each other. One was on overdrive, and the other wanted to sleep for the next few years. When she went to reply, she was already half asleep and no longer cared for keeping up her strong appearance for the man who was practically becoming her pseudo-father.

    “I don’t know.”

    Chapter 16

    Chapter Notes hello all!

    leave me some comments to reply to whilst i'm travelling tomorrow night pls!! hope y'all enjoy some yelena focused content and an insight into her developing relationship with Melina.

    (more alexei to come i promise)

    As the sun dipped below the horizon, casting a warm glow over the outskirts of Saint Petersburg, Yelena and Sonya descended the sleek Quinjet onto the sprawling farmland that carried a familiar scent of earth and a complicated sense of home. Melina, with her keen sense of timing, awaited them at the landing site. She was dressed in all black, her hair half pulled up, and her boots covered in what Yelena assumed to be some animal manure – probably pig.

    Sonya darted off the Quinjet, saying a quick hello to Melina before running off down the fields to find Antonia. The wind carried her laughter back to the landing site as she almost toppled over Alexei-the-Pig in her haste. The moment Yelena’s boots touched the ground of her homeland, her adoptive mother walked straight for her, arms outstretched for a short embrace. Yelena reciprocated the gesture, relishing in the fact that genuine affection had grown between them over the past couple years.

    “Come in my dear. Look at you, so westernised.” Melina held her at arm’s length trying to get a good look at her.

    Yelena rolled her eyes.

    You’d think they had been separated for a decade with the way her mother was acting. She had seen Melina two months ago.

    As the two women made their way towards the farmhouse, their conversation flowed easily, a mix of curious questioning from Melina about what she had spent so long in America for this time and their normal discussion of the ever-present issue of saving the rest of the widows. Melina’s farm had always sparked conflicting feelings within Yelena. It's wide-open spaces and comforting smell of home cooked food provided a stark contrast to the dark world they are so wholly immersed in and were born into. But it was also home to the root of Yelena’s trauma.

    After all, her mother and father aided the Red Room more than most.

    As Melina reached for the farmhouse door it burst open and a tall figure came bounding out, beaming with an unbridled excitement.

    “Yelena. My daughter home again and so soon!” Alexei bellowed as he scooped the blonde up in a bear hug.

    Yelena not one to be caught off guard, slapped her father’s arm, urging him to put her down and stop cutting off her air supply. Alexei quickly released her with a hearty chuckle, obviously having learnt from the last time.

    “How was America? Did you see its Captain? Did he mention me? Did you get me a souvenir?” He enthusiastically shouted, wrapping an arm around Yelena’s shoulders, and practically hauling her into the house, leaving Melina to follow behind them. “Maybe next time Papa. I am here because there is something important, I need to share with you both.” Yelena rolled her eyes, her tough exterior softening in the presence of her adoptive father.

    It was only when the tight grip from around her shoulders leave did Yelena notice the aroma of a home-cooked meal enveloping them. A few steps further into the kitchen and the table was set, Melina had spared no effort in preparing a complete Russian feast for the return of her daughter. The three took their seats, not without the floor creaking from the force at which Alexei flung himself into his seat at the head of the table.

    Alexei wasted no time in bombarding questions about her time in America and the blonde had no problem sharing her favourite stories, embellishing some details to please her puppy- like father and downplaying others to dissuade the man from jumping on a plane to experience it himself. Like most of the things she shared with her parents, the assassin left out names. Melina and Alexei had never had a slither of Kate Bishop’s name and she planned to keep it that way, after all, if the two knew she had someone in her life who wasn’t them or a widow, Alexei would never let her hear the end of it.

    In their midst of their laughter about a story Melina was telling of Alexei almost tranquilising himself whilst trying to do so to a pig, Sonya and Antonia emerged from the backdoor. The two were clad in their mission gear, a large difference to the three sat around the table. Sonya exchanged a knowing look with Yelena, a silent understanding passing between the two, before the blonde exchanged some quick pleasantries with the other widow in the room. “Не будь курицей.” Sonya mumbled to Yelena as the two women made their way out, the sound of the Quinjet taking off happening not a moment later.

    Amidst the clinking of cutlery and the surprisingly hearty banter bouncing around the table, Yelena seized a moment of relative quiet when it eventually popped up. She had to pick her moments in this house, so there was not long to ponder the decision of how to break such news to her parents.

    “There is something I need to tell you,” The youngest at the table began, only to be interrupted by a loud belch from her father before Melina offered and attempted to refill his glass, in and amongst the man’s swinging arms reaching across the table to fill his plate with thirds.

    “Mama. Please. It is important.” Yelena insisted to her more sensible parent, her tone cutting through Melina’s focus on Alexei.

    The blonde watched as the two shared a glance. Her mother’s face were serious, Yelena’s tone having cut her jovial expression. Meanwhile, Alexei held a smirk and couldn’t help himself opening his big mouth.

    “I know what this means Melina,” He started, hitting the back of his hand against Melina’s arm as he amped himself up, “They do this line in all the movies. Our little girl has met someone special.”

    Yelena didn’t think she’d ever heard her father’s voice go so high. Her eyes rolled and whilst waiting for her parents to compose themselves, the blonde downed a few shots of vodka. She needed to compose herself too, for she had blissfully forgotten that having a serious conversation and breaking significant news to this particular duo was always going to be somewhat of a mission in itself.

    When Alexei had died down in his excitement, after several minutes of asking Yelena questions and failing in getting any answers, the blonde took a deep breath before alternating her gaze between the two. She decided to focus on Melina when she saw the lingering mirth swimming around in her father’s eyes.

    “I have met no one. It is about Natasha.”

    The atmosphere shifted entirely, a contemplative silence replacing the playful banter that had been flowing. Melina’s expression steeled over, and Yelena saw her clench her jaw. Alexei, ever emotional, looked like he was about to burst into tears at just the mention of her name so Yelena bit the bullet.

    “What a stupid saying Kate Bishop. Do not go around biting bullets. Not good for your teeth. No… no good at all.”

    “Наташа вернулась.”

    The room fell silent, her parents faces flicking through so many different expressions Yelena couldn’t have counted them even if she had been trying too. The news hung in the air for several moments before Melina’s eyes widened in astonishment and Alexei’s constant smirk had faded and his face was just pure disbelief.

    Melina, always the composed one, was the first to find her voice. "Natasha... alive? But we mourned her, we... This is not possible." Melina's hands trembled slightly, betraying her many years of training. Yelena had never seen her mother like this.

    Her eyes sought Yelena's for reassurance, but the youngest of the mismatched family merely nodded, confirming the unbelievable truth. Those familiar eyes searched Yelena's face again for any sign that this might be some elaborate joke, but the blonde’s expression remained earnest.

    “Невозможный. I thought... we all thought..." Alexei, still grappling with the revelation, leaned back in his chair, running a hand through his hair first and then down to his thick beard.

    Yelena took a moment to compose herself before delving into the tale of Natasha's resurrection. She explained about the infinity stones, the twisted tale of her sister and Clint Barton, and the Avengers' relentless pursuit to save the world to honour her sacrifice. The room echoed with questions, her parents hanging on every word, trying to make sense of the updated narrative unfolding before them.

    Melina's face shifted from astonishment to concern. "Is she safe, Yelena? How can we be sure she's not in danger? These are the people who got наша маленькая девочка killed." Yelena assured her mother that Natasha was quite safe. She spoke of the Avengers, their unwavering commitment to protecting each other as much as the blonde hated to admit it, especially out loud. The complexity of emotions in the room continued to evolve, a mixture of disbelief, joy, and concern for the family member they thought would never join them at this table again.

    "And what of her loyalties? She is fraternising with my enemy." Alexei growled. Yelena sighed, taking another shot of vodka before she delved into Natasha's friendship with Captain America and how she was pretty sure her father was thinking of someone else. Alexei recounted the battles he had fought against Steve, and the genuine commitment he showed to his obvious lie was commendable or he had spent so much time convincing himself of the lie that now he believed it to be completely true.

    Yelena navigated the rest of the conversation as delicately as the greatest assassin of all time was capable of. She tried to provide reassurance to her ever fretting and overreactive parents, possibly downplaying the intricacies of the situation and the reasons why Natasha hadn’t come with her to see them. The night wore on and the atmosphere in the farmhouse only became more riddled.

    As the conversation gradually wound down almost an hour later, Yelena found a quiet second to excuse herself, feeling the weight of her exhaustion settle in.

    "I need some rest. It has been a long day," she said, standing up from the table. Melina and Alexei only nodded in acknowledgement, not fighting their daughters departure. Yelena made her way to her room, the rustic décor of her space enveloping her in a sense of familiarity. All of her few belongings were in the same place she had left them, and the bag she brought with her had been placed at the end of her bed waiting for her to reside for the night. The blonde pulled her phone from her pocket before she got changed into something more comfortable. Once she had climbed under the covers and made herself comfortable, the assassin turned on her phone for the first time that day and was shocked when she didn’t have a spam of notifications from a certain brunette.

    Kate Bishop was a known double texter.

    Yelena’s brows furrowed as she scrolled through their text chain, expecting to find the usual barrage of texts from Kate. The brunette was incapable of saying everything she wanted to in a single text, instead sending text after text so much so Yelena had learnt to expect the last one was most likely not the last. The unusual silence on her phone screen was strange, no witty remarks, no teasing messages nor any crazy tales from the journey to the Barton’s – just an eerie absence.

    The concern that flickered within Yelena fired her brain into thinking about every worst possibility that could’ve happened to Kate between the time she had left and now. The blonde told herself that this was not unreasonable, after all, Kate was her friend who was wanted dead by more than one person at this current moment in time. She knew Kate well enough by now to realise that something was definitely wrong, and the brunette had already been slowly spiralling in her grief since Yelena had arrived in New York.

    This thought sparked something else in the assassins mind.

    Doubt.

    Kate had been struggling since Yelena’s arrival. This was a common pattern. At Christmas and now more recently too. The assassin sighed as she realised, she was a big part of the brunette’s troubles, sure, she was smart enough to know she was not the only messed up person in the brunette’s life, but the blonde definitely had more enemies than most. Even in knowing this Yelena couldn’t shake the nagging feeling that she might be causing more harm than good, inadvertently pulling Kate more and more into the dark and stormy part of her life she never wanted the brunette to experience. The assassin stared at the ceiling, the newly thought about complexities settling heavy on her chest, and the uncommon silence echoing around her parents’ house only amplified the turmoil in her mind. She reached for her phone again, her thumb hovering over the keyboard on the screen. It was with a heavy heart she threw the phone back on the bed again. Now she had properly acknowledged her own role in Kate’s struggles she was torn between the instinct to protect who she cared about most in the world or hope that distancing herself from her might decrease the turbulence in her life.

    The Barton’s farm in the middle of nowhere had to be pretty peaceful.

    The whole thing with Kate had started out as a casual exploration for Yelena. Treading carefully around the brunette. The blonde had only wanted to see what all the fuss was about New York and suddenly she had fallen into a strange friendship with the woman she had thrown off a roof over Christmas, and that woman was also her sister’s best friend’s, who she had been planning to kill, protégé. The dynamic between the two had always been complex and layered, they came from two different worlds and yet Yelena couldn’t think of someone she liked more than Kate Bishop.

    Their relationship had become even more intricate in recent weeks, at least from Yelena’s point of view. The added elements of individual struggle, familial troubles and the almost overwhelming addition of simple affection had spun the blonde into a tizzy and yet the assassin couldn’t bring herself to climb out of it. The urge to unravel the silence that Kate had put up in between them, whether she meant to or not, made Yelena come face to face with the fear of having to battle with the possibility of discovering something she wasn’t ready to come across.

    Yelena finally closed her eyes, letting out a sigh.

    Tonight, she would choose to respect Kate’s space, hoping the brunette would break the silence in between them whilst she slept. The rhythmic sounds of the night outside, along with the rather loud snores of both Alexei’s, gradually seeped into her consciousness, and sleep met the assassin who seeked solace in its temporary reprieve.

    In the darkness behind her closed eyelids, flashes of the Red Room flickered like a slideshow of her past that her mind refused to forget. Images of soldiers in dimly lit corridors, the cold and clinical rooms and the weight of her forced actions bore down on her. Faces danced in her subconscious, dead ones, and those still alive, friend and foe.

    The blonde tossed and turned in the swirl of emotions her mind was caught in. Yelena found herself back on a mission, the familiar scent of danger hung in the air as she navigated through familiar shadows with a stealth that was ingrained into her very being. Other widows were around her too, their faces distorted by her memory, as if her own dream wanted her to be and to feel isolated.

    Sneak peeks of all too familiar tattoos blurred through her vision, large silhouettes of men through a doorway, clad with multiple guns and their familiar drawl escaping their mouths. The blonde jolted awake, beads of sweat forming on her forehead. She once again experienced the transition from her disorienting dreamscape to a largely quiet farmhouse. Yelena sat up in her bed, head swinging around checking every entrance and exit. Her breathing was heavy as the vivid memories lingered in the recesses of her now awake mind. The blonde reached for her phone in that moment, her dream a stark reminder of the threat they were against and that even in the happiest of moments the past could resurface and demand it not wait even a second to be acknowledged.

    Kate? No crazy stories from the Barton’s this time?

    The blonde pressed send.

    The next afternoon, the house buzzed with a lively energy. Yelena had spent the entire morning training in the backyard with other widows and found herself in need of a break. It was nice having a familiar environment after her night plagued with dreams, and the simplicity of the conversation was refreshing after all the complexities she’d experienced in America.

    Americans made everything so complicated.

    The women shared short comments about another’s form or a subtle dig at one of the widow’s latest life updates.

    When Yelena had retired from the group, the crisp air of Saint Petersburg surrounded her as she walked towards a familiar barn at the bottom of the hill from her parent’s house, where she knew Fanny would be waiting. The barn door creaked open, and Yelena was met with the comforting scent of hay and the soft rustle of straw underfoot.

    Fanny, an American Akita, with a subtle mischievous glint in her eyes, wagged her tail excitedly upon seeing Yelena.

    "Fanny, you've been behaving yourself, I hope," Yelena teased, crouching down to pet the enthusiastic dog.

    Fanny responded with an exuberant bark, her tail wagging furiously as she tried to climb up Yelena’s legs until the blonde knelt down and wrapped her arms around the dog. The blonde was reminded of Kate and Lucky as she breathed in the dog’s familiar scent and the pace of her breathing against Yelena’s chest. Despite the complexities of Yelena's life, Fanny remained a steady friend, offering unconditional love and a welcome distraction from the weight of her responsibilities, which were both things Yelena didn’t have much of in her life, or at all before she had rescued Fanny.

    Yelena sat down on a hay bale in the corner of the barn, the farthest place away from the pigs she could get whilst still being in the building. Fanny curled up beside her, happy to enjoy a quiet moment of reprieve with her owner. Yelena's fingers idly traced patterns in Fanny's fur as she reflected on her time since she had arrived the previous day. The camaraderie with the other widows, the shared drills, and the conversation she had had with her parents had made this short trip something similar to a bad family holiday and yet, in this quiet barn, surrounded by the simple pleasures of a loyal dog and the strangely comforting sounds of snorting pigs, Yelena found a sense of grounding she hadn’t had since she had been in bed with Kate that one morning at the Avenger’s Compound.

    The assassin hadn’t even noticed how the sun had dipped lower in the sky, casting a warm glow over the farm, until she eventually trudged out of the barn hours later with Fanny leisurely strolling at her heels. The farmhouse awaited their return as they wandered up the hill, the lights from the widow’s houses lighting their way. Yelena slumped back into the swinging porch seat after having made eye contact with Melina through the window. Melina, somehow having the motherly talent of always being attuned to her daughters moods, emerged from the farmhouse minutes later, holding a cup of tea for the pair of them and a knowing look in her eye as she joined Yelena on the swing.

    “You’ve been busy today.” Melina spoke matter of factly after a couple moments silence. Yelena ran her spare hand through her uncommonly dishevelled hair, her fingers idly pulling apart a knot in the strands as she sighed. “Yes. It has been rather filled.” Melina offered a comforting pat to the blonde’s thigh as she took a sip from her mug. “You need to rest Yelena dearest. You are always such a busy body.” Her mother sighed. Yelena thought she sounded much like Alexei when these words came out of her mouth. Holding back her snort, the blonde felt the weight she’d be drowning under last night resurface in the lines of her frown.

    “It is what I was trained for.” Yelena shrugged. Her day had not been at all busy, but her mother had not seen her lolling in the barn all afternoon and the blonde was seemingly in the mood to pick a fight.

    Melina, not taking the bait, softened her body position, her concern evident in the way her back slouched. “You’re more than just your training Yelena. I know I am in no position to try to remind you of this, but it is true, no matter how hard you want to fight it to avoid whatever else you’re feeling.”

    A moment of quiet understanding resonated between them as Fanny wandered up from whatever she had been sniffing on the grass and curled up at Yelena’s feet. The silence was broken from a loud crash coming from inside the house and then again by Melina’s huff that she left out.

    “You’re more like your father than you think. Natasha has always been more like me: she had coldness down to a T and she always wanted to fight the next fight.” Melina’s voice carried a mix of pride and nostalgia as she spoke.

    Yelena turned her head to look at the woman she called her mother. Melina had a pensive look on her face as she thought of her eldest daughter. Yelena hesitated in interrupting her, wanting to keep the moment intact in urge of her continuing.

    Melina sighed and Yelena was rewarded for her patience.

    “Natasha was a force to be reckoned with, even from a young age. But I was reminded when you two showed up here with your father all those many years later just how much. She was always destined for something beyond what anyone could give her, and it did not surprise me when I learnt she found it herself. And now she is out there once more, fighting battles we can only imagine.”

    Yelena thought hard on her mother’s words, contemplating the decisions she had made when it had come to Natasha. It was confusing hearing about her sister from another familial point of view. Melina did not seem angry at her daughter, who had blazed a trail with the Avengers after having fought her past for the opportunity but had ultimately chosen death as her fate. Melina did not seem mad that she had left the three of them behind without so much of a second thought.

    The differences between the three of them were even more apparent to Yelena in this moment.

    Melina carried on, “You, my dear, have always been more of a lover than a fighter. Even as a little girl your heart was your strength. The awful skills that you acquired in the Red Room may have kept you alive, but your heart is what led you to survive. Natasha fought to protect and to defy everything she had ever known. She had heart too, but you fight to connect Yelena. You always wanted to meet more people than we were allowed to and… every night you snuck into our bed… broke my heart just a little bit more.”

    Melina paused.

    “You have never been cold Yelena and there’s is beauty in that.”

    Her mother’s words hung in the air, and the blonde felt a sense of vulnerability she had never had with the woman before. It was a such a unique and motherly perspective on her nature, one she hadn't thought of at all nor fully understood until this very moment. Yelena had always prided herself on her skills as an assassin and the lethal prowess she had honed in the Red Room as that was all she had known for most of her life, but Melina saw something more. Yelena’s eyes welled with tears as she looked into her mothers, whose gaze softened as she wrapped an arm around her daughter.

    “You must forgive her Yelena. Second chances do not come for most.”

    “I am so angry at her.” Yelena huffed, her voice emotional and frustrated. Melina’s voice held a sense of pleading as she asked Yelena for forgiveness which this time may extend beyond the fragile familial ties that bound the two sisters. Her mother squeezed her shoulder as she spoke once more.

    “Natasha’s choices affected us all dearest, and I would be concerned if you did not feel such anger. Forgiveness is not about condoning ones actions Yelena. It is about freeing yourself from the burden of such resentment.”

    Yelena’s eyes flickered from one of her mother’s eyes to the other as a mix of defiance and childlike frustration rattled through her. She had spent so much of her life fuelled by anger, and being taught how to use it against others, that now whilst being faced with the complexities of her sister’s return, she had to grapple the unfamiliar territory of family and how that influenced her willingness to forgive.

    “I don’t know if I can.” The blonde admitted quietly to her mother, eyes fixed on Fanny’s chest moving up and down with each of breath the dog took.

    “You cannot carry your anger forever Yelena. Emotions like these fester and will only hurt you in the long run. Take it from someone who knows.” Melina sighed before deciding to change the subject, sensing Yelena’s tension rising. “Now tell me about New York.” “Mama. I have told you everything about New York.”

    “You might be able to lie to everyone else on the planet dearest, but I am your Mama.” Melina cocked an eyebrow, earning a grumble from Yelena.

    “Я убью Соню.”

    “Leave poor Sonya alone. She only told me because you would not answer my calls and I asked her why.”

    “And what did she tell you?” Yelena leant her head back before turning it slightly so she could see Melina’s face once more.

    “That you were being kept busy by a friend.”

    “Она заставляет это казаться чем-то, чем оно не является.” Yelena groaned at the tone in her mother’s voice.

    Melina let out a soft chuckle at her daughter’s discomfort, yet she probed the blonde a little more as she did not seem reluctant to talk.

    “Tell me about this friend then.” Melina emphasised.

    Yelena rolled her eyes and stayed quiet for a moment. Her mother studied her face as the cogs whirred inside the assassins head about whether or not to share about Kate Bishop. She had sworn to herself she was never going to mention her name but now the moment had arrived, and she was actually bonding with her mother for the first time in years, Yelena could not help but want to talk about the brunette.

    “Do not make me regret this. And not a word to Alexei.” Yelena pointed a finger at her mother whilst sending a glare her way.

    “Whatever you wish Yelena.”

    The blonde’s eyes turned away from Melina’s face and instead focused on the finishing sunset that sat on the horizon.

    “Her name is Kate. Kate Bishop.” Yelena knew as soon as the words left her mouth how fond she sounded, and bit her lip in an effort to stop herself.

    Melina’s brow furrowed slightly catching the action, but she remained silent, a small smile dancing over her lips.

    “We were not meant to be friends. She is Barton’s protégé. You know, Nat’s friend? The archer?”

    Melina nodded as the blonde’s tone raised in question.

    “She was there when I was hired to kill him. Kate insists I threw her off a roof… I didn’t! But it is quite funny when she tries to argue about it with me…” Yelena laughed softly as she recalled this to Melina who was quite amused by her daughter in this moment. “She’s quite funny all the time really…” The blonde trailed off, silence coming between the two women once again.

    The blonde didn’t speak for quite some time after this. Fanny obviously wanted to hear more about Kate, much like Melina, and soon her head was propped on Yelena’s thigh, staring the blonde down for her to continue. Yelena obliged, the blonde reached her hand out and started scratching behind the dog’s ears.

    “Kate has a dog. His name is Lucky. He’s a golden retriever and ever so much trouble.” Yelena smiled, “Kate insists you and Lucky are going to be best friends.” She continued turning her head for a quick at Melina as she said this, before looking back at Fanny. “But I told her under no circumstance is she to feed you pizza. Lucky might have a terrible diet, but you do not.” Yelena spoke to Fanny directly, the dogs head titling at the sound of the blonde’s playful voice.

    “Kate Bishop is why you’ve been sneaking off all these times?”

    “I was not sneaking. I also always come back. I came back to tell you about Наташа. I could’ve have just called instead.” Yelena said flatly.

    “So why didn’t you?”

    “It felt better said in person.” Yelena shrugged.

    “See. Lover not a fighter.” Melina said with a sparkle in her eye.

    Yelena scoffed at her mother, batting away the hidden compliment once more. They had already had that conversation tonight and she did not wish to think about her sister anymore. “Come on. Tell me more about New York.” Melina elbowed Yelena lightly in the side. “You mean about Kate?”

    “If New York is code for Kate, then yes.” Melina played her nosiness off nonchalantly. “Kate… just sort of snuck up on me.” Yelena started after taking a minute to compose herself.

    “She must be quite talented to sneak up on a trained assassin.”

    “I did not mean literally Mama.” Yelena rolled her eyes, feigning annoyance, but the subtle grin on her face betrayed her true feelings.

    Melina's eyebrows arched with further intrigue.

    “She… she got under my skin and for whatever reason, I just can’t shake her.” Yelena almost whispered before pondering for a moment.

    Melina picked up the ball beside the swing, lobbing it down the field for a now restless Fanny who had been comforting her human all day long. Yelena stayed quiet as the dog ran up and down multiple times, trying to search for a word that could capture the essence of Kate Bishop. The blonde realised she would never be capable of it because the word doesn’t exist. “Kate is… ugh.” Yelena huffed in frustration in herself.

    She hadn’t spoken to anyone about Kate besides Sonya and even then, it was not of her own accord, Sonya just had a way of getting information out of Yelena without the blonde actually admitting to anything. This was getting put on the spot to talk about something she knew absolutely nothing about.

    “You do not have to Yelena. I only wanted to know more of your life after I missed so much of it.”

    “I-I want to…I just don’t have the words. I cannot put her into words.” Melina softened completely then, wrapping both arms around the blonde, and pulling her towards her. Yelena made no fuss to get out of the embrace, even fully relaxing into her mother’s touch.

    “It is not often you do not have words моя самая маленькая девочка.”

    “You have not met Kate. She talks so much. So much.” Yelena laughed softly. “But?” Melina encouraged.

    “It is the first time in my life someone has wanted to talk to me that much. She spoke that much when we first met and that was really not the time for that. Kate is… stubborn.” Yelena snorted, thinking back to Christmas when the brunette had done everything in her power to stop the blonde.

    Melina smiled at the serene look on Yelena’s face as the blonde continued talking. “She is fascinating. She had the fortune to be able to be anything and to have everything she ever wanted, and all she wanted was to be the next Clint Barton.” Yelena drawled lightly, “She is a good fighter and even better at making trouble. Kate is fearless…bold and when I am around her, everything just feels…”

    “Mmm?” Melina prodded softly, showing Yelena she was still listening.

    “She’s fiercely independent and has this sense of humour… she makes me laugh… a lot. I don’t know?” Yelena sighed making Melina chuckle.

    “You don’t know? You seem to know everything about her, my dear.” Melina teased. “I don’t know why. Most people suck.” Yelena shrugged rather nonchalantly, a hint of a smile lingering on her lips.

    “But this Kate Bishop, she is not most people to you?”

    “No. No she… she’s…” Yelena glanced at Melina, searching for understanding in her mother’s gaze.

    “Sometimes, someone comes along and manages to break through all the noise. Like when your father’s old radio stops its crackling and that sultry man’s voice breaks through.” Melina said wistfully.

    “Гросс, мама.” Yelena shook her head.

    Melina reached to gently squeeze Yelena’s hand.

    “Kate is your someone honey.”

    “How do you know?”

    “I am your Mama. I know everything.” Melina squeezed the blonde’s hand again as she scoffed.

    “Maybe. She’s just… different. And I like that.” She paused, turning to look at her mother, a small smile playing on her lips, “I think she likes me too, despite my best efforts to get her not too.”

    “Our people have a way of finding us Yelena. We are an example of that, even though we have tried to resist it most. Perhaps Kate is the exception to our rule.” “Maybe,” The blonde conceded softly, “Maybe she is.”

    Chapter 17

    Chapter Notes hello hello hello its the end of another week so here is another chapter for y'all.

    have written nothing new this week as i have not been at home but hoping to write at least a chapter tomorrow evening once i get in from work :)

    Kate heard whispered voices out on the landing as she rolled over in bed for the twenty-sixth time that day and the four-hundred-and-forty-fifth time that week. She had been at the Barton’s for five days now and had barely left her bedroom. Lucky was curled up in her arms, quite content with the amount of time they’ve spent horizontally lately, and when he had needed to go outside to let out some energy, Kate let him out of the bedroom door and off he went.

    “It’s been days and she’s barely left that room.” Clint muttered as Nat and Laura joined him on the landing, voice hushed as the three exchanged worried glances. “We can’t keep her in the dark forever.”

    Laura nodded; her gaze fixed on the closed door. She leant back against the banister, looking down the stairs to make sure none of the kids were in close proximity. “She’s just lost her mom. Telling her all of this right now might not be the best thing to do. It’s a lot for anyone to handle and she’s already shutting herself off, let alone add a crap ton more on top of what she is already dealing with.”

    “The idea for her to come here was to let her be safe whilst she healed, not hide indefinitely.” Nat argued.

    “I think Yelena would very much like her to remain hidden.” Laura mumbled taking Clint and Nat by surprise. At their startled looks she continued, “I spoke to Sonya. She is under the impression Yelena would burn the world down before she sees Kate get hurt again.” “Yelena is also kidding herself if she thinks she can make that one stay away from the fight.” Clint pointed towards the door in front of them. Clint ran a hand through his hair, conflicted by the desire to shield Kate from pain and the realization that is too stubborn to not go into battle headfirst. “She’s as stubborn as they come.”

    “Speaking of stubborn, has anyone spoken to моя сестра?” Nat asked out of curiosity. The couple beside her shook their heads in unison, the silence reverberating across the landing.

    “Has Steve made any progress?” Laura questioned the two Avengers of the group. “He got in contact with Bucky and by happenstance, Sam was with him. I think Bucky had some contacts he was going to call in favours for but that is the last I heard.” Nat shrugged noncommittally, uncertainty clouding her features.

    The uneasy silence settled over the landing as the trio exchanged concerned glances. The weight of their shared worries hung in the air like a thick fog. Laura looked Nat up and down before a sigh left her mouth. Nat looked at her confusedly, not missing the subtle scrutiny. “Is your sister anything like you in terms of impulsivity?” Laura questioned the redhead somewhat light-heartedly, though the gravity of the situation lingered beneath her words. “You think she’s gone after them solo?” Clint muttered, crossing his arms. "Yelena can be impulsive but she’s not stupid. She's always had her own way of doing things. She's not a carbon copy of me, but then again, she could’ve changed her ways since I knew her. And I don’t know what she’s capable of doing when it comes to Kate.” “Do you think it’s likely?”

    “It wouldn’t surprise me if she had. But going up against these people alone? That’s reckless, even for her. Моя маленькая сестра fights on instinct. From what we know, these people have made no active move on Kate since we left the city, she’d have no motive to make such a rash move.” Nat spoke bluntly.

    Laura, feeling a growing sense of urgency, suggested, "Maybe we should ask Kate if she's heard from Yelena. If Yelena reached out to her, Kate might have some insight into what's going on."

    “If Yelena has taken matters into her own hands, we need to find her before things escalate further." Clint said, as he headed towards Kate’s bedroom door, the two women heading for the top of the stairs.

    Kate had just reburied her head in her pillow, trying to block out the voices, when a knock sounded at her door. The brunette huffed before Lucky rolled out of her space and jumped of the bed. He pawed heavily at the door handle until it swung open, and Kate couldn’t help but groan at her all-too-clever dog.

    The door creaked open, revealing Clint, who entered the room with a quiet resolve, shutting the door behind him. Lucky darted towards him, tail wagging, offering a momentary distraction before the man approached Kate’s bedside with a comforting smile. “Mind if I sit kiddo?”

    Kate motioned to the empty space on the bed where Lucky had vacated. After Clint had sat down, Lucky must’ve felt rather left out. Sensing the need for his comforting presence, he jumped back up and settled between them. His head found a place on Kate's lap, and she absentmindedly ran her fingers through his fur as a small, grateful smile played on her lips. Clint studied Kate’s face. She looked exhausted. This made the worry in Clint swirl in his stomach even more. The kid hadn’t moved further than the hall bathroom since she’d been here. The dark circles under her eyes were heavy, and her neck was still lightly mottled from her run in with Kingpin.

    “If you came in here to lecture me… I am going to let you know that I will not be listening to a word of it.” Kate’s words were muffled into her pillow, but Clint heard them clear enough. “No lecture kid. Just a question for you.” He approached the bed with a knowing look, understanding the mix of frustration and exhaustion that fuelled Kate's defiant tone. “In that case, shoot.”

    “Have you heard anything from Yelena? Any idea where she might be?"

    “She’s in Russia.” Kate's head turned slightly, her eyes meeting Clint's. “Anything more than what we already know?” Clint questioned further, the look in Kate’s eye already telling him she wasn’t going to tell even if she did know. “I heard you talking on the landing.” The brunette’s tone even and unapologetic. “How much did you hear?”

    “All of it.”

    “So?”

    “She’s in Russia.” Kate reiterated, her response stubborn and resolute. “Kate.” Clint said frustratedly.

    “Clint.” Kate mirrored, the unspoken understanding passing between them. Yelena and Kate’s isolation from the rest of the group had added another layer of complexity to an already precarious situation, and both knew there were more questions than answers. Clint studied the brunette as she sat up and leant against the headboard. Her expression was guarded which was unusual, especially for being here at the farm, and because Kate was pretty much an open book.

    “We need more than that kiddo. What’s Yelena doing in Russia? And why the secrecy?” “She’s at her parents place.” Kate sighed exasperatedly. “Telling them that their daughter is back from the dead and all that jazz.” The brunette continued after a hesitant pause. Clint arched an eyebrow at the revelation. He guessed it made sense, but he did wonder why she hadn’t taken Nat with her. He understood that reuniting with family, especially after the kind of life Yelena led, wasn't a simple affair and even more so telling her parents that their other daughter was mysteriously resurrected.

    "Melina and Alexei?" Clint asked, trying to wrap his head around the situation. "How are they taking it? Why didn’t she take Natasha with her?”

    “I haven’t spoken to her.” Kate shrugged, finally revealing the piece of information Clint had been after. “Yelena’s always been guarded about her family. And given everything else that is going on, I think she needed to get away and deal with it on her own terms.” Clint nodded slowly, processing the hidden meaning in Kate’s words of Yelena wanting space away from Natasha. Silence fell between them, the weight of the situation still lingering in the air. Clint broke the quiet with a sigh.

    “You know her best kiddo. Do you think she’d go after these people alone?” “Clint. This is Yelena we’re talking about. She’s been doing this practically since she was born. If she has gone alone, she’d be fine.” Kate’s lips curled into a half smile. “She’s not invincible kid. She’s as human as you and me.”

    “Yelena's got connections, Clint. More than you even. She’s resourceful. If she's going after these people, she’s not going alone.” The brunette said confidently.

    “What makes you so sure?”

    “Because I know Yelena.” Kate said with a small grin.

    “That look on your face doesn’t fill me with confidence Kate.”

    "It's Yelena we're talking about, Clint," Kate said, her earlier exasperation giving way to a spark of humour. "She's not exactly one for subtlety - around here anyways. If she was about to go on a murderous rampage, she would make sure we knew about it.” Kate chuckled, a mix of pride and amusement in her eyes.

    Clint just sighed making Kate let out a small chuckle, before she slumped back down in her bed again.

    “Any requests for dinner?”

    “I’m not hungry. But Lucky told me wants pizza.”

    Clint found Laura and Nat in the kitchen, cups of tea in their hands, while they watched the kids play out of the window. The faint sounds of laughter and the sight of his three children running around offered a brief respite from the lingering conversation with Kate. The kitchen felt warm and inviting, a contrast to the tension that lingered upstairs. With the information Clint had just obtained from Kate, he approached Laura and Nat, his expression serious. They glanced up, their eyes meeting Clint's, sensing that something had shifted.

    "Anything?" Laura inquired, her tone a mix of curiosity and concern.

    She's in Russia, at your parents' place.” Clint nodded to Nat, “Apparently, she needed some space." Clint sighed, taking a moment before responding.

    Natasha's gaze narrowed, her instincts kicking in. "Space from what?"

    "Seems like she wanted some distance from everything, especially from the compound and maybe... from you." Clint explained, the unspoken implication hanging in the air as it left his mouth.

    Laura exchanged a quick look with Natasha, realizing the added layer of complexity in the situation. "That doesn't sound good."

    "Kate doesn’t seem worried, but she also didn’t confirm if Yelena thinks she can handle things on her own." Clint added. “She’s gone to Russia to tell your parent’s you’re back Nat.” "I would not want to have that conversation with those two if the shoe was on the other foot. But I know she won’t tell Melina and Alexei a thing about the situation either to even get their help." Natasha frowned, a hint of frustration in her voice. “I don’t care if she hates my guts, I don’t want her to die because of a stupid decision.”

    “The pot is calling the kettle black.” Clint said in between coughs, earning himself a glare from the redhead across from him.

    “That was different.”

    “Was it?” Clint questioned rhetorically, his gaze meeting Nat’s with a knowing look. The room fell into a long silence.

    Having endured days of Kate's persistent silence at her parents' house, Yelena finally reached the point of frustration. The blonde executed her quickly thought of escape plan in the early hours of the morning. She bid a quiet farewell to Melina, who was always an early riser and then with stealth worthy of her assassin training, the blonde slipped out before Alexei could rouse from his slumber and convince her to extend her stay.

    Yelena swiftly procured a car from the nearest town. The engine purred to life as the roads stretched out before her, an endless ribbon of asphalt winding through landscapes both familiar and unknown. Yelena, her mind buzzing with thoughts of the strained silence left behind, drove with purpose, determined to confront the issues plaguing her mind. The stolen car became a vessel of contemplation as Yelena replayed the scenes of the past week in her mind. Yelena navigated the dimly lit streets towards an undisclosed location, her turns swift and purposeful. The air inside and out the car carried a chill, but her determination warmed her from the inside.

    The car rocked as it fought its way up the incline until she reached a secluded spot where a shadowed figure waited. At the overlook of a rolling hill in the vast expanses of Russia, Yelena found herself standing against the brisk wind, her gaze fixed on the sprawling landscape below. The endless plains stretched out like an untamed canvas, a mosaic of greens and browns merging seamlessly under the azure sky. They were tinted with white as a brief snowfall had hit the night before, but not enough to cover the ground. That would happen once Yelena was long gone.

    It was in this desolate place that Yelena found Rick Mason, the arms dealer whose shadowy connections and discreet services made him a valuable ally.

    Rick leaned against a sleek, unmarked plane, a sly grin on his face as Yelena approached. “Tsarina! Missed me, did you?"

    "Save the banter, Mason. I'm here for a plane, not you." Yelena rolled her eyes, a smirk playing on her lips and a hint of amusement betraying her stoic exterior. "You're never any fun. You know that right? But alright, let's talk business.” “Put it on Nat’s tab.” Yelena shrugged as she walked towards the plane, running a hand along its smooth side.

    “How is she?” Rick responded with a sly smirk, his tone teasing.

    Yelena held back her scoff. She should’ve known the news would have reached Rick’s ears somehow. This man always seems to know everything. A trait that simultaneously impressed and annoyed her.

    “Fine.”

    "Sure, sure. She sounded great when she phoned and asked if I had seen you recently.” Rick raised an eyebrow, his grin widening.

    “Что ты ей сказал?”

    “Relax, Tsarina. I told her nothing. Where is this plane headed off to? New York?” The man teased as he walked into the plane, fiddling with buttons on the control panel. His eyes ever glistening. Rick had given Yelena many a plane to field to New York over the past 10 months.

    Yelena ignored him as she lugged her bags up the ramp, Fanny following close on her heels as she bounded out of the car. Rick gave the dog a quick hello before holding out a hand for one of the bags the blonde was holding. She dropped it in his arms, leaving herself a free hand to open the storage box and put the rest of the ones in her arms into it without bother. “I am headed to the Barton’s if you must know.” Yelena said as she settled Fanny into the co- pilots seat, strapping her in to be triple sure of her safety.

    Rick's eyebrows shot up in mock surprise. "Ah, the infamous Barton farm. I've heard some interesting rumours about you and the said archer's protégé. Anything I should know?" "Don't believe everything you hear. Rumours mean nothing.” Yelena scowled at Rick's teasing, her cheeks flushing slightly.

    "Alright, alright. No need to get all defensive. But, in case you're interested in some other rumours, I've got some news for you."

    "Spill." Yelena arched an eyebrow, a rare sign of genuine curiosity.

    Rick leaned against the back of Fanny’s chair as Yelena sat in the pilot’s seat, firing up the plane’s engines, his tone lowered into a conspiratorial whisper.

    "Word is, Valentina has some new recruits.” Rick casually mentioned as he continued to assist Yelena with the plane.

    Yelena's eyes narrowed, the news grabbing her attention. She paused in her preparations, turning to face Rick with a mix of curiosity and suspicion. "I have no business with Valentina," she said shortly and with a hint of disgust.

    “I just provide the info. Thought you’d like to keep tabs on her. She’s not someone you so simply cut ties with.” Rick shrugged, a nonchalant grin on his face. He leaned against the plane, crossing his arms, as if he were sharing gossip rather than discussing potential threats. Yelena's expression remained unreadable, but the cogs in her mind were turning. Yelena knew better than to underestimate Valentina. The woman operated in the shadows, pulling strings, and manipulating events to suit her agenda. She was as much of a threat as Dreykov had been and the blonde knew if Val was up to something, it was not going to end well for anyone involved.

    "What's her game now?" Yelena inquired, her tone betraying a reluctant curiosity. "Who knows? But if there's one thing Valentina loves, it's power. She's got her fingers in a lot of pies, and I'm just one messenger delivering the slices." Rick spoke, his nonchalance unwavering.

    Yelena scoffed, a mixture of frustration and resignation. The last thing she needed was another layer of complexity to an already intricate situation.

    "When you get the details, send them over. I'll look into it."

    "You're a real charmer, Tsarina. Just remember, Valentina plays the game better than most." Rick chuckled, seemingly amused by Yelena's stoicism. “Oh, and bring Kate Bishop around soon. I’d so love to meet the woman who… tamed the infamous Yelena Belova.” He exaggerated.

    “I am not an animal Mason.” Yelena scowled and she crossed her arms defensively. “Come on, Yelena. Let me have my spy romance novel fantasy. The brooding assassin and the sharp-archer – it’s a match made in action movie heaven!” Rick, undeterred by Yelena's dismissive response, straightened up with a grin.

    Yelena’s scowl deepened at the persistent teasing. As if her and Kate could ever be afforded the luxury of a life like a movie, let alone one with such outlandish ideas about romance. Yelena didn’t love.

    Yelena couldn’t love.

    It’s not what she was made for.

    Rick having noticed the look on the blonde’s face held his hands up in mock surrender. “Alright, alright. I’m sorry I've got a soft spot for unconventional love stories." He said sarcastically, his tone still light and teasing.

    “Get off my plane Mason.” Yelena's expression remained unyielding, her irritation evident. "Sure thing, Tsarina. But if you ever decide to spice up the drama in your life, I want to be the first to know." Rick chuckled, seemingly unbothered by Yelena's stern tone. Rick departed after this, not without a flashing her one last teasing smile, leaving Yelena to finish her preparations with a mix of exasperation and bemusement.

    As the blonde took to the skies, the prospect of bringing Kate around for a meeting with the eccentric information broker lingered in the back of her mind. Despite her resistance to Rick's playful suggestions, a part of Yelena couldn't deny the curiosity about how their worlds might collide. The same thought occurring in relation to her parents also. Their world was steeped in complex history and was one Yelena had always kept at arm’s length, even from Sonya. The prospect of suddenly merging different facets of her life and introducing Kate to her parents felt like one of the intricate dances they’d been taught in the Red Room. She couldn’t predict the outcome if she put a step wrong, but the idea of allowing the most important groups of people in her life to coalesce both intrigued and unnerved her. Yelena's mind wandered between the complexities of her relationships – the unexpected bond with Natasha, the burgeoning connection with Kate, and the distant but undeniable tie to her parents. Yelena had been moulded into a weapon and trained to operate in the shadows, and yet now she found herself navigating the murkiness of her emotions and most personal connections. It was a journey she hadn't anticipated, one that challenged the very core of her beliefs. And all it was doing was proving Melina’s perspective of her nature, that she was not a fighter. The blonde felt as if this one simple trip to Russia had rocked her entire world of its axis.

    The notion of love had always been foreign to Yelena. For most of her life, she honed her skills in combat and precision. And although these may be similar to the concept of love in terms of its intricate complexities and vulnerabilities, love still very much felt like an intangible concept to the blonde. It had been something she had observed from afar, but never dared embrace for herself.

    Yelena, even with two loving parents and a sister, couldn’t shake the belief that she wasn’t made for love. The very skin that covered her bones seemed to run with blood filled with detachment and resilience, both qualities that made her excel in the harsh world she had grown up in, but the first made her mind believe love was a luxury she couldn’t afford. It was a weakness, a vulnerability waiting to be exploited.

    To love means to care, and the more you care, the more you have to lose. It meant to willingly expose oneself to pain, and pain was a hand she had been dealt all too often.

    She had convinced herself that love was not what she was made for.

    However, as the plane shot through the night sky and the hum of the engines provided a backdrop to the quiet turbulence within her, Yelena thought hard on recent events. The unexpected resurrection of Natasha, her sister who she had loved more than anyone in the world had stirred emotions within Yelena she thought she had successfully buried. It had exposed vulnerabilities she was unaccustomed to acknowledging.

    And then there was the undeniable bond she had found within a plucky archer who alone challenged the very foundation of Yelena’s carefully constructed beliefs and convictions. Kate Bishop had broken into Yelena’s life in the most unexpected of ways and her sharp wit and stubborn spirit had become both a source of frustration and fascination for the blonde. The brunette was very much an anomaly in the calculated and controlled world Yelena had constructed around herself.

    Amidst the contemplative atmosphere she had created in the aircraft, Yelena felt a yearning for the chance to breath outside of her head and for a touch of light-heartedness. The blonde’s gaze shifted to Fanny who was still sat contentedly in the cockpit, her eyes firmly fixed out the windscreen on the passing sky on all sides of them.

    A playful idea sparked in Yelena’s mind as she watched her companion quietly, and a small smile tugged at the corners of her lips as she retrieved her phone from her pocket. The dim light within the plane played on the gleaming surface of aviator goggles she had noticed earlier. They sat on the side of the control panel, and Yelena couldn’t resist her temptation. She grabbed them before approaching Fanny, who broke her gaze on the sky to look at her with curious eyes. The dog was practically the embodiment of canine innocence. The googles soon found themselves delicately positioned atop Fanny’s head, with her blinking in momentary confusion. It didn’t last long as she caught sight of the moon out of the window again and this seemed to distract the akita from her new role as pilot. Yelena quickly snapped a candid shot of Fanny looking remarkably ridiculous with aviator goggles perched on her furry head.

    Opening up her text chain with Kate, Yelena sighed.

    Kate? No crazy stories from the Barton’s this time?

    Kate Bishop?

    Please tell me Lucky didn’t eat your phone, that would be unfortunate. I’m taking your silence as confirmation this in fact happened (Hi Lucky’s stomach!) Hey Kate, quick question: do you think Lucky would be interested in a career change? I hear there's an opening for a superhero dog model. We just need to work on his smouldering gaze and heroic stance.

    The jobs been booked now. Hope you’re happy with yourself. I’m sure Lucky will be devastated when he hears the news.

    Kate Bishop?

    I think Alexei the Pig just stole my sandwich. I think he’s trying to establish dominance in the chemically subjugated secret agent hierarchy. I might need backup.

    The brunette had not answered a single one of her texts since they had been separated from one another. Yelena could see they had been delivered, but not a single one had been read. Sending the picture to Kate, Yelena added yet another playful message alongside it. Is Lucky on strike as your personal secretary? Did he accidentally delete your entire inbox, or is he just holding out for better treat incentives? Maybe Captain Fanny can negotiate a peace treaty with him – I heard she's a skilled diplomat when she's not busy piloting planes. Yelena smirked to herself, imagining Kate's reaction to the canine pilot antics. The mental image of Kate's raised eyebrows and amused expression brought a subtle warmth to Yelena's otherwise focused demeanour. It would only be a couple more hours till she touched down in Iowa and then Kate had no choice but to talk to her.

    Once Clint had left the room, Kate pulled her phone into view. The brunette had not looked at her phone all week, not wanting to deal with the incoming calls from lawyers, and journalists, nor from the funeral directors, or her aunt or Jack.

    With a hesitant sigh, Kate unlocked the screen, her eyes immediately noticing the avalanche of notifications waiting to be acknowledged. The sight of missed calls, voicemails, and unread messages sent a wave of apprehension through her. She scrolled through the overwhelming sea of alerts, each one a reminder of the life-altering events that had transpired.

    A mixture of guilt and exhaustion settled in the pit of her stomach as she saw the names and numbers that demanded her attention. The legal matters surrounding her mother's estate seemed to have multiplied in her absence. Lawyers were vying for her time, and journalists sought statements that she wasn't ready to give.

    Her aunt's one missed call stood out, an echo of the limited family connections and unspoken emotions. Kate felt a pang of guilt for avoiding the one effort her aunt had made, but the weight of her grief had kept her submerged in a sea of solitude.

    The funeral director's number blinked ominously, a reminder of the inevitable finality that awaited her. Kate took a deep breath, recognizing that she couldn't delay these responsibilities forever. With a hesitant touch, she pressed the voicemail icon, bracing herself for the barrage of voices that would soon flood her ears.

    As the first message played, Kate's gaze flickered to the untouched messages from Yelena and the voice coming from her phones speakers faded into the background. The familiar thread of light-hearted banter and playful exchanges seemed incongruent with the sombre atmosphere that surrounded her. Kate found herself in a delicate balance, standing on the precipice of a reality that demanded her attention while yearning for the brief respite that a few text messages could offer.
