    With a heavy heart, Kate pressed play on the voicemails left by Jack. She had not spoken to him since she had found out about her mother’s death despite his best efforts. Each message carried a weight of concern and love, Jack's voice a mixture of compassion and familial warmth. As the messages played, Kate found herself alternating between gratitude for the support and an overwhelming sense of guilt for having kept him at arm's length during what couldn’t have been an easy time for her mom’s fiancé either.

    Or is it now ex-fiancé?

    Amidst the expressions of condolences and offers of assistance, one particular voicemail stood out. Jack's voice held a tentative yet hopeful note as he shared an idea that both surprised and touched Kate. He spoke of wanting to hold the Bishop Christmas party in memory of her mother, a celebration of life amid the sombre reality of her recent passing. Kate's heart swelled with a bittersweet mix of emotions. The thought of the annual family gathering, now taking on a poignant meaning in her mother's absence, was both heartwarming and heartbreaking. It was a testament to Jack's attempt to bring light into the darkness that had settled over the Bishop family and yet Kate couldn’t feel anything but the usual dread she had for such events. The offer of a Christmas party in memory of her mother felt like a lifeline, a way to navigate the upcoming holidays without succumbing entirely to grief.

    After all, Kate could not intrude at the Barton’s for Christmas again. She had done so last year, and the warmth of the Barton family had helped her cope with what she had experienced in the week building up to the holiday.

    However, this year was different. The idea of joining the Bartons for Christmas, even with what she was sure would be a heavily extended invitation, felt like an intrusion into a space that had once welcomed her but was now overshadowed by the heavy clouds of grief. Plus, she had already intruded enough this past week, let alone do the same when next month rolled around too.

    As she battled her mind and tried to pay attention to Jack’s ramblings, another text from Yelena pinged through to her phone. Tapping on the notification, Kate's screen illuminated with an image of Fanny, , donning aviator goggles. The unexpected sight brought a brief but genuine smile to Kate's face, momentarily diverting her attention from the heavy thoughts that had consumed her.

    The sight of the canine pilot, coupled with Yelena’s playful caption, momentarily transported Kate into a realm where laughter and joy could coexist with her sorrow. It was in that moment of introspection that she realized Yelena had been worried about her. Scrolling through the unanswered text chain, Kate couldn't ignore the evidence of genuine concern that threaded through each message. The realization hit her with a gentle force. Yelena cared enough to worry about her well-being, to reach out repeatedly despite the lack of response. It struck Kate that the blonde had broken her own unspoken rule of double texting and the brunette let a smile take over her face.

    As Kate contemplated the text chain, she couldn't help but appreciate the sincerity in Yelena's attempts to bring a touch of levity into her life. The playful banter, the amusing pictures of Fanny, all of it was a concerted effort to bridge the gap that had emerged during Kate's isolation in grief. The unspoken understanding that Yelena had breached her own rules for the sake of checking on Kate and the significance of that didn’t escape the brunette. Kate couldn’t help herself as she took a closer look at the picture before responding with a brief message… or three.

    Captain Fanny for the win! Forget superheroes, we've got a four-legged aviator ready to take on the world.

    I hope she's got the landing gear paw-fected ;)

    I’m going to start writing her a theme song right now.

    Chapter 18

    Chapter Notes hi hi hi enjoy!

    The small aircraft descended gracefully, touching down in a secluded clearing surrounded by the quiet embrace of nature. Yelena and Fanny, the latter still adorned in aviator goggles, disembarked from the plane. The brisk morning air greeted them as they surveyed the serene landscape. Yelena had chosen the landing spot strategically, ensuring a stealthy approach to the Barton residence just in case anyone was following her.

    Yelena contemplated her next move as she studied her surroundings, the idea of stealing a car crossed her mind. However, the thought of parking a stolen vehicle on the driveway of an Avenger's house didn't sit well with her. She envisioned the awkward conversation that would follow, and it was enough to dissuade her from that particular plan.

    Laden with bags and supplies, they set off on foot, traversing the mile or two that separated the clearing from the Barton's house. The early morning sun cast long shadows, painting the landscape in hues of gold and amber as they navigated the quiet countryside. The pair would’ve landed whilst the time could’ve still been considered night, but Mason pointedly left out the information of the planes rather terrible fuel efficiency, meaning the blonde had had to stop to refuel about just over halfway into her journey, so Yelena had stopped for a couple of hours to allow time for the refuelling but also to let Fanny stretch her legs. Yelena couldn't help but appreciate the unexpected beauty of the walk. The tranquillity of the surroundings offered a stark contrast to the chaos and danger that often accompanied her missions. She supposed that is why Barton had decided to live here. Iowa was a stark difference from the Avenger Compound. The blonde snorted to herself as she realised the unintentional pun. Fanny trotted alongside her, tail wagging, seemingly unfazed by the unknown surroundings passing by her furry head.

    The path to the Barton's house stretched out before them, a winding trail through the tranquil countryside. Yelena's senses were on high alert as they moved stealthily through the early morning mist, the only sound the soft crunch of leaves beneath their feet. As they neared their destination, the first rays of dawn began to paint the sky with hues of pink and gold. Yelena felt a surge of anticipation as she approached, her heart pounding with a mixture of excitement and apprehension. When the Barton's house came into view, a welcoming beacon amidst the quiet countryside, the blonde marvelled at the quaint charm it possessed. The warm glow of lights hinted at the early stirrings of the household, but Yelena assumed it was probably only Laura awake.

    After making their way up the driveway, Yelena and Fanny stepped up onto the front porch. Yelena surveyed the area before knocking gently on the door, the anticipation building within her. As it swung open, revealing a surprised but welcoming Laura Barton, Yelena couldn't help but let a small smile appear on her face. The expression on Laura's face shifted from curiosity to recognition, her eyes widening with genuine surprise.

    "Yelena," Laura exclaimed, the astonishment evident in her voice. "And who is this?” The woman smiled as she reached down to pet the sitting dog by Yelena’s feet. “This is Fanny. Do not worry, she is much better behaved than Lucky.” Yelena chuckled, a glint of mischief in her eyes.

    Laura's laughter resonated through the doorway, and she stepped aside, gesturing for Yelena and Fanny to enter. The familiar scent of the Barton home greeted them, a comforting blend of warmth and familial love. As Yelena crossed the threshold, she took in the familiar surroundings, her eyes landing on the decorations that adorned the living room. Pictures of the couple, and their kids were hung on the walls, along with photos where Natasha appeared in them too. There were the odd couple of frames that had silly photos of the Avengers and various others with people Yelena did not recognise. She assumed these were more Barton family members.

    The aroma of brewing coffee and the quiet sounds of morning filled the air as she followed Laura into the kitchen. Yelena felt a sense of ease settle over her. Fanny was not as keen to follow, deciding to sniff every object in her vicinity. The dog's exploration took on an almost investigative quality, as if she were on a mission to catalogue the scents and secrets of the Barton household.

    Laura chuckled, watching the scene unfold.

    Yelena couldn't help but join in the laughter, appreciating the levity that Fanny brought to the moment. "She's just making sure everything is up to her standards," Yelena remarked, the subtle playfulness in her tone mirroring the antics of the inquisitive canine. Laura gestured to the table, but Yelena shook her head, preferring her spot leaning against the kitchen counter instead. The older woman in the room just smiled as she turned back to the coffee machine, handing Yelena the first mug that finished before taking the second for herself.

    “What brings you here so early?" Laura inquired with a genuine curiosity. Yelena considered Laura’s question as she took a sip of her hot drink. "Needed a change of scenery," the blonde eventually replied with a wry smile and a small shrug. Laura raised an eyebrow, her expression inviting further explanation. Yelena continued, her gaze momentarily flickering to the window. “Melina and Alexei are a lot.” The blonde groaned out, her words carrying a hint of vulnerability compared to her usual demeanour around the Barton woman.

    Laura nodded in understanding, appreciating the unspoken complexities behind Yelena's simple statement. The acknowledgment of the challenges posed by Yelena's family members provided a glimpse into the intricacies of her life, underscoring the person that hid beneath her stoic exterior.

    "I can imagine. Even the most normal family dynamics can be... intense," Laura replied with a knowing smile, her own experiences colouring the understanding in her eyes. As they shared a quiet moment, the sound of hushed morning conversations and the occasional clink of utensils in the kitchen created a comforting backdrop. Yelena leaned back, her exhaustion evident despite the early hour. A yawn escaped her, betraying the toll that her journey had taken on her.

    "The rest of the family is still asleep. You look like you could use some rest too honey.” Laura, sensing the weariness in Yelena, gently suggested.

    Yelena nodded appreciatively, grateful for the kindness extended by the Barton family. Laura continued, updating Yelena on what had transpired with Kate during her stay, the challenges she faced, and the resilient spirit she displayed. Laura outlined them with a compassionate precision that conveyed both empathy and concern.

    "Kate's finally been dealing with the aftermath of her mother's passing," Laura explained, her tone reflective of the weight of the situation. "It’s hit her hard, as you can imagine. The funeral arrangements, legal matters, and the constant influx of calls from lawyers and journalists—it's been overwhelming. She's been avoiding everyone. She’s barely left her bedroom since she’s been here. She’s not been eating much either.”

    "Then there's the matter of Kingpin," Laura continued, her voice lowering as if divulging a secret. "We know he’s been making moves, and Kate's caught in the crossfire. But if she's been specifically targeted for a reason, then the threat is more significant than I think she realizes. Steve's been trying to get more information, but it's been a challenge." Yelena's brows furrowed slightly at the mention of Kingpin, the gravity of the situation becoming ever clearer. The dangerous dance between Kate and powerful adversaries added a layer of urgency to Yelena's need to tell Kate about her parents, even though it was a conversation the blonde wanted to put off indefinitely. Yelena's gaze sharpened, determination flickering in her eyes.

    “She will be safe, Laura Barton.” Yelena stated, her commitment unwavering. The with me went unspoken, neither women needed to hear it to know what the blonde meant. Laura couldn't help but smile at Yelena's bravado, appreciating the fierce loyalty that underscored her words. "I have no doubt about that," Laura replied, her own confidence in Yelena evident.

    “She’s more capable than I think we all realise sometimes.” Yelena said quietly a moment later.

    “Just don't let her catch wind of you calling her 'capable.' She’ll never let us hear the end of it." Laura added with a playful glint in her eye.

    Yelena's face softened into a smirk, acknowledging the teasing. "She can be a handful, but that's what makes her interesting." Yelena replied with a small shrug, her tone carrying a mix of amusement and genuine affection.

    Laura chuckled softly. "Interesting, huh? You're quite fond of her, aren't you?" she teased, a knowing smile on her lips.

    “She's...different." Yelena admitted, her voice softening. Yelena's expression turned slightly more contemplative, her eyes reflecting the depth of her connection with Kate. She didn’t know why she was sharing so much with Laura, it was just something about the woman that drew you in.

    "Well, I'm glad she's got someone like you looking out for her," Laura said warmly, her affection for both Kate and Yelena evident in her words. Laura smiled in understanding, recognizing the sentiment behind Yelena's words.

    When the blonde yawned again, it seemed like Laura Barton had officially had enough of watching Yelena struggle.

    “How about I show you where you can get some shut eye?" Laura suggested, her maternal instincts shining through.

    "I could use a good nap before I deal with your husband.” Yelena admitted, a hint of a smirk playing on her lips. Laura chuckled in response.

    “First room on the left is Nat’s or end of the hallway on the right is Kate’s.” Laura whispered as they headed up the stairs, bags in hand. “Or I can set up the pull-out down in the basement if you prefer. It’s up to you honey.” The soft sounds of their footsteps echoed in the quiet house.

    Yelena considered the options, appreciating Laura's thoughtful suggestions, weighing the comfort of each against the desire for closeness to Kate.

    The choice was clear in her mind.

    "I'll share with Kate." she decided, her voice barely above a whisper.

    Laura nodded in understanding, a warm smile spreading across her face. "Alright, I'll leave you to it then. If you need anything, just let me know," she whispered back before gently squeezing Yelena's shoulder in reassurance. "Yelena, having you here will mean the world to her," Laura said as she turned to leave, a motherly warmth in her eyes. Yelena returned the smile gratefully, feeling a sense of belonging in the Barton household that she hadn't expected. She hadn’t even flinched as Laura touched her and the blonde figured that must mean something. As Laura headed back downstairs, Yelena made her way to Kate's room, the weight of her decision lifting with each step she took towards the brunette.

    Yelena pushed open the bedroom door, almost immediately getting knocked over by a very excitable Lucky. His wagging tail and joyful barks filled the room, a clear sign that he was thrilled to have her company. Yelena chuckled, realizing that Lucky could probably smell Fanny on her, making her an instant hit with the energetic pup.

    "Легкий, Lucky! I missed you too.” Yelena laughed, scratching behind his ears as he continued to express his delight with boundless energy. The blonde opened the bedroom door once more after he’d gotten all his wiggles out, the golden retriever darting out of the room, his tail still wagging with unbridled excitement.

    With Lucky occupied, Yelena took a moment to change into comfier clothes, shedding the weight of the day's journey for a more relaxed attire. The blonde then made the couple step journey to Kate’s bed, where the archer lay peacefully asleep. Her front was to the wall, the covers pulled tightly around her. Yelena couldn't help but feel a sense of tenderness toward the slumbering archer.

    Careful not to disturb Kate, Yelena slipped into the bed behind the brunette and under the covers not wrapped around her body, eventually finding a comfortable spot beside her. The blonde turned on her side, so she was facing Kate’s back, her gaze lingering on the side of Kate’s sleeping face and a soft smile played on her lips.

    As the quiet moments passed, Yelena felt a sense of calm settle over her. The steady breathing of the sleeping archer, the distant sounds of Lucky and Fanny's playful antics downstairs, Yelena allowed herself to close her eyes, her exhaustion washing away. Yelena found herself slipping in and out of a drowsy state, in tune with the rhythm of Kate's steady breathing. Yelena sleepily shifted, feeling an instinctive pull to be closer to Kate. The blonde draped an arm over Kate’s waist, her hand landing on the brunette’s lower stomach.

    Clint descended the stairs, muttering his normal good morning to his wife, kissing her cheek as he passed her on the way to the coffee machine. The enticing aroma of freshly brewed coffee filled the kitchen, coaxing him further into wakefulness.

    The archer still in the semi-daze of early morning failed to notice the extra presence in the room. His three kids were sat around the dining table, all dressed and ready to head out to school. It was only Cooper still slurping his milk from his cereal bowl, Lila watching on with a face of disgust. Nate had his head under the table, talking a load of nonsense to Lucky who was happy to entertain the young boy in hopes he’d get any scraps of breakfast dropped down to him.

    Fanny was sat beside the front door, her head on her paws as she lay over the vent that sat there, the warm air obviously being something the akita was a big fan of. It took a beat for Clint's groggy mind to register the unexpected second dog in his morning routine. His eyes widened, and he blinked in surprise, momentarily forgetting the coffee in his hand as his eyes landed on the new addition. Fanny lifted her head up and titled it slightly before placing it back down unbothered.

    Laura couldn't contain her laughter at Clint's befuddled expression.

    “Where did the second dog come from?” Clint quipped, scratching the back of his head in his confusion.

    Laura chuckled before taking a sip of her coffee. "Oh, you missed the grand entrance this morning. Yelena flew in with Fanny in tow," she explained, a mischievous glint in her eyes. Clint's eyebrows shot up in surprise. "Yelena is here? As in, in our house? Right now? he asked incredulously.

    Laura nodded, enjoying the opportunity to fill Clint in on the morning's events. “That is what I said dear yes. She’s here.”

    Clint blinked, processing the information.

    “I guess she's here to stay?" he asked, a hint of amusement in his voice. "Seems like it. The Barton household just got a bit more interesting, and I wouldn't have it any other way." Laura nodded, her smile widening. “We did extend the invite.” She added as somewhat of an afterthought to evaporate any lasting shock Clint had left in him. The man hummed in response as he made a show of downing the last of his coffee before rounding up the kids and getting them out of the door. Laura joined in the bustling morning routine, helping to gather backpacks, ensuring lunchboxes were packed, and giving each child a quick peck on the cheek before they headed out for the day.

    "Alright, everyone in the car." Clint called out, herding the kids towards the waiting vehicle, pointedly ignoring Nate’s protests that they couldn’t possibly leave the new dog home alone. His argument was that he was the only one she liked and that he had to be there with her. Laura followed, nudging Nate into the back seat, ensuring Fanny would be just fine, her efficient multitasking skills evident as she ensured everyone was settled before climbing into the driver's seat. With a glance at Clint, she flashed a quick smile.

    "Ready for a grocery run after drop-off?" she asked, the morning sun casting a warm glow on her face.

    The man groaned.

    He hated shopping.

    Nat woke up at around 9am, the house quiet as she stepped out of her bedroom and headed down to the kitchen. Feeling a sense of calm in the quiet house, Natasha decided to make herself some toast. The rhythmic sound of the toaster filled the kitchen as she prepared a simple breakfast, the routine a comforting anchor in the midst of the unpredictable life she led. Natasha took a moment to stretch, feeling the tension of sleep slowly dissipate from her muscles. With a contented sigh, she moved to the countertop, the rhythmic clinking of the toaster and the gentle spread of butter on warm bread created a soothing backdrop to the quiet morning.

    As she sat down to eat, enjoying the solitude of the morning, the peaceful atmosphere was suddenly interrupted by the joyful clamour of paws. Lucky and a dog had never laid eyes on before burst through the doggy door, their tails wagging energetically as they bounded into the kitchen. Natasha chuckled at the duo's exuberance, appreciating the lively presence they brought to the quiet house.

    With a plate of toast in front of her, Natasha settled into the chair, savouring the quiet moment. The dogs, seemingly aware of her peaceful breakfast routine, lay down nearby. The redhead rolled her eyes at Lucky as his own eyes were fixed on the bread, waiting for the occasional crumb that might fall.

    Pulling her phone from her pocket, where she had stuffed it whilst still half-asleep, she realised she had a few messages from Clint.

    Don’t worry, Nate did not succeed in his plan to steal the neighbour’s dog. She’s called Fanny and she belongs to your sister.

    Speaking of said sister, she’s upstairs with Kate.

    We’ve gone for groceries. Be back around 10.

    Nat brought her eyes away from the phone to look at the other dog again. Fanny, with her wagging tail and unbothered demeanour, seemed blissfully unaware of the emotional currents swirling in Natasha's thoughts.

    A pang of bittersweet sadness tugged at Natasha's heart. Yelena, her impulsive and unpredictable sister, had managed to fulfil one of her dreams - a dog companion, that looked just like the ones she used to draw with chalk on the pavement when they were little back in Ohio. Natasha couldn't help but feel a twinge of regret that she hadn't been there with her to experience the moment Yelena had gotten the dog.

    As she watched Fanny watch Lucky sniff the kitchen floor with the same face Lila looked at Cooper at whenever he did something that mildly grossed her out, Natasha couldn't deny the depth of her emotions. It was a mix of sorrow for the missed opportunity to share in Yelena's joy and a touch of longing for the days when the sisters shared a closeness with one another. Yet, despite the twinge of melancholy, Natasha couldn't deny the tender touch of affection for the canine companion. Fanny, obviously named after one of Natasha's old aliases - Fanny Longbottom - carried a sentimental weight that resonated with Natasha. The nostalgia wrapped around the dog's name felt like a silent acknowledgment of the sister’s shared history and the love they hold for one another. Even if Yelena seemed to hate her guts right now.

    Natasha, suddenly wanting to lay eyes on her sister for herself, stuffed her phone back in her pocket. After making a quick detour via the dishwasher, the redhead headed up the stairs. The soft sounds of footsteps on the carpeted hallway accompanied Natasha as she approached Kate's bedroom. A gentle knock and then push of the door revealed a scene that caught her off guard. There, in the quiet sanctuary of Kate's room, lay the unexpected tableau of her sister and the archer fast asleep, nestled together in an embrace that seemed to defy everything she knew about Yelena to be true. This included the blonde’s normal aversion to physical touch.

    Natasha's eyes widened in surprise, her gaze taking in the sight of Yelena, a woman who typically detested being touched, curled up behind Kate in an uncharacteristically vulnerable manner. The shock of the scene was replaced by a mixture of curiosity and a subtle warmth that settled in Natasha's chest. Yelena's usual guard was lowered, her defences seemingly forgotten in the solace of sleep, especially seeing as Nat knew any widow would most likely wake up if they sensed someone in their close vicinity. The sight was both endearing and perplexing to Natasha, who couldn't help but marvel at the unexpected intimacy unfolding before her.

    Yelena had her face tucked into Kate’s back; the covers pulled up to her waist. This allowed Nat to slightly see the arm that her sister had flung over the brunette’s waist. The arm draped over Kate's waist seemed to convey a silent reassurance from the blonde and Natasha was eager to see if there was a change in Kate when the two woke up.

    In that quiet bedroom, Natasha found herself contemplating the depth of her sister's connection with Kate. It was a connection that transcended the boundaries Yelena had erected around herself. The archer seemed to provide a sanctuary that even Yelena, with all her strength and resilience, sought in moments of rest.

    Deciding to leave them undisturbed, Natasha quietly retreated from the room, closing the door with a soft click.

    Kate blinked sleepily; the world still hazy as she lifted her head slightly off the pillow. The wall was mottled with rays of sun trying to blast their way through the closed curtains, indicating it was probably rather late in the day. The brunette put her head back on the pillow as she slowly lulled back into sleep again.

    But sleep wouldn’t come again.

    As her consciousness gradually hit her, Kate became aware of the weight pressed against her back. Confusion flickered in her still groggy mind. It wasn’t Lucky, otherwise she’d have slobber all over her shoulder like most mornings. The brunette turned her head, only to be met with the tousled blonde hair of none of than an asleep Yelena Belova. The realization hit her with a shock, and her eyes widened in surprise. Blinking away the remnants of sleep, Kate squinted at the sleeping figure beside her. Yelena lay there, peacefully oblivious to the waking world, her arm draped over Kate's waist. It was a sight that elicited a range of emotions in the archer - shock, curiosity, and a subtle warmth that spread through her like a warm drink on cold day.

    The surprise had jolted Kate awake, dispelling the remnants of drowsiness in an instant. Her heart raced as she struggled to comprehend the situation. Yelena, who had seemingly appeared out of nowhere, lay there as if she belonged, her presence a sudden and unexpected intrusion into Kate's morning routine. The brunette knew Yelena would have shown at up at some point, but she just hadn’t expected it to be so soon. Kate figured she would’ve spent more time at home in Russia than the blonde had.

    For a moment, Kate simply stared, her mind racing to catch up with the reality unfolding before her. The blonde’s nose crinkled slightly as she slept, a soft sigh escaping her lips as she shifted, ending up closer to Kate. The archer hadn't known Yelena was here, hadn't anticipated waking up to find the blonde assassin in her bed. The realization left her momentarily stunned, unsure of how to react to this unexpected turn of events. Kate's thoughts swirled with questions and uncertainties. Why was Yelena here? Why had she suddenly shown up now? What was the time? When did she get there? Did Clint know she was here?

    And maybe the most important one, did she bring Fanny?

    Kate slowly turned around to face Yelena, trying to disturb the assassin as little as possible as the blankets shifted around them. The blonde didn’t move from her spot, just laid there, still lost in the peaceful depths of slumber. The early morning light played on Yelena's features, casting a gentle glow over her usually guarded expression.

    The archer's gaze traced the lines of Yelena's face, the curve of her cheek, and the strands of blonde hair that framed her peaceful features. The air in the room held a quiet tension, laden with unspoken questions and a sense of the unknown. If the blonde was here, that meant Kate could finally find out what Yelena had been keeping from her.

    What everyone had been keeping from her.

    For a moment, Kate simply observed, trying to decipher the enigma that was Yelena Belova. The unexpectedness of finding her in bed, the vulnerability on display, and the uncharted territory of their evolving connection left Kate contemplating the complexities of their relationship. There was a subtle softness in Yelena's features, a vulnerability that contradicted the fierce warrior persona Kate was accustomed to.

    Kate did not know how long she sat there just observing the blonde until Yelena let out a soft sigh and blinked her eyes open. The blonde looked confused at first, the disorientation of waking in an unfamiliar place momentarily clouding her awareness. But as the fog of sleep lifted, Yelena's gaze fell upon Kate, who lay beside her, watching her with a curious intensity. A small, bemused smile tugged at Yelena's lips as she realized where she was. The blonde rolled onto her back on from where she had been turned in towards Kate’s chest. The brunette didn’t move from her sideways position, her head balanced on her propped-up elbow.

    With a soft exhale, Yelena broke the silence, her voice hoarse from sleep but tinged with a note of sincerity. "Good morning," she murmured, her gaze lingering on Kate's face, searching for any sign of what lay beneath the archer's blank exterior. Kate, still processing the unusual turn of events, met Yelena's gaze with a mix of curiosity and wariness. "Morning," she replied, her voice carrying a cautious edge. A pause lingered between them before Kate, unable to contain her burgeoning curiosity, ventured into the uncharted territory of questions. "When did you arrive? How’d you get here? You should’ve woken me up! Did you bring Fanny with you?" The archer's tone was measured, but the inquiry revealed the threads of uncertainty woven into her thoughts. Yelena, meeting Kate's gaze unflinchingly, offered a small, exasperated smile. "Arrived early hours of this morning and yes Kate Bishop, Fanny's here too," she answered, her words a deliberate dance around the deeper questions that hung in the air.

    Kate nodded, absorbing the information but sensing there was more beneath the surface. "Alright," she conceded, realizing that pushing for answers immediately might not yield the clarity she sought. "So, what's the plan now?"

    A mischievous glint sparkled in Yelena's eyes as she quirked an eyebrow. "Food first. I don't do well on an empty stomach, and neither do you." Her attempt at lightening the mood was met with a reluctant smile from Kate.

    “I’m not hungry.”

    “You’re eating. Come.” Yelena said flatly.

    The blonde rolled out of the bed, Kate taking a moment to look her up and down. Yelena, dressed in one of the brunette’s hoodies and her own joggers – Kate’s were too long - caught Kate's scrutiny and raised an eyebrow.

    "Like what you see?" she teased, a playful smirk playing on her lips.

    Kate, caught off guard, blushed slightly but recovered with a casual shrug. "Just appreciating the fashion choice, that's all."

    “That is not a compliment to me Kate. It is your hoodie.” Yelena chuckled, her laughter ringing with a warmth that eased any lingering tension.

    "Well, if it looks that good on you, maybe you should consider a wardrobe upgrade." Yelena shot her a mock glare. "I'll stick to stealing yours. It has a certain charm."

    Chapter 19

    Chapter Notes been working like mad so have been a little bit away from writing this lately! post is a little later this week, think its been 9 days? so sorry about that, hope you all enjoy :)

    As they descended the staircase, the aroma of breakfast wafted through the air, enticing even the supposedly uninterested archer. In the kitchen, Laura was busy preparing a meal, and through the window, Kate spotted Clint and Nat outside, chopping wood.

    “Morning you two… or should I say afternoon.” Laura greeted as they entered, her eyes flicking between Kate and Yelena. If she was shocked Kate was downstairs for the first time since she had arrived at the Bartons, she didn’t show it. “You’re just in time for lunch. Hungry?”

    “We are starving.” Yelena emphasised and answered for Kate who looked rather unsure on her feet.

    "Good, because I made enough to feed a rather large army." Laura smiled, motioning towards the spread on the kitchen table.

    Yelena wasted no time in claiming a seat at the table, and with a subtle gesture, invited Kate to join her. However, the archer hesitated, a mix of uncertainty and discomfort evident on her face.

    "Kate Bishop. I did not come all this way to watch you starve. Food will do you good," Yelena encouraged, patting the seat beside her. Her tone was gentle, understanding the apprehension that lingered in the air.

    Kate glanced at Laura, who observed the scene with keen interest. With a subtle nod and an encouraging smile, Laura silently conveyed her support, inviting Kate to take this small step towards normalcy. Reluctantly, Kate took the seat beside Yelena, her eyes flickering between the spread on the table and the blonde beside her. Yelena, sensing the underlying tension, offered a reassuring smile, silently acknowledging the significance of this moment. As they settled at the table, Yelena took charge of the situation, grabbing a plate and expertly filling it with an array of dishes. Kate, still feeling a bit overwhelmed, watched as Yelena added portions of her favourite dishes, almost as if the blonde had memorized her preferences.

    "Eat.” Yelena said, placing the plate in front of Kate. The archer looked down at the spread, a mix of gratitude and reluctance in her eyes. The brunette looked back to the blonde a moment later, the assassin looked back with her mouthful of food. She nodded her head down to Kate’s plate before shoving another forkful into her own mouth.

    Kate picked up her own cutlery, fiddling with the food on her plate. Laura had turned back around, plating up her own lunch, as well as two more for Clint and Nat. Kate found herself struggling with the simple act of taking a bite. The fork felt heavy in her hand, and the flavours that usually delighted her palate now seemed distant and unappealing. Yelena, having finished her mouthful, noticed the archers continued hesitation. "You're not eating," Yelena observed, her tone gentle but direct.

    Kate glanced at her plate; her appetite further dampened by the worry etched on Yelena's face. "I'm just not hungry," she mumbled, attempting to mask the deeper struggle within. “You need to eat, мой маленький ястреб. It is important.” The blonde leaned in closer, her voice soft and whispered.

    The archer nodded, but the internal battle was evident in her eyes.

    Yelena reached for a small roll, spreading a generous layer of jam on the bread. She handed it to the brunette who offered a faint smile. The blonde didn’t mind if she started small and simple as long as she had something in her stomach.

    As Kate took a tentative bite, Yelena continued to subtly encourage her, engaging in light conversation to distract from the weight of the unspoken challenge. She’d reach to squeeze the brunette’s arm or tap a pattern on Kate’s thigh, anything to distract her from the motion of eating.

    Laura, observing the subtle interplay, couldn't help but feel a sense of satisfaction at witnessing the major influence the arrival of Yelena had had on Kate. For starts, the brunette was downstairs and actually eating something. The change in Kate was palpable. The mere presence of Yelena seemed to have sparked a shift in the archer's demeanour, who though still navigating the complexities of her emotions, appeared more present. She exchanged hushed conversation with the blonde beside her, their heads tilted together, looking as if they were two naughty kids plotting something.

    When Kate let out a laugh, Laura looked up from her own plate in surprise. She had been minding her own business, quite happy to eat in quiet and leave the two across from her to their own chatter. But the archer's laughter, however tentative, resonated in a way that hadn't been heard since she arrived at the Barton residence.

    The door creaked open as Clint and Nat entered, their cheeks rosy from the chilly air outside. The aroma of food greeted them, and Clint's stomach audibly growled in response. A scattering of wood chips clung to their clothes, evidence of their earlier venture. Laura greeted them with a warm smile.

    "Perfect timing, you two," she remarked, motioning for them to join the others at the table. "Lunch is ready."

    Clint and Nat exchanged a knowing look, their shared understanding evident in the way they moved together, almost as if they were in sync. As they settled into their seats, they couldn't help but notice the change in atmosphere, the subtle shift that had occurred in the Barton household since Yelena's arrival.

    Kate, who had been engaged in conversation with Yelena, looked up at the newcomers with a faint smile, a glimmer of warmth in her eyes. It was a small but significant gesture, one that didn't go unnoticed by Clint and Nat.

    "Hey there, sleepyhead," Clint teased, ruffling Kate's hair as he took the seat beside her. "You finally decided to join the land of the living?"

    Kate rolled her eyes but couldn't hide the hint of amusement in her expression. "Shut up, Clint," she retorted, but there was a lightness in her tone that hadn't been there before. Nat, sitting across from them, observed the scene with a sense of quiet satisfaction. She exchanged a knowing look with Laura, the unspoken acknowledgment between them a testament to the bond that stood between the two women. Can’t say the same for yours.”

    “You're brave for insulting my fashion sense while looking like that.” The redhead deadpanned.

    “I prefer functional over fashionable. Something you used to consider.” Nat raised an eyebrow.

    "I think she’s good." Kate mumbled. The comment earned a shared chuckle from the group, the banter weaving a light-hearted thread into the atmosphere. Kate's subtle blush didn't go unnoticed, and Yelena, catching the moment, shot her a teasing grin.

    Yelena, noticing Kate's reaction, couldn't resist adding fuel to the fire. "Oh, you think so, do you мой маленький ястреб?" she teased, her eyes locking onto Kate's, a playful glint in them.

    Yelena feigned offense, placing a hand over her heart. "I'm wounded, Kate. I thought we had something special."

    "I hate to break it to you, Yelena, but Kate's standards are pretty high." Clint, joining in the teasing, added with a smirk, "She’s used to my impeccable fashion sense. You've got some competition.”

    "Please, Barton. Your sense of style peaked in the '90s… if at all." Yelena rolled her eyes playfully.

    Natasha smirked, appreciating the light banter and the change in atmosphere that Yelena seemed to bring with her. The tension that had lingered in the Barton household for days was gradually dissipating, replaced by a more palpable sense of ease.

    The group fell into an easy rhythm of conversation, a mix of banter, purposely avoiding the ongoing situation with Kingpin, and shared laughter that echoed through the Barton home. Kate was still rather quiet throughout the whole exchange, but it was a major improvement. The dynamics in the house had shifted, and it wasn’t lost on Clint, Nat, or Laura. Clint shot a curious look at Kate, who, for the first time in days, seemed more present and engaged. Nat, too, noticed the subtle change in her archer’s demeanour and exchanged a knowing glance with Clint and Laura.

    “You doing okay, kid?” Clint asked, his concern evident in his tone.

    Kate’s head turned from where she was quietly talking to Yelena nodded, a small but genuine smile playing on her lips. “Yeah, I’m good.”

    Clint studied Kate's face for a moment longer than usual, the worry lines on his forehead betraying the concerns that had been occupying his thoughts. For the past week, he had watched over Kate like a hawk, his protective instincts on high alert, even if the brunette hadn’t left her bedroom. The weight of responsibility hung heavy on his shoulders, and every sleepless night and whispered conversation in the hallway had etched deeper lines on his face.

    As Kate smiled, Clint couldn't help but marvel at the resilience of the young archer. She had faced loss, betrayal, and the looming threat of Kingpin, yet here she was, mustering a smile that carried a glimmer of hope.

    Clint found solace in these small moments: the reassurance that Kate was holding up, that she was finding her way through the storm. He had played many roles in his life – husband, father, an Avenger, a marksman, a protector – but being a somewhat father like figure to Kate held a significance that he hadn’t quite fully figured out yet.

    Clint's mind briefly wandered to the day Kate had entered his life, a fiery and determined young woman with a bow in hand and seemingly a death wish. The journey they had shared had been fraught with challenges, losses, and unexpected twists, yet their bond had endured. He glanced at Laura, the silent understanding between them speaking volumes. Clint knew Laura shared his concerns for Kate, each passing day bringing them closer to the edge of a precipice that held the unknown. The burden of the past weighed heavily on their shoulders, and as much as Clint wanted to shield Kate from it, he knew she was bound to confront the harsh realities sooner or later. She still didn’t know about her father’s role in this whole spiral either.

    With a silent nod, Clint redirected his attention to the lively banter around the table. Kate, now engaged back in her conversation with Yelena, seemed to be in good spirits. Clint couldn't help but hope that the presence of the blonde Russian – a wildcard in their carefully strategized lives – might be the one to pull Kate out of her grief.

    Whilst thinking of the blonde, she chimed in, her tone laced with a hint of playful sarcasm. "She's practically a ray of sunshine now that I'm here." Yelena said, her voice carrying a hint of teasing. “Actually, I’m pretty sure she's better than good. Turns out, I'm not the worst babysitter.”

    Kate shot Yelena an amused glance, playfully rolling her eyes. “You're not babysitting me, Yelena. I'm perfectly capable of taking care of myself.”

    Yelena feigned offense, placing a hand over her heart dramatically. “Ouch, Kate Bishop. Here I am, offering my expert services, and you shoot me down.”

    Clint chuckled, shaking his head at the playful banter between the two. “Alright, alright. No need for a full-blown comedy routine. Let's just enjoy lunch.”

    Kate shot Yelena a look, torn between annoyance and amusement. "And you should know, I’m always a ray of sunshine."

    Yelena shrugged with a scoff, "If that's what you want to believe."

    The banter between the two elicited a round of chuckles from the rest of the table. Clint exchanged an amused glance with the two others in the room he actually acknowledged as adults, recognizing the subtle transformation in Kate's demeanour. The arrival of Yelena seemed to have worked wonders, bringing a spark back to Kate's eyes that had been absent for too long.

    Laura turned her attention to Kate, a warm smile on her face. "Well, it's good to see you smiling again. Whatever Yelena did, it's a welcome change."

    Kate shot Yelena a mock glare. "She just won't stop raiding my wardrobe. I'm going to run out of hoodies at this rate."

    Yelena grinned unapologetically. "Blame me for having excellent taste."

    The dimly lit, inconspicuous apartment held an air of secrecy as Steve Rogers sat across from Sam Wilson and Bucky Barnes. Steve had flown out to meet Bucky after asking his old friend if he might have any leads. The room was filled with tension as they prepared to discuss the unsettling information Steve had gathered.

    Bucky's gaze remained stoic as he listened to Steve recount the details. Sam, who happened to be with Bucky when Steve had called, perched on the edge of a worn-out armchair, observed both men intently. Steve took a deep breath before diving into the complex narrative.

    "Untraced Russian super soldiers," Steve began, and immediately, he noticed the subtle tightening of Bucky's jaw. "After the snap, while the world was in chaos, the Russians, particularly Hydra remnants, saw a chance to strike when the world was at its weakest." As Steve continued, now pacing the room with a sense of urgency, he detailed the global response to the snap and the power vacuum left in its wake as Sonya had described. "Russia, they wanted control, and they believed the energy from the snap could give them a tactical advantage. They aimed to harness that power, turn the bad into good, and take control of Earth."

    Bucky's gaze remained fixed on Steve, his face blank but expression grave. It remained the same as Steve spoke of the power surge on Earth after the snap and the Russian scientists' alleged desire to harvest that energy.

    "The Russians created the Lufuthai, a group of super soldiers, possibly using the power from the snap," Steve revealed, watching for any reaction from Bucky.

    The room fell into a brief silence as Sam and Bucky absorbed the weight of the information. Bucky's gaze shifted between Steve and the floor, his mind processing the connections. Sam broke the silence.

    "So? They exist and what? None of us have ever come across them. I assume you mean to hunt them down and find them. Why antagonise them for no reason? Do you have a death wish?” Sam asked, his tone steady.

    Steve took a moment, meeting Sam's steady gaze with a sense of conviction. "Sam, it's not just about the existence of these super soldiers. It's about what they're connected to. Clint’s got a protégé. Her name is Kate Bishop. She's not just a random target; she's connected to the bigger picture."

    Leaning in, Steve began to unravel the intricate web of connections that tied Kate Bishop to the emerging threat. "Kate's father, Derek Bishop, had ties to organized crime, and it seems that these Russian super soldiers, Lufuthai, have a vested interest in her. It goes beyond a simple vendetta or kidnapping. There's something more significant at play here." "So, you’re saying these super soldiers are working for someone? Shocker." Sam raised an eyebrow, his tone sarcastic as he absorbed the information.

    Steve nodded. "The trail leads to Wilson Fisk, or Kingpin as most know him. The Lufuthai seem to be directly involved with him, and we've seen what Fisk is capable of. If we don't act now, they'll have a powerful ally with resources and influence that we can't ignore. We can't let them strengthen their grip on the world by allying with someone like Kingpin." "Okay, so we're dealing with super soldiers working for the Kingpin. That still doesn't answer why we should go after them. We've got our hands full already." Sam leaned back, rubbing his temples as he processed the gravity of the situation.

    “What do you mean?” Steve questioned. He had not been informed of any current goings-on. “Fury’s got us working with a group of young hero’s. He’s got us particularly focused on a Kamala Khan.”

    “The one who was with Carol?”

    “She was also there when Captain Rambeau got sucked into a different universe. Fury wants her back Steve. Thinks this kids the key.”

    “No. Fury wants to be the one to figure out how to travel universes.” Bucky butted in flatly. "Okay look, if we don't deal with this now, it's only a matter of time before the world is under the thumb of people like Fisk and those super soldiers. We can't let them operate unchecked. Clint’s in the crossfire, and innocent lives are at stake. If we have a chance to stop this before it escalates, we have to take it." Steve turned the conversation back to the matter at hand. "You're talking about stepping into a docile hornet's nest, Steve. They’re not a major active threat. Do you even know where they operate from? What's even your plan?" Sam asked. Steve leaned back, a determined glint in his eyes. "We gather intel and then we confront them. It's not about picking a fight; it's about preventing a much larger one down the line. We can't let Hydra's remnants and the likes of Kingpin manipulate the world's future." Sam glanced at Bucky, silently seeking his input. Bucky, despite his stoic demeanour, nodded in agreement. "We can't afford to turn a blind eye to this. But I will say, something about this doesn’t add up at all." The man with the metal arm spoke cautiously.

    "Buck, I know it sounds like a stretch, but we've seen the impossible happen before. Oh, and another thing, Natasha's back. She's alive." Steve explained slowly like he was talking to a frightened child.

    "Natasha's alive? How?" Bucky's eyes widened; his disbelief shared with Sam. Steve nodded, his gaze steady. "It's a long story, which we haven’t figured out at all yet, involving the Red Skull and Carol but she's back. And she's not alone. Yelena, her sister, is involved in this too. They've got a stake in stopping whatever Hydra's remnants and the Kingpin are planning."

    Bucky leaned forward, his brow furrowing. "You're telling me Natasha is back, and now she's tangled up in this mess?"

    "Exactly. It might just be a coinciden-“ “No. It’s too unlikely.” Bucky shook his head.

    “If whatever brought her back, is connected to the larger threat we're facing now, she is determined to help Clint and Kate whatever it takes.”

    Sam interjected; his scepticism evident. "So, we're trusting Natasha, who was supposed to be dead, to have our backs in this? What if she’s not who she says she is?" Steve met Sam's gaze with unwavering confidence. "I know it's a lot to take in, Sam, but Natasha's actions have always been about protecting the world. If she's involved, it means there's a reason. We can't afford to dismiss any help we can get, especially from someone who knows the ins and outs of Hydra."

    “Alright, Steve. We’ll help, but we need to keep an eye on Natasha. I've learned not to trust things that seem too good to be true." Bucky, still processing the news of Natasha's return, finally spoke up.

    “We stay vigilant, but we can't let doubt cloud our judgment. Our priority is to stop Lufuthai, Kingpin, and anyone else pulling the strings. We need to pool our resources, and put an end to this before it spirals out of control." Steve spoke determinedly.

    As the gravity of the situation settled in, Sam interjected with a quizzical expression. "Hold on a second, go back a second. Natasha has a sister? She kept that quiet.” Steve sighed, realizing the need to address the gaps in their knowledge. "Yes, Yelena is Natasha's sister. They grew up together in the Red Room. She's a formidable ally. Natasha kept it under wraps because it’s not a nice part of her past.”

    “No part of their past is nice.” Bucky mumbled; his eyes glazed over in thought. Bucky's murmured words cut through the air, his eyes distant as memories from his own tumultuous past resurfaced.

    "So, she's been hiding a super-spy sister from us all this time? Would’ve been helpful when we had an army of aliens coming for our necks.” Sam remarked, a hint of sarcasm in his voice.

    “Sam, you've got to understand. Natasha's life was a maze of secrets, and she navigated it alone for a long time. You cannot fault her for wanting to protect those she loves.” Bucky explained.

    Steve added, "Yelena is no different. She's got her own reasons for being involved in this, and I trust Natasha's judgment. We need all the help we can get, and Yelena is an asset in this fight."

    Sam, while still sceptical, nodded in reluctant agreement, realizing the intricacies of Natasha's choices. "Fine, but we need to know what we're dealing with here. What’s the sister like? Have you met her?”

    Steve took a moment to gather his thoughts before responding, "Natasha and Yelena, they have their differences. Nat's more calculated, strategic. Yelena, on the other hand, strikes me as more instinctive, raw. They're not on the best terms right now, but they share a common goal – stopping whatever's going on with these super soldiers and Kingpin." As the weight of their new allies settled in, Steve continued, "And about Kate Bishop – Kingpin stabbed her. She's in bad shape, and we can't let that slide. It's personal now, and we're not letting Fisk and his goons get away with it."

    “Steve. It’s not personal. We don’t know this kid.” Bucky said flatly, Sam nodded his agreement.

    Steve sighed before slumping down into a chair. He now felt compelled to provide more context about Kate.

    "Before we dive headfirst into this, you should know how Kate and Clint crossed paths. She's not just some random kid caught in the crossfire. Clint and Kate met last Christmas, during a rough time for both of them. Kate's family was targeted, and she found herself facing threats she couldn't handle alone. Clint stepped in… for reasons of his own.” Steve trailed off, knowing Sam and Bucky knew nothing of Clint’s ties to the Ronin.

    Steve hesitantly continued a moment later, painting a picture of the unlikely mentorship that had developed. "He took her under his wing, trained her, and, in a way, adopted her into the family. Now, he treats her like his fourth child, you know Clint, he’s fiercely protective. What happened to Kate isn't just an attack on an ally; it's an attack on Clint’s family. Our family. Kate became Hawkeye, not just in name but in skill. She's a skilled archer. Kid's got heart, determination, and some very powerful allies.”

    As Bucky absorbed the details, a furrow appeared on his brow, and he finally questioned Steve, "Be as that may. Where did you get all this information so quickly? Surely intel on unknown super soldiers cannot be that common.”

    "There's someone we need to talk about – Sonya. She's a Black Widow, just like Natasha. She provided us with all this information. She was monitoring the situation during the snap, gathering intel on forces whilst we were gone. Sonya is the key to understanding what we're up against."

    Sam's eyebrows shot up in surprise. "Another Black Widow? How did we not know about her before?"

    Steve explained, "There are a lot of black widows we don’t know about Sam, and we have no business knowing either. Sonya is a close friend of Yelena’s and helped Kate out of some trouble.”

    Bucky, still sceptical, leaned forward, his gaze piercing. "And how do we know we can trust her? Black Widows are all known for being masters of deception."

    Steve nodded, acknowledging the scepticism. "I get it, Bucky, I do. Yelena trusts her, Nat trusts Yelena. My hands are tied. We owe Sonya for all this intel.”

    "So, we're trusting this Sonya based on Yelena’s word and then trusting Yelena because she’s Natasha's sister? That's a lot of trust to put in a network we barely knew existed." Sam chimed in.

    “It’s a risk. But we’re running low on people here Sam. Tony’s gone. Vision too. Thor, Bruce, Carol, The Guardians are all off Earth. Wanda’s turned her transmitter off. Strange is… being strange. We don’t have much to work with right now. Sonya has given us crucial intel, and Yelena has a personal stake in this. Natasha may keep secrets, but she'd never put her sister in harm's way willingly."”

    “We’ve all seen too many people play both sides. Trust is earned, not given." Bucky said quietly. “Just because Yelena is Nat’s sister doesn’t mean she’s trustworthy. What’s her stake in all this? It cannot just be she wants to tag along because her sister is involved.” Steve considered Bucky's question carefully before responding. "It's not just because Natasha is involved. Like I said, Yelena has her own reasons and we’d be stupid not to consider them. She and Kate Bishop are close friends, and Yelena seems extremely protective of Kate." Sam, ever the pragmatist, interjected, "So, Yelena's personal stake is her friendship with Kate?”

    "And when someone like Kingpin stabs Kate…” Steve trailed off whilst Sam mimed out the action of a fight scene ending with him falling to the ground having been shot in the head. Bucky, rolling his eyes at Sam as he pulled himself up off the floor, seemed to grasp the personal motivations at play. "Alright, I can understand that. We all have people we'd go to great lengths to protect."

    Steve added, "That's why we need to trust Nat’s judgment. Yelena’s fighting for the same reasons we are. She's fighting for her friend, for someone she considers family. Can’t fault a person on that.”

    “So… what’s our play?”

    Chapter 20

    Chapter Notes here's a chapter on this easter sunday for y'all.
