    enjoy! xx The vast Barton farm sprawled out before them, blanketed in a pristine layer of snow. Underneath the sprawling branches of a large oak tree, Yelena and Kate huddled together for warmth. The cold air was crisp, and their breaths created delicate clouds in the winter chill. Lucky and Fanny, the two dogs, frolicked nearby, leaving pawprints in the freshly fallen snow.

    Kate sat close to Yelena, the shared body heat providing a sense of comfort in the biting cold. The brunette was bundled up in an unfathomable number of layers whilst Yelena and her Russian blood seemed perfectly content in just the one coat. The quietude of the farm, interrupted only by the distant sounds of nature and occasional playful barks, set the stage for a conversation of more profound significance.

    "Yelena," Kate began, her eyes fixed on the horizon as she hesitated, "can you tell me about my parents now? What do you know?"

    Yelena's gaze softened as she regarded the brunette beside her. The two had been sat outside for a reasonable length of time, the blonde answering all Kate’s questions about her trip to Russia and the pair had been enjoying watching their two furry friends play together. The weight of the sudden request hung in the air, but Yelena understood the need for Kate to know about the ghosts surrounding her past.

    With a deep breath, Yelena started to share what little she knew.

    "Your parents were… they cared about you a lot; I am sure." Yelena's voice held a gentle tone, as if handling something fragile. "They had their secrets, like everyone does, but I am sure they loved you."

    Kate nodded, absorbing the words. The winter landscape around them seemed to echo the quiet gravity of the conversation.

    "The others didn't want you to know too much, to protect you, I guess," Yelena continued, her eyes fixed on the distant hills. "SHIELD knew of your parents for decades.” “SHIELD kept tabs on my mom and dad. Nick Fury knew about mom and dad?!” Kate exclaimed.

    Yelena gently grabbed Kate’s flying arms by the wrists, bringing them to her lap to hold them down before she continued.

    “Your father was trying to strike up a deal with the Russian military about some tech he developed. SHIELD wanted to broker one as well. When both learnt of each other chasing the same company for their armouries, both deals fell through. Your grandfather than passed soon after and that is when Derek became involved with Kingpin.”

    Kate listened intently, grateful for the fragments of information that Yelena shared. The air between them carried a mixture of vulnerability and understanding. The brunette took in a few shaky breaths as Yelena paused. The blonde raised an eyebrow in question to if Kate was okay for her to continue.

    “Please.” Kate said shakily.

    “Kingpin and your father took advantage of the new power Derek held. A rich, high blooded, CEO in New York is not someone to underestimate, especially when partnered with Fisk.” Yelena’s voice became more unsure as she carried on.

    “What Yelena?” Kate caught on when Yelena stopped and turned her focus away from Kate’s face and towards the dogs a little away from them.

    “There is no going back after you hear this, Kate. It will change everything.” Yelena warned the brunette, slowly turning her head back to meet her eyes.

    “I need to know. I-I can’t not know.” The archer stuttered.

    Yelena only squeezed the brunette’s wrists tighter before sliding her hands down to intertwine their fingers instead.

    “They got cocky.” Yelena sighed, the tone in her voice alluding to what she was going to say immediately.

    Kate inhaled sharply, tears welling up behind her eyes already.

    “A deal with the European mafia went south.” Yelena carried on slowly, only to stop when Kate let out a sob. The weight of the revelation settled heavily on Kate's shoulders, the bitter truth causing her heart to ache. Tears streamed down her cheeks as the cold winter air seemed to cut even sharper in the wake of Yelena's words.

    The blonde hesitated briefly, gauging Kate's reaction before continuing, “Your father did not die in the Battle of New York Kate. He was shot. They used the battle as a cover up.” Yelena spoke with a solemnity that echoed the gravity of the situation.

    The truth, though painful, held a strange kind of liberation. Kate's breath hitched, her chest tightening as Yelena's words sank in. “Did mom know?” Kate's voice trembled with a mix of anguish and disbelief.

    “Да.” Yelena confirmed in Russian, after getting over her slight initial shock that that was Kate’s first question, the word hanging in the air between them. “Fury believes you could be involved with Kingpin.” The blonde said cautiously, she might as well get it all out in the open in one go.

    The words hung in the air, their impact rippling through the snowy landscape. Yelena knew the gravity of what she was saying and braced herself for Kate's reaction. “What?!” Kate's incredulous exclamation cut through the quiet, her eyes widening with a mix of shock and frustration.

    “You inherited everything of your parent’s company. You know how New York’s high society works and you can wield a weapon. It’s not that far-fetched for someone who is just looking at the facts on a database.” Yelena shrugged nonchalantly, whilst maintaining her usual calm exterior.

    The nonchalant gesture belied the weight of the accusation, as if Yelena sought to strip away the sensationalism and present the facts starkly. Kate would’ve appreciated if she hadn’t still been reeling from the revelation about her parents, and now had to grapple with the added complexity of being suspected by those she had considered allies. Kate's mind raced, grappling with the unexpected twist. The pieces of the puzzle began to fall into place, forming a disturbing image that she had never considered. The weight of suspicion now pressed upon her, casting a shadow over her grief.

    Yelena watched as tears streamed down Kate's face, her heart wrenching at the sight of the brunette's anguish. A part of her wanted to reach out, to offer comfort and solace in the face of such devastating news. But another part hesitated, unsure if her presence would be welcomed after delivering such painful truths. Yelena wrestled with her own conflicting emotions. She had been the bearer of this burden, the one who had shattered Kate's illusions and laid bare the harsh realities of her past.

    Would Kate still want her around after this?

    Was she even deserving of offering comfort in the wake of such pain?

    Yet, despite her doubts, Yelena found herself drawn to Kate's side, unable to ignore the palpable grief that radiated from the woman beside her. With hesitant movements, Yelena tentatively reached out, her hand hovering uncertainly over Kate's shoulder. "О, маленький ястреб," Yelena's voice was soft, barely above a whisper, "I'm... I'm so sorry."

    The words felt inadequate, a feeble attempt to assuage the depth of Kate's sorrow. But still, Yelena remained, her presence a silent offering of solidarity in the face of overwhelming despair.

    Kate turned towards Yelena, her tear-stained face a portrait of raw vulnerability. In that moment, their eyes met, and Yelena saw a glimmer of something amidst the pain – a flicker of understanding, and not a hint of blame.

    Without a word, Kate leaned into Yelena's embrace. The blonde wrapped her arms gently around Kate, pulling her close. Without a word, she leaned in, her lips brushing against Kate's ear as she whispered soft words of comfort and reassurance.

    "У меня есть ты, малышка. Я не позволю никому причинить тебе боль.” Yelena murmured, her voice a soothing melody amidst the quiet of the winter landscape. She felt Kate's body tremble against her own, the weight of her grief palpable in every breath. Yelena's fingers delicately stroked Kate's hair, the rhythmic motion a soothing gesture as if trying to gently erase the pain etched on the archer's heart. The winter landscape around them stood witness to a fragile moment of connection, where words fell short, and the language of touch bridged the gaps left by the unspoken, much like it had that morning at the compound where something had shifted between them.

    As Yelena continued to whisper comforting words in Russian, her tone softened with an affectionate tenderness. "Ты такая сильная, Кэйт. Я горжусь тем, как ты справляешься." Her words were a gentle reassurance, a declaration of pride in Kate's strength. With a subtle shift, Yelena tightened her embrace, drawing Kate even closer. Feeling the warmth of Yelena's body against her own, Kate instinctively sunk into her side, seeking solace in the comforting presence of her friend. Kate stirred slightly, her gaze shifting to the source of a new sound. Laura emerged from the doorway, her expression softening at the sight of the two women sitting beneath the oak tree.

    Laura's approach was unhurried, her steps measured as she made her way across the snowy ground. When she reached them, she offered a warm smile, her eyes filled with understanding. The lines of worry etched on Laura's face softened as she observed the position taken up by Yelena and Kate.

    As she settled beside them, Laura's gaze shifted between Yelena and Kate. With a gentle touch on Kate's shoulder, she conveyed silent support before turning her attention to Yelena. "Nat told you about Derek, didn't she?" Laura's voice carried a mix of curiosity and empathy. Yelena met her gaze, nodding in confirmation. The unspoken understanding between them deepened, acknowledging the complexities of the truth that had been unveiled. Yelena met Laura's gaze, her expression unapologetic yet tender. "Kate needed to know," she replied simply, her voice carrying a note of conviction.

    Laura nodded in understanding, her gaze shifting to Kate, who looked up at the blonde from where her head was on the assassins shoulder with a mixture of vulnerability and gratitude. "Thank you, Lena," Kate whispered softly, her voice barely audible above the rustle of the wind.

    “Всегда.” Yelena mumbled against the archer’s temple, before pursing her lips to subtlety plant a kiss there.

    As Yelena murmured the Russian word for "always," Laura couldn't help but feel a sense of admiration for the strength and resilience that Yelena embodied. It seemed so easy for the blonde to be so vulnerable even after everything she has been through. It was a testament to the young woman that’s for sure.

    Laura's smile softened at the exchange between Yelena and Kate. She felt a swell of warmth in her chest, touched by the tenderness that permeated the air around them. The gentle kiss that Yelena pressed to Kate's temple spoke volumes, a silent reassurance of her presence and Laura couldn't help but feel a pang of emotion at the sight, recognizing the trust the blonde had put in her to witness the moment occur between her and Kate.

    With a soft sigh, Laura leaned back against the trunk of the oak tree, content to bask in the quiet beauty of the moment. She watched the two dogs chasing each other around the field in front of them as Clint’s truck pulled up in the driveway, the chatter, and squeals of her three kids echoing their way a few minutes later.

    Laura stood up, brushing off a bit of snow from her pants, and turned to Kate and Yelena. "Alright, you two. As much as I'm enjoying the scenic view of you both freezing out here, I think it's time to head inside before you catch a cold." She shot them a teasing grin. Kate nodded, holding onto Yelena's hand as they stood up together. Yelena spared a glance at Kate, her gaze filled with a quiet understanding of the emotions that lingered beneath the surface.

    As they made their way towards the house, the dogs bounding ahead of them, Laura motioned for them to follow. "Come inside, say hello to the kids. They've been dying to meet you, Yelena. And Kate, they've missed you so much honey." Laura added with a playful wink, her words carrying a hint of knowing.

    As they entered the warmth of the Barton farmhouse, the aroma of a freshly cooked meal greeted them. The Barton woman must have had the dinner slow cooking since Kate and Yelena had gone outside after lunch. Laura encouraged Yelena and Kate to join the lively atmosphere inside, assuring them that warmth and comfort would fix all, as well as warn off any cold that lingered in their bones. She also mentioned that the kids were eager to meet Yelena, having heard stories from Clint about the mysterious blonde who had become a part of their extended family.

    "Say hello to the kids Yelena, and then I'll whip up some hot cocoa," Laura suggested, her smile bright and inviting.

    Young voices chirped up from the living room as Laura finished speaking. “Mom? Did you say Yelena?”

    “Auntie Nat is your sister here?”

    Lila soon came running into the kitchen, her socked feet slipping on the tile. The Barton children's excitement filled the kitchen as they raced in, their eyes wide with anticipation. Lila skidded to a halt before Yelena, their gazes flickering with curiosity and eagerness. Cooper walked into the room much more calmly. He stuck out his hand eagerly to the blonde who reached out and shook it at Kate’s nudge.

    “I’m Cooper. This is Lila.” He said pointing to his sister beside him. Lila, more reserved but equally intrigued, simply stared up at Yelena with a contemplative expression. Kate chuckled at the children's enthusiastic reaction, a mix of pride and amusement colouring her features.

    “You don’t have red hair like Auntie Nat.”

    Yelena, ever the enigma, felt a twinge of discomfort under the scrutiny of the young Barton children. Their innocent observations, while endearing, brought a hint of vulnerability to the usually composed assassin. She met Lila’s eyes before offering a small smile. Yelena wasn't accustomed to engaging with children, and the unspoken challenge in Lila's statement left her momentarily at a loss for words.

    Kate, sensing Yelena's hesitation, stepped in with a playful smile. "No, she doesn't, but she's just as awesome as Auntie Nat, if not more so."

    Yelena shot Kate a grateful look, appreciating the way the archer effortlessly diffused the tension.

    Natasha who had been observing the scene from the living room, decided to join the conversation. Nate was clinging to her neck as she held him up on her hip, a bright grin on his face.

    "They say you're like Auntie Nat but with much better jokes.” Cooper remarked, his eyes wide with anticipation. His index finger pointed as his mom and dad who watched on gleefully.

    Natasha let out a gasp as if she was offended, pulling a giggle from Nate whose whole body jumped up at the action.

    “Traitors.” The redhead said in Clint and Laura’s direction.

    Cooper and Lila giggled as the three adults started bickering jokingly. Clint raised his hands in mock surrender. "Hey, we just call it like we see it. The playful banter filled the kitchen, laughter mingling with the warmth of familial bonds as Natasha, Clint, and Laura engaged in their light-hearted exchange. Nate, sensing the jovial atmosphere, joined in with his own infectious laughter, his giggles adding to the joyous chorus.

    Yelena observed the scene with a soft smile, the playful dynamics between the Barton family members a stark contrast to the sombre world she often inhabited. Despite her initial hesitation, she found herself drawn into the cheerful atmosphere, the genuine affection and camaraderie evident among the Bartons.

    As the laughter subsided and the playful bickering came to an end, Yelena's gaze shifted to Kate, who stood beside her, a small smile playing on her lips, a stark change from the woman she was outside not long ago. The shock and anguish was still swirling in the brunette’s eyes though.

    Nate, having been placed on the floor when Natasha had stated chasing Clint around the kitchen, walked over to Yelena and reached out towards the blonde as he got closer to her legs, his fingers grasping at the air in an attempt to get closer to her. Kate’s gaze on the kitchen suddenly softened and Yelena looked to where the brunette had her eyes now fixed. The blonde observed the little boy's curious approach. Yelena felt a gentle tug on her heart as she noticed Nate's determined steps toward her. The soft patter of his tiny feet against the kitchen floor created a heartwarming rhythm. The blonde crouched down, meeting Nate at his level and offered him a friendly handshake. The little boy's eyes widened in surprise, his fingers hesitating before tentatively reaching out to reciprocate the gesture. Yelena couldn't help but chuckle at Nate's adorable attempt at a handshake, his enthusiasm evident in every movement.

    As their hands met, Yelena maintained a warm and encouraging smile, creating an instant connection that transcended words. Nate's face lit up with joy, and he giggled in response. Yelena found herself enchanted by the simplicity of this interaction, the genuine delight in Nate's eyes reflecting the innocence of childhood.

    “I’m Nate. Are you Auntie Yelena?”

    Yelena’s head swung round to Clint and Laura at the little boys innocent question. Clint and Laura exchanged a glance, a shared smile passing between them at Nate's innocent but astute question. Clint chuckled before nodding, "Yep, that's Auntie Yelena." Laura added with a warm smile, "And she's a friend of Kate's."

    Nate's eyes widened with excitement; his attention now fully captured by Yelena. "Auntie Yelena and Kate are friends?" he asked, his voice filled with awe.

    Kate nodded, playing along with a grin. "Yes, Nate, best friends!" The brunette laughed at the exaggerated eye roll from Yelena.

    Nate's grin grew even wider, and he reluctantly dragged his gaze from the blonde to Kate with a beaming expression. "That's so cool, Kate! You have cool friends! I want cool friends too!"

    The adults in the room couldn't help but share a collective chuckle at Nate's enthusiasm, the warmth of the moment embracing them in the heart of the Barton farmhouse. Nate suddenly turned around and ran full force at Natasha’s legs, encircling both arms around them like a hug, his face looking up at her.

    “Auntie Nat! Did you know Auntie Yelena and Kate are best friends?!”

    Natasha glanced down at Nate, a playful smile tugging at the corners of her lips. "Really? Best friends, huh?" she replied, feigning surprise as she ruffled Nate's hair affectionately. "Well, that's interesting news."

    Cooper and Lila, who had been observing the scene, exchanged amused glances. Cooper decided to chime in with a cheeky grin, "Is that true, Auntie Yelena? Are you and Kate best friends?"

    Yelena, caught off guard by the sudden attention, shared a bemused look with Kate before responding with a playful smirk, "Being best friends with Kate is a tough job, but someone's got to keep her out of trouble," Yelena replied with a sly grin and a shrug, her eyes flickering mischievously. Her apprehension was still simmering slightly but the kids reaction to her had reassured her mostly. She glanced at Kate, who rolled her eyes with a teasing smile. Lila joined in, her eyes glinting with curiosity. "Do you have secret handshakes and everything?"

    Yelena leaned in conspiratorially, lowering her voice dramatically. "Oh, absolutely. But they're highly classified. Kate and I take our best friendship very seriously." Cooper raised an eyebrow, the knowing big brother look in his eye as he indulged Lila’s line of questioning, "Classified handshakes?”

    Kate, unable to contain her laughter, joined the banter. "Yeah, but they're so secret that even I don't know them. Yelena makes them up on the spot."

    “But to answer your question miniature Barton one… Best friends might be an understatement,” Yelena replied with a playful smirk, her eyes twinkling mischievously. "Let's just say Kate and I have an... adventurous partnership." She winked, enjoying the opportunity to indulge in a bit of playful banter, anything to make Kate smile really. As Yelena's words hung in the air, she couldn't help but notice the subtle blush that crept onto Kate's cheeks. The archer shot a glance in Yelena's direction, a mix of embarrassment and amusement playing in her eyes. The blonde much preferred this than the brunette’s tear- stained cheeks and puffy eyes.

    "Auntie Nat, can Auntie Yelena stay for hot cocoa too?" Lila chimed in, obviously sick of the quiet that had taken over, her eyes sparkling with excitement.

    Natasha looked over at Yelena with a playful smirk, clearly enjoying the children's antics. "What do you say, Auntie Yelena? Cocoa and chaos sound like a good combo?" With a half-smile, she glanced at Natasha before nodding in agreement, "Sure. But I want extra marshmallows.”

    As the group migrated to the living room, the air buzzed with the anticipation of shared laughter and camaraderie. Laura, the matriarch of the family, busied herself in the kitchen, expertly preparing hot cocoa for the boisterous group. The three kids claimed one couch, Lila and Nate pulling Natasha down onto it with them, whilst Cooper laughed at them from the end he sat on. The redhead couldn't resist their enthusiasm and laughter, allowing herself to be playfully pulled down into the midst of the youthful excitement. Clint took himself swiftly to his armchair, observing the delightful chaos with a fond smile, content to let the kids revel in their joy.

    Yelena and Kate sat down, side by side on another couch, leaving room for Laura when she came in as well. She soon joined them, carefully balancing a tray of cocoa. With hot cocoa in hand, the family's laughter and chatter reached a crescendo, blending seamlessly with the crackling fire.

    Kate’s eyes travelled around the room slowly as she took in the sight of this happy family and compared it to her own. The laughter of children, the flickering flames in the fireplace, and the comforting aroma of cocoa all seemed like scenes from a dream, a dream that felt both comforting and foreign to her.

    Her mind drifted back to her own family, the shadows that loomed over her recent revelations about her father, Derek. The truth about his true cause of death and the betrayal from both her parents weighed heavily on her heart. The pain lingered beneath the surface, threatening to bubble up and disrupt the idyllic atmosphere in the Barton’s living room. Despite the overwhelming emotions tugging at her, Kate did her best to push them down. She knew that this moment was about finding solace and healing, not dwelling on the past. As she took a sip of the hot cocoa Laura had prepared, she let the warmth soothe her, both physically and emotionally.

    Yelena, sensing the turmoil beneath Kate's calm exterior, subtly squeezed her free hand in a reassuring gesture, whilst her tongue chased the thousands of marshmallows swimming round her mug. It was a silent acknowledgment, a reminder that she was not alone in this sea of emotions. The family's laughter and chatter acted as a comforting backdrop, a distraction that Kate willingly embraced.

    Kate didn’t let Yelena let go of her hand and instead began gently twirling Yelena's fingers, she couldn't help but notice the intricate designs etched into the metal of her rings. Each one seemed to tell a story, a silent testament to Yelena's life before this moment, before they found themselves nestled in Barton’s warm and welcoming home. And even with all the tales the blonde’s scars and jewellery told, and all the crazy stuff that had happened to Kate in the past few months, they somehow managed find eachother over and over again. Yelena, usually guarded and reserved, found herself surprisingly at ease to be affectionate in the rest of the Barton family’s presence. The soft touch of her fingers, the warmth of her gaze, it all seemed to melt away the barriers Yelena had built around herself. She allowed herself to lean into Kate's touch, savouring the simple intimacy of the moment amidst the chaotic warmth of the family gathering.

    As Yelena sat beside Kate, their fingers intertwining repeatedly, she felt a strange sensation wash over her - a realization shining like the first light of dawn.

    For the first time in her life, she had something to lose.

    It was a startling revelation, one that caught her off guard amidst the warmth of the family gathering. Yelena had always prided herself on her independence, her ability to navigate the world alone, untouched by the bonds of attachment. Sure, for most of her life she couldn’t help but think that way, but the blonde had still stuck to those same rules after Oksana had freed her, unlike Sonya who took the complete opposite approach. But in Kate's presence, she found herself unravelling, her carefully constructed walls crumbling like sandcastles before the tide.

    The gentle touch of Kate's fingers, the warmth of her gaze when it landed on her every couple minutes, each moment spent with her felt like a gift, a glimpse of a world Yelena never dared to imagine for herself.

    And now, faced with the prospect of losing it all, Yelena realized just how much she had come to cherish Kate's presence in her life.

    It was a terrifying realization, to acknowledge the vulnerability that came with caring for someone so deeply. Yelena had always been the one to walk away, to protect herself from the pain of attachment. But with Kate, it was different. With Kate, she found herself wanting to stay, to fight against the currents pulling her away. Yelena knew that she had found something worth fighting for, someone worth holding onto with all her heart.

    When Kate let out what must’ve been her sixth yawn in the past five minutes, her eyes barely being able to be held open, Yelena rose to her feet as Natasha was mid-sentence. The blonde turned around to face the brunette slumped in the couch cushions, an unspoken invitation on her face for Kate to join her. Kate, with a contented smile, admitted that she was feeling a bit tired. Yelena snorted as the brunette’s head lolled again, the woman practically seconds away from falling asleep.

A mixture of affection and concern softened Yelena's features, a subtle vulnerability breaking through her typically stoic demeanour. Kate, with a cascade of unruly locks free around her face, let sleep tilt her head until it fell sideways into the plush cushions.

    Yelena's heart swelled with tenderness as she gazed down at Kate, her features softened by sleep. With a gentle touch, Yelena brushed a stray lock of hair from Kate's forehead, her fingertips lingering against the warmth of her skin. It was a simple gesture, but the others in the room knew of it significance in terms of Yelena and her past.

    “Kate. Come on маленький ястреб. You will get bad back like this.” Yelena mumbled in her native Russian, her words a soft caress that cut through the quiet of the room. Kate stirred slightly at the sound of her voice, her eyelids fluttering but not opening. The exhaustion of the day held her in its gentle grasp, unwilling to release its hold.

    The blonde decided against waking the tired archer, knowing even in sleep the brunette was stubborn as anything. Yelena crouched beside the couch, a quiet determination in her movements as she gently slid on arm beneath Kate’s knees and another behind her back, before effortlessly lifting her from the couch. Kate stretched in her new position, letting out a loud breath, her head finding a resting place in Yelena’s shoulder. A soft sound of contentment escaped her lips as she nestled into the warmth of Yelena's embrace. As Yelena began to carry Kate towards the stairs, Natasha, who had been observing the scene with a playful twinkle in her eyes, much like Clint and Laura, couldn't resist making a teasing comment. "Look at you, Yelena. All soft and caring. Who would've thought?" Yelena shot Natasha a deadpan look, her expression one of mock annoyance. "Shut up, Natasha. The маленький ястреб will be useless in a fight with a bad back.” "Little hawk, huh? What’s next? Lovey-dovey confessions?" Nat chuckled, the smirk never leaving her lips.

    Yelena rolled her eyes, a gesture that conveyed both exasperation and her exhaustion. "Don't be ridiculous, Natasha. I'm just ensuring she doesn't end up with a bad back. It's purely practical." Her Russian accent added an extra layer of sharpness to her words, a familiar defence mechanism she often employed, but the warmth in her eyes betrayed a different truth.

    As Yelena continued up the stairs with Kate nestled in her arms, the atmosphere shifted from the banter of the living room to a more intimate setting. The staircase seemed longer than usual, each step echoing in the silence of the house, the quiet creaking beneath them marked the transition from the shared space of the family gathering to the private cocoon of Kate’s bedroom.

    She carefully laid Kate down on the bed, tucking the blankets around her with a tenderness that belied her usual stoic demeanour. Kate had awoken slightly at the change of position, her eyes half-lidded as she mumbled a contented sigh. Yelena stepped away and closed the door behind them, shutting out the world and leaving them in a bubble of their own. The air was charged with unspoken emotions as Yelena turned to face Kate, taking a few steps to be back at the bedside.

    She gently cups Kate's face in her hands, her eyes searching for any sign of distress as the brunette tosses slightly, trying to get comfortable, her touch feather-light yet filled with an intensity that spoke volumes. Yelena's fingers traced a soothing pattern on Kate's cheek, a gesture that spoke of a desire to offer solace and ease. Once Kate stopped moving, with a soft smile, the blonde began to turn away, her intention clear - to head back downstairs and leave Kate to the peaceful stillness of the night, even if it meant heading back to the living room which included a smirking Natasha.

    As Yelena took a step, ready to make her way back to the living room, she felt a gentle tug on her hand. Surprised, she turned to find Kate, her eyes heavy with drowsiness but filled with a shy vulnerability that mirrored the soft glow of the bedside lamp.

    "Wh’re you goin’?" Kate murmured, voice slurring, it being half asleep. Yelena opened her mouth to answer as Kate squeezed her hand softly and mumbled, “Stay…” her voice a whispered plea, and Yelena's heart fluttered at the sincerity in her words. Without a word, Yelena allowed herself to be pulled towards the bed. Kate rolled over, creating space for Yelena to join her, and with a hesitant yet genuine smile, Yelena obliged. The mattress creaked slightly under their combined weight, and a sense of quiet intimacy settled between them.

    As Yelena settled beside her, Kate's gaze held a mix of sleepiness and gratitude. Yelena closed her eyes as she curled herself into a ball, ignoring the balls of blue fluttering tiredly at her.

    Minutes passed before Kate, overcome with sleepiness, shifted slightly. Yelena felt the brunette move from her side onto her back, a sigh escaping her lips as her back sunk into the mattress. The blonde felt a hand on her upper arm before a little force was applied. Kate shyly rolled the blonde over and pulled Yelena on top of her, their bodies aligning in a way that felt oddly perfect. Yelena, too exhausted to fight the delirious actions of her favourite archer just went with the movement.

    Her eyes widened for a moment, surprised by the sudden shift, but as she gazed up at Kate's sleepy face, a warmth enveloped her. Kate's shy, yet bold gesture became a silent invitation, a whispered acknowledgment of the connection they had forged. Yelena, her initial surprise giving way to a soft smile, nestled into the embrace, finding solace in the unexpected moment.

    With a tender touch, Yelena let her lips trail along the bare skin of Kate's collarbone, a gentle kiss that spoke of a deeper affection. The room, now filled with the soft sounds of their breathing and the gentle warmth of shared intimacy, cradled them like a mother rocks a baby to sleep.

    In that quiet moment, as Yelena's lips lingered against Kate's collarbone, a myriad of emotions swept through the assassin. The touch was gentle, almost hesitant, as if Yelena were navigating uncharted territory. It wasn't a lack of desire but rather a wariness that had been ingrained in her through a life of espionage and survival.

    As Yelena allowed herself to be vulnerable, she couldn't help but confront the unspoken fears that lurked in the recesses of her mind. Intimacy, with its ability to expose the depths of one's emotions, had always been a source of trepidation for her. The dark web of her past experiences, filled with loss and betrayal, and ultimate control, had shaped a fortress around her, designed to keep everyone at arm’s length.

    Yet here she was, tangled in delicate threads of intimacy with Kate, and Yelena found herself questioning the impact Kate was having on her carefully guarded walls.

    "What are you doing to me малышдевочка?" Yelena mumbled, her thoughts echoing in the hushed corners of her mind.

    It was a question layered with vulnerability, a question that laid bare the complexity of emotions swirling within her.

    The kisses on Kate’s forehead.

    The cuddling in bed at the compound.

    Kate’s leg slotted in-between her own.

    The nonchalant touches on the back, the thigh, playing with her fingers. But the gentle kiss on Kate's collarbone, though just another simple gesture, felt like a crack in the armour she had spent a lifetime building.

    For the first time in her life, Yelena found herself standing at the precipice of emotions she had never ventured into before. The concept of romantic feelings was foreign to her, a territory she had never allowed herself to explore.

    As Kate lay beside her, the soft sounds of their breathing being the only noise in their bubble, Yelena grappled with a question that lingered in the depths of her consciousness. Was the tenderness she felt for Kate purely platonic, a bond formed out of desire for connection in a lonely world or was it something more? Something tinged with a hint of longing that she couldn't quite shake?

    The distinction between romantic and platonic feelings blurred in Yelena's mind. She had never allowed herself the luxury of contemplating such emotions, and now, faced with the enigma that was Kate Bishop, she found herself standing on the edge of the unknown. Yelena's gaze shifted to Kate's peaceful sleeping face beneath her, the vulnerability evident even in slumber. A soft smile played on her lips as she traced the contours of Kate's features with her eyes. There was a tenderness in Kate's vulnerability, a beauty in her authenticity that tugged at Yelena's heartstrings. And yet, even as she felt drawn to Kate in ways she couldn't explain, Yelena hesitated to label her feelings.

    As her body nestled against Kate, the weight of the unspoken question lingered. Her thoughts circled like a hawk, uncertain of where to land.

    It was a daunting prospect, to confront the depths of her own emotions, to acknowledge the possibility of romantic attraction. For Yelena, who had always prided herself on her stoicism and self-reliance, it was something she was unprepared to embrace.

    Yet, as Kate's rhythmic breathing intertwined with her own, Yelena felt a strange comfort, a sense that maybe, just maybe, there was something beautiful in embracing the vulnerability she had long tried to suppress.

    Another week drifted by all to quickly at the Barton farm, a languid stretch of time where the days seemed to blend together in a quiet anticipation. Clint, Laura, Natasha, Yelena, and Kate found themselves caught in a limbo, waiting for news from Steve, the man having flown out to meet Bucky and Sam at the end of the previous week. The routine at the farm became a mix of training, shared meals, childish laughter, and the playful antics of their furry companions.

    In the mornings, the crisp air carried the scent of dew-covered grass as the team gathered for training sessions. Clint, with a watchful eye passed on his expertise to Kate as she rebuilt the muscle in her shoulder after having not been allowed to shoot for the past 3 weeks, the twang of bowstrings often echoing across the expansive fields. Laura occasionally joined in, displaying her own formidable skills with a precision that spoke of a life well-acquainted with the art of combat and of a marriage to an accomplished bowman.

    Nights brought a different rhythm. The family gathered around the dinner table, the clinking of utensils and laughter creating a symphony of shared moments. The kids kept the mood light when they came home from school, the days being more of a sombre mood. Clint and Laura tried to keep their environment as stress free as possible, not wanting them to being to worry when at the minute, nothing was even happening.

    Kate and Yelena often found themselves falling into an easy companionship during the day when they didn’t have the kids to occupy their attention – the two were a big hit, especially with Nate who enjoyed the two having more energy than Clint and Laura to chase him around. Whether it was sitting side by side during meals sharing whispers or a quiet moment on the porch, their connection deepened in the unspoken language of shared glances and often fleeting yet meaningful touches.

    The antics of Lucky and Fanny added a touch of chaos to the routine. The dogs keenly accompanied Yelena on her morning runs, Lucky often laying down halfway through and only rejoining the other two when they passed him on their way back, where he would magically spring back to life with an impressive burst of energy. Fanny found her own entertainment amidst the daily hustle. Unperturbed by Lucky's attempts to engage her in playful camaraderie, she elegantly ignored his advances. Instead, she opted for quiet rebellion, choosing to curl up in sunlit patches by the windows, the warmth a luxury she rarely experienced in the cold landscapes of Russia.

    As the afternoon sun dipped lower in the sky, casting light shadows across the Barton farm, Yelena and Laura found themselves on the porch swing, a silent duo observing the training session unfolding in the front yard. Clint, Nat, and Kate engaged in their respective activities, each absorbed in the rhythm of their own routines.

    Clint watched Kate as she drew her bow, offering occasional tips and guidance. His gaze, weathered by years of experience, tracked every movement of the arrow, his advice a blend of mentorship and paternal concern. Yelena did not miss the way his eyes would flick to Kate’s stomach when she drew an arrow back rather forcefully. The brunette’s wound was fully healed, and logically he had nothing to worry about but… this was Clint. Nat, not one to be outdone, had hung a punching bag from the sturdy oak tree, her blows shaking the branch above the bag as it swung around.

    Lucky ran laps around the training trio, his barks of encouragement blending with the swish of arrows and the thuds against the punching bag. in the midst of the orchestrated chaos, Lucky's exuberance got the best of him. With an unforeseen burst of energy, he darted toward Kate, running into her legs and causing her to lose her balance.

    The unexpected collision resulted in Kate stumbling over, her bow falling to the floor and her arms windmilling as she tried and failed to regain her footing. A chorus of laughter erupted from the nearest onlookers as she landed on her backside: Clint with a hearty chuckle, Nat pausing mid-punch to smirk, and even Fanny huffed as if she was amused. The akita watched the spectacle with an air of nonchalance, her tail twitching as she sat by Yelena’s feet, her head resting on the toe of the blonde’s boot.

    Laughter echoed in the air as Kate looked up from her seated position, a mix of embarrassment and amusement on her face. Lucky, having completed his impromptu obstacle course, sat beside her, wagging his tail as if to say, "Mission accomplished." The brunette reached a hand up to scratch behind his ears, a smile plastered on her face as she petted the dog.

    Yelena's lips curved into a smirk, her eyes sparkling with a mischievous glint. Laura nudged her playfully, a silent acknowledgment of the humour in the situation. Yelena, often reserved and stoic, found amusement in the predictability of the moment. She had told Kate many times that Lucky needed training by a firm hand; he was a rascal. The corners of her eyes crinkled with a rare smile as she continued to watch Kate dust herself off with a bemused expression.

    Laura turned to Yelena with a thoughtful look on her face. The gentle creaking of the porch swing provided a comforting backdrop to their conversation along with the far-off laughter that echoed across the yard, they created a space for introspection amidst the tranquillity of the farm.

    "Yelena," Laura began, her voice carrying a genuine curiosity, "what are your plans after all this… mess?" The woman questioned herself as she ended her sentence, unsure of how to describe their current situation.

    Yelena, guarded with her emotions met Laura's gaze with a level stare. The question lingered in the air, and Laura, with a hint of vulnerability turned her head to gaze across the yard with a blank stare, continued, "You know, Natasha used to talk about wanting a family before Vormir happened. I'm not sure if that's still the case or not. People change. And coming back from the dead? That’s going to change someone."

    Yelena nodded in understanding, recognizing the profound impact that Vormir had on Natasha, for she knew the impact it had had on herself. Leaning back on the porch swing, Yelena considered the question further before answering, "I never thought much about it," she admitted in her distinctive Russian accent. "Survival was the priority for so much of my life. But now, I am free…” The blonde said with a smile and a sense of levity that Laura had not heard in her voice before, “Yet… I am still not sure."

    Laura, sensing the weight behind Yelena's words, continued with a touch of sincerity, "Have you ever wanted a family, Yelena?"

    Yelena's gaze drifted, her eyes scanning the vast fields before her, as if the landscape held the threads of a past, she was still unravelling.

    "Да," she replied, a quiet affirmation that seemed to carry the weight of untold stories. "I wanted a Мама and a Папа like the storybooks had. I wanted a сестра that I coul-" Yelena stopped herself for a moment, the unspoken words lingering in the air. Taking a breath, she continued, "Yes, Laura Barton. I guess I did, but not in the same way Natasha dreamed." Laura listened, sensing the complexities woven into Yelena's desires. The Russian phrases carried a poignant melody, a glimpse into a yearning for familial connections that had been overshadowed by the harsh realities of life.

    "Sometimes," Laura spoke, her voice softening, "we seem to find ourselves in places we never expected. Nat may not have gotten the great love and the children she wished for, but she managed to find two families. You could have the same, Yelena.”

    Yelena considered Laura's words, her gaze returning to the farm. “This farm… it's... different. I never thought I'd find myself in a place like this. It’s… quiet, peaceful.” The tranquillity of the farm, a stark contrast to the tumultuous life Yelena had known, held a certain allure. "Different can be good," Laura said, her eyes reflecting a shared appreciation for the calm that surrounded them – the kids weren’t home yet. "Take the calm as a chance to redefine what family means for you, to build something that resonates with who you are now." Yelena nodded thoughtfully, the notion of redefining family echoing in her mind. It was a concept she hadn't considered before – the possibility of creating a family that reflected the person she had become, rather than one defined by her past. The bonds with her pseudo- family were intertwined with duty, manipulation, and a shared history of a life shaped by the sinister designs of the Red Room. The idea of building a family that resonated with her present self, free from the constraints of the Red Room's expectations, felt liberating. "I've always been... alone," Yelena admitted, her words carrying a weight that hinted at years of solitude. “But I do not mind it. It is easier sometimes... shutting everyone out.” Yelena added, her tone a mixture of acceptance and resilience.

    Laura recognized the duality in Yelena's statement—the acknowledgment of the comfort found in solitude, juxtaposed with the underlying longing for something more. “It’s also sounds rather lonely.” Laura commented, her voice carrying a gentle concern only a mother could manage. She observed Yelena's conflicted emotions, the fine line between self- preservation and the isolation that threatened to become a barrier to genuine connection. "You might come to find, my dear, that we often find solace in the most unexpected places," Laura continued, her gaze drifting towards her husband once more. A tender smile played on her lips as she spoke, her words carrying a wisdom born from years of experience. “You might not be as alone as you think."

    Yelena turned to Laura many minutes later, her eyes reflecting the subtle shifts in her emotions.

    "You know," Yelena began, her voice carrying a sincerity that Laura had been accustomed to when it was just the two of them, "I don't feel as lonely as I used to." Laura met Yelena's gaze with a knowing smile.

    "Sometimes," Yelena continued, her words measured yet genuine, "it feels like I've stumbled upon something I didn't know I was missing." The blonde finished as her hands started running through Fanny’s fur. Though it seemed like Yelena's comment referred to the dog, Laura sensed that the blonde's thoughts were focused elsewhere.

    Laura smiled softly, recognizing the depth behind Yelena's words. She watched as Yelena's gaze drifted, lost in contemplation, her fingers tracing patterns in Fanny's fur. “You don't have to carry the weight of the world alone, Yelena. You’ll learn that soon enough. Clint and I are pretty well-versed in the subject nowadays, and we’ll teach you all about it honey.” Laura teased, though an undertone of seriousness simmered beneath the comment. “It is all I know.” Yelena murmured softly, her voice carrying a weight that hinted at years of carrying burdens too heavy for one person to bear alone.

    “Hmm?”

    “The weight of the world.”

    “Why’s that sweetheart?” Laura inquired gently; her tone filled with maternal concern. “Who do you go to when the person who used to comfort you is the one who brought you pain?” Yelena's question hung in the air, heavy with the weight of unresolved emotions and the ache of betrayal.

    Laura, perceptive and compassionate, sensed the depth behind Yelena's words. "Do you mean Natasha?" she asked gently, her voice a soothing balm that invited Yelena to share the burden she carried.

    Yelena hesitated; the vulnerability etched on her face. "I... I shouldn't be talking about this. I'm sorry," she apologized hastily, her instinct for self-preservation kicking in. In her mind, Laura was not just a sympathetic ear but also a friend of Natasha's, someone who might find it difficult to navigate the complexities of Yelena's feelings. She got caught up in the conversation and forgot she was not talking to Kate who was a neutral ear in this whole situation – the blonde thought Kate was actually more on her side, but the brunette would never admit it for her fear of being beat up by Nat.

    Before Laura could respond, Yelena, grappling with a mixture of emotions, stood up abruptly. "I shouldn't have said anything. I don't want to burden you with this. You are her family.” she declared; the air heavy with the unspoken pain she carried. With a quick nod of apology, Yelena retreated, the echo of her footsteps fading into the evening.

    Clint, Nat, Kate, and Lucky approached the porch steps around a half hour later, their cheeks red and foreheads sweaty from their activity. Lucky panted quickly, his tongue lolling out, heading straight inside to splash water all over the floor no doubt.

    The door swung shut, muffling the sounds of Lucky's enthusiastic water escapades. The group walked up the porch steps, a glow of accomplishment evident on their faces. Kate bounced up the steps, the fact she was able to start shooting again had really improved her mood over the past week.

    Laura looked up from her thoughts, a welcoming smile gracing her face. "Back already? You guys look like you've been through a workout."

    Clint chuckled, wiping a bead of sweat from his forehead. "Well, someone decided to make it a bit more interesting by adding some unexpected hurdles to the training session," he gestured towards Kate, who was trying to suppress a grin.

    Kate shot Clint a playful glare. "Hey, I can't control what Lucky decides to do. Blame him." Natasha smirked, adding, "Lucky's just keeping things lively around here. Can't fault him for that."

    The brunette approached Laura, who was still sat on the porch swing. Kate scanned the area, her brow furrowing in confusion. "Hey, Laura," she called out, "Where'd Yelena go?" Laura turned towards Kate, her expression softening with concern. "I think she needed some space."

    Kate’s brow furrowed. Yelena had looked completely content sat out here with Laura when she had looked over a couple times earlier, the blonde had even looked like she was holding back a laugh when Kate ended up on the floor from Lucky’s overexcitement. "Is everything okay?" Kate asked, her voice laced with worry.

    Before Laura could respond, Clint's phone rang, interrupting the conversation. With a quick glance at the caller ID, he answered the call, stepping aside to speak with Steve in private. The urgency in Clint's voice hinted at the importance of the conversation, leaving the rest of the group to exchange worried glances.

    Kate's apprehension grew as she watched Clint's expression shift from curiosity to grave concern. She exchanged a quick glance with Natasha, who was already scanning the area for any signs of trouble.

    After a few moments, Clint ended the call, his jaw set in a grim line. "Someone turn on the TV. Now." he instructed, his tone leaving no room for argument.

    The urgency in his voice spurred the group into action. They hurried inside, gathering around the television in the living room. Nat quickly found the remote and switched on the TV, flipping through channels until she landed on a news broadcast.

    It was nearing the beginning of December when the group next heard from Steve. Heavy snowfall had blanketed the landscape in the past week, turning the farm into a winter wonderland. The serene beauty, however, couldn't mask the underlying tension within the household.

    The snow had pretty much trapped Kate in Iowa, much to her frustration. She was eager to get back to New York City, but the weather had other plans. The snowy roads, blizzard-like winds and freezing temperatures made travel nearly impossible, leaving her stuck in the heartland.

    Yelena, on the other hand, seemed unaffected by the weather. She spent most of her time on her phone, a furrowed brow and a steely gaze revealing the intensity of her conversations. She made calls home and contacted various contacts, all in an effort to unravel the intricacies of her Valentina situation. Since that night at the farm, Yelena hadn't elaborated further on the details, leaving the others in the dark, much to their annoyance.

    The message from Steve had bought a glimmer of hope.

    The notification chimed on the arrival of Steve's message, breaking the subdued atmosphere in the living room. Clint, Natasha, Kate, and Yelena gathered around the phone as Steve's message unfolded: Clint, I'm back at the Compound, and I've come across some information that could be crucial. However, it's not something I'm comfortable sharing over the phone. The stakes are high, and we can't afford to take any chances. Meet me at the Compound as soon as you can. Stay safe. Steve The room had fallen into a contemplative silence as each member of the group absorbed the message that Clint read out. Natasha's stoic expression betrayed a flicker of concern whilst Clint's jaw clenched as his eyes reread the message over and over.

    Yelena, who had been engrossed in her own intense phone conversations, looked up from her device with an undecipherable gaze. The weight of her Valentina situation mingled with the uncertainty of Kate’s with Kingpin was a lot to bear already, let alone without having to go back to the place that had once been her worst nightmare. The blonde looked back to her phone a second later, fingers tapping away on the keyboard almost immediately. Natasha was first to speak and voiced the sentiment that was on everyone's mind. "Well, this just got a whole lot more interesting."

    “I wonder what he’s got.” Clint mused; his expression wary but intrigued none the less. The group hadn’t heard from Steve in what seemed like weeks. The last they heard was that he had met up with Bucky and coincidentally Sam to fill them in and hope to get some insight on the Russian operatives they were coming up against. Clint, Natasha, and Kate had found themselves in a state of limbo, caught between the desire to act and the lack of information to guide their actions. The farm, usually a place of warmth and camaraderie, now felt like a temporary refuge from the storm brewing outside and within the confines of their tangled circumstances.

    The silence in the house was occasionally broken by the crackling of the fireplace or the distant howl of the wind, but most commonly by a laughing Nate or a squealing Lila. Kate's restlessness could not be fixed by a snowball fight like the kid’s was. Her mood was evident as she paced around the living room, her eyes occasionally flicking towards Yelena, who remained engrossed in her conversations, her expression unreadable.

    Natasha watched Kate's restless movements with a mixture of sympathy and concern. She could sense the weight of the situation bearing down on the relatively inexperienced woman, the uncertainty of their circumstances taking its toll. There was a familiar restlessness in Kate that Natasha recognized, a reflection of the impatience she had often portrayed when Fury would not let her go out on every mission that came to his desk. Yet, there was more to it than the youthful eagerness Nat had possessed, although Clint had informed the redhead Kate also had that in bundles. The young woman's energy was palpable, her determination to make a difference evident in every step she took.

    Natasha sensed the weight of responsibility pressing on Kate's shoulders. The burden of the unknown, the desire to protect those she cared about, and the frustration of being confined by circumstances—all of it was etched on Kate's face. Natasha recognized that look, having worn it herself in countless high-stakes situations. Natasha admired Kate's spirit, her ability to confront adversity head-on. She understood the struggle of finding one's place in a world filled with danger and uncertainty. Natasha saw in Kate a reflection of her own younger self, eager to prove herself and carve out her own path in a world filled with enhanced persons. It was even more impressive to the redhead knowing the comfy background that the archer came from. It would have been so much easier for Kate to cruise through that life as a rich man’s daughter than face challenges to protect those she loves, or strangers in need of assistance.

    Natasha observed Kate's restless pacing with a keen eye and Natasha recognized the telltale signs of a mind racing with unspoken thoughts. She glanced at Yelena, catching her sister's attention. In a swift exchange of glances, Natasha spoke in Russian, her tone low but urgent. "Делай что-то," she urged Yelena, her voice carrying the weight of concern. Natasha knew that Yelena, with her unique understanding of Kate, could find a way to ease the tension that seemed to be building within the young Avenger.

    The blonde raised her face out of her phone at the sound of her native tongue, and green eyes moving to look at Kate after being nodded in the direction of the brunette by Natasha. Yelena, in response to Natasha's subtle directive, rose from her seat and approached Kate. She placed a hand on the woman’s back as she walked up behind her, the archer jumping slightly, not even realising the blonde was there because she was so caught up in her head. Natasha watched as Yelena began speaking to her in a calming tone. The two engaged in a brief conversation, and as Yelena's words worked their magic, Kate's restless energy seemed to subside. Natasha observed the exchange with a sense of satisfaction, knowing that her sister had always had a knack for connecting with people in ways that transcended language. In that moment, the unspoken bond between Yelena and Kate became even more apparent to the redhead.

    Whether the bond went deeper than friendship?

    That was still unclear to Nat.

    It was almost 3am when Yelena practically silently opened the front door of the Barton’s home, the cold winter air blasting its way into the heat emitting from the house. The blonde shut the door just as quietly behind her, not without nudging the two dogs back inside first, Fanny especially eager to follow her owner out into the night.

    Yelena had barely made it halfway down the driveway when Natasha, ever vigilant, sensed her departure. In a heartbeat, Natasha emerged from the house, closing the distance with purposeful strides. She caught up to Yelena, her gloved hand reaching out to gently grasp the blonde's shoulder, halting her in her tracks. The blonde did not react to the contact, her senses noticing Nat’s presence as soon as the redhead had opened the front door. Nat turned Yelena around, so they were facing eachother. The silence between them spoke volumes.

    "Where are you going?" Natasha questioned harshly; her breath visible in the frigid air. "I need some air," The younger assassin replied tersely.

    Natasha studied Yelena's face, “No. You are running.” Natasha declared with a conviction that cut through the chilly air. It was a statement, not a question, an assertion born from years of understanding the nuances of each other's actions.

    Yelena's resolve wavered for a moment, the mask of stoicism slipping to reveal the turmoil beneath. She hesitated in her response to Nat’s call out. The silence hung heavy, broken only by the distant whispers of the night. Natasha's words pierced through Yelena's defences, cutting through the layers of evasion and restraint. The accusation hung heavy in the air, an uncomfortable truth that Yelena couldn't deny. She felt exposed, vulnerable under Natasha's penetrating gaze.

    Yelena's resolve faltered, the weight of Natasha's observation pressing down on her like a leaden cloak. She opened her mouth to speak, but the words caught in her throat, choked by the swell of emotions threatening to overwhelm her. For a moment, Yelena stood frozen, her mind racing with a myriad of conflicting thoughts and feelings. She wrestled with the urge to retreat, to flee from the uncomfortable confrontation unfolding before her. Natasha's hand on Yelena's shoulder softened its grip, now offering comfort rather than restraint. "Whatever it is. We'll face it together, like we always have," Natasha reassured, her voice carrying a quiet strength that only pulled a scoff from Yelena’s mouth. “Бред сивой кобылы.” The blonde pulled her arm from the redhead’s grasp, breaking whatever moment they were about to have. The Russian phrase, a colourful expression akin to "nonsense," conveyed Yelena's dismissal of Natasha's reassurance. It was evident that the scars of their shared history ran deep, and Yelena's trust in promises had been fractured. Natasha's brow furrowed in concern as Yelena's tone turned sharply dismissive. "You're a liar, Natasha," she accused, her voice sharp and cutting. "All you do is make promises and then break every single last one of them." Yelena's frustration boiled over, her once simmering anger bubbling to the surface. The pain of their fractured relationship and the wounds from past betrayals were etched across Yelena's face. In the stillness of the night, she finally found the words to voice the deep-rooted hurt that had festered within her. "Do you even realize what you did to me on Vormir?" Yelena's voice trembled with a mixture of sorrow and anger. "All I had in this world was you, моя старшая сестра, and then you threw yourself off a cliff like it was nothing. Like I was nothing."

    Natasha winced at the accusation, her own eyes reflecting a mix of guilt and remorse. She had known the impact her sacrifice would have on those she left behind, but the gravity of Yelena's pain was a heavy burden to bear.

    "You thought of everyone else," Yelena continued, her voice breaking. "How it would affect your team, how it would save the world. How Barton should live instead of you. But you didn't think about me, did you? You didn't consider what losing you would do to the one person who cared about you the most. You thought about your new family before the one you threw to the side like trash." Her fists clenched at her sides, her nails digging into her palms as she fought to contain her rage.

    The weight of Yelena's words hung in the air; a poignant reminder of the emotional toll Natasha's sacrifice had taken on those who loved her. Yelena's anger was intertwined with the profound sense of abandonment she had felt when Natasha chose duty over their bond. “I did it for you Yelena. I did it so you could live the life you always dreamed младшая сестра.” Natasha spoke for the first time, her voice uncharacteristically wobbly. Yelena, however, was not easily swayed. She looked at Natasha, her expression a mix of disbelief and sorrow. "Dreamed?" she scoffed bitterly. "I never dreamed, Natasha. All I had were nightmares. The Red Room made sure of that. But if I had, if I could have dreamed while stuck in that Red Room hell, I would never have a dreamed of a life without my сестра.”

    Natasha's eyes glistened with unshed tears as she listened to Yelena's painful admission. The weight of her actions bore down on her, a heavy burden that she couldn't shake off. "I never wanted to leave you alone, Yelena. You had Melina, Alexei, the widows… I-I thought I was giving you a chance at something better."

    Yelena's shoulders slumped, the fire in her eyes dimming. "Better? I would have chosen a lifetime of those nightmares if it meant having you by my side, Наташа." "I'm sorry, Yelena," Natasha whispered, her voice choked with emotion. "You made a choice, Natasha," Yelena spat out, her voice laced with bitterness. "And you left me behind to deal with the consequences. I had to pick up the pieces you left while you moved on to whatever comes next. I had to learn to live without you, and I finally was doing just fine without you, and then-” The blonde spoke harshly before taking a breath. Natasha watched as her sister looked up to the sky, her chest heaving up and down as she collected herself.

    “You think you can just come back here and pretend like everything's fine?" Yelena's voice cracked with emotion, her anger giving way to the raw hurt that lay beneath. "Well, it's not fine, Natasha. It's not fine at all." Yelena's frustration spilled out, her voice rising with each word. "I had to find out you were gone by the news. Through some TV anchors half-hearted apologies and condolences. Turns out none of your snobby friends know I exist, except for Barton.” The blonde was shaking with anger now.

    Natasha's eyes widened; regret etched across her features. "Yelena, I didn't mean to—" Yelena's laughter, bitter and devoid of humour, interrupted Natasha's attempt at an explanation. "You didn't mean to? Well, congratulations, Natasha. You succeeded. You left me alone, just like everyone else. Again."

    "I did what I had to do," Natasha responded, her voice gentle but firm. Yelena's eyes narrowed, her frustration evident. "You always do what you have to do, don't you? You always had to be the hero.”

    A shadow of guilt passed over Natasha's features. Yelena took a step back, the cold air biting into her skin.

    "You promised me, Natasha," Yelena continued, her voice carrying the weight of betrayal. "When we were little, you promised we'd get out of the Red Room together. But you escaped, and I was left behind, chemically subjugated."

    Natasha's expression tightened, the memory of that broken promise haunting her. "And then, after we defeated the Red Room, you promised to see me soon, to keep in touch," Yelena went on, her voice growing more accusatory. "But did you?"

    Natasha struggled to find the right words, knowing she had failed Yelena in more ways than one.

    "No, you didn't," Yelena answered her own question, bitterness seeping into her tone. "You left me waiting… watching any scraps of news to catch glimpses of you in your fancy tech, next to your fancy friends. And then there was the snap. I come back, and you're dead. Five more years of my life, lost to something outside of my control. Tell me you don’t see it. Look me in the eye and tell me you don’t see the irony in that.” The blonde snapped. Natasha's eyes glistened with unshed tears as she listened to Yelena's pain. "You don't just get to come back from the dead and start telling me how I should live my life. Я не та шестилетняя девочка, которую вы помните, которая ждет, пока ее старшая сестра-герой придет и спасет ее.”

    Natasha felt the sting of Yelena's words, a painful reminder of the time she had lost with her sister. Yelena had grown into a formidable woman, capable of navigating the complexities of a dangerous world.

    “Working for Valentina gave me a sense of purpose when I had nothing. It paid well and I was good at it. The situation it puts me in now is far from ideal, but I can handle myself.” The blonde said in a calmer voice as she explained herself.

    “Was? You no longer do?”

    “Technically I guess I am still employed. I have not taken a contract for many months.” Yelena responded cryptically.

    “Why?”

    Yelena only shrugged in response. Yelena's gaze bore into Natasha's as if she was challenging the redhead to pry.

    Natasha, undeterred by Yelena's challenging gaze, leaned forward slightly, her eyes narrowing with a mix of concern and determination. "Yelena, where are you going?” she asked, her voice steady.

    Her voice was low and edged with determination as she responded, "I'm going to take the head off the snake.”

    Natasha's eyes widened further, realizing the gravity of Yelena's intent. "Yelena. Killing Kingpin won't solve anything. Besides, death is too easy a punishment for a man who has made so many suffer so much.”

    “Greed is a powerful force even a prison cannot contain Natasha. That is why I blew Dreykov to smithereens. He would not have stopped, not even behind bars.”

    “You cannot compare Fisk with Dreykov.” The redhead snarls.

    “They may not share blood, but they are cut from the same cloth,” Yelena shrugs, “But… I guess you’re right. This is a totally different situation.”

    “Thank you.” Natasha responds, hoping Yelena is reconsidering her approach. “It is different because I will not sit by and let Kate be tortured by an evil man. If I have to get my hands dirty to protect her, then so be it. If I have to choose between letting him live and risking Kate's safety, or ending him and ensuring she's safe, the choice is obvious.” Yelena asserts, her eyes filled with a determination that Natasha recognizes all too well. Natasha sighed, recognizing the fierce protectiveness Yelena felt toward Kate. "I understand, Yelena. But there's more at play here than just vengeance."

    Yelena's gaze hardened, her resolve unyielding. "I'm not just seeking vengeance, Natasha. I'm protecting my family. You might not understand that, but I won't let my history become Kate’s future.”

    Natasha knew there was no changing Yelena's mind on her want for Fisk’s head at that moment. Natasha recognized the depth of Yelena's commitment, understanding the lengths she would go to shield those she cared about.

    As Yelena turned to leave, Natasha called out, "Wait, Yelena."

    The blonde stopped, glancing back at Natasha with a questioning look. "I don't have time for this, Natasha."

    "You can't just leave, not without saying goodbye to Kate," Natasha pleaded, her eyes searching Yelena's for a hint of understanding.

    The blonde scoffed, "I'm not in the mood for sentimental farewells."

    "I get it, Yelena. I know you're angry, and I understand why. But don't let that anger drive you away without at least giving Kate a chance to say goodbye. She cares about you, and you her… more than you're willing to admit." Yelena's gaze wavered for a moment, a flicker of vulnerability breaking through her tough exterior. Natasha pressed on, "She's been through enough, losing her mom and now dealing with all this. Leaving without a word will only hurt her more. You owe her that much."

    Yelena hesitated, torn between her anger and the underlying truth in Natasha's words. Yelena hesitated; her gaze fixed on the distant horizon. The weight of her decision pressed heavily upon her, but Natasha's words resonated with her. Slowly, she nodded before walking straight past her sister and back up the driveway.

    The blonde hadn’t felt like making the long plane journey to St Petersburg tonight anyways. The exhaustion from the emotional confrontation with Natasha weighed heavily on her, and in that moment, all she longed for was the comfort of Kate's arms. She wanted to feel the reassuring embrace of someone who understood her in ways that no one else could. Yelena's steps were heavy with weariness as she made her way to the bedroom, where Kate was likely still sleeping. Upon entering the bedroom, she noticed Kate curled up in bed, her form outlined by the gentle light filtering through the curtains. The sight of Kate, peacefully asleep, offered a momentary reprieve from the turmoil that had gripped Yelena. The tension in her shoulders began to ease as she approached the bed, the weariness of the night taking its toll.

    With a sigh, Yelena dumped her bag on the floor, not bothering with the usual meticulous organization. The weight of the night seemed to lift slightly as she shed the layers of her outer self, the burden of her responsibilities momentarily set aside. In the dim light, she changed into more comfortable clothes, the act a small ritual of shedding the armour she wore in the outside world.

    Yelena climbed into bed with careful precision, the mattress giving a soft creak under her weight. As she settled under the covers, she instinctively moved closer to Kate, her tired body seeking the comforting presence of the brunette.

    She carefully squeezed herself into Kate's arms, finding a comfortable spot in the curve of her archer’s body. The warmth that radiated from Kate enveloped Yelena, offering a sense of security and comfort. With a quiet sigh, Yelena pressed herself against Kate's warmth, fitting into the curve of her body as if it were a custom-made mould.

    The movement stirred Kate from her slumber, her eyes fluttering open halfway. In the dim light, she registered Yelena's presence, and a drowsy smile tugged at the corners of her lips. Yelena's familiar scent and the comforting weight of her presence were a welcome interruption to Kate's dreams.

    "Lena?" Kate mumbled; her voice heavy with sleep. "You okay?"

    Yelena pressed a gentle kiss to Kate's forehead, her lips lingering for a moment before she whispered, her fingers gently tracing patterns on Kate's arm., “Just tired." Kate didn't press further, the archer not fully awake and evidently content with the added warmth, simply nodded and nestled deeper into the pillows. The brunette also shifted slightly, making room for Yelena to settle even closer. "Sleep," Kate mumbled, her voice a soothing murmur.

    Yelena draped an arm over Kate's waist, holding her close and burying her face into Kate’s chest. The blonde felt the tension in her own body begin to dissipate. The events of the night, the heated argument with Natasha, the decision to confront Kingpin, all faded into the background. With Kate's heartbeat as her guide, Yelena found a momentary respite from the storm that raged outside. As the world slept beneath a blanket of snow, Yelena allowed herself to succumb to the warmth and kindness of Kate's embrace.

    And if Yelena held onto the brunette a little tighter that night, well, that was just how she needed it to be.
