    In the living room of the Avengers compound, Clint, Nat, Steve, Bucky, and Sam gathered on the comfortable couches, catching up on the events that had transpired since they last met. The raised voices of Kate and Yelena reverberated through the living room, creating an awkward silence among the remaining Avengers. Clint exchanged a knowing glance with Natasha, both recognizing the distinct sound of a heated argument. Steve's brow furrowed with concern, while Sam and Bucky shared a glance, clearly picking up on the tension. Sam leaned back in his chair, raising an eyebrow. "Sounds like the newbies are having a heated discussion. Are we expecting a catfight, or is it something more serious?" Natasha shot him a disapproving look, her concern evident. “Normally you can’t get them away from each other. I’ve never heard them so much have a disagreement, let alone shout at one another like this.”

    "Yeah, this isn't the usual. Something's up." Clint agreed, a frown on his lips. "Maybe we should give them a moment to cool off. It's been a tense day for everyone." Steve said into his drink.

    The tension in the living room heightened as Kate's voice echoed through the corridor, the group exchanged uneasy glances, the seriousness of the situation sinking in. “Don’t come and find me until you have figured it out, Yelena."

    "That doesn't sound good," Bucky remarked, his eyes flicking towards the hallway. The sound of Kate's frustrated footsteps echoed in the corridor not a moment later, indicating her departure from the confrontation. The group sat in silence for a few moments, waiting for Yelena or Kate to break the silence but they didn’t.

    Clint poured himself a drink and settled into an armchair, a comfortable routine after a long day. "So, Steve, what's the latest?" he inquired, taking a sip from his glass. Steve leaned forward, his forearms resting on his thighs, "Bucky and Sam recently visited the Raft to talk to Zemo.” He nodded to the duo as he mentioned their names, “It turns out, he had some more information about Nagel, the scientist behind the Flag Smashers' serum, which he hadn’t previously shared."

    Bucky nodded, adding to Steve's revelation. "Wilfred Nagel was a scientist who had recreated the super solider serum after being recruited by HYDRA, he was later recruited by the CIA. Nagel was able to make significant progress in its development as the CIA possessed Isaiah Bradley's blood samples. After the blip, the CIA terminated their super solider programme, so Nagel turned to someone called the Power Broker to fund his research. The Flag Smasher’s stole all the vials he made.”

    Natasha, always quick to connect dots, raised an important question. "Considering Nagel's background with HYDRA, do we think there's a possibility he might have been involved in developing the Lufuthai serum?"

    “There is a gap. Think about it. HYDRA fell but Nagel still would’ve had access to their facilities that were never found. We cannot say for certain SHIELD found every last one.” Clint acknowledged the possible connection.

    “Can we talk to Nagel?” Nat questioned.

    “Dead.” Sam said shortly, “Zemo killed him. His hatred for super soldiers runs deep and this guy was creating them like he was creating Sims.”

    “What did Zemo have to say?” Clint asked, brushing off the fact their one source was dead.

    Bucky and Sam entered the dimly lit room on the Raft Prison where Zemo was held. The former Baron was sitting calmly on a chair, a faint smile playing on his lips as the two approached.

    "Zemo," Sam said with a nod, trying to keep the conversation civil. "We need information about Wilfred Nagel and his connection to any surviving Russian super soldiers, besides him,” Sam stuck his hand up and his thumb out sideways, indicating to Bucky, “What do you know?"

    Zemo leaned back; his eyes locked on the two Avengers. "Nagel," he mused, as if recalling a distant memory. “He was quite the bleeder. His laboratory was no longer sanitary if I recall correctly.”

    Bucky crossed his arms, his expression stern. "Cut to the chase, Zemo. Does the name Lufuthai ring any bells?”

    Zemo's smile widened. “Nagel went underground when HYDRA fell, much like many of his ilk. It made it difficult for the CIA to track him down when they needed his expertise." “Where?” Sam hurried Zemo along. They were against the clock.

    “Nagel's expertise in creating super soldier serums caught the attention of the CIA. Jack Pincer, their liaison, faced the challenge in locating him. HYDRA loyalists weren't eager to be found at that moment in history, or, well ever and Nagel was no exception. Even I will say he was anything but stupid. The CIA needed a skilled tracker, someone familiar with the underworld. Pincer turned to a former SHIELD agent who now worked under him.” Zemo's eyes gleamed with satisfaction. "Ah, so that is the piece of the puzzle you're truly after,” He drawled seeing the glance Bucky and Sam shared, “I don’t believe I’ve been offered anything for this information.”

    Bucky's jaw tensed, his gaze narrowing at Zemo. "You know we're not here to make deals with you."

    "But consider this a valuable piece of information. Nagel's involvement with the Lufuthai might lead you to more dangerous territories. You'll find that this trail is not as straightforward as you think."

    Bucky's jaw clenched, his irritation evident. "Zemo. We're offering you a chance to see the world free of more super soldiers. Sokovia would be avenged," he stated, his tone laced with determination.

    Sam crossed his arms, his patience wearing thin with Zemo’s empty ramblings. "Tell us what you know, Zemo. We're not here to negotiate."

    Zemo leaned back, considering their words. "Very well," he conceded with a sigh. "Nagel was initially reluctant to work with the CIA. But Pincer managed to appeal to his scientific curiosity and convinced him to join their cause. Nagel's work involved enhancing the super soldier serum, making it more potent and efficient. This was more HYDRA’s focus than Nagels, which we know was more of a subtle, modernized, and nuanced variation, the CIA wanted… well, a copy of him.” Zemo slowly nodded to Bucky.

    Bucky's expression didn’t change, his gaze remained fixed on Zemo. "Did he succeed?" Zemo nodded slowly. "He managed to refine HYDRA’S formula, creating a more stable and powerful version of the serum. The CIA lost control of the situation when half the world disappeared, including Nagel. That is why the programme was scrapped.” “So, you’re telling us… Nagel created a more stable version of the serum that HYDRA failed to complete in Siberia.”

    “Yes.” Zemo confirmed with a knowing look.

    “So, what happened to it?” Sam pressed; his brow furrowed with suspicion. “I think you already have the answer to your question.” Zemo replied cryptically. “But how?”

    “That is beyond my knowledge I am afraid my friends.” Zemo admitted, a slither of frustration marring his voice.

    “And we are sure he was telling the truth? This is Zemo.” Natasha glanced around the room sceptically, trying to see if anyone felt the same.

    "As much as we can trust Zemo," Bucky replied, his expression serious. "But he has no reason to lie about this. It's not like he's looking to hinder our cause, not when it's practically everything he stood for when he was a free man."

    Sam raised an eyebrow, injecting a touch of humour into the serious discussion. "Do we only have Zemo to rely on for intel? Last time I checked, he wasn't exactly on the Avenger's speed dial."

    Natasha's gaze narrowed as she considered the implications. "Who's this ex-SHIELD agent Zemo mentioned? Do we have a name?"

    "That's a loose end we need to pull on and follow. Zemo's not one to throw around names so I doubt he’ll tell even if he does know, and if there's a former SHIELD agent involved, we need to know who it is and if they’re alive.” Steve agreed with Nat.

    "SHIELD had files on everyone. It's a needle in a haystack situation, though. Hundreds of names. The organization was massive. We could be chasing shadows." Clint chimed in with an idea of where they could start but it would take them weeks and they didn’t have that amount of time.

    "We need something more specific to narrow down the search. Zemo mentioned a CIA liaison named Jack Pincer who recruited Nagel. If we find out who that former SHIELD agent working for him was, we might have a lead." Sam piped up.

    Yelena's voice cut through the tense atmosphere like a knife.

    "Valentina.”

    The familiar Russian drawl made the group’s heads turn around to where she was standing in an instant, surprised by her sudden appearance and the revelation she brought. The room fell silent for a moment, the revelation sinking in. Natasha's eyes narrowed slightly, "Valentina?”

    "How do you know this?" Sam questioned; his curiosity piqued.

    "I have my ways of gathering information.” Yelena shrugged, a smirk playing on her lips. With a calm demeanour, Yelena mockingly continued, "Contessa Valentina Allegra de Fontaine. She used to work for SHIELD." Her words hung in the air, stirring a new wave of curiosity among the Avengers.

    "You didn’t think to mention this earlier?” Natasha's eyes narrowed as she absorbed the information.

    “You didn’t ask.” Yelena said smarmily. Yelena's timely information raised a few eyebrows, but the urgency of the situation took precedence.

    Sam rolled his eyes, a hint of sarcasm lacing his tone. "Oh, sorry, I must have missed the memo where we were supposed to anticipate your sudden bursts of helpfulness, Yelena." Yelena shot him a mock offended look before shrugging. "I'm full of surprises." Her casual demeanour in delivering critical information was a stark reminder of her unpredictable nature.

    "Well, next time, how about volunteering any info you have before we start pulling our hair out?" Clint quirked an eyebrow at her.

    “Okay Barton. After her parents - who served Leviathan, a secret terrorist network headquartered in Russia - were killed, Valentina was recruited. SHIELD heard of her parents' abilities and how she was shaping up to be the same." Yelena said rapidly, her words firing like a verbal onslaught, clearly aiming to wind up Clint.

    Clint raised an eyebrow at Yelena's quick retort but didn’t say anything back in fear of being on the receiving end of her frustrations, and the archer had a feeling she wouldn’t hold back like she probably had with Kate.

    “We need to find out what she's after and if she's connected to Kingpin. Any leads on her current whereabouts?" Nat pulled the group back to their main line of conversation. “I've got some contacts digging into it.” Yelena, maintaining her stoic expression, responded. “Sonya?” Clint questioned.

    “I would not involve Sonya unless it was a necessity.” The blonde shook her head. Natasha's piercing gaze fell on Yelena. "We don't have the luxury of sidelining resources, especially if Valentina is involved. Sonya might have valuable intel.” Yelena did not miss Nat’s secret hint towards the widows.

    “They will not be having anything to do with this.” Yelena’s jaw tightened. “Why not?”

    “Because I will not ask them. And I will not use them for personal gain.” Yelena spat at her sister who almost recoiled at the tone of the blonde’s voice.

    Natasha squared her shoulders, meeting Yelena's intense gaze. "This isn't about personal gain, Yelena. It's about protecting people, including the ones we care about. If they can help, we should consider it."

    Yelena's expression remained hardened. "I won't put their lives on the line. Not for this. Not after everything they've been through."

    “Not even to save Kate’s life?” Nat’s question was a low blow. It struck a nerve, and Yelena's expression faltered for a moment. The mention of Kate's name added another layer of complexity to the already tense conversation, and as someone who had become an unexpected but significant part of her life, her name struck a chord.

    Yelena's expression then tightened at Natasha's mention of Kate. The mention of someone she cared about shifted the dynamics of the conversation. "Don't play that card, Natasha. Kate can handle herself. I don't need you using her to guilt-trip me."

    Natasha's gaze held a mixture of concern and frustration. "Yelena, we're talking about stopping Kingpin and whatever Valentina is up to. This goes beyond personal vendettas. Lives are at stake, including Kate's."

    “Kate would not want the widows to fight for her.” Yelena retorted, her voice tinged with defiance. "She wouldn't want anyone risking their lives for her. She's not helpless, Natasha." The blonde acknowledged the irony in her words to her sister, realizing that what she told Kate didn't truly reflect her thoughts about the brunette. She was simply angry and needed an outlet, and unfortunately, Kate became the unintended target in that moment. “Kingpin is a threat, and we need all the help we can get. Valentina's involvement adds another layer of danger.” Nat sighed at her sister’s stubbornness, “The widows were trained for situations like this. And you don't get to decide what Kate wants or doesn't want. And she certainly wouldn't want you to put her safety above everything else."

    Yelena's gaze softened for a brief moment, a flicker of doubt crossing her features before she regained her composure. "I'll do what I have to do to keep my family safe. Even if it means going against you."

    "Aren't you guys family…? You know what? I’ve decided this is my new favourite soap opera." Sam couldn’t resist chiming in mid argument.

    Yelena shot him a deadpan look, unamused by the levity in the situation. "This is not a joke, birdman."

    Sam raised his hands in surrender, acknowledging the seriousness of the conversation. "Alright, alright. Just trying to lighten the mood. We've got enough enemies without turning on each other."

    Yelena rolled her eyes at the banter but remained steadfast in her decision. "I'll work with you until this threat is over, but don't expect me to change my stance on involving others. The widows are off limits Natasha.” She said turning to face the redhead before turning on her heel and walking out of the room.

    As Yelena walked out of the room, her decisive footsteps echoing in the corridor, the lingering question hung in the air. Clint, glancing at Natasha, asked, "Where do you think she's going?"

    Natasha's gaze remained fixed on the door through which Yelena had just exited. "She's going to do things her way. We can't control her, and trying to force her into our strategy might backfire. Yelena has her own methods, and we'll have to trust that she knows what she's doing. She's not one to sit idly by. If she thinks there's a lead or a threat, she'll go after it, with or without us."

    "Guess we'll have to keep an eye out for any surprise entrances or exits. It's like having a ninja in the house." Sam remarked with a smirk.

    “She’s gone to go make up with Kate.” Steve said quietly, his gaze fixed on the doorway where Yelena had disappeared.

    “Why are you so certain?” Bucky questioned.

    "Everything Yelena's done since I met her has been centred around family and those she loves. Even when she's frustrated, that drive remains. And, well, Kate's her family as much as Nat is." Steve's response was measured, his eyes reflecting a depth of understanding. Bucky raised an eyebrow, still sceptical. "You sure about that, Rogers?" Steve nodded. "Yeah. I've seen enough of it to recognize the signs. Yelena might not always agree with everyone, but when it comes down to it, she’ll go after Kate every time." Natasha's voice carried a reflective tone as she recounted the moment from the farm. "After our fight at the farm, I expected Yelena to come after me, to continue the fight or demand answers. But instead, she went to Kate. It's... telling, in a way."

    Her gaze shifted to the others, seeking confirmation or perhaps a different perspective on the matter. "Yelena's actions have always spoken louder than her words. She's fiercely loyal to those she cares about, and her priorities are clear. If she's left the room in this middle of this…”

    Bucky, ever the sceptic, crossed his arms. "Doesn't mean she won't do something reckless." Sam chimed in with a smirk, "We're talking about the sister to the woman who told the government to, and I quote, ‘kiss her ass’. ‘Reckless' might as well be her middle name."

    As Yelena ascended the stairs, her thoughts swirled in her mind. The echoes of her and Kate’s heated argument still resonated, a discordant melody that unsettled her. She knew she had to find Kate, to bridge the gap that had erupted between them.

    The dimly lit corridors of the Avengers compound felt like a labyrinth, and each step she took seemed to echo the distance that had materialized. The blonde swore the building had no furniture at all sometimes, most of the compound was empty corridor after empty corridor. Yelena couldn't shake the weight of her own words from her head - the sharpness of her retorts and the bitterness she hadn't intended to unleash – she could only imagine how they were haunting the brunette.

    The assassin wondered how things had escalated so quickly, how a disagreement had morphed into a clash of emotions. Yelena's mind replayed the moments, the frustration that had clouded her judgment, the unchecked anger that had spilled over. Her instincts, honed in the harsh realities of her life, had betrayed her in that moment and Kate had borne the brunt of it.

    Yelena couldn't escape the nagging worry that she had pushed Kate away, perhaps irreparably. Even if the brunette had told her to come and find her once she had figured it out. The bond she shared with the archer was a fragile thing, woven with trust and vulnerability, a type of relationship that the blonde had never had before. Yelena knew she had to navigate the terrain between them carefully if she wanted to salvage what they had. In her search for Kate, Yelena questioned her own motives. Why had she let her anger overtake reason? Why had she allowed the ghosts of her past to cast shadows on her present? The answers eluded her, buried beneath layers of pride and stubbornness. As she reached the top floor, apprehension gripped Yelena. She steeled herself for the confrontation, knowing that apologies were not her forte. Yet, she couldn't bear the thought of Kate harbouring resentment towards her. This past year had pretty much been her and the archer against the world.

    She finally found the brunette at the largest window at the end of the top floor, gazing out of it into the snowy landscape beyond. Yelena hesitated for a moment before approaching. "Kate," Yelena's voice was softer now, her voice barely above a whisper, lacking the sharp edge from their earlier confrontation. The brunette didn’t turn, but the air between them felt heavy anyway. The blonde hesitated for a moment, taking in the sight of her friend silhouetted against the dim light filtering through the window.

    "I'm sorry, мой маленький ястреб,” Yelena began, her voice trembling slightly, she had noticed the tension in her friend's shoulders and her heart clenched with guilt, "I shouldn't have said those things. I let my anger get the best of me, and I took it out on you. That was wrong, and I regret it so so much."

    Yelena continued so quietly she didn’t know if the brunette could even hear her, "I care about you, Kate. More than I thought I could care about anyone. And I don't want my issues with Nat or anyone else to make you leave.”

    As Yelena spoke, she heard a subtle sound, like a quiet sniff. It was then that she realized Kate was crying. Without hesitation, Yelena walked forward and wrapped her arms around Kate from behind, the warmth of the blanket cocooning them both. Gently, Yelena began to sway side to side, the motion soothing, almost instinctual. With each movement, she whispered soft words of comfort, her lips brushing against Kate's shoulder in tender caresses. She pressed gentle kisses to the back of Kate's neck, her touch a silent promise of reassurance and love.

    Feeling Kate's shoulders tremble, Yelena initiated more affection, gently rubbing small circles on Kate's arms as if to offer comfort through touch. She nuzzled her face into the crook of Kate's neck, pressing a kiss against the soft skin there.

    "I hate seeing you upset, Kate. I never meant to hurt you," Yelena murmured, her voice a soothing melody in the stillness of the night. "I should've never let my frustration spill over onto you. You don't deserve that." Yelena tightened her hold, providing a silent anchor for Kate in the midst of emotional turmoil. The gentle snowfall outside seemed to mirror the delicate balance they were trying to find within their relationship.

    "Forgive me, мой маленький ястреб," Yelena whispered, her lips brushing against Kate's ear. "I'll do whatever it takes to make things right between us. Natasha has taken so much from me. I won’t let her take you too.” Yelena could feel the tension slowly seeping out of Kate's shoulders as she held her close.

    The words hung in the air for a moment, the weight of Yelena's apology mingling with the quiet of the upper floor. And then, as if in response to the sincerity in Yelena's voice, Kate turned around within the circle of Yelena's arms. Their eyes met, the vulnerability in Yelena's gaze mirrored in the depths of Kate's. The blonde searched for any sign of forgiveness, her heart pounding in her chest. Kate's expression softened, a gentle understanding passing between them.

    With a trembling breath, Kate reached up to cup Yelena's cheek, her touch tender and forgiving. "There is nothing to forgive, Yelena," she murmured, her voice barely above a whisper. "I know you didn't mean it."

    Yelena closed her eyes briefly, savouring the warmth of Kate's touch against her cheek. In Kate's embrace even in the Avenger’s Compound, Yelena felt a rare sense of ease wash over her, a calmness she hadn't experienced in what felt a long time. The exhaustion of the day's emotional turmoil weighed heavily on her, and she allowed herself to sink into Kate's warmth, her body relaxing against the brunette's comforting presence.

    It was an unusual vulnerability for Yelena, who had spent most of her life hardened by the harsh realities of her upbringing and the dangerous world she inhabited. But in that moment, with Kate's arms wrapped around her, she felt safe enough to let her guard down, to let herself be vulnerable in a way she rarely allowed. The trust she placed in Kate was implicit, unspoken yet profound. Yelena knew that Kate would protect her, just as she would protect Kate. The brunette’s fingers traced a reassuring pattern on Yelena's back, the harsh edges of the day softening with every stroke.

    “Я никогда не буду заслуживать тебя.” The blonde whispered sleepily into the crook of Kate’s neck, her face pressed against the warm skin there.

    The soft glow from the living room spilled into the hallway as Kate and Yelena made their way downstairs. As they entered, they found the rest of the group engaged in various activities – some deep in conversation, others immersed in the glow of electronic devices. Clint, Steve, Natasha, Bucky, and Sam looked up as the pair entered, their eyes conveying a mix of curiosity and amusement. Yelena wore her trademark stoic expression, but Kate couldn't help but blush under the collective gaze.

    "Kissed and made up then?" Clint raised an eyebrow, a knowing grin playing on his lips. Kate shot Clint a playful glare, her cheeks still tinged with pink. "Mind your business, Clint." Yelena, seemingly unfazed, deadpanned, "Jealous? Missing your wife?”

    Clint laughed, leaning back in his chair. "Okay, enough. We wouldn't want to interrupt your late-night activities. Head to bed then, lovebirds." Yelena shot a mock salute, while Kate couldn't help but roll her eyes. The banter continued as they made their way to the kitchen, the group sharing a moment of lightness amid the threats they faced.

    A few mornings later, the first sunlight of a rainy day filtered through the windows of the Avengers compound, casting a glow over the kitchen where snacks were being devoured by the group rather than an actual lunch being made. Once more the Compound fridge was empty.

    Kate paced back and forth, a restless energy radiating from her, multiple pairs of eyes watching her walk to and from one end of the room to the other. She could barely contain her eagerness to get back into the city after being away for what felt like an eternity. The desire to check on her apartment, make sure things were in order, and maybe even swing around the city rooftops tugged at her.

    Natasha, Clint, and Steve were seated in various corners of the room, discussing the latest intel on Kingpin and Valentina. Their attention shifted to Kate, her impatience radiating like a tangible force.

    "Kate, we've been through this," Clint spoke, his tone firm yet with a hint of understanding. "You can't just waltz into the city right now. It's too dangerous."

    Natasha chimed in, "Yeah, there's a whole list of people who would love to get their hands on you. We can't risk it."

    "I can't stay cooped up here forever," Kate declared, frustration evident in her voice. “I have a life. I have friends. I can handle myself. Besides Kingpin and Valentina aren’t just going to stroll up in broad daylight to kill me, it would be plastered all over the news.” The brunette threw her arms up in the air in her annoyance.

    “Kate, it's not that we don't trust you. You’ve not been seen in public or in the city since before your mother’s death. Your return will stir up a lot of attention, and there is no way Kingpin and Valentina are going to miss your face on the front of the New York Times.” Natasha tried to placate the brunette again, but this just seemed to rile the archer up more, Kate’s fists clenching by her sides. Natasha raised an eyebrow, maintaining her calm demeanour. "Kate, this isn't like dealing with a few petty criminals. We're talking about Kingpin, a man who's used to playing in the shadows and pulling strings. You showing up in the city is like waving a red flag in front of a bull."

"And what, you're going to lock me in here? Like Tony Stark did to Wanda? Treat me like some delicate flower? I'm not going to sit around while everyone else gets to roam free.” Kate spat.

    Clint sighed, "We're not locking you up, Kate. We're strategizing. Sam and Bucky are out, gathering intel. They'll be back soon."

    Kate huffed, clearly not satisfied with the explanation. "Gathering intel while I'm stuck here twiddling my thumbs. Great." As Kate voiced her frustration, Yelena walked into the room, catching the tail end of the conversation. She couldn't help but smirk at the scene unfolding. "What's the drama, маленький ястреб?" Yelena teased, her eyes flickering between Kate and the rest of the group, the assassins hand touching Kate’s lower back as she came to stand beside the archer.

    "We're trying to keep Kate from charging into the city guns blazing," Clint explained with a wry smile.

    Yelena's smirk widened. "Ah, the impulsive archer wanting to take on the world alone. Classic. Reminds me of someone." The blonde shot a directed glare at Clint who rolled his eyes.

    Kate leaned into Yelena’s side, her mouth close to the blonde’s ear as Nat and Clint shared blows about Clint’s reckless stupidity he had also possessed when he was Kate’s age. Yelena's smirk that had been plastered on her face faltered and was replaced by a look of understanding as Kate spoke softly to her. The Russian assassin listened attentively, her hand gently squeezing Kate's lower back in a reassuring gesture. Clint and Nat stopped their verbal assault upon one another as they became curious about the hushed conversation, Steve had already been watching.

    “Come then маленький ястреб. Let’s not waste the sunshine.” The blonde assassin said with a subtle smirk, and gently guided Kate out of the room, leaving the others to watch them leave. “This is very stupid, and I will say that I told you such when it blows up in our faces, but fine, we shall go see daddy Bishop.”

    “Don’t call him that ever again and you can say ‘I told you so’ as much as you like.” Kate mumbled in response, her comment bringing the smirk back to Yelena’s face. The two take the stairs down to the garage. Yelena opens the box on the wall containing way too many keys for one building to have. She grabs one set at random, clicking the button a few times whilst her eyes scan the garage. Huffing when none of the vehicles lights light up, she throws the key back in the box, before grabbing a smaller set in the bottom right. “Come Kate Bishop… and grab two of those.” The blonde points to a pile of helmets stacked in the corner of the room. Kate’s eyes widen but she does what she is told, before speedily walking after Yelena who is practically the other side of the garage by now. Yelena had settled herself on a sleek black motorbike, the hum of the engine already indicating readiness, she gestured for Kate to join her. The Russian assassin extended her hand, gesturing for one of the helmets. Kate handed it to her, still curious about the unexpected turn of events. Yelena's eyes sparkled with a mischievous glint as she secured her helmet in place.

    "Ever been on one of these, маленький ястреб?" Yelena inquired with a teasing grin, her Russian accent adding an extra layer of charm to the question.

    Kate's eyes widened, a mix of excitement and trepidation dancing in her gaze. "Uh, not really." The brunette pulled on the second helmet in her hands, and stepped forwards towards the bike before hesitating.

    Yelena chuckled at Kate's uncertainty, finding her adorable in that moment. "Here, маленький ястреб," she said, patting the seat behind her.

    Kate approached the bike tentatively, feeling a rush of nerves mingled with excitement. She hesitated for another moment before Yelena reached out, gently guiding her into position. With a firm yet gentle touch, Yelena adjusted Kate's posture, positioning her thighs securely against the sides of the seat, fitting the brunette’s front to her own back. The blonde then faced forwards again, before blindly reaching for Kate’s arms and bringing them to wrap tightly around her waist.

    "There you go, what is the American saying? Warm as a rug?” Yelena remarked with a grin, her accent lending a playful lilt to her words.

    Kate couldn't help but snort in return, “Snug as a bug?”

    Yelena's grin widened at Kate's correction. "Right, snug as a bug. You Americans and your quirky expressions." She revved the engine, the powerful hum filling the garage. With a mischievous gleam in her eye, Yelena added, "Hold on tight, Kate. We're going for a ride." As the motorcycle roared to life, Yelena expertly maneuvered it out of the garage and onto the open road. Kate clung to Yelena, the wind whipping through her hair as they sped away, leaving the Avengers compound behind.

    The sudden roar of a motorbike engine echoed through the compound, catching the attention of the group gathered in the kitchen. Clint raised an eyebrow, his eyes narrowing with curiosity. "Well, someone's in a hurry. That better not be one of our bikes." Natasha glanced toward the source of the sound, her view out of the window facing the drive clear from her seat, her senses on high alert. "Моя сестра такая глупая.” she muttered in Russian, the words carrying a blend of exasperation and affection.

    Steve looked up from the newspaper he was reading, concern etching his features. "Is that Kate on the back?"

    Natasha sighed, her gaze fixed on the disappearing motorbike. "It's Yelena and she’s taken Kate with her. What an idiot.”

    Clint chuckled lightly, shaking his head. "Well, that's one way to handle a stubborn archer. Get an even more stubborn assassin."

    "I get letting off steam, but going into the city right now? It's not exactly the safest move." Steve leaned back in his chair, tapping his fingers on the table.     Natasha turned her attention to Clint, a furrow forming on her brow. "How can you be okay with Kate running headfirst into danger? We know the risks out there."

    Clint leaned back, crossing his arms, and let out a sigh. "Because that's who she is, Nat. You can't cage a bird and expect it to be happy. Kate's got her own way of dealing with things, and sometimes it means taking risks. It's not like we can stop her. Yelena, too. They've got their own minds."

    Natasha took a moment before responding, her expression still stern. "I get it, Clint. I do. But we're dealing with dangerous forces, and their impulsiveness could lead to unnecessary complications. We're not trying to cage them, just guide them away from unnecessary risks." Clint raised an eyebrow. "Guidance or control, Nat? You've got a habit of being a bit overprotective with those you care about."

    Natasha shot him a glare. "It's called looking out for the people you love, Barton.” Clint leaned forward, "Nat, I know you've got a protective streak, and I respect that, I do. If being a father has taught me one thing is that there's a fine line between guidance and control. Yelena's had enough of the latter in the Red Room. The last thing she needs is to feel stifled, even if it comes from a place of love. She's her own person, it’s about you trusting her to make the right calls." Clint's gaze softened as he regarded Natasha, sensing the conflict within her. "Nat, do you trust her?" he asked gently.

    Natasha hesitated, her expression troubled. "I want to, Clint. But sometimes I feel like I don't even know who she is anymore. Yelena's been through so much, and I worry that she's become someone different because of it."

    Clint placed a comforting hand on Natasha's shoulder. "She's still your sister, Nat. Talk to her.”

That's practically your middle name, маленький ястреб." She chuckled, a hint of affection underlying her teasing tone.

Thoughts of her parents' betrayal, their deaths, and the complicated mess they left behind consumed her. The brunette, now shaking, turned out of the other kitchen door, running up the nearest set of stairs.

    Yelena's keen senses picked up the hurried footsteps echoing through the corridor, and without a moment's hesitation, she stood up from the couch, ignoring the looks from the chatting group around her and the blonde followed Kate's trail. Quiet as a shadow, she ascended the stairs and found Kate's bedroom door ajar.

    Pushing it open gently, Yelena stepped into the room to find Kate curled up on her bed, shoulders shaking with silent sobs. Without a word, Yelena approached her, her presence a silent comfort as she sat down beside the distraught young woman. Yelena didn't speak. She didn't need to. Instead, she wrapped her arms around Kate, offering a silent embrace that spoke volumes of understanding and support. She didn't pry, allowing Kate the space to grieve and collect herself. She didn't need to ask what had happened; the anguish radiating from Kate was palpable.

The brunette said in between sniffs.

Yelena's voice held a quiet strength as she continued, her own experiences with loss adding weight to her words. "When Natasha died, it felt like a part of me died with her. But I found solace in knowing that I could carry on her legacy in my own way, while still being true to myself." Yelena's gaze softened, a silent reassurance passing between them. "Your parents loved you, Kate. And wherever they are now, I believe they'd want you to find your own path.” Kate sniffled, wiping away her tears, her voice slightly muffled. "You know, the party would be a good excuse to catch up with Franny and Greer." She attempted a small smile, the first glimmer of hope in the midst of her sorrow. "I haven't seen them in ages, and I miss them." Turning to Yelena, Kate hesitated for a moment before speaking again. "Would you... come with me?" she asked softly. "I mean, I want to introduce you to Franny and Greer, but only if you want to. I don't want to drag you into anything you're not comfortable with." Her gaze held a mix of hope and uncertainty, waiting for Yelena's response.

The weight of Kate’s grief hung heavy in the air, but there was also a sense of solace in their closeness. Kate rested her head against Yelena's shoulder, her fingers tracing absentminded patterns on the fabric of Yelena's shirt, the brunette extremely careful not to raise the material and brush bare skin in fear of the blonde’s reaction. Yelena's arm encircled Kate's waist, holding her close, providing a sense of comfort in the dimming light. Yelena's hand dipped under Kate's shirt, her touch gentle yet reassuring as her fingers traced along the contours of Kate's bare back. The blonde's eyes were closed, as if savouring the moment, and a small, contented smile played on her lips. Uncertain of how to react, Kate hesitated for a moment before a tender smile formed on her lips. For a moment, Kate was at a loss for words, her heart pounding in her chest as she struggled to make sense of the flood of emotions swirling within her. Yelena's gesture was a silent acknowledgment of something, Kate didn’t know exactly of what, but it was something.

    Tentatively, she mirrored the gesture, her own hand venturing under the hem of Yelena's shirt. Her fingertips made gentle contact with the smooth skin, tracing delicate patterns across the small of Yelena's stomach. Kate's eyes flickered to Yelena's face, searching for any sign of discomfort or hesitation. She moved slowly, giving Yelena enough time to stop her if the touch crossed any boundaries.

    For a moment, Yelena tensed, her breath catching in her throat, but then she relaxed under Kate's touch. Encouraged by Yelena's response, Kate continued, her fingertips exploring the soft skin with gentle caresses. Sensing Yelena's relaxation at the current position, Kate paused not wanting to push, the brunette stopping her hand hesitating just below the edge of Yelena's ribcage. But before she could withdraw it completely, Yelena's hand covered hers, guiding it further until it was splayed out on her stomach. Kate's heart skipped a beat at the intimate gesture, her breath catching in her throat as she felt the blonde exhale deeply. Yelena's eyes remained closed, her expression serene, as Kate's hand rested on her stomach. After a beat, Yelena broke the silence, her voice a soft murmur. "You know, маленький ястреб, you're lucky I like you." She cracked one eye open, giving Kate a teasing grin. "Otherwise, I might have to teach you a lesson about boundaries."

    “Do you like me enough that you’ll come to the party with me?” Kate's face lit up, a hopeful glint in her eyes. “You know, meet Franny and Greer, maybe dance a little?" Yelena chuckled, a low, throaty sound that reverberated in the quiet room. "You're incorrigible."

    "Just one of my many charms," Kate replied with a playful wink, before laying her head back down on the blonde’s chest. “Come onnn Lena. It’ll be so boring without you there, plus, Fran and Greer have been desperate to meet the friend who they say have ‘stolen me away from them’.”

    Yelena's fingers traced idle patterns on Kate's back as she considered the invitation. "Should I be worried about facing a pair of disgruntled friends at this party?"

    Kate laughed softly, the sound a soothing melody in the quiet room. "Nah, they're just being dramatic. But seriously, it won't be the same without you. They’ll love you, promise." Yelena chuckled, her fingers gently tracing circles on Kate's back. "I hope you haven't painted me as some kind of saint to your friends. I'm not exactly known for my charm and social skills. I’m no one good Kate.”

    “Why don't you see yourself as good? You've done plenty of good things, saved lives even." Yelena's gaze shifted from the top of the brunette’s head to the ceiling, a flicker of vulnerability crossing her features. "I've done a lot of things, Kate. Good and bad. It's not as simple as putting a label on it."

    "A lot of that wasn’t you, Lena," Kate insisted. "and that doesn't define who you are now. You've changed, and you're helping people. That's pretty good in my book." Yelena sighed, her fingers absentmindedly tracing patterns on Kate's back. "It's not that easy. The things I've done, the people I've hurt - it doesn't just go away.     Kate couldn't help but chuckle, not Yelena's words but the situation, a playful glint swimming in her eyes. "You know what? I haven't told Franny and Greer anything about you. I've kept them in suspense, just to wind them up."

    Yelena arched an eyebrow, a hint of amusement crossing her features. "Really? And here I thought you were building up my mysterious allure."

    Kate grinned mischievously, the blonde feeling her cheek move against her collarbone. "Well, that too. But it's more fun this way. Keeps them guessing."

    Yelena let out a soft laugh, the tension in her shoulders easing slightly as Kate pressed a light kiss on the nearest bare skin to her lips.

    "And don't worry about expectations. Just be yourself. That's all anyone really wants." Yelena sighed, her resistance softening. "You make it sound so simple." "Sometimes, it can be," Kate replied, her tone earnest.

    Yelena's expression softened, her walls slowly crumbling under the weight of Kate's words. "You always know what to say, don't you?"

    "Comes with the territory of being a superhero, I guess." Kate yawned.

    Yelena rolled her eyes, but there was a subtle warmth in her gaze as she closed her eyes again, content to stay in the quiet intimacy of the moment.
