    Kate lowered her bow, a sheepish grin on her face. "We were just brainstorming ideas." "Well, hold off on the William Tell routine for now," Sonya said, her voice turning serious once more. "If those are drones, taking one out might not be the best course of action. We need to capture one if possible, or at least get a closer look at its tech." Steve stepped forward, his jaw set. "We were just discussing a plan when you arrived. Sam's on recon, Clint and Kate are heading out with EMP arrows, and Bucky and I are monitoring security feeds."

    Sonya raised an eyebrow. "Sounds like you have it under control, Captain America. But hey, a little extra muscle never hurt anyone, right?"

    She strode towards the kitchen door, "Besides, someone's gotta keep things interesting around here."

    As Sonya disappeared from sight, Sam let out a chuckle.

    “So, that’s Yelena’s friend? That tracks.” He said out loud, a hint of amusement dancing in his eyes.

    Bucky snorted, crossing his arms in front of his chest. "Great. Just what we need. Another loose cannon with a mysterious past." He couldn't deny there was a certain lightness to Sonya, but Bucky had a long history with Black Widows, and it wasn't always a smooth one. He wasn't about to welcome another one with open arms, especially someone Steve hadn't vetted.

    “Quite the character, isn't she?" Clint said, a smile wide on his face. Sam chuckled. "You could say that, Clint. You know her well?"

    Clint shook his head. "Not really. She was here a few weeks back, seemed to take quite a liking to my wife. Seems like she operates in the shadows, takes on freelance gigs. Just another highly skilled ex-assassin with a taste for danger, if I had to guess." The door swung open again with a flourish, and Sonya reappeared, a mischievous glint in her electric blue eyes. "Speaking of danger," she announced, a playful smile on her lips, "where is the small blonde one?” Her gaze lingering for a moment on Kate before flicking to Clint. "Did she finally decide to take up knitting or something?"

    Clint rolled his eyes. "Really, Sonya? Back to height jokes already?"

    Sonya grinned, unfazed. "Hey, someone's gotta lighten the mood around here, be glad you’re not on the end of them... yet. Besides, a little friendly ribbing never hurt anyone… well, maybe not unless you're on the receiving end of a Black Widow takedown." She winked at Kate, who couldn't help but return a small smile.

    "We haven't seen her since this morning. Same with Nat now that I think about it.” Steve muttered. “Although, Nat did mention yesterday that she was thinking of heading to St Petersburg so at least we have some sort of lead there. Her sister just disappeared.” Sonya's expression hardened. A disquiet settled over the group. The arrival of the mysterious drones, Yelena's sudden disappearance, and now this strange connection between the two women – it all felt too coincidental. “There’s a pattern emerging here, and I don't like it one bit."

    "Maybe that's something we should look into later," Steve said, his voice firm. "Right now, our priority is those drones. Sonya, any ideas on how to approach them?" “No,” Sonya's gaze darted towards Kate. "you and Yelena are practically inseparable. Any idea where she might have vanished off to…?"

    Kate, taken aback by the sudden shift in attention, stammered for a moment. "I, uh… no, not really. We haven't spoken since last night… maybe she’s just running some errands…?” The brunette trailed off.

    Sonya raised an eyebrow, unconvinced. "Errands, huh? That doesn't sound like Yelena. Unless those errands involved blowing something up or extracting information from a particularly unfriendly source, of course." A wry smile played on her lips for a fleeting moment, but it never quite reached her eyes. "Still," she continued, her voice turning serious once more, "it is strange. You two are usually thick as thieves."

    Bucky snorted.

    Sonya ignored him. Her gaze flicked back to Steve. "Alright, new plan. We need to expand our search. Steve, you mentioned Nat might be in St. Petersburg? I can contact Melina. She might know something about Nat's whereabouts. I'll try patching her in and see if she's heard from either Natasha or Yelena."

    Bucky and Steve stood at the map table, watching the bodies outside move into their positions to take down the drones.

    Clint, stood on the front porch, with a practiced flick of his wrist, nocked an arrow especially designed to disrupt electronics. Sonya watched on, a few paces to the right side of Kate, took a different approach. She realised brute force, was not going to work. Her gaze darted towards Kate, who stood fiddling with her quiver, a frown creasing her brow. "Kate," Sonya said, her voice low, "forget the fancy arrows for now. We need a distraction, something to throw those drones off their game."

    Kate's eyes lit up with a mischievous glint. "A distraction, huh? Kinda my specialty.” With a smirk, she grabbed a handful of regular arrows and nocked one on her bow. Taking aim at a nearby tree, she fired. The arrow thudded harmlessly into the bark. The drones, momentarily startled, shifted their focus towards the sound.

    "Now!" Sonya shouted, the signal for action.

    Clint, with lightning reflexes, launched his EMP arrow. It arced through the air, a streak of blue light, before slamming into one of the drones. A shower of sparks erupted, and the drone sputtered, its mechanical whirring grinding to a halt. It spiralled out of control, crashing into the ground below.

    A cheer erupted from Sam above them, the noise echoing, but the celebration was short-lived. The remaining two drones seemed to redouble their efforts, circling the compound with renewed urgency.

    Sam, frustrated, buzzed closer, attempting to get a better look. "They're fast," he reported over the comm. "They keep anticipating my moves... their wings are a different material… it’s weaker."

    Sonya gritted her teeth. They needed a way to disrupt their flight pattern, to force them to make a mistake.

    Suddenly, inspiration struck.

    "Kate," she called out, "I need you to hit one of those drones, but not in a critical area. Just a glancing blow, something to mess up its flight path."

    Kate hefted her bow, her expression a mix of concentration and excitement. This was the kind of challenge she thrived on. She narrowed her eyes, focusing on one of the drones as it zipped past. With a deep breath, she released the arrow.

    Time seemed to slow down. The arrow flew through the air, a blur of white against the blue sky. It connected with the drone's wing, weak just like Sam said, with a satisfying ping, sending the machine into a violent spin. The other drone, startled by its companion's erratic movements, faltered for a split second.

    That split second was all Clint needed. He launched another EMP arrow, this one finding its mark true. The last drone erupted in a ball of sparks and plummeted to the ground. A whoop of joy rose from Clint's throat. Sam, circling overhead, pumped his fist in the air, whooping as he swooped to the ground and landed. The Falcon wings snapping shut onto the pack on his back.

    Sonya, however, remained cautious. She approached the downed drones with slow, deliberate steps. Only after a thorough inspection, confirming they were indeed disabled, did she allow herself to relax.

    "Nice shooting, Hawkeye," she said to Kate, a genuine smile gracing her lips. "Yelena wasn’t lying when she said you were the best.”

    Kate's heart skipped a beat. The name hung heavy in the air, a stark reminder of their missing friend. She forced a casual shrug, trying to brush off the compliment. "Just lucky, I guess." Sonya, however, wasn't convinced. She noticed the slight frown that flitted across Kate's face, the same one that had appeared earlier when Yelena's name was mentioned. A flicker of concern crossed Sonya's features.

    “Oh… what did you do?”

    Chapter 31

    also follow my twt @BishBishBelova “Oh… what did you do?” Sonya asked, crossing her arms as she stood in front of Kate. The two woman fell silent as Sam came to pick the drones up off the floor, taking them inside to examine them. He shot the two a confused look as he followed Clint’s back inside to join Bucky and Steve.

    “Why are you automatically assuming it was me?” Kate asked defensively. Sonya just raised an eyebrow and didn’t dignify the archer with a response. Kate exhaled loudly, tilting her head back to look at the sky, before lifting her hands to her face and wiping them downwards before she looked back at Sonya.

    "Nothing," Kate said finally, her voice clipped. "We just… haven't seen eye to eye lately. It's no big deal."

    Sonya studied her for a moment, her blue eyes sharp. She wasn't one to pry, but the concern for Yelena tugged at her. "Look," Sonya said, her voice softening, "I know Yelena. She can be… a handful, to say the least. But she also cares deeply about her friends. If something's bothering you, maybe talking about it could help."

    "Easier said than done," Kate grumbled, fiddling with an arrowhead in her jacket pocket, "Yelena's not exactly the Hallmark card type. Talking things out isn't really her strong suit." A hint of frustration crept into her voice.

    A flicker of curiosity crossed Sonya’s features. "Funny," she said, her voice low, “She talks about a lot of things, but you, when Yelena first mentioned you, I was surprised Kate Bishop… you were a topic she seemed strangely reluctant to discuss."

    Kate's head snapped up, surprise momentarily erasing the frustration from her face. "What do you mean?" she asked, her voice sharp.

    “When she came back to Melina's for Christmas, she was a mess. Quiet, withdrawn, and most definitely depressed. Then the day before New Years, Rick shows up with a jet for Yelena and boy, is she cagey about where she’s headed. Yelena packs a light bag in record time, and suddenly she's all full of energy and rearing to go. Antonia and I put a tracker on the jet. Imagine our surprise when it landed right here, in New York City.” Sonya spoke slowly, as if trying to ease the memory out of her mind.

    Sonya continued when Kate didn’t add to the conversation, “When Yelena finally did return to Melina's in the new year, she was back to her usual self. Cracking jokes, training like a demon… but wouldn't utter a word about her trip. Not a peep. It was like a switch had flipped. The depressed Yelena vanished, replaced by this… energized version, a happier version.” Sonya's gaze met Kate's, a hint of amusement flickering in the blue depths. “And now I know more of the story… I know that was all because of you.”

    "You know," Sonya began, her voice softer now, "when Yelena came back one time in the summer…" She trailed off, letting the words hang in the air.

    Kate looked up, a flicker of curiosity sparking in her eyes. "July?”

    Sonya chuckled, a hint of mischief in her tone. “Of course, you know the month.” Sonya sorts, “Well, let's just say I gave her a hard time about being so secretive. Teasing her mercilessly, you know, the usual sibling kind of stuff. And wouldn't you know it, one night, after a particularly brutal training session, she just… spilled the beans." Kate's eyebrows shot up in surprise. "She… she told you about New York?" Sonya grinned, a genuine smile this time, devoid of its earlier cynicism. "Every detail. All the sneaking into your window, the late-night visits, the movies you made her watch, apparently, you are quite an intrigue Bishop." A teasing lilt crept into her voice. "She even called you her friend which I’ll admit shocked me."

    Heat flooded Kate's cheeks, a mixture of surprise and… something else, something warm and fuzzy that she couldn't quite define. So, Yelena hadn’t minded their time together in New York? Kate deep down always thought she rather annoyed the assassin and that Yelena only stopped by when she was in the city on business. But the blonde had in fact confided in Sonya about it? The revelation shifted the narrative in her mind.

    "Wait, just to be clear," Kate stammered, her voice barely a whisper. "She told you everything? About New York, about us…" Her voice trailed off, unsure how to articulate the unspoken bond they shared.

    Sonya rolled her eyes with a laugh, "Pretty much everything. Though, let's just say she wasn't exactly forthcoming about the details of your… late-night activities." She wiggled her eyebrows suggestively, sending a fresh wave of heat to Kate's face.

    Kate sputtered, a blush creeping up her neck. “There were no… activities! We were just… hanging out." The words sounded lame even to her own ears. “I-I mean she did fall asleep in my bed… b-but that’s all that happened.”

    Sonya only raised an eyebrow.

    “O-ok, and maybe a hug, but I swear nothing else happened. Like at all. Nope. Nothing.” Kate rambled on unable to stop herself.

    Sonya's smile widened. "Of course. Although," she added, her voice dropping to a conspiratorial whisper, "Yelena did not include those little details you just shared.” Kate groaned, burying her face in her hands. This was torture. Sonya, clearly enjoying her discomfort, pressed on.

    "So," Sonya said, her voice dripping with mock seriousness, "care to enlighten me on what exactly happened last night that caused this… rift between you and Yelena? Because let me tell you, the way people are trying to kill you right now, I figured she wouldn’t let you out of her sight, and here she is… nowhere to be seen.”

    Kate hesitated. Part of her wanted to shut down the conversation, to retreat back into the comfortable group setting where she wouldn’t be interrogated by her best friends best friend? But another part, a curious and maybe even hopeful part, yearned to understand. To understand why it felt like Yelena had been pushing her away, why their friendship seemed to be hanging by a thread.

    Taking a deep breath, Kate decided to take a chance. "Look," she began, her voice barely above a whisper, "things with Yelena… they've been complicated and last night it just kind of blew up. We don't always see eye to eye believe it or not. She has this… need to charge headfirst into danger, and I…" She trailed off, searching for the right words. "Try to rein her in, keep her safe?" Sonya supplied, her voice gentle. Kate nodded gratefully. “Not that exactly. I just want her to tell me before she does something stupid, or even let me help. She makes these big sweeping decisions without consulting anyone. But it feels like… like I'm nagging her and the last thing I want is to make her feel like she’s being controlled, and I- but sometimes I worry…" Her voice cracked slightly, and she looked away, unable to meet Sonya's gaze.

    Sonya reached out, placing a comforting hand on Kate's shoulder. "You worry about her," she said softly. "That's clear. And she worries about you too. In her own… unique way, of course."

    "You think so? That’s what Clint said." Relief mixed with surprise in her voice. Having Clint's words echoed by Sonya felt like a confirmation, even if Yelena had practically done that already.

    Sonya squeezed her shoulder gently. “He’s alright that one. Don’t know why Tsarina tried to kill him. So stupid.” Sonya rolled her eyes, “Yelena may not always show it, but she’s a big softie, especially with people she loves. And trust me, Kate Bishop, you're definitely on that list."

    Kate, however, couldn't quite swallow the whole thing. Appreciation flickered in her eyes for Sonya's reassurance, but a niggling doubt remained. "Love?" she echoed, the word sounding foreign on her tongue when applied to Yelena. "She wouldn’t say that,” Kate scoffed, “Besides, if I started pulling stunts like she does, running off on my own and not telling anyone…" She trailed off, the unspoken accusation hanging heavy in the air. Sonya chuckled, a dry but knowing sound. "Believe me, Kate Bishop, you'd hear about it from Yelena for a week straight. Double standards are her middle name." She winked, her gaze steady. "But that's just Yelena. She also has this… hero complex a mile wide. She won’t ever admit it, but she feels she needs to save the day, even if it means putting herself in danger."

    Kate felt a frustrated sigh escape her lips. "That's exactly what bothers me! Why is it okay for her to do whatever she wants, but if I even think about doing something remotely risky, she acts like I'm about to jump off a cliff blindfolded?"

    Sonya considered Kate's outburst for a moment; her earlier amusement replaced by a thoughtful frown. "Maybe," she said slowly, "because Yelena blames herself for a lot of things. For what happened in the Red Room, for the people she lost… and maybe, just maybe, for dragging you into this mess."

    Kate bristled at Sonya's words. "Dragging me into this mess?" she scoffed. "Come on, Sonya. Like Yelena had any control over the fact that my parents ended up tangled with Kingpin and a bunch of killer Russians. If anything, it's the other way around! I was the one who stumbled onto this whole situation, the one who got mixed up in a fight with her and Clint… and well, then I think it was just an accident how we became friends after that, but none of it was Yelena’s doing! It’s all my mess. I’m the one all these people want to kill!” "Is that right?" Sonya said, her voice teasing. "So, you're telling me the great Kate Bishop, Hawkeye in her own right, needs rescuing?"

    Kate rolled her eyes. "That's not what I'm saying at all. It's just… frustrating. She acts like she's my guardian angel or something, swooping in to save me from every little scrape. I can take care of myself, you know? I'm a trained archer, I can handle a fight. Especially a verbal one in front of a crowd of people. It’s not like Valentina was going to gut me like a fish in front of the New York Elite, was she?” The brunette muttered sarcastically. Sonya's smile softened. "There's no doubt about your skills, Kate. You're more than capable. But maybe Yelena sees something else. Maybe she sees a kindred spirit, someone who reminds her of herself before the Red Room, before all the violence and pain." Kate pondered Sonya's words. The idea that Yelena saw her as an equal was a comforting thought. But Sonya's phrasing struck a nerve. With a playful jab, Kate countered, "Great. So, she looks at me and sees a six-year-old running around in a superhero costume? That makes me feel loads better. Thank you, Sonya." The archer threw her arms up in the air dramatically. "Of course not! Maybe a bit of youthful idealism, a spark of that pre-Red Room innocence. Something she… well, something she maybe envies a little. Something we all do…" Her gaze softened further. "Look, Kate, I know Yelena about as well as you do, trust me, she wouldn't be this invested in someone she saw as a helpless kid. You bring out a different side of her, a lighter side. Maybe even a hopeful one."

    Kate considered this, the frustration giving way to a thoughtful frown. "Hopeful, huh? That's not a word I'd associate with Yelena. More like brooding and sarcastic... oh and a pain in my arse."

    Sonya snorted. "Oh, she can definitely be all of those things too. But there's more to her, Kate. You know that as well as I do, you just have to… know where to look.” Sonya winked, hoping the brunette would catch on and get the message she didn’t need to worry so hard. A sudden realization dawned on Kate, her eyes narrowing as she looked at Sonya. “Wait a minute," she said, her voice laced with suspicion. "You know where Yelena is, don't you? That whole story about her possibly being back at Melina's… that was a lie, wasn't it?" "Now, Kate Bishop, where would you get such an idea?" she said, her voice light and teasing. "You are the most annoying, secretive person I know. I swear, sometimes I just want to…" She trailed off playfully, mimicking the motion of strangling someone. “To you and Yelena also.”

    Sonya swatted playfully at Kate's arm. "And sometimes I want to duct tape you and Yelena to a chair and force the pair of you to see what’s right in front of your eyes. Honestly, the denseness of you both is enough to make a saint swear."

    Kate, still chuckling, nudged Sonya with her elbow. "Alright, alright, I get it. We're both a little… slow on the uptake sometimes. But seriously, what's with the cryptic messages? Is this some kind of weird spy test?"

    Sonya rolled her eyes, but a hint of a smile played on her lips. She knew she was being theatrical, but sometimes a little frustration could be a good thing. “A test? Maybe. But listen, Kate, some things are better figured out on your own, even more so when involving Yelena. Trust me, when you finally crack the code, the satisfaction will be ten times better. Ты можешь поблагодарить меня, когда проведешь ночь отличного секса.” Sonya smirked and wiggled her eyebrows when she spoke in Russian.

    With that, Sonya turned and began walking purposefully towards the direction of the building that housed the destroyed drones. She muttered to herself under her breath, a mischievous glint still in her eyes.

    "Let's see what kind of tech these bad boys are packing. Maybe some repulson tech I can repurpose for my next… project." She left the sentence unfinished, a knowing smirk playing on her lips.

    Kate, ever the curious one, jogged after Sonya, her playful annoyance morphing into genuine concern. "Wait, wait, wait!" she called out. "What project? Can I help? I’m great with exploding things! And what did you mean by 'see what's right in front of our eyes'? Sonya, come on…”

    The brunette continued pleading after Sonya as they entered the building and continued up the stairs.

    The wind howled a mournful tune across the snow-covered rooftops, each gust tugging at Yelena’s braid as she pressed her ear to the icy surface. Below, the monolithic bulk of the CIA headquarters loomed, a fortress of glass and steel against the twilight sky. Rick's intel had come through last night and had been cryptic, a single burner phone call with a terse message: "Valentina's crew. Langley. Today." It wasn't much, but it was enough for Yelena. The thought of Valentina Allegra de Fontaine, the ruthless Countess, meddling in her and Kate’s affairs sent a familiar surge of anger through her.

    Yelena shifted, the movement sending a cascade of loose snow tumbling off her back, which showed how long she had been laid up there. Muttering a curse, she adjusted her position, seeking a clearer view of the building's main entrance. Her white combat suit, a relic of her wardrobe nowadays, blended seamlessly with the shadows of the setting sun and the glow it beamed off the snow-covered surroundings. The biting cold was a familiar adversary, a stark contrast to the stifling warmth of the state during the summer months. Below, the usual choreography of the CIA headquarters played out. Bureaucrats shuffled in and out, their briefcases and brief moments of urgency a stark contrast to Yelena's own mission. She scanned each face meticulously, the practiced efficiency of her Red Room training kicking in. But none of them matched the descriptions Rick had relayed – no mysterious operatives, no elite soldiers, just… people. Ordinary people with briefcases and tired eyes.

    Yelena cast a glance at her tablet, propped against a nearby brick jutting out from the building. On the screen, a grid of live feeds displayed the various entrances and exits of the Langley complex. Hours of painstaking camera hacking courtesy of a tech-savvy, and very expensive, contact had granted her this digital vantage point. Every doorway, every side entrance, every delivery bay – all under her watchful eye. Yet, Valentina's recruits remained frustratingly absent.

    Disappointment gnawed at her.

    Had the intel been faulty? Was this entire stakeout a colossal waste of time? Had she made a mistake? Leaving Kate, impulsive and headstrong as ever, alone in New York while she chased shadows here?

    That question particularly hammered at Yelena's resolve.

    A muscle in Yelena's jaw clenched tight. Kate was a fighter, yes, but a green one. Clint Barton might be a grudging mentor, but even the best hawk couldn't keep a sparrow from diving headfirst into trouble. So, the blonde had made sure Kate was actually being watched. She had sent Sonya, a walking encyclopaedia of espionage and deadpan wit, to keep Kate out of trouble whilst she was away. As much as Clint Barton cared for Kate, Yelena didn’t fully trust him not to lose her in the jungle that is New York City.

    The thought of Kate surrounded by a gaggle of superheroes brought a reluctant smile to Yelena's lips. Getting into trouble with a bunch of superpowered babysitters watching over her? It was practically an Olympic sport for Kate Bishop. Yet, the image also brought a pang of something else, a feeling she couldn't quite define.

    It was the memory of the other night that flickered in her mind, sharp and unwelcome. Kate, eyes blazing with a mixture of defiance and hurt, slipping out of the ballroom like a foot on a banana skin. The frustration, the helplessness of watching her disappear into the night. It had been a long time since anyone had gotten under Yelena's skin like that. Pushing the memory aside, Yelena forced herself to focus. Dwelling on emotions was a luxury she couldn't afford. She hadn’t done it before, and she certainly wasn’t going to start now. Kate was safe. That was the only thing that mattered. She had a job to do, and she wouldn't let a bout of misplaced concern cloud her judgment.

    Yelena returned her gaze to the live feeds. Her eyes scanned every corner, every shadow, searching for a sign, a clue that would explain the puzzling absence of Valentina's recruits. Maybe Rick's intel truly was wrong. Maybe the Countess was playing a different game altogether, leaking false information that she knew Yelena would trail. One thing was certain – Yelena Belova wouldn't leave Langley empty-handed. She would find what she was looking for, even if it meant turning the entire building upside down. And when she did, she'd make sure Valentina regretted ever crossing her path.

    Suddenly, a splash of colour on one of the feeds caught Yelena's eye. It was like a beacon in the sea of muted greys and browns – a bright Hawaiian shirt, loud enough to make a parrot jealous. And who, in their right mind, would wear such a thing in the middle of a snowy December afternoon? Especially when Christmas was just days away.

    Yelena zoomed in, her jaw dropping in disbelief. There, swaggering up to the front door of the CIA building like he owned the place, was none other than Alexei Shostakov, the Red Guardian and her own father. His usual outgoing demeanour was paired with a surprising air of confidence, though the way he fiddled with the collar of his monstrosity of a shirt suggested otherwise.

    Yelena couldn't help but let out a strangled laugh, a sound that echoed oddly in the quiet evening. Of course. This entire operation just went from perplexing to downright ridiculous. "Attention, Valentina. You might want to prepare yourself for a rather… colourful visitor." She muttered to herself under her breath. Yelena needed to see this for herself, to gauge Alexei's intentions firsthand. With a practiced ease, she began to army crawl towards the edge of the rooftop, the snow crunching softly beneath her. Reaching the ledge, she carefully peeked over, her eyes immediately finding her target.

    This unexpected development flipped the script entirely. Why was Alexei here? Had he finally taken Valentina's offer? The thought sent a flicker of anger through Yelena. Using her father as a pawn in her little game – Valentina truly had no shame.

    Alexei, looking every bit out of place in his flamboyant attire. He fidgeted nervously, glancing around like a cornered bear. Was he scared? Or simply uncomfortable? Or just well, being Alexei? Yelena couldn't tell from this distance.

    A nagging suspicion began to gnaw at her. This whole scenario felt off. Antonia had come of her own accord to meet with Valentina in the days before. Yelena knew Antonia’s intentions, but her father’s were unknown to the blonde. Antonia had made it out of the building with information that she was now looking into, Yelena did not hold hope in Alexei to do the same.

    Maybe Melina involved? Had she somehow convinced Alexei to play a part in a larger scheme, one that Yelena hadn't anticipated? The questions swirled in her mind, a tangled mess of possibilities.

    Yelena squinted through the binoculars she had pulled out of her vest pocket; any lingering amusement quickly replaced by a simmering anger. Valentina herself had emerged from the automatic doors of the CIA building, her tailored black suit a stark contrast to the snow- covered landscape. She marched towards Alexei with a determined stride, her posture rigid and unforgiving.

    Yelena could practically hear Valentina's sharp words through the lenses, her lips pursed in a thin line. The woman was clearly not happy with Alexei's flamboyant entrance, or perhaps his appearance in general. A string of rapid-fire insults, laced with frustration and a hint of something that might have been fear, flew from Valentina's lips. Alexei, for his part, simply shuffled his feet and said something inaudible in response, his bravado taking a back seat, but Yelena could still see it front and centre as if sat on her father’s shoulders. Valentina threw her hands up in exasperation, a fleeting flicker of something akin to pity crossing her features before it was masked by steely resolve. With a final shove, she ushered Alexei through the doors, the automatic entrance hissing shut behind them. Yelena scowled, a bitter taste settling on her tongue. So much for Alexei being some kind of mastermind. He looked more like a reluctant pawn, strong-armed into doing Valentina's bidding. The question remained – why? What information was so valuable that the Countess needed Alexei to risk exposure at the CIA?

    Yelena placed the binoculars down, her mind racing. The original plan of tailing Valentina's recruits was out the window. Now, her focus had shifted entirely. She had to find a way to get inside the CIA building, to follow Alexei and Valentina, and uncover what secrets Val was after from her father. It was a risky move, but the potential reward – exposing Valentina's operation and rescuing her father from her clutches – was too great to ignore. The blonde assassin packed up her gear, stuffing it all into the backpack that sat by the rooftop wall, its location hidden by the barriers overlapping edge. She’d come back for it later. Yelena grabbed her phone from her pocket, hastily ripping off one glove so her fingers would actually activate on the touchscreen.

    Yelena wasted no time as she dialled a familiar number.

    “Ты один?”

    The clatter of forks and the murmur of conversation filled the air as Sonya speared a stray olive from the communal bowl. Surrounded by the unlikely group of Kate Bishop, Clint Barton, and a surprisingly jovial Bucky, Sonya felt a pang of… something unfamiliar. Maybe camaraderie? It was a strange feeling, one she wasn't entirely comfortable with. Suddenly, her phone buzzed in her pocket, the familiar ringtone slicing through the chatter. Yelena's name flashed on the screen. An eyebrow shot up. This could get interesting. Exchanging a quick glance with Kate, who mirrored her curiosity, Sonya excused herself from the table. "Excuse me for a moment," she announced, grabbing her phone. "Looks like Melina got my message. I'll be back in a sec."

    Bucky, perched across from Clint with a glint in his eye, snorted. "Sonya and Melina on the phone? I want to be a fly on the wall for that one.”

    Clint, simply grunted in response, his gaze flickering between Kate, who was now pretending to be deeply engrossed in a tablet, and the retreating form of Sonya. The archer’s brow then furrowed as if he had only just processed what Bucky said.

    “You know Melina, Buck?”

    “We’ve crossed paths.” The solider shrugged.

    Sonya slipped out of the kitchen, the murmur of conversation fading behind her. Reaching a quiet corner of the Compound, she answered the call. "How’s Virginia?" she answered, her voice adopting a playful lilt.

    Yelena's voice, a mixture of amusement and urgency, filled her ear. Sonya listened intently as the story unfolded, a picture of the disgruntled Alexei in a Hawaiian shirt painting a particularly vivid image. Laughter bubbled up in her chest, but she forced it down, focusing on the situation at hand.

    "A Hawaiian shirt? In this weather? Алексей must have lost a bet," Sonya remarked, her voice laced with sarcasm. But the humour faded as Yelena recounted the rest of the evening. "Sounds like a meeting of sorts. An agreement of terms. Like Antonia’s.” "More like a hostage situation," Yelena muttered. "There's no way Alexei agreed to this knowing what he was getting into."

    Intrigue warred with concern in Sonya's gut. Yelena diving headfirst into the CIA headquarters wasn't exactly ideal. Yet, the thought of Alexei being strong-armed by Valentina sent a surge of rage through her. "Intriguing," Sonya said, her amusement fading. "Так каков план, Белая Вдова? Собираетесь ли вы штурмовать ЦРУ и спасти своего своенравного отца?”

    Sonya could practically see Yelena smirk through the phone. The woman thrived on chaos, and this situation was tailor-made for her skillset. A mischievous smile sparked on Sonya's own face as she imagined the scene Yelena would cause.

    "Something like that," Yelena replied, a hint of said smirk in her voice. “Do you have a plan beyond 'infiltrate the CIA and improvise'? Because let's be honest, your improvisation skills can be… destructive." Sonya asked hesitantly, knowing Yelena’s response before she even replied.

    "I can handle it," Yelena countered, a touch defensive.

    "I know you can," Sonya conceded. But there was a 'but' coming, and Yelena knew it. "But," Sonya continued, her voice softening slightly, "have you considered talking to Kate about this first? Letting her know what you're getting yourself into?"

    Yelena scoffed. "Why? I've never needed anyone's permission before."

    "Look, I know you two have a… complicated dynamic. Kate cares about you, Yelena. And if something happened, well…" Sonya trailed off, the unspoken threat hanging heavy in the air. “You hated that Natasha blindsided you with her death. Look how it affected you. Imagine doing that to Kate and how it would affect her. Because if you want my opini-“ “I don’t.” Yelena interrupted, her voice tight.

    “I don’t think she’d survive it.” Sonya finished, ignoring Yelena’s protest, her words firm. Yelena sighed, a war raging within her. The urge to be her usual independent-self clashed with the memory of the raw pain Natasha's sacrifice had inflicted. Sonya was right. Kate doesn’t deserve that kind of punishment.

    Fine. Yelena would send a text.

    But a full explanation over the phone? Absolutely not. There just wasn't time for that. "Alright, alright," Yelena conceded, a touch of annoyance lacing her voice. "I'll send her a text. I haven't got all night to explain the intricacies of international espionage to the маленький ястреб.”

    Sonya couldn't help but smile. This was progress, however begrudging. "A text will do," she agreed. "Just… try not to make it sound like you're off buying groceries. A little urgency might be appreciated.” Sonya chuckled, shaking her head. "You know, Yelena, for someone who claims not to care, you sure do have a soft spot for our little hawk," she teased, a playful glint in her eyes.

    Yelena snorted. "Don't worry, I can manage a cryptic message. Oh, and Sonya. Stop being ridiculous." With that, she ended the call, pulling out her phone and composing a quick text to Kate. It wasn't perfect, but it would have to do.

    This tip off had just gotten a whole lot more complicated.

    The stainless-steel table in the compound kitchen was littered with the disassembled remains of a rather sophisticated-looking drone. Sam, with a furrowed brow, carefully separated a bundle of wires from a miniaturized circuit board.

    "Alright," he began, addressing the others gathered around the table, "so from what I can gather, this little guy here" - he tapped the circuit board - "is the brains of the operation. Probably receives encrypted signals for navigation and target acquisition, much like a hawk as a predator." He gestured to a tangle of wires leading away from the board. "These feed into this gyro and accelerometer here, which keep it stable in flight. Basically, the tech resembles the appearance."

    Bucky grunted, scratching his beard. "Encrypted signals?”

    Steve pointed to a small, nondescript box nestled amongst the wires. "What about that?" Sam picked it up, examining it with a shrug. "Looks like a power source of some kind. Maybe lithium-ion battery. Not sure what the specs are, though."

    Clint, leaning back in his chair, chuckled. "Man are you two making me feel young.” The archer laughed at Bucky and Steve before turning to Sam who had paused, “Lost already?" Sam shot him a look. "What's that supposed to mean, Barton?"

    "Means you're drowning in technobabble," Clint drawled. "This stuff is basic espionage tech. Been around for years."

    Bucky snorted. "Basic for you, maybe. Sounds like gibberish to me. The old days were so much simpler."

    Just then, Kate, who had been quietly observing the disassembled drone, spoke up. "Actually Clint, Sam's on the right track. That circuit board most likely uses a surface-mount technology for miniaturization. The specific encryption protocol is difficult to determine without further analysis, but it could be a variant of AES-256."

    The room fell silent. All eyes turned to Kate, who met their stares with a cool composure. Sam blinked, a slow grin spreading across his face. "You know your stuff." "Not bad, kid. Didn't know you were drone-savvy." Clint chuckled.

    A hint of pride flickered in Kate's eyes. "I've been doing some… extra-curricular reading," she admitted. "Besides, my parents created a security company, I’ve been hearing this stuff since I was a kid. Plus some of the tech used in trick arrows isn't that different from this in actuality, Clint."

    “So, what’s the AES… thingy?” Sam asked, his interest piqued. He'd heard the term before, but the specifics were fuzzy.

    Kate smiled, pleased to share her knowledge. "The AES, which stands for Advanced Encryption Standard, is basically a fancy way of scrambling information," she explained. "Imagine it like taking a message and turning it into a jumbled mess of letters and numbers, like Scrabble. The encryption key is like a secret decoder that lets you unscramble the message and read it again. The U.S Government uses it to protect classified data." The brunette shrugged.

    "Think of it like this," Clint chimed in, "You got a top-secret recipe for Laura Barton's World- Famous Super Snacks hidden in a vault. The AES is the vault door, keeping the recipe safe. The key is the combination that lets you open the door and get to those delicious snacks." Sam chuckled. "World-famous…? Accurate.” His eyes glazed over for a moment, a dreamy smile on his face. "Those chocolate chip cookies, man… They could bring world peace, I swear. Clint. That’s our solution. Kill Kingpin with baking.”

    Clint laughed, bumping Sam playfully with his shoulder. "Settle down there, Wilson. Before you start drooling on the table."

    Just then, the kitchen door swung open, and Sonya slipped back in, a sly smile playing on her lips. "Speaking of good cooking," she announced, catching the tail end of Kate's sentence. "Natasha is indeed at Melina’s.”

    “So, Yelena isn't…" Kate started.

    "Nope," Sonya cut her off, popping a piece of gum in her mouth.

    Kate, though, was starting to get impatient. "Sonya,” she interjected, her voice laced with frustration. "Where is Yelena? Can you just tell me already?"

    Sonya sighed dramatically, feigning helplessness. "Wish I could, Kate, but you know how Yelena is. Clandestine ops, classified intel, all that jazz. She said it wouldn't be appropriate for me to share the details." She winked at Kate. "But trust me, it's nothing you need to worry your pretty little head about."

    Kate narrowed her eyes at Sonya's wink. There was something about the whole situation that felt off. Yelena wouldn't have brushed her off like that, or maybe she would’ve, yet there was also the nagging suspicion that Yelena might actually be doing something she wouldn't want Kate to know about.

    "Look," Sonya continued, her voice softening slightly, at the look on Kate’s face, "I know this is all a bit… unexpected. Yelena can handle herself, Kate. Whatever she is doing, is not without purpose.”

    Kate bit her lip, torn between her trust in Yelena and the gnawing unease in her gut. Sonya's words rang true, but something about the situation just didn't sit right. "I…" she stammered, unsure of what to say.

    Sonya watched Kate closely, the playful glint in her eyes fading slightly. She wasn't used to feeling this off-balance. Usually, her lies flowed effortlessly, but seeing the raw worry flicker across Kate's face made it difficult to maintain her facade. Taking a chance, Sonya added, hesitantly, "Kate. She said she would text you before… before she left her current position…?"

    The question hung in the air, and the weight of it seemed to shift the atmosphere in the room. Clint stifled a snort, but Steve sent him a warning glance. Bucky, ever perceptive, raised an eyebrow at Sonya's hesitation. Something was definitely up.

    Kate's brow furrowed even deeper. The more Sonya spoke, the less she believed every word that left her lips. "Before she left her current position?" she repeated, her voice tight. "What does that even mean?"

    Sonya shrugged, but the gesture lacked its usual confidence. "Just what I said. Yelena said she'd send a text before… you know, moving on to the next phase of the mission or whatever."

    "Or whatever?" Kate echoed, her voice laced with suspicion. "Sonya…”

    A heavy silence descended upon the room. The air crackled with tension. Even Clint seemed to sense the shift in mood. Sonya knew she was pushing Kate to her limit, but the lie was already in motion, and she had to see it through. Taking a deep breath, she tried a different tactic.

    "Look, Kate," she began, her voice gentle, "I understand you're worried. But trust me, Yelena is a capable fighter. She’s been doing this her whole life. Besides," she added, a sly smile returning to her lips, "knowing Yelena, she's probably having the time of her life. She lives for situations like this.” Sonya smiled more to herself than for those in the room. The lightness of Sonya's voice did little to dispel Kate's growing unease. In fact, it only intensified her suspicion. A cold dread settled in her stomach.

    “She's going to do something stupid, isn’t she?"

    The question hung heavy in the air, a silent plea for reassurance. But Sonya, for the first time, hesitated. The carefree facade she'd maintained was crumbling. Looking at the raw worry etched on Kate's face, a pang of guilt twisted in her gut. Perhaps, she thought, she'd pushed the deception a little too far.

    Just then, a sharp buzz cut through the tension. Kate practically leaped for her phone, snatching it up with trembling hands. The others watched with bated breath as she stared at the screen, her face a mask of conflicting emotions. Finally, she looked up. "It's from Yelena," she said, her voice barely a whisper.

    Everyone leaned in, anticipation thick in the air. Kate cleared her throat and read the message aloud, her voice shaky. "'Promise me you will never feed Fanny pizza.'” A stunned silence followed. Clint snorted, breaking the tension. "Seriously? That's all she has to say?"

    Kate, however, oddly had a hint of a smile played on her lips. "That's Yelena," she murmured, a newfound resolve in her eyes.

    Sonya let out a relieved breath. Maybe, just maybe, she'd managed to salvage the situation. "See, Kate?" she said, her voice lighter. "Nothing to worry about."

    “Well, she still sounds like Yelena,” Kate conceded sarcastically, “but of all things she could’ve texted… oh…” Kate’s face fell. “She’s telling me Fanny is mine to look after if… if she dies.” The brunette’s head snapped to look at Sonya, her eyes burning Sonya’s skin. Sonya sighed, caught between her loyalty to Yelena and the growing suspicion in the Compound. She knew she couldn't keep up the charade forever. "Alright," she admitted, her voice defeated. "You got me, she’s not, not doing something stupid. I can't tell you the details. It's classified."

    "Classified?" Sam scoffed. "Come on, Sonya. I know you don’t owe us anything, nor does Yelena, but look at the kid.” He nodded to Kate’s pinched face.

    Sonya chewed on her lip, her gaze flitting between the concerned faces around her. An unfamiliar pang of… fondness? Yes, fondness, flickered in her chest. It was a strange sensation, this bond she'd developed with these ragtag heroes. Back in the Red Room, loyalty was a weapon, a tool for manipulation. Here, it felt different. Here, it felt… real. She sighed, the weight of their concern pressing down on her. Maybe a little honesty wouldn't hurt. Just a little.

    "Fine," she finally relented, a hint of a smirk playing on her lips. "Here's what I can tell you. Yelena got a tip-off. A good one, from a source she… trusts." Her eyes flicked to Kate, who perked up slightly at the mention of trust. "Seems Rick, bless his fuzzy head, stumbled onto something interesting. Something Yelena feels compelled to follow up on." Rick Mason, for all his eccentricities, had a knack for finding information. And Yelena, well, Yelena had a knack for dealing with it, often in spectacularly messy ways. "So, it's Rick involved in this?" Clint asked, his voice thoughtful and somewhat on edge, "Does he know the nature of the mission?"

    Sonya shook her head. "Not a clue. Knowing Rick, he probably just spilled a cryptic message and ran for the hills before Yelena could interrogate him further."

    A chuckle escaped Clint's lips. "Sounds about right. So, what now? Do we just sit here twiddling our thumbs while Yelena goes rogue?"

    Sonya met his gaze, a steely glint in her eyes. "Rogue? Barton, please. Yelena's a solo act, but she's not reckless… хорошо, she’s not reckless all the time. Let's just say she has a certain fondness for… improvised solutions."

    Clint snorted. "Improvised solutions that usually involve a lot of explosions and property damage if she’s anything like her sister."

    Sonya shrugged, a hint of a smile playing on her lips. "Hey, if it gets the job done, right? Besides, who else are you going to call when you need a heavily armed ballerina to take down a rogue Hydra base hidden underneath a kindergarten?"

    Suddenly, Kate, who had been uncharacteristically quiet throughout Sonya's story, rose from her chair. "Excuse me, guys," she interjected, her voice laced with a range of emotion. "I… I need to make a call."

    The others looked at her in surprise. "A call?" Steve repeated. "Who to?" Kate hesitated for a moment, then squared her shoulders. "Yelena," she said strongly. "I may not know the whole story, but I'm not sitting around here waiting for something bad to happen. I'm going to find her."

    A collective sigh filled the room. They all understood Kate's concern, but a solo mission to find Yelena was just as risky, if not more so, than Yelena's own mission, whatever it may be. "Kate," Clint began, his voice gentle but firm, "that's a bad idea. Yelena wouldn't want you to put yourself in danger."

    "Maybe not," Kate countered, her jaw set, "but I can't just do nothing. I don’t want her in danger either, but here she is… again.” The last word came out laced with a frustration and helplessness that resonated with everyone in the room.

    Sonya watched Kate, a flicker of admiration sparking in her eyes. This girl, despite her lack of experience, had a fierce loyalty to her best friend that was almost… endearing, if she wasn’t also so stupid.

    "Look, Kate," Sonya began, her voice softening slightly, "Believe me, the last thing I want is for Yelena to get hurt. You going after her alone would be more than a nightmare for her than anything that could happen to her where she is.”

    "Because I would get in her way I suppose?” Kate shot back, her voice tight with frustration. "So what? Instead, I just sit here and wait for her to get herself blown up in some forgotten corner of the world? That's not happening."

    Sonya sighed, a weary smile tugging at the corners of her lips. There was a fire in Kate's eyes, a stubborn determination that mirrored Yelena's own. This was going to be harder than she thought.

    "Alright," she conceded, raising her hands in surrender. "Here's the thing. I know you care about Yelena, and frankly, I admire your loyalty. But I'm under strict instructions to keep you out of trouble. Strict instructions that come directly from…" she hesitated, searching for the right words, "well, let's just say someone who cares about you a whole lot." Kate's scowl deepened. "Oh, so that's why you suddenly showed up?" Her voice dripped with sarcasm. "Because Yelena thinks I need a babysitter?"

    The accusation wasn’t wrong, but Sonya held her ground. "Look, Kate," she said firmly, "it's not about babysitting. It's about making sure you don't do anything rash that could get you hurt, or worse, cause Yelena to get hurt.”

    "Like I’m supposed to believe a word you say?” Kate scoffed. "Like you haven't been lying through your teeth this whole time?"

    Sonya winced. She couldn't blame Kate for being angry. Keeping secrets wasn't exactly a recipe for trust. But there was more to the story, things Sonya couldn't reveal just yet. "I know I haven't exactly been forthcoming," Sonya admitted. "There is a reason for that reason. A reason that has to do with keeping Yelena and yourself safe. And right now, the best way you can help our friend is by staying put."

    "Keeping her safe?!" Kate shrieked, her voice cracking with a mixture of anger and despair. "How can you say that? She's out there alone, facing who knows what, and you expect me to just… stay put?”

    "Kate," Steve interjected, his voice calm but firm. "Sonya is just trying to-" Kate cut him off with a dismissive wave of her hand. "Save it, Cap. This is between me and Sonya." Her gaze locked onto Sonya's, a fierce challenge blazing in her hazel eyes. "You want to keep me safe? You want to keep Yelena safe? Then tell me the truth! Tell me what she's up against, and maybe, just maybe, I can actually do something to help!" Sonya's heart ached for Kate. She saw the raw fear and determination mirrored in the young woman's eyes, a reflection of Yelena's own spirit. But the truth, the whole truth, was locked away, classified information that could put not only Yelena but the entire team at risk. Especially when Sonya knew they wouldn’t hesitate to fly to Virginia at the first utter of the information.

    "I can't." Sonya said, her voice filled with regret.

    That was it.

    The final straw.

    In a move that surprised everyone, Kate slammed her hands down on the table, the force sending a tremor through the room. "Then don't!" she screamed, her voice laced with raw emotion. "Don't tell me anything! If you can't trust me enough to share the truth, then what's the point of any of this? Let Kingpin and Valentina kill me already for all I care. Let them finish the Bishop line! I say to finish the fucking job!”

    Before anyone could react, Kate whirled around and stormed out of the room, slamming the door shut behind her with a deafening bang. The silence left behind was heavy and oppressive.

    The others exchanged worried glances. They all understood Kate's frustration, but her outburst had left them at a loss. Only Steve seemed unfazed. He simply nodded towards the door Kate had exited through.

    "Give her some space," he said quietly. "She'll come around."

    The others exchanged some glances which indicated they thought otherwise. -

    Downstairs, in the dimly lit gym, Kate could barely see straight. Rage and frustration clouded her judgment, a suffocating tightness constricting her chest. She needed an outlet, a way to channel the storm of emotions churning inside her.

    Without bothering to tape her hands or put on gloves, Kate launched herself at the heavy punching bag hanging from the ceiling. Her fists pounded against the worn leather; each blow a silent scream. Sweat dripped down her face, blurring her vision, but she didn't stop. She pounded the bag until her arms burned, until her knuckles throbbed, until the only sound in the room was the rhythmic thud of her fists and the ragged gasps escaping her lips. But the pain wasn't enough. It didn't drown out the roar of frustration that echoed in her head. Tears welled up in her eyes, stinging the salty sweat already tracking down her cheeks. With a choked sob, she unleashed another primal scream, the sound raw and desperate. "Why are widows all the damn same!" she shrieked, each word punctuated by a brutal blow to the bag. "Nothing's ever…what it seems! Just…secrets and… lies!" The brunette gasps for breaths in between each punch.

    Blood began to seep from a split knuckle, a crimson stain blooming against the worn leather. But Kate barely registered it, the pain a mere whisper compared to the emotional turmoil within. Another blow, another scream, another tear that escaped, tracing a glistening path down her cheek.

    Exhaustion finally began to set in, her arms trembling with fatigue. But even as her body gave out, her spirit remained defiant. Sinking to her knees, Kate rested her forehead against the rough canvas of the punching bag, sobs wracking her body. She felt lost, adrift in a sea of secrets and lies.

    The frustration, the helplessness – it all came crashing down, a tidal wave of emotion that threatened to drown her.

    Beneath the brunette’s anger, beneath the fear, there was another, deeper ache. A grief she'd kept buried for so long, a constant dull throb in the back of her mind. The grief for her parents, ripped away from her in a violent act of betrayal, one that had simmered through her childhood unbeknownst to her.

    Tears, not just of frustration, but of displaced grief, streamed down her face, mingling with the sweat that slicked her skin.

    Images flickered behind her eyelids – her mother's gentle smile, her father's booming laugh. Memories so precious, so fleeting, they felt like a dream from another life. They had tainted all of them for her, her childhood, her innocence, and yet deep down, she was still the young girl who missed her dad with a ferocity that took her breath away. The only difference was that the pain had doubled.

    And Yelena. The only other person who seemingly truly understood the way she felt about her parents, the only other person who bore the emotional scars of being unwanted and betrayed, had left her too.

    Kate wouldn't let Yelena leave too. Kate had promised that to Yelena and now to herself. Neither of them would be alone again.

    With a ragged sob, Kate pushed herself back to her feet. Her vision blurred, but she hardened her gaze. Wiping her tears with the back of her hand, she stumbled out of the gym, her body a mess, but her heart set on a single purpose.

    Justice.

    For herself.

    And for Yelena.

    The late afternoon sun cast a cold, orange glow on the snow-dusted sprawl of Langley, Virginia. Yelena crouched low on the lip of the rooftop; her loose hairs plastered to her forehead with sweat despite the biting chill. Across the alleyway, the imposing edifice of CIA headquarters loomed, a fortress of glass and steel bristling with security measures. For an ordinary person, it would be an impenetrable obstacle.

    For Yelena Belova, it was any other Tuesday.

    With a practiced flick of her wrist, Yelena checked the grappling hook nestled in her forearm holster. The metal gleamed dully in the dying light. A single, silent prayer escaped her lips, for there was no knowing what she was walking, well, falling into this time. With a silent count, she sprang. The grappling hook launched from its holster, the cable whipping through the air with a satisfying snap. It snagged cleanly on the opposing rooftop, and Yelena propelled herself with the power of honed muscle and sheer will. She swung across the snowy chasm, a light blur against the snowscape.

    Landing silently on the slick rooftop, she crouched low, assessing her surroundings. A single security guard patrolled the perimeter of this roof, his breath puffing out in white clouds as he shuffled in the cold. Yelena waited, her body a study in predator-like stillness, until the guard's back was turned. Then, with the grace of a panther, she launched herself. One swift kick landed squarely on the back of the unsuspecting guard's head. He crumpled to the ground with a muffled grunt, unconscious before he even knew what hit him. Yelena didn't waste a moment. Locating the roof access hatch, she popped it open with practiced ease. A ladder descended into a darkened stairwell, the only sound a faint hum of ventilation, the sterile air thick with the metallic tang of cleaning supplies.

    With a final glance at the now-falling snow, Yelena descended into the unknown, a ghost in the gleaming machine of the CIA. The secrets she sought lay hidden somewhere within, guarded by more than just walls and security guards. Here, in the sterile heart of American intelligence, deception was as common as air conditioning.

    Her original plan, a daring rooftop infiltration followed by a confident strut through the halls, had evaporated the moment she'd seen the security protocols in place. This wasn't a simple smash-and-grab mission – not that Alexei would come quietly or be easily dragged. No, this required stealth of the highest order.

    Yelena scanned the deserted hallway she’d fallen into. Cameras blinked red in the distance, their silent scrutiny a constant reminder of the ever-watchful eyes. Alexei and Valentina could be anywhere in this labyrinthine building. Wandering the halls openly was an invitation for disaster.

    Thinking fast, Yelena spotted a vent cover hanging slightly ajar at the end of the corridor. With a silent curse, she squeezed through the narrow opening, her body folding into itself like a human origami sculpture. The air inside the vents was dry and dusty, the metal scraping uncomfortably against her uncovered skin. But it offered a hidden path, a way to navigate the building unseen.

    She began to crawl, her movements slow and deliberate. The hum of ventilation grew louder, punctuated by the muffled murmur of conversation filtering up from somewhere below. Yelena held her breath, straining to hear. Was it them? Alexei's gruff voice, Valentina's sharp retort? The conversation snippets were brief, tantalizingly out of context. A mention of protocols, an asset retrieval mission gone wrong…

    Yelena cursed silently. These weren't the juicy details she craved, no hidden or buried secrets. But every conversation was a piece of the puzzle, a breadcrumb leading her closer to her quarry. She needed to be patient, to follow the trail wherever it led. As the conversation faded, Yelena continued her trek through the tunnel. The claustrophobic darkness pressed in on her, but she pushed forward, fuelled by a relentless determination. Somewhere in this maze of vents, she would find her answers. Somewhere in this building, the truth awaited.

    Suddenly, a muffled conversation erupted below, clear as day through the thin metal duct. Yelena froze, her heart hammering against her ribs. This time, the voices were unmistakable. She inched closer, every fibre of her being focused on the conversation below. "You see, Valentina," a gruff voice, laced with a thick Russian accent, boomed, "she's a natural. Learned faster than any other Widow ever trained. I remember that one mission in Siberia? Took down fifteen men single-handedly. Made me damn proud when the General told me it did."

    A shiver ran down Yelena's spine. Siberia. The mission that haunted her sleep, a bloody blur of violence and fear. Fifteen men. The number echoed in her head, a stark reminder of the monster they'd turned her into.

    "Alexei," a woman's voice, calmer but no less steely, countered, "this is why we need Yelena on our side. She's a loose cannon, yes, but her skills are invaluable." "Hah!" Alexei scoffed. “You said she said no. That girl's stubborn as a mule, just like her mother that one. Don’t tell Melina I said that.”

    A sharp laugh escaped Valentina ."Melina? Alexei, darling, you think I care what Melina thinks? I’ve been done playing nice with those Red Room rejects for years now." Her voice grew steely once more. "Yelena's a problem I'm already dealing with. My new team are out there right now, hunting down the latest batch of escapees. I’ve lost eight this past week, courtesy of your little Yelena."

    Alexei's laughter bubbled in his throat. "Eight? That’s my girl.” He threw his arms up in celebration.

    Yelena flinched, the weight of his praise feeling heavier than any condemnation. Here was the man who'd raised her, who also shouldered some responsibility for the monster she'd become, revelling in the carnage she'd wrought.

    "She's a thorn in my side, Alexei. A skilled thorn, but a thorn, nonetheless. And I need you to find a way to neutralize her." The weight of those words settled on Yelena like a lead blanket. Neutralize. A cold, clinical term for what they truly desired - her elimination. “We're building something new, something bigger. Yelena is getting in our way.”

    A flicker of unease crossed Alexei's face, quickly masked by a forced chuckle. "Right, right. The future and all that. So, what about Yelena then? You said you needed to… neutralize her?"

    "Neutralize," Valentina repeated, the word dripping with distaste. "Not necessarily eliminate. Let's just say... she's become a bit of a… liability. Her meddling is causing problems. We need her out of the picture, at least for the foreseeable future."

    Alexei bristled. "You can't just… put my girl out to pasture! She's not some disposable asset, Valentina. That’s my little girl."

    A steely glint entered Valentina's eyes. Valentina's lips thinned into a disapproving line. "Alexei," she said, her voice laced with a dangerous calm, "this isn't some backyard brawl. We need a solution, not a proud papa moment. Besides, nobody said anything about disposal, Alexei. I simply require her absence. A change of scenery, perhaps. Somewhere she can't cause any more trouble… for us."

    Alexei hesitated, torn between blind loyalty to his pseudo-daughter and a healthy dose of fear for his own well-being. "And what happens if she… refuses this change of scenery?" Valentina's smile was devoid of warmth. "Then," she said, her voice a low purr, "we'll have to employ more… persuasive methods."

    The unspoken threat hung heavy in the air, a chilling reminder of the woman’s ruthless efficiency. Yelena, listening from above, held her breath. Neutralize. Change of scenery. These were euphemisms for her death, used by Valentina to manipulate Alexei into helping her, a lie, an empty promise for her safety when Val would love nothing more than to vanish Yelena like a ghost.

    "Do you even know who she's been associating with lately, Alexei?" Valentina's voice dripped with venomous sarcasm. "The very people who all but pushed your other little girl off a cliff?”

    Alexei scoffed, a dismissive wave of his hand. "The Avengers? Bunch of over-glorified show ponies. Couldn't hurt a fly if they wanted to. Captain America is nothing compared to me – The Red Guardian.” He flexes his muscles with a growl, “The girl's gotta make friends somewhere. Always been a lonely one has our Yelena. I tell her I do, take that frown of your face, you look scary, but does she listen to her dear old отец? Нет.”

    Valentina's lips curled into a cunning smirk as she leaned in closer to Alexei, her eyes glinting with satisfaction. "Lonely, you say? Well, perhaps she's not as alone as you think," she whispered, her tone dripping with calculated deceit. "In fact, I heard a little rumour recently. A certain someone we thought was long gone might have made a miraculous comeback."

    Alexei's eyes widened in surprise, "What… what are you talking about?" he stammered, his voice tinged with uncertainty, nervous for what information could come tumbling out of his mouth.

    Valentina's smile widened, relishing in the manipulation at play. "Oh, you know who I'm talking about, Alexei," she purred, her voice smooth as silk. "The Red Room's most prized asset. The Black Widow herself."

    Alexei's jaw dropped, his expression a mixture of shock and disbelief. "Natasha… alive?" he breathed, his voice barely above a whisper. “Wow. I did not know?” The man tried to lie, tried, being the operative word.

    Valentina nodded slowly, enjoying every moment of the revelation. "Yes. It seems you clearly had no idea…” The woman drawled as she confirmed with a wicked glint in her eyes. Alexei tried to salvage the lie, a desperate attempt to maintain some semblance of control. "Maybe Yelena mentioned something… in passing, you know? These girls, always gossiping…"

    Valentina's humour evaporated faster than the condensation on a glass of ice. "Alexei," she cut in, her voice a steely blade, "don't waste my time. You may be a useful tool, albeit it not the sharpest, but you're not a good liar and nor are you indispensable. And right now, your usefulness to me hinges on your ability to follow instructions."

    Alexei shrunk under her withering gaze. The playful banter had vanished, replaced by a cold professionalism that sent shivers down his spine. "Instructions?" he croaked, his bravado thoroughly deflated.

    "Yelena," Valentina stated flatly, her voice leaving no room for argument. "She's become a liability. Dispose of her.” Valentina's lips curled into a humorless smile at Alexei’s reaction to her order. "Family is a luxury we can't afford in this line of work, Alexei. Especially not when family becomes a loose cannon with a fondness for taking down our assets." A heavy silence descended upon the room, broken only by the distant hum of ventilation. Alexei knew the truth. He wouldn’t be able to contain Yelena, or reason with her. He knew was being handed a veiled order to eliminate his own daughter. The weight of the task pressed down on him like a physical weight for Yelena would not leave where she wanted to be, or hide under his order, nor anyone else’s.

    "A month," Valentina finally said, her voice devoid of emotion. "You have a month to get this… situation under control. After that, well, let's just say the consequences for failure are… unpleasant."

    A single bead of sweat rolled down Alexei's temple, leaving a glistening track on his weathered face. He looked like a man caught in a rip current, pulled under by a force far stronger than himself. Yelena, listening from above, felt a surge of adrenaline. Valentina wanted her dead. Her own "father" was tasked with her elimination, but Val had not given him a direct order to take Yelena’s life. Just her free will.

    Oh, the irony.
