"Which means…" She trailed off, letting the implication hang heavy in the air. Laura's eyes widened in horror. "Two days," she breathed, her voice barely a whisper. The room erupted in a flurry of activity. Clint shot to his feet, his face grim. Natasha's hand instinctively went to the holster at her hip, her eyes blazing with fury. "We need a plan," Steve said, his voice firm and commanding. "Yelena, tell us everything you remember about that conversation."

    Yelena, however, rolled her eyes at the sudden surge of panic. “Valentina isn't psychic. She doesn't know if Alexei did anything or not. She can't exactly check in with him and ask if he's gotten rid of his pain-in-the-ass daughter, can she? Alexei's practically under house arrest with Melina keeping an eye on him. Valentina's not getting to him anytime soon. Plus, she saw me half dead pretty recently, I’d say she’s not worried about me at the moment." Clint lowered himself back into his chair, while Natasha simply stared at her, a mix of scepticism and grudging reluctance in her gaze.

    "Yelena's right," Nat admitted after a moment. "Valentina wouldn't risk blowing her cover by contacting Alexei directly. And there is no way she could find Melina’s house.” Yelena nodded in agreement. "Exactly. I can handle myself. For now, I just need to lay low. Let Valentina think Alexei's done the job. I'll figure out a way to deal with her later." Bucky, ever the blunt one, spoke up, his metal arm gleaming under the light. "How exactly do you plan to 'deal with her' Yelena? Because from where I'm sitting, 'dealing with Valentina' sounds an awful lot like…" He trailed off, letting the implication hang heavy in the air. Yelena, for her part, didn't flinch. She met Bucky's gaze head-on, a cold glint in her own eyes. "Maybe it is," she said, her voice devoid of emotion. "Someone needs to make her pay." "Whoa, whoa, whoa," Clint interjected, holding up his hands in a placating gesture. "Let's pump the brakes here. Killing people isn't exactly the Avengers' M.O." "Since when?" Bucky scoffed. "We put down threats, Clint. And Valentina sounds like a pretty damn dangerous threat to me. She's got her fingers in all sorts of bad stuff, and now she’s recruiting. You really want more Valentina copycats to carry her legacy after she’s gone?”

    "There may be other ways to deal with Valentina," Steve said, his voice firm but laced with a hint of weariness. "We can gather intel, expose her network… There has to be a way to take her down without resorting to…" He trailed off, not needing to finish the sentence. “No.”

    “Nat?”

    “If Valentina wasn’t lying about her connections with Kingpin and they are truly working together, exposing her network would take us years. She’s the Director of the CIA Steve. That’s international links, allies, enemies. Your method may work with Kingpin… but not her.” Natasha said plainly.

    Steve frowned, his ever-present moral compass stirring uneasily. "So, you're fine with murder now?" he asked, his voice laced with disappointment.

    Natasha met his gaze unflinchingly. "This isn't about some moral high ground, Steve," she countered, her voice laced with a hint of frustration. "This is about protecting ourselves, protecting the world from a woman who clearly has no qualms about using and discarding people like pawns." She paused, her eyes flashing with a dangerous glint. "Besides, this isn't exactly something new, is it?"

    Yelena, however, wasn't interested in their moral debate. She slammed her fist on the table, startling everyone. "People who act without reason cannot be reasoned with," she declared, her voice ringing with a cold fury. "Valentina doesn't care about right or wrong, only about furthering her own agenda.”

    Sam spoke up. "And what exactly is that agenda? We have no idea what her endgame is, nor Fisk's for that matter."

    Yelena's gaze flickered to Kate, then back to Sam. "Fisk is focused on the mayoral election, and on the Bishop family," she said, her voice low and dangerous. A flicker of something dark passed through her eyes, a reminder of the cold, calculating woman she used to be. "Valentina... she wants control. To stop history from repeating itself, she says." She paused, her mind racing. "She lost everything because of the Avengers, mainly her SHIELD job. Her ex-husband ran off with the Wakandans and her contacts dried up because of his link with the Black Panther."

    "So, Valentina is working with the biggest New York mob boss and using their funds behind their backs to assemble a team of morally grey heroes because she hates us?" Steve summarized, disbelief evident in his voice.

    Yelena shrugged, a nonchalant expression on her face that belied the storm of emotions churning within her. "It does sound rather stupid when you put it like that," she admitted, a hint of a smirk playing on her lips.

    Kate snorted, amusement warring on her face. Yelena returned the look with a cheeky smirk. "So, what's the plan?" Bucky asked, cutting through the stunned silence. "Hunt Valentina down and take her out?"

    Natasha let out a humourless chuckle. "Easier said than done," she replied, her voice laced with a hint of grim determination.

    "What about Kingpin?" Laura interjected, her eyes narrowing in thought. "He's still out there, and if he wins the election, he'll make every enhanced person in New York's life a living hell."

    Sam raised an eyebrow. "There can't be that many enhanced people living in New York," he said, his voice laced with scepticism.

    “Moonknight, The Punisher, Jessica Jones, Daredevil, Strange, Spiderman, shall I keep going? And not to mention the Avengers Compound is in New York. That is not a factor to overlook.” Clint listed off.

    Sam crossed his arms, his scepticism giving way to cautious consideration as Clint rattled off the list of enhanced individuals in New York. "Alright, so maybe there's more than I thought," he conceded, but the doubt in his voice lingered. "But what's our play here? We can't just go after all of them at once."

    Steve nodded in agreement. "There has already been a surveillance attack on the compound," he said, a grim look on his face. "If Fisk wins the election, what is there to stop him from getting rid of it completely?"

    Laura’s brow furrowed as she processed the gravity of their situation. "Kingpin's got his hands in everything. If he takes office, it won't just be the compound that's at risk. He'll have eyes and ears everywhere, controlling the narrative in the city. We need to stop him before it gets to that point."

    Yelena's voice cut through the room, drawing everyone's attention. "You're all looking at this the wrong way," she said, her accent giving her words an extra edge. "You're thinking of them as two separate problems—Val and Kingpin. But they're not. They're the same enemy, just two heads of the same beast."

    Bucky, leaning against the back of his chair, raised a eyebrow. "That may be true, but we still have to fight them on two fronts. It's not like Valentina is based in New York." Yelena's eyes narrowed as she considered his point. "No, she's not in New York, but she’s been there before. We know she’s got business in the city, and that's reason enough to set a trap."

    Natasha leaned forward, arms resting on the table as she gave Yelena a measured look. "I don’t think Valentina’s going to be fooled by something as simple as a fake text message or business meeting," she cautioned.

    Yelena shook her head, a smirk tugging at the corner of her lips. "No, she won’t be. But Kingpin’s goons? They’re not nearly as smart. We can use them to draw her out. They’ll act as her eyes and ears in the city, and if we shake the tree hard enough, she’ll come looking to see who’s messing with her operations."

    Sam nodded slowly, seeing the pieces starting to come together. "So, we use Kingpin’s people to lead us to Valentina. Stir up enough trouble, make it look like a threat to her business, and she might just take the bait."

    The team exchanged glances, the plan beginning to take shape, when Laura, who had been quietly listening, spoke up. "What about Marlene Fisk?" Her voice was calm but carried a weight that made everyone turn toward her. "Her records were scrubbed clean. That’s not something you overlook. We need to find out why and how she fits into all of this." Yelena nodded, her expression turning serious. "I’ll get the Widows to look into it." Everyone in the room looked at her, a mixture of surprise and confusion evident on their faces. Natasha was the first to voice the unspoken question, her tone cautious. "I thought the Widows were off limits. We agreed to let them live their lives, free from all of this." Yelena met Natasha’s gaze, her eyes unwavering. "Yes, they are off limits—to all of you. But I am not you." Her voice was firm, a clear line drawn between her and the others, with an added smirk for good measure. "The Widows trust me, and they believe they owe me so…” The blonde shrugged.

    The room fell silent as Yelena’s words hung in the air, the weight of her statement sinking in. Natasha's eyes narrowed slightly, her protective instincts flaring, but she said nothing. She understood Yelena's position better than anyone—her sister had always operated in the shadows, navigating a world where the lines between allies and assets were often blurred. Clint cleared his throat, breaking the tension. "So, we have a dual strategy—use Kingpin's goons to draw out Valentina, and dig into Marlene Fisk's connections. If we can find something solid on her, it might give us the leverage we need."

    Bucky, who had been silently processing the plan, nodded in agreement. "It’s risky, but it’s better than waiting for them to make the first move. We need to stay ahead of them." Bucky exchanged a glance with Sam, both of them coming to the same conclusion. "We should head back to New York," Bucky suggested. "The Compound’s a good base, and we can start moving pieces on the board from there."

    Sam nodded, already thinking several steps ahead. Steve straightened; his decision already made. "I’ll come with you. We’re going to need as many people on the ground as possible, and I don’t want to leave anything to chance."

    Clint, who had been listening intently, raised an eyebrow. "What about us? What’s our move?"

    Sam turned to him, his expression serious. "They’ve got to have supply shipments heading somewhere. Disrupting those wouldn’t be a bad place to start. Hit them where it hurts. It’ll mess with their timeline and force them to react."

    Clint nodded, seeing the logic in the plan. "Makes sense. I’ll start contacting some old friends and find out if and where such shipments are coming from and where they’re going." Before the conversation could move forward, Kate spoke up, her voice eager. "I’ll go too. I know New York better than any of you."

    Her offer was met with immediate resistance. Clint and Laura both shook their heads, almost in unison. "No," Clint said firmly. "It’s too dangerous. You’ve done enough, Kate." Laura’s voice was softer but no less resolute. “You’re one of his targets for whatever reason Kate. You’re not going to do what others can when things are about to get even more dangerous.”

    Kate bristled at the protective tone, her hands clenching into fists. "I can handle myself. I’ve been training for this. I’m not a kid anymore."

    Clint’s expression softened, but he didn’t relent. "I know, but this isn’t just a training mission. It’s going to get ugly. We’re dealing with people who don’t play by the rules." Kate opened her mouth to argue, but Natasha cut in, her voice calm and measured. "Kate, this isn’t about doubting your abilities. We need to be smart about who we send into the field and the smartest move is not sending what he wants right to where he wants it." As the tension in the room thickened, Natasha’s sharp gaze flicked to Yelena, who had remained unusually quiet. Nat noticed the subtle way Yelena’s eyes lingered on Kate, not with surprise or concern, but with a curious indifference. Natasha could see the wheels turning in Yelena’s mind, as if she was weighing something, calculating the risks versus the rewards. Natasha studied her sister closely, sensing that Yelena’s silence held more weight than her words ever could.

    Kate, undeterred by Clint and Laura's objections, continued to argue her case. “I’ve been living in New York my whole life. I know the city, I know the people, and I know how to navigate through it better than anyone here.”

    Steve, always the voice of reason, stepped forward, his tone calm but firm. “I get that, Kate, but Bucky and I—we grew up in Brooklyn. We know New York as much as you do, and we’ve seen it through some pretty tough times.”

    Kate, not missing a beat, deadpanned, “You knew New York a century ago, Steve. It’s changed. A lot.”

    There was a brief, stunned silence as the room took in Kate's blunt remark. Even Bucky cracked a small, amused smile, appreciating the quick wit. Steve didn’t take offense, though there was a faint glimmer of acknowledgment in his eyes. He knew she was right in some ways—the New York he once knew was vastly different from the one that existed now, especially with all the complexities of the modern world.

    Clint, sensing the growing tension, tried to redirect the conversation. "Kate, it's not about whether you know the city. It's about who we’re dealing with and the fact they are interested in you.”

    But Kate wasn’t backing down. "And that’s exactly why you need me. My name can get us into places that you might not even know exist. You need every edge you can get, and I’m it." Natasha’s eyes remained on Yelena as the argument continued, watching the subtle shifts in her sister’s demeanour. Yelena’s expression hadn’t changed much—still that calm, detached curiosity—but Natasha could see her mind was working overtime, analysing every word, every possible outcome. Yelena wasn’t just thinking about the mission; she was thinking about Kate, about how this could all play out.

    Laura, who had been quietly listening, finally interjected. "Kate, your name can’t get us anywhere that the name Captain America can’t. If we need to open doors, Steve’s got more than enough pull."

    Kate’s gaze flicked to Laura, her determination unwavering. "Steve going around flaunting the name and his shield isn’t going to be very subtle. At least a Bishop coming and going to these places isn’t unheard of. My presence wouldn’t raise alarms; Steve’s would. You send Captain America to some of these places, and it’s like sending a flare into the night. But me? I grew up in the company of the people Kingpin is friends with. The political circle is heavily intertwined with the New York elite. It wouldn’t be unheard of for a Bishop to be seen at certain events, but Captain America? He’d stick out like a sore thumb."
